Here’s the next piece as arepo-ready implementation specfor turning the WRP docs you just put into Conduit into structured Nebula artifacts, chunks, and cross-references.docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdMarkdown# WRP Document Projection Rules**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula / WRP integration**Purpose:** Define deterministic rules for projecting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, levels, and cross-references.---# 1. ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning13.2 Chunk IDsFormat:<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning/chunk/01Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.13.3 Re-import stabilityOn re-import:if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stableif a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new idsif a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported14. Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. Future ExtensionsThe following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)embedding generation and vector indexingrole-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itselfsupersession lineage across chunk revisionsbidirectional Conduit synchronizationLLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristicsconfidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments20. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is Here’s the next companion doc as the operational layer for the review-state schema.docs/nebula/review-workflow.mdMarkdown# Nebula Review Workflow**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula governance / corpus maintenance**Purpose:** Define how review state is assigned, updated, interpreted, and used to prioritize attention across Nebula artifacts, sections, and chunks.---# 1. PurposeNebula stores a growing corpus of architecture notes, specifications, migration plans, ontology documents, implementation plans, and execution-adjacent material. Not all corpus material is equally current, equally trustworthy, or equally relevant to active work.This document defines a **review workflow overlay** that allows Nebula users and roles to mark corpus material as:- needing review- under active review- reviewed- current focus- outdated- questioned- supersededThe review workflow exists to answer a different question than lifecycle status.## Lifecycle status answers:- Is this artifact active, draft, deprecated, or superseded in the corpus?## Review status answers:- What should we pay attention to right now?- What should be trusted by default?- What needs inspection before it influences implementation?- What should be deprioritized or excluded from normal retrieval?Review state is therefore a **triage and trust overlay** on top of the corpus, not a replacement for artifact lifecycle semantics.---# 2. Core Principles## 2.1 Review state is separate from artifact lifecycleAn item may be:- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`- `status = SUPERSEDED` and `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- `status = DRAFT` and `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Lifecycle describes what the artifact **is**.Review state describes what the team should **do about it**.## 2.2 Review state is primarily an attention and trust signalReview state is used to:- focus corpus maintenance- guide retrieval ranking- reduce accidental reliance on stale documents- identify blocking or suspect specs- surface active areas of architecture work## 2.3 Artifact-level review is the default starting pointNebula SHOULD support review state at:- artifact level- section level- chunk levelHowever, the initial operational workflow assumes:- **artifact-level review is primary**- section/chunk review is optional and targetedThe system MUST NOT require chunk-by-chunk review to be useful.## 2.4 Review state is allowed to be provisionalReview state is not a certification regime. It is acceptable to mark an item:- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`without yet knowing the final replacement or fix. The goal is to make uncertainty visible and actionable.---# 3. Review Scope LevelsNebula review annotations may apply at three scopes.## 3.1 Artifact scopeApplies to an entire document / artifact such as:- `wrp-v1-protocol`- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `wrp-v1_2-traversal`- `wrp-migration-plan`Artifact scope is the default and most common review target.## 3.2 Section scopeApplies to a specific section within an artifact when the document is mixed-quality.Example:- the WRP protocol document is generally current- but the `Execution Semantics / Receipts` section is outdatedSection review SHOULD be used when:- only one part of a large artifact is stale or questionable- the artifact should remain broadly retrievable without blanket demotion## 3.3 Chunk scopeApplies to a specific chunk when review needs to be precise.Chunk review SHOULD be used sparingly and mainly when:- a particular invariant is suspect- a specific migration step is obsolete- a specific rationale chunk remains valuable even inside an outdated section---# 4. Review Status VocabularyThe following review statuses are defined by `schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`.## 4.1 `UNREVIEWED`The item has not yet been reviewed for current validity or relevance.Use when:- a document was imported but not yet triaged- a new chunk has not been evaluated## 4.2 `NEEDS_REVIEW`The item should be reviewed soon because it may be stale, incomplete, or important to current work.Use when:- the document is likely relevant to current implementation- the document predates a major architectural shift- the document appears important but confidence is low## 4.3 `UNDER_REVIEW`The item is actively being reviewed, rewritten, or reconciled.Use when:- you are actively comparing it against current architecture or code- Builder/Architect/Inspector are working through it now## 4.4 `REVIEWED`The item has been reviewed and is believed to be usable in normal work.Use when:- the document is current enough for default retrieval- known issues are minor or already called out## 4.5 `CURRENT_FOCUS`The item is a current focus of architecture or implementation attention and should be surfaced prominently.Use when:- active work depends on this item now- the item is central to the current execution stream- the item is the present working center of a subsystem redesign## 4.6 `OUTDATED`The item is known to be out of date relative to the current architecture, runtime, or workflow.Use when:- the document predates a material redesign- its prescriptions are no longer safe defaults- it still has historical value but should be demoted## 4.7 `QUESTIONED`The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt.Use when:- parts of the document conflict with newer understanding- the model may be wrong, not merely old- the document should be examined before it is trusted## 4.8 `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval.Use when:- there is a clear replacement artifact or replacement chunk set- the supersession is intentional and not merely suspected---# 5. Review PriorityReview priority answers: **how urgently should this item be revisited?**Allowed values:- `CRITICAL`- `HIGH`- `MEDIUM`- `LOW`## 5.1 Priority guidance### `CRITICAL`Use when:- the item is blocking implementation- the item is actively misleading current work- the item governs current execution and is likely wrong or stale### `HIGH`Use when:- the item is central to near-term architecture or implementation- review delay would materially slow work or degrade decisions### `MEDIUM`Use when:- the item matters, but not immediately- it should be triaged in the near future### `LOW`Use when:- review is backlog hygiene- the item is historical or peripheral---# 6. Attention ReasonsAttention reasons explain **why** an item needs review or focus.The first review-state schema defines these reasons:- `BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIME`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE`- `CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODEL`- `REQUIRES_MIGRATION`- `DUPLICATED_ELSEWHERE`- `NEEDS_LEVEL_REVIEW`- `NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`Multiple reasons MAY be attached to the same item.## ExampleA migration document might be:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `reviewPriority = HIGH`- `attentionReason = [REQUIRES_MIGRATION, OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE]`---# 7. Who May Set Review State## 7.1 Human authority is primaryThe human operator is the authoritative source of review state.In practice, this means you may set review state manually based on reading, comparison, or implementation experience.## 7.2 Roles may propose review state, but not silently finalize itThe following roles may recommend review changes:- **Inspector**- flags contradictions, stale invariants, missing migration updates, or retrieval hazards- **Architect**- flags architectural obsolescence, boundary drift, or rationale conflicts- **Builder**- flags implementation-blocking ambiguity or mismatch with actual code- **Explorer**- flags duplicate or related documents that may need consolidationThese role recommendations SHOULD be recorded as annotations or proposals, but SHOULD NOT silently overwrite the effective review state unless explicitly authorized.## 7.3 Importers may initialize, not decideImporters and projectors MAY set initial values such as:- `UNREVIEWED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW` when the source predates a known migration boundary- `OUTDATED` when explicit source metadata says soHowever, importers SHOULD NOT autonomously mark an item `REVIEWED` or `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`.---# 8. Effective Review State ModelNebula may store multiple review annotations over time. The system therefore needs a rule for determining the **effective review state** used in retrieval and dashboards.## 8.1 Effective review state per scopeEach reviewable object (artifact, section, chunk) SHOULD expose a single **effective review state** for operational use.This effective state may be materialized directly on the object row or computed from annotations.## 8.2 Default precedence ruleIf multiple annotations exist for the same object, the effective review state SHOULD be determined by:1. most recent human-authored authoritative annotation2. otherwise most recent approved role recommendation3. otherwise importer-initialized default4. otherwise `UNREVIEWED`## 8.3 Status severity tie-breakIf multiple candidate annotations are equally authoritative and recent enough to conflict, use the following severity ordering to avoid false optimism:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `UNDER_REVIEW`- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `UNREVIEWED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`This severity ordering is for tie-breaking only and MUST NOT be interpreted as a universal ranking of importance.## 8.4 Why `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is not treated as “most severe”Superseded material is often safe to ignore rather than urgent to fix. It is not necessarily a live problem. Therefore it should not outrank `QUESTIONED` or `CURRENT_FOCUS` in attention logic.---# 9. Artifact / Section / Chunk Rollup RulesReview state may exist at multiple scopes simultaneously. The workflow needs rules for how lower-level review state influences higher-level summaries.## 9.1 Artifact effective review is primaryArtifact review status is the main corpus-level triage signal and SHOULD be set explicitly rather than inferred whenever possible.## 9.2 Section and chunk review do not automatically overwrite artifact reviewIf an artifact is marked `REVIEWED` but one chunk is marked `QUESTIONED`, the artifact does not automatically become `QUESTIONED`.Instead, the artifact SHOULD receive one or more rollup indicators such as:- `needsAttention = true`- `attentionReason += NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`- optional `focusScore` boost- optional “contains questioned chunk” derived flag## 9.3 Optional artifact rollup policyImplementations MAY define a rollup threshold such as:- if ≥ 30% of chunks are `OUTDATED` or `QUESTIONED`, artifact effective review becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`- if any chunk is `CURRENT_FOCUS`, artifact `focusScore` is boosted- if all chunks are `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`, artifact may be proposed as `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`But this rollup SHOULD be advisory until chunk review is common enough to trust statistically.---# 10. Review ActionsThe review workflow recognizes the following actions.## 10.1 Mark Needs ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- optionally priority and attention reasonsUse when an item should enter the review queue.## 10.2 Start ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Use when active review or rewrite has begun.## 10.3 Mark ReviewedSet:- `reviewStatus = REVIEWED`- `lastReviewedAt`- optional summaryUse when the item is current enough for normal use.## 10.4 Mark Current FocusSet:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`Use when the item is a live center of implementation or architecture work.## 10.5 Mark OutdatedSet:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`Use when the item is no longer a safe default but may still be historically useful.## 10.6 Mark QuestionedSet:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`Use when the item may be wrong, not merely old.## 10.7 Confirm SupersededSet:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- set `supersededBy` if knownUse when a replacement is clear and the old material should be demoted from normal retrieval.---# 11. Relationship Between Supersession and ReviewSupersession and review are related but distinct.## 11.1 Supersession is a semantic relationshipExample:- `wrp-v1-protocol-v0` is superseded by `wrp-v1-protocol`This is modeled as:- `supersededBy`- `supersedes`- lifecycle `status`## 11.2 Review supersession is an operational confirmationAn item becomes `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when the team has decided it should be treated as superseded for retrieval and attention purposes.## 11.3 Auto-promotion ruleIf `supersededBy` is set, the system MAY propose:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`but SHOULD NOT automatically finalize it unless configured to do so.Reason:- some superseded artifacts still matter during a migration period- some artifacts are partially superseded but still operationally relevant---# 12. Review Workflow for Corpus TriageThis section defines the simple human workflow the system is meant to support.## 12.1 Initial triage passAs you review the corpus, each artifact SHOULD be assigned one of:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`with optional:- priority- attention reasons- short review summaryThe goal is not perfection. The goal is to make the corpus sortable and navigable.## 12.2 Triage heuristics### Mark `CURRENT_FOCUS` when:- active implementation or redesign is centered on the artifact now### Mark `NEEDS_REVIEW` when:- the artifact is probably important but confidence is not high enough- the artifact predates a major design change- the artifact is about to become implementation-relevant again### Mark `REVIEWED` when:- the artifact is current enough to be used normally### Mark `OUTDATED` when:- the artifact still has historical value but should not be trusted as a default guide### Mark `QUESTIONED` when:- the artifact may encode wrong assumptions or contradictions### Mark `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when:- a replacement exists and default retrieval should normally prefer the replacement---# 13. Retrieval EffectsReview state MUST influence Nebula retrieval.## 13.1 Default retrieval behaviorUnless explicitly overridden:- `CURRENT_FOCUS` receives a strong ranking boost- `REVIEWED` receives a positive ranking boost- `NEEDS_REVIEW` remains retrievable but slightly demoted relative to reviewed/current material- `OUTDATED` is demoted- `QUESTIONED` is demoted for Builder/Architect defaults but may be boosted for Inspector- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is excluded or strongly demoted from default retrieval## 13.2 Role-specific review-state behavior### BuilderPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Demote:- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`Exclude by default:- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`### ArchitectPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Allow:- `QUESTIONED`- selected `OUTDATED` material when rationale still matters### InspectorPrefer:- `QUESTIONED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `OUTDATED`because those often indicate the places where validation and contradiction analysis are most needed.### ExplorerAllow broad inclusion, including:- `OUTDATED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`when historical lineage or unresolved questions matter.---# 14. Dashboard / Queue BehaviorNebula SHOULD support a review queue over artifacts.## 14.1 Default review queueThe default review queue SHOULD show artifacts where:- `reviewStatus IN (NEEDS_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW, CURRENT_FOCUS, OUTDATED, QUESTIONED)`- OR `needsAttention = true`ordered by:1. `reviewPriority`2. `focusScore`3. `updatedAt` or `lastReviewedAt`## 14.2 Suggested dashboard slicesUseful corpus views include:### Current FocusArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`### Needs ReviewArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`### Questioned / RiskyArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`### Outdated but not yet supersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`### SupersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`---# 15. Recommended Initial SQL ShapeFor the first operational implementation, Nebula SHOULD materialize current effective review state directly on `nebula_artifact`.Recommended columns:- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `needs_attention`- `last_reviewed_at`- `review_summary`- `focus_score`Optional on `nebula_chunk`:- same fields, nullableReview history SHOULD be stored separately in `nebula_review_annotation` with fields such as:- `id`- `target_type`- `target_id`- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `attention_reason_json`- `needs_attention`- `reviewed_by`- `review_summary`- `created_at`---# 16. Example Review Annotations## 16.1 Current focus artifact```json{"id": "review:annotation/wrp-v1_2-traversal/2026-06-21","type": "ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo": "wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal","reviewStatus": "review:CURRENT_FOCUS","reviewPriority": "review:CRITICAL","attentionReason": ["review:BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION"],"needsAttention": true,"lastReviewedAt": "2026-06-21T13:00:00Z","reviewedBy": "role:architect","reviewSummary": "Traversal engine spec is the current implementation center and should remain top-ranked for Builder and Architect retrieval."}16.2 Outdated migration sectionJSON{"id":"review:annotation/wrp-migration-plan/execution-cutover/2026-06-21","type":"ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo":"wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan/section/execution-cutover","reviewStatus":"review:OUTDATED","reviewPriority":"review:HIGH","attentionReason": ["review:OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE","review:REQUIRES_MIGRATION"],"needsAttention":true,"lastReviewedAt":"2026-06-21T13:10:00Z","reviewedBy":"role:inspector","reviewSummary":"This section predates the traversal split and should not be used as the default guide for execution cutover."}17. SummaryNebula review workflow exists to turn the corpus into a manageable attention system rather than a passive archive.The governing rule is:Lifecycle status tells us what an artifact is; review state tells us whether we should trust it, revisit it, focus on it, or route around it right now.The initial operational model is intentionally simple:review at artifact scope firstmark items as current focus / needs review / reviewed / outdated / questioned / supersededrecord priority and attention reasonlet retrieval and dashboards honor that stateonly descend to section/chunk review when precision is worth the effort---# Where we are nowWe’ve now inserted the review-governance pair:1. **`schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`**2. **`docs/nebula/review-workflow.md`**So we can go back This is the piece that turns everything you’ve built so far into something executable instead of just well-structured theory.This is youractual compiler spec.docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdMarkdown# WRP → Nebula Projection Pseudocode**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula ingestion / WRP compiler**Purpose:** Define deterministic algorithm for converting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, review overlays, and cross-reference graphs.---# 1. OverviewThis document specifies the **projection compiler pipeline** that transforms WRP markdown documents into structured Nebula graph data.Input:- WRP markdown documentsOutput:- NebulaArtifacts- NebulaSections- NebulaChunks- NebulaCrossReferences- Review overlays (optional but supported)- Conduit links (if present)The pipeline is deterministic, idempotent, and replay-safe.---# 2. High-Level Pipelineparse_markdown()→ build_ast()→ resolve_artifact()→ build_section_tree()→ segment_chunks()→ classify_chunks()→ assign_levels()→ assign_review_overlay()→ extract_cross_references()→ emit_graph()→ upsert_store()---# 3. Core Data Structures (Logical)## ArtifactArtifact {idkeysource_pathstatus}## SectionSection {idartifact_idparent_section_idheadingordinal}## ChunkChunk {idsection_idordinaltextchunk_kindlevelnormative_strength}## ReviewOverlay (optional)ReviewOverlay {target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason[]}## CrossReferenceCrossReference {source_idtarget_idrelation_type}---# 4. Step 1 — Parse Markdown```pseudofunction parse_markdown(source_text):ast = MarkdownParser.parse(source_text)return astRules:preserve heading hierarchypreserve code blocks as atomic nodespreserve tables as atomic nodespreserve block quotes as semantic units5. Step 2 — Artifact Resolutionpseudofunction resolve_artifact(file_path, registry):if registry.contains(file_path):return registry.get(file_path)if STRICT_MODE:throw Error("Unknown artifact in strict mode")return create_artifact_from_path(file_path)Artifact key mapping:derived from filenamenormalized slug6. Step 3 — Build Section Treepseudofunction build_section_tree(ast):root = new SectionTree()current_stack = []for node in ast:if node.type == HEADING:level = node.levelwhile current_stack.top.level >= level:current_stack.pop()section = new Section(heading=node.text,parent=current_stack.top)current_stack.push(section)root.add(section)return rootRules:##→ Section###→ child section####+→ either nested section or flatten depending on config7. Step 4 — Chunk Segmentationpseudofunction segment_chunks(section):chunks = []buffer = []for block in section.blocks:if is_boundary(block, buffer):chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))buffer = []buffer.append(block)if buffer not empty:chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))return chunks7.1 Boundary rulespseudofunction is_boundary(block, buffer):if buffer.empty:return falseif block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:return trueif block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:return trueif semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):return trueif buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:return truereturn false7.2 Semantic shift heuristicpseudofunction semantic_shift(a, b):if a.kind != b.kind:return trueif switches_between("RATIONALE","IMPLEMENTATION","PROTOCOL_RULE"):return truereturn false8. Step 5 — Chunk Classificationpseudofunction classify_chunk(chunk):text = chunk.textif contains("must not", text):chunk.normative = PROHIBITEDelse if contains("must", text):chunk.normative = REQUIREDelse if contains("should", text):chunk.normative = RECOMMENDEDelse:chunk.normative = INFORMATIVEchunk.kind = classify_kind(text)return chunk8.1 Chunk kind classifierpseudofunction classify_kind(text):if matches_definition_pattern(text):return DEFINITIONif contains_protocol_keywords(text):return PROTOCOL_RULEif contains_invariant_keywords(text):return INVARIANTif contains_algorithm_structure(text):return ALGORITHMif contains_schema_fields(text):return DATA_MODELif contains_migration_language(text):return MIGRATION_STEPif contains_open_question_markers(text):return OPEN_QUESTIONif contains_rationale_markers(text):return RATIONALEif contains_example_markers(text):return EXAMPLEreturn OVERVIEW9. Step 6 — Level Assignmentpseudofunction assign_level(chunk):if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:return L1if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:return L2if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:return L3return L210. Step 7 — Review Overlay Assignmentpseudofunction assign_review_overlay(entity, context):overlay = new ReviewOverlay()if entity.is_new:overlay.status = UNREVIEWEDif contains_staleness_signals(entity):overlay.status = NEEDS_REVIEWif matches_current_focus_tags(entity):overlay.status = CURRENT_FOCUSif contains_conflict_signals(entity):overlay.status = QUESTIONEDif superseded_by_exists(entity):overlay.status = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDreturn overlay11. Step 8 — Cross Reference Extractionpseudofunction extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):refs = []for token in chunk.text:if token matches artifact_key:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=artifact_id(token),type=DEPENDS_ON))if token matches section_heading:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=section_id(token),type=REFERENCES))if token matches known_concept:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=concept_id(token),type=MENTIONS))return refs12. Step 9 — Emit Graphpseudofunction emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):graph = NebulaGraph()graph.add(artifact)for section in sections:graph.add(section)for chunk in chunks:graph.add(chunk)for ref in refs:graph.add(ref)return graph13. Step 10 — Upsert Store (Idempotent)pseudofunction upsert_store(graph, db):for node in graph.nodes:db.upsert(node.id, node)for edge in graph.edges:db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)Rules:idempotent writesstable IDs requiredno duplicate edges unless explicitly allowedpreserve existing review annotations unless overridden14. Determinism RulesProjection MUST be deterministic:same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunksno LLM-based randomness in core pipelineonly heuristic classification allowedno sampling variabilityIf classifier improves:version bump requirednew projection run produces new revision lineage15. Failure Modes15.1 Unknown artifact→ fail in STRICT_MODE15.2 ambiguous chunk boundaries→ prefer splitting over merging15.3 classification uncertainty→ default to OVERVIEW + INFORMATIVE15.4 missing references→ ignore silently (do not fail pipeline)16. Minimal Implementation ContractA valid implementation MUST:parse markdown into structured ASTbuild deterministic section treesegment chunks deterministicallyclassify chunks without external LLM dependency (LLM optional later)assign level + kind to every chunkemit graph with stable IDssupport idempotent re-import17. OverviewNebula does not retrieve documents.It retrieves a **ranked subgraph of semantic chunks**.Every query is evaluated through:- role profile (Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer / Conduit)- chunk kind (semantic intent)- level (L1–L4 abstraction)- review state (trust + attention overlay)- cross-reference density (graph connectivity)- task intent (implicit or explicit)The output is a **scored ranked set of chunks + their local graph neighborhood**.---# 2. Core Retrieval ObjectA retrieval result is not a document.It is:RetrievalResult {chunkscoreexplanationneighborhood[]}Neighborhood includes:- parent section- sibling chunks- referenced chunks- optionally upstream/downstream traversal nodes---# 3. Retrieval Pipelinequery→ intent_classification→ role_profile_resolution→ candidate_chunk_selection→ scoring→ graph_expansion→ reranking→ filtering→ return---# 4. Role ProfilesEach role defines **what “relevant” means**.---## 4.1 BuilderBuilder optimizes for implementation correctness.### Preferences:- L1 chunks strongly preferred- ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE- MIGRATION_STEP when executing transitions- REVIEWED and CURRENT_FOCUS### Demotions:- RATIONALE (unless directly tied to implementation)- OUTDATED- QUESTIONED### Boost factors:- normative chunks (REQUIRED > RECOMMENDED)- high retrievalBias chunks---## 4.2 ArchitectArchitect optimizes for system correctness and structure.### Preferences:- L2 chunks- PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DATA_MODEL- RATIONALE (strongly valued)- OPEN_QUESTION (for unresolved design space)### Demotions:- overly implementation-specific L1 noise- trivial EXAMPLE chunks---## 4.3 InspectorInspector optimizes for contradiction detection and system validation.### Preferences:- QUESTIONED- INVARIANT- OUTDATED- OPEN_QUESTION- cross-reference-heavy chunks### Behavior:- actively surfaces inconsistencies- boosts conflicting review states- prioritizes low-confidence or high-risk nodes---## 4.4 ExplorerExplorer optimizes for understanding and knowledge traversal.### Preferences:- OVERVIEW- RATIONALE- EXAMPLE- high connectivity chunks### Behavior:- expands neighborhoods aggressively- favors graph traversal depth over strict relevance- includes historical/superseded context when useful---## 4.5 Conduit (Execution Role)Conduit optimizes for executable transformation.### Preferences:- MIGRATION_STEP- ALGORITHM- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA- PROTOCOL_RULE- L1 chunks only### Behavior:- strips non-normative noise- prioritizes determinism- prefers minimal required graph for execution---# 5. Chunk Scoring FunctionEvery chunk receives a score:score =role_weightkind_weightlevel_weightreview_weightgraph_weightfreshness_weight---## 5.1 Role weightDefined per role profile preferences.Example:- Builder: +2 for L1- Architect: +2 for L2- Inspector: +3 for QUESTIONED- Explorer: +2 for OVERVIEW---## 5.2 Chunk kind weightFrom `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`:- PROTOCOL_RULE → +3 for Architect- ALGORITHM → +3 for Builder/Conduit- RATIONALE → +3 for Architect/Explorer- OPEN_QUESTION → +3 for Inspector/Architect- EXAMPLE → moderate boost for Explorer---## 5.3 Level weightL1: +3 for Builder/ConduitL2: +3 for ArchitectL3: +2 for ExplorerL4: +2 for all roles (meta awareness bonus)---## 5.4 Review weightCURRENT_FOCUS → +4REVIEWED → +2NEEDS_REVIEW → +1UNREVIEWED → 0OUTDATED → -2QUESTIONED → +2 for Inspector, -2 for BuilderSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED → -4 (default)---## 5.5 Graph weightChunks gain score from graph structure:- + connectivity (degree centrality)- + cross-reference richness- + being referenced by current focus nodes- + participation in migration chains---## 5.6 Freshness weightBased on:- last reviewed timestamp- recency of updates- proximity to current focus artifacts---# 6. Candidate SelectionBefore scoring, Nebula selects a candidate set:```pseudo id="c8xk1a"function select_candidates(query):if query.role_hint exists:seed = role_preferred_chunks(query.role)else:seed = semantic_search(query.text)expand seed using:- direct references- parent sections- sibling chunksreturn seed7. Graph Expansion PhaseAfter scoring top candidates:for chunk in top_results:expand:parent sectionreferenced chunksupstream dependenciesdownstream dependenciesThis produces alocal subgraph, not just a ranked list.8. Filtering RulesAfter scoring:removeSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDunless explicitly requestedremoveOUTDATEDfor Builder unless overriddenpreserveQUESTIONEDfor InspectorpreserveRATIONALEfor Architect/Explorerenforce role-level safety filters9. Explanation GenerationEvery retrieval result MUST include:explanation = {"why_selected": [],"role_alignment": "","chunk_kind_match": "","review_state_influence": "","graph_signals": []}``` id="v1k2zq"This is critical for debugging the system and for human trust calibration.---# 10. Retrieval Modes## 10.1 STRICT MODE- only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS- no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED- minimal graph expansionUsed for execution / Conduit---## 10.2 EXPLORATION MODE- broad inclusion- heavy graph traversal- includes OUTDATED + SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED if relevantUsed for learning / architecture discovery---## 10.3 DIAGNOSTIC MODE- Inspector role default mode- boosts QUESTIONED and conflicts- surfaces contradictions explicitly---## 10.4 EXECUTION MODE- Builder + Conduit hybrid- minimal graph- deterministic chunks only- excludes RATIONALE unless required---# 11. Conflict ResolutionIf two chunks compete:Priority resolution:1. CURRENT_FOCUS overrides all2. REVIEWED overrides NEARLY EVERYTHING except CURRENT_FOCUS3. QUESTIONED overrides OUTDATED for Inspector4. SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED loses by default5. graph centrality can override weak semantic differences---# 12. Key Design Principle> Nebula retrieval is not search. It is weighted cognitive reconstruction.The system is not trying to find documents.It is trying to reconstruct the **relevant slice of the system’s mental model for a role and intent**.---# 13. OverviewNebula produces a **ranked semantic subgraph**.Conduit consumes a **deterministic execution DAG**.This document defines the transformation layer between them.Input:- NebulaChunks- NebulaSections- NebulaArtifacts- CrossReferences- Review overlays- Role-scored retrieval result setOutput:- ConduitExecutionGraph (DAG)- ExecutionNodes- TransitionEdges- ExecutionReceipts---# 2. Core Principle> Nebula explains what is relevant. Conduit decides what is executable.Not all retrieved content is executable.Only chunks that satisfy **execution constraints** may become DAG nodes.---# 3. Execution Eligibility RulesA Nebula chunk is eligible for execution if:```pseudo id="elig1"function isExecutable(chunk):return (chunk.kind in EXECUTABLE_KINDSAND chunk.reviewStatus NOT IN {OUTDATED, SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED}AND chunk.normativeStrength in {REQUIRED, RECOMMENDED})3.1 Executable chunk kindsALGORITHMPROTOCOL_RULEINVARIANTMIGRATION_STEPDATA_MODELACCEPTANCE_CRITERIAIMPLEMENTATION_NOTE``` id="execk1"---# 4. Node ConstructionEach executable chunk becomes a **Conduit Node**.```pseudo id="node1"function toExecutionNode(chunk):return ExecutionNode(id = chunk.id,type = chunk.kind,level = chunk.level,payload = extract_semantic_payload(chunk),preconditions = infer_preconditions(chunk),postconditions = infer_postconditions(chunk),review_state = chunk.reviewStatus)4.1 Payload extractionPayload depends on chunk kind:ALGORITHM → pseudocode / structured logicDATA_MODEL → schema definitionPROTOCOL_RULE → constraint logicMIGRATION_STEP → imperative actionACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA → validation predicates5. Edge Construction (DAG Formation)Edges are derived from Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction build_edges(nodes, references):edges = []for ref in references:if ref.type == DEPENDS_ON:edges.add(DependencyEdge(ref.source, ref.target))if ref.type == REFERENCES:edges.add(ReferenceEdge(ref.source, ref.target))if ref.type == MENTIONS:edges.add(SoftLinkEdge(ref.source, ref.target))return edges5.1 Edge typesDependencyEdge (hard constraint)execution order requiredReferenceEdge (soft ordering)preferred ordering but not requiredSoftLinkEdge (contextual)informational only, no execution ordering6. DAG Constructionpseudofunction build_execution_dag(nodes, edges):dag = DirectedAcyclicGraph()for node in nodes:dag.add_node(node)for edge in edges:dag.add_edge(edge)if dag.has_cycles():resolve_cycles(dag)return dag6.1 Cycle resolution strategyIf cycles exist:Priority resolution:break edges from LOWER level → HIGHER levelbreak edges from RATIONALE → ALGORITHMpreserve PROTOCOL_RULE dependencies over EXAMPLE linksif unresolved → mark as NEEDS_REVIEW in Nebula7. Execution Plan CompilationOnce DAG is constructed:pseudofunction compile_execution_plan(dag):topo_order = topological_sort(dag)plan = []for node in topo_order:step = ExecutionStep(node_id=node.id,action=resolve_executor(node),inputs=get_inputs(node),outputs=declare_outputs(node))plan.append(step)return plan8. Executor ResolutionEach node type maps to an execution handler.pseudofunction resolve_executor(node):switch node.type:case ALGORITHM:return AlgorithmExecutorcase DATA_MODEL:return SchemaExecutorcase PROTOCOL_RULE:return ConstraintExecutorcase MIGRATION_STEP:return MigrationExecutorcase ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:return ValidationExecutor9. Execution Context BindingEach execution step runs with:JSON{"role":"Conduit","mode":"EXECUTION","strict_mode":true,"allowed_chunk_kinds": ["ALGORITHM","MIGRATION_STEP","PROTOCOL_RULE"],"review_filter": ["REVIEWED","CURRENT_FOCUS"],"determinism":true}10. Execution Order SemanticsExecution follows:DATA_MODEL first (schema foundation)PROTOCOL_RULE second (constraints)ALGORITHM third (logic)MIGRATION_STEP fourth (state transitions)ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA last (validation)This is asemantic ordering constraint, not just topological sorting.11. Execution ReceiptsEvery execution step produces a receipt:JSON{"node_id":"...","status":"SUCCESS | FAILED | SKIPPED","timestamp":"...","inputs": [],"outputs": [],"validation_result": {},"trace": []}Receipts are stored back into Nebula as:execution provenancerollback anchor pointsaudit trail for WRP transitions12. Failure Handling12.1 Execution failureIf a node fails:mark ExecutionReceipt = FAILEDpropagate failure upward via dependency edgesflag Nebula chunk as NEEDS_REVIEW12.2 Invalid nodeIf chunk is not executable:keep in Nebula graphexclude from DAGoptionally mark:REVIEW_STATUS = QUESTIONED12.3 Cycle resolution failureIf DAG cannot be resolved:halt executionemit diagnostic graphsend Inspector mode review request13. Role Interaction ModelExecution binding respects Nebula role system:Builderconsumes ExecutionPlanproduces code / system changesArchitectvalidates DAG structureensures invariants preservedInspectorreviews failures and contradictionsConduitexecutes deterministicallyExplorernot part of execution path14. Key InvariantsThese MUST always hold:Execution DAG is acyclicOnly eligible chunks become nodesReview-filtered chunks cannot executeReceipts are immutable once writtenNebula is source of truth, Conduit is execution engineNo execution without resolved role context15. Conceptual ShiftThis is the critical transition:Nebula describes structureConduit enacts structureWRP defines legality of transformationTogether they form:Nebula = semantic graphWRP = formal rulesConduit = execution runtime16. SummaryThis binding layer enables:deterministic execution from semantic graphstraceable DAG-based system evolutionreview-state-aware execution safetyrole-driven execution semanticsbidirectional traceability (execution → Nebula → WRP)17. Final PrincipleNothing executes unless it exists as a validated semantic node in Nebula.And:Nothing exists in Conduit unless it can be traced back to a Nebula chunk.---# What you now have (full system closure point)At this moment, you’ve defined a complete closed loop:## 1. OverviewThe WRP Validation Engine sits between:- Nebula → semantic graph- Conduit → execution DAGIt ensures that:> Every executable plan is consistent with WRP rules, Nebula semantics, and system invariants.It is a **pre-execution proof gate**, not a runtime monitor.---# 2. Validation Pipelineinput_dag→ structural_validation→ semantic_validation→ invariant_verification→ dependency_consistency_check→ execution_safety_check→ validation_report---# 3. Core Data Structures## Validation Report```json id="vr1"ValidationReport {dag_idstatus: PASS | FAIL | DEGRADEDstructural_issues[]semantic_issues[]invariant_violations[]warnings[]suggested_fixes[]}Invariant DefinitionJSONInvariant {iddescriptionscope: GLOBAL | ARTIFACT | CHUNK | EXECUTION_STEPseverity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUMcondition_expression}4. Structural ValidationEnsures DAG correctness independent of semantics.pseudofunction structural_validation(dag):assert dag.is_acyclic()assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)return PASSStructural rulesDAG MUST be acyclicall nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunksno dangling references allowedall edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs5. Semantic ValidationEnsures node meaning aligns with WRP + Nebula expectations.pseudofunction semantic_validation(dag):for node in dag.nodes:if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")if node.review_state == OUTDATED:mark_warning(node)if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")return reportSemantic constraints5.1 Protocol purity rulePROTOCOL_RULE nodes MUST NOT contain:side-effect logicmutation operationsexecution commandsThey define constraints only.5.2 Algorithm determinism ruleALGORITHM nodes MUST:be deterministicnot depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration5.3 Migration consistency ruleMIGRATION_STEP nodes MUST:reference a valid prior statedefine explicit transition target6. Invariant Verification EngineThis is the core of WRP correctness.6.1 Invariant evaluation looppseudofunction invariant_verification(dag, invariants):violations = []for invariant in invariants:for node in dag.nodes:if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):violations.append({"node": node.id,"invariant": invariant.id})return violations6.2 Example invariantsGlobal execution invariantsNo node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution pathAll PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chainNo cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chainsWRP-specific invariantsEvery ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULEEvery MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transitionEvery ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node7. Dependency Consistency CheckEnsures graph coherence across Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction dependency_consistency(dag):for edge in dag.edges:if edge.type == DEPENDS_ON:assert topological_order(edge.source) < topological_order(edge.target)if violates_level_constraints(edge):mark_error(edge)Level constraint rulesL1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logicL2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationaleL3 nodes MUST NOT define execution dependencies8. Execution Safety CheckThis step ensures the DAG is safe to run under Conduit.8.1 Safety rulespseudofunction execution_safety(dag):assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)return PASS8.2 Strict mode constraintsIn STRICT execution mode:only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowedQUESTIONED nodes forbiddenOUTDATED nodes forbiddenSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely9. Validation Severity ModelEach issue is classified:CRITICAL → blocks executionHIGH → requires interventionMEDIUM → warningLOW → informationalFailure policypseudoif CRITICAL exists:status = FAILhalt_execution()elif HIGH exists:status = DEGRADEDrequire_human_review()else:status = PASS10. Suggested Fix GeneratorFor each violation:pseudofunction suggest_fix(issue):switch issue.type:case OUTDATED_DEPENDENCY:suggest("Replace with superseding artifact")case INVALID_PROTOCOL_MUTATION:suggest("Move logic to ALGORITHM chunk")case MISSING_REFERENCE:suggest("Add cross-reference or dependency edge")case LEVEL_VIOLATION:suggest("Promote/demote chunk level or split chunk")return suggestion11. Validation Modes11.1 STRICT MODEUsed for Conduit executionno warnings allowed to escalateCRITICAL = immediate stop11.2 DEVELOPMENT MODEUsed during ingestionallows warningsgenerates fix suggestionsdoes not block graph creation11.3 INSPECTOR MODEUsed for audit / debugginghighlights contradictionssurfaces all invariant violationsmaximizes visibility over pass/fail12. Integration with NebulaValidation engine consumes:NebulaChunksReview overlaysCross-reference graphChunk kindsLevel assignmentsIt produces:ValidationReport nodes in Nebulaexecution gating signals to Conduitoptional review state updates13. This is the point where the system stops being a “compiler pipeline” and becomes aruntime with state, scheduling, and recovery semantics.Up until now, Conduit has been implied as an executor.Now we define it as areal execution kernel.docs/conduit/conduit-runtime-scheduler-and-lifecycle.mdMarkdown# Conduit Runtime Scheduler & Execution Lifecycle Manager**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Conduit core runtime**Purpose:** Define scheduling, execution lifecycle, concurrency model, and failure recovery semantics for WRP-derived execution DAGs.---# 1. OverviewConduit is a deterministic execution runtime for validated Nebula-derived DAGs.It is responsible for:- scheduling execution steps- managing concurrency- tracking execution state- handling retries and failures- emitting execution receipts- ensuring deterministic replayability---# 2. Core Principle> Conduit does not “run code.” It executes validated semantic graphs under strict lifecycle control.Every execution is:- deterministic where possible- replayable- traceable to Nebula chunks- governed by WRP validation guarantees---# 3. Execution Lifecycle StatesEach node transitions through a lifecycle:PENDING→ READY→ RUNNING→ COMPLETED→ FAILED→ RETRYING→ SKIPPED→ COMPENSATED---## 3.1 State definitions### PENDINGNode is waiting for dependencies or scheduling.### READYAll dependencies satisfied; eligible for execution.### RUNNINGNode is actively executing.### COMPLETEDExecution succeeded and produced valid output.### FAILEDExecution failed irrecoverably for current attempt.### RETRYINGNode is scheduled for re-execution.### SKIPPEDNode is intentionally bypassed (policy or conditional logic).### COMPENSATEDNode failure has been resolved via compensating action (migration or rollback logic).---# 4. Scheduler ModelConduit uses a **dependency-aware priority scheduler**.---## 4.1 Scheduling loop```pseudo id="sched1"while true:ready_nodes = get_ready_nodes(dag)prioritized = rank(ready_nodes,priority_function)for node in prioritized:if can_run(node):dispatch(node)4.2 Priority functionpseudopriority(node) =role_priority_weight(node)+ review_priority_weight(node)+ chunk_kind_weight(node)+ dependency_depth_weight(node)- failure_penalty(node)4.3 Dependency depth weightNodes deeper in dependency chains may be prioritized to unlock downstream execution faster.depth_score = longest_path_from_root(node)5. Concurrency ModelConduit supports controlled parallel execution.5.1 Execution constraintsA node MAY execute in parallel if:pseudocan_parallelize(node) =node.has_no_shared_mutation_targetsAND node.dependencies_satisfiedAND not_conflicting_with_running_nodes(node)5.2 Conflict rulesTwo nodes conflict if:they modify same conceptual statethey depend on each other's outputsthey share non-isolated resource contexts5.3 Concurrency policydefault: conservative parallelismmigration mode: stricter (serial execution preferred)exploration mode: relaxed (higher parallelism allowed)6. Execution Dispatcherpseudofunction dispatch(node):mark(node, RUNNING)executor = resolve_executor(node.type)context = build_execution_context(node)try:result = executor.execute(node.payload, context)mark(node, COMPLETED)emit_receipt(node, result)except error:handle_failure(node, error)7. Execution Context BuilderEach node executes with a structured context:JSON{"node_id":"...","dag_id":"...","role":"Conduit","mode":"EXECUTION","strict_mode":true,"nebula_trace": [],"allowed_chunk_kinds": [],"validation_signature":"WRP_VALIDATED","determinism":true}8. Failure Handling System8.1 Failure classificationpseudofunction classify_failure(error):if transient(error):return RETRYABLEif dependency_missing(error):return BLOCKINGif semantic_violation(error):return INVALID_DAGreturn FATAL8.2 Retry policypseudoif RETRYABLE:if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:schedule_retry(node)else:mark(node, FAILED)8.3 Blocking failure propagationIf a node fails due to dependency:downstream nodes → SKIPPED or PENDINGupstream nodes unaffectedDAG remains valid but partially executable8.4 Compensation modelFor MIGRATION_STEP nodes:failures MAY trigger compensating stepsrollback DAG may be generated9. DAG Execution GuaranteesConduit guarantees:deterministic execution order for identical inputsidempotent retries (when possible)no execution without READY stateno execution of invalidated nodesstrict adherence to WRP validation outputs10. Execution ReceiptsEvery execution produces a receipt:JSONExecutionReceipt {node_iddag_idstatusstart_timeend_timeinputsoutputslogsvalidation_ref}Receipts are:immutablestored in Nebulaused for future graph refinementused for failure analysis and review updates11. Scheduling Policies11.1 STRICT POLICYUsed for production execution:no speculative executionno retry beyond limitno OUTDATED or QUESTIONED nodesminimal concurrency11.2 OPTIMIZED POLICYUsed for performance execution:moderate concurrencypredictive schedulingprioritizes unlocking downstream nodes11.3 EXPLORATION POLICYUsed for discovery:high concurrencyrelaxed ordering constraintsallows partial execution of graph branches12. Deadlock PreventionDeadlocks are prevented via:topological schedulingcycle detection (from WRP validation layer)fallback serial executionforced dependency resolution orderingIf deadlock is detected:1. pause execution2. emit diagnostic subgraph3. request inspector review13. System Integration13.1 Nebula integrationConduit reads:validated DAGschunk metadatareview overlayscross-reference structureConduit writes:ExecutionReceiptsfailure annotationsinferred review updates13.2 WRP integrationConduit only executes DAGs that:pass WRP validation enginesatisfy invariant checkscomply with strict mode rules13.3 Validation gate couplingpseudoif not WRPValidationReport.PASS:abort_execution()14. Invariant Conflict ResolutionConflicts occur when:- two invariants contradict- invariant holds only in subset of branches- invariant improves one dimension but harms another---## 8.1 Resolution hierarchy1. cross-branch stability wins2. execution consistency wins over theoretical rules3. simulation convergence wins over static rules4. governance override is final fallback---## 8.2 Merge strategyConflicting invariants may be:- merged into conditional invariant- split into context-dependent rules- downgraded to heuristic rules---# 9. OverviewNebula is now fully self-modifying:- invariants evolve (WRP)- graphs evolve (Nebula)- execution evolves (Conduit)- reasoning evolves (multi-agent fabric)- futures evolve (simulation)This creates a risk:> the system can optimize itself into incoherenceThis layer prevents that.---# 2. Core Principle> A self-modifying system must preserve a fixed point of interpretability.Even if everything else changes:- meaning must remain traceable- execution must remain bounded- governance must remain authoritative- identity of system components must remain stable---# 3. Fixed Point DefinitionA **fixed point** is a property that must remain invariant across all:- graph versions- branches- simulations- mutation cycles∀ t ∈ system_time:FIXED_POINT(t) = TRUE---# 4. Fixed Point SetNebula defines a minimal invariant spine:---## 4.1 Structural fixed pointsThese CANNOT be modified:- existence of GraphState abstraction- existence of Conduit execution layer- existence of WRP validation gate- existence of governance authority layer- existence of mutation proposal pipeline (not direct mutation)- existence of temporal versioning system---## 4.2 Semantic fixed pointsThese MUST remain consistent:- nodes represent semantic units- edges represent typed relationships- execution receipts are immutable records- simulation results are non-authoritative- governance is final mutation authority---## 4.3 Process fixed pointsThese MUST always hold:- no execution without validation gate- no mutation without proposal stage- no direct cross-layer mutation bypassing governance- no simulation affecting main branch directly---# 5. Anti-Drift Constraint System---## 5.1 Drift definitionDrift occurs when:- system optimizes away structural clarity- abstraction layers collapse- role boundaries blur- validation becomes redundant or bypassed---## 5.2 Drift detection```pseudo id="drift1"function detect_drift(system_state):if missing_layer(system_state):return CRITICAL_DRIFTif bypass_rate(validation_gate) > threshold:return DRIFTif mutation_directness increases:return DRIFTreturn STABLE5.3 Drift responseIf drift detected:freeze mutation systemenforce strict mode in Conduitelevate Inspector agent weightrequire L3 governance review6. Meta-Governance Layer (L4)A new layer is introduced:L4: Meta-Governance Layer``` id="lg4"---## 6.1 ResponsibilitiesL4 governs:- whether WRP itself can change- whether governance rules can evolve- whether simulation semantics can change- whether agent roles can be redefined---## 6.2 RestrictionsL4 CANNOT:- execute DAGs- directly mutate Nebula graphs- bypass L3 governance decisions without trace---## 6.3 Authority hierarchyL4 > L3 > L2 > L1 > L0But:> L4 changes are extremely rare and require full-system consistency validation.---# 7. WRP Stability ConstraintWRP evolution is restricted by:---## 7.1 Fixed-point ruleAny new invariant must satisfy:```pseudo id="fp2"if new_invariant alters fixed_point_set:reject7.2 Non-circular validation ruleAn invariant cannot be validated solely by systems it modifies.At least one independent layer must validate it:simulation engine ORgovernance ORcross-agent consensus8. System Identity ConstraintNebula must preserve identity:It must always remain a system that:executes graphsvalidates correctnesstracks temporal evolutionsupports governed mutationIf any of these is removed → system is invalid.9. Safe Self-Modification EnvelopeSelf-modification is allowed only within bounds:9.1 Allowed changesnode classification tuningedge optimizationinvariant refinementscheduling optimizationagent weighting adjustments9.2 Forbidden changesremoval of governance layerremoval of validation gateelimination of simulation isolationcollapse of temporal model into single statedirect execution without DAG construction10. Recovery Mode (System Collapse Protection)If fixed-point violation is detected:1. halt all mutation activity2. lock WRP to last stable version3. isolate simulation engine4. restore last known stable GraphState5. require L4 review``` id="recov1"---# 11. Fixed Point Stability MetricSystem health is measured as:``` id="fpm1"stability =fixed_point_compliance+ governance_consistency+ validation_integrity- structural_drift- mutation_entropy``` id="stab4"---# 12. Meta-Circular Safety Rule> The system is allowed to modify itself only if it preserves the ability to reason about itself.If interpretability is lost → system is considered failed, even if execution continues successfully.---# 13. Integration MapNebula↓Multi-Agent Fabric↓Conduit Runtime↓Validation Engine↓Self-Healing Layer↓Governance Layer↓Simulation Engine↓WRP Invariant Synthesizer↓Meta-Governance Layer (L4)   ← this layer↓Fixed Point Stability Constraint↓System Continuity Guarantee---# 14. Final Principle> A self-modifying system is only safe if it preserves a minimal, non-negotiable structure that defines what it is, regardless of how it evolves.---# 15. System OutcomeThis establishes:- bounded self-modification- controlled recursive evolution- structural invariance across time- prevention of semantic collapse---# 16. Self-Awareness Without AuthorityCritical separation:CapabilityAllowedAuthorityObserve selfYesL0–L3Model selfYesL1–L3Validate self-modelYesL2Modify system via self-modelNoL4 only14.
