PurposeThis document defines how **WRP artifacts managed through Conduit** are projected into the **Nebula knowledge graph / document corpus**, and how those artifacts are stratified by **abstraction level** so that different roles and agents can retrieve the right amount of context.The immediate goal is to support the first WRP work packet now tracked in Conduit:1. **WRP v1.0** — protocol formalization2. **WRP v1.1** — DAG data model & compilation pipeline3. **WRP v1.2** — execution traversal engine4. **WRP migration plan**These four artifacts must not remain isolated implementation plans. They must become **queryable architectural knowledge** inside Nebula so that:- builders can retrieve concrete implementation guidance,- architects can retrieve subsystem rationale and relationships,- inspectors/validators can retrieve invariants and migration constraints,- future harvests and work requests can cross-reference WRP material directly.This document therefore specifies:- the **projection model** from Conduit/WRP artifacts into Nebula;- the **`level` stratification model** for Nebula documents, chunks, and references;- the **artifact taxonomy** for WRP knowledge units;- the **retrieval policy** by role;- the **migration strategy** for the initial WRP corpus.---# 2. Context and Position in the StackThe working architectural chain is:```textNebula → WRP → Conduit → LOSM / runtime implementationwith the following responsibilities:Nebulalong-form architectural memorymarkdown-authored specificationschunked knowledge corpuscross-reference graphopen questions / unresolved decisionsretrieval substrate for planning and implementationWRP (Work Request Protocol / Work Request Package)canonical execution-facing representation of workprotocol, DAG model, traversal semantics, migration disciplinethe bridge between long-form intent and executable workConduitexecution-oriented work managerreceives concrete plans / work requeststracks dependencies, acceptance criteria, receipts, affected filesis not the authoritative home for large concept documentsLOSM / runtimeexecution engine, orchestration, persistence, validation, receiptsThe practical rule is:Nebula owns long-form architectural knowledge. Conduit owns executable work tracking. WRP is the formal bridge between the two.This document defines how that bridge is materialized in storage and retrieval.3. Design GoalsThe projection and stratification model must satisfy the following goals.G1. Preserve long-form WRP knowledge in NebulaThe WRP packet tracked in Conduit must be represented in Nebula as durable, queryable, versioned knowledge.G2. Preserve execution alignment with ConduitNebula entries must retain enough metadata to map back to the Conduit work packet(s) that implement them.G3. Support role-specific retrievalThe same corpus must serve multiple retrieval surfaces:Builder / implementerArchitect / plannerInspector / validatorExplorer / researcherG4. Separate abstraction levels cleanlyImplementation details should not drown architectural reasoning, and architectural rationale should not flood implementation prompts unless explicitly requested.G5. Preserve explicit cross-referencesProtocol rules, DAG semantics, traversal rules, migration tasks, invariants, and open questions must be linked explicitly rather than relying only on embedding similarity.G6. Remain compatible with the existing Nebula markdown-ingestion pipelineThis design should extend the existing markdown import / chunk / cross-reference model rather than replacing it.4. Core Decision4.1 Canonical ruleWRP artifacts are authored or curated as Nebula documents, then projected into Conduit as executable work packages.Conduit may hold the immediate execution plans, but Nebula remains the authoritative architectural memory for:protocol definitions,subsystem specs,migration rationale,invariants,open questions,design history.4.2 Projection directionThere are two distinct projection paths:A. Authoritative knowledge projectionNebula markdown/spec document→ Nebula document rows / chunks / cross references→ optional WRP artifact registration→ Conduit plan / work request generationB. Execution trace back-projectionConduit plan / execution receipt / implementation status→ WRP artifact linkage→ Nebula document metadata updates→ cross-linked execution referencesSo the system is not one-way. The long-form knowledge projects downward into executable work, and execution status projects upward into Nebula metadata and trace links.5. Scope of WRP Artifacts Covered by This SpecThis document covers the initial WRP corpus:WRP-1 — WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefines the formal work request protocol, message shape, identity, versioning, semantics, and lifecycle assumptions.WRP-2 — WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefines the DAG representation of work, node/edge semantics, compilation from protocol-level requests into executable graph structures, and compilation invariants.WRP-3 — WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefines the traversal/execution model over the WRP DAG, execution context, cursor/receipt semantics, deterministic traversal defaults, and isolation rules.WRP-4 — WRP Migration PlanDefines how existing work representations, legacy plans, or runtime workflows migrate into the WRP model with compatibility constraints and staged rollout.The schema and rules in this document are generic enough to apply to future WRP artifacts as well.6. Terminology6.1 Conduit PlanAn execution-oriented item managed by Conduit, typically containing:titleprojectaffected filesacceptance criteriadependenciesreceipt trail6.2 WRP ArtifactA versioned architectural / protocol artifact in the WRP family, such as:protocol specDAG model spectraversal engine specmigration planfuture validation / governance extensions6.3 Nebula DocumentA markdown-origin or spec-origin long-form document stored in Nebula.6.4 Nebula ChunkA chunked section or paragraph group extracted from a Nebula document for retrieval and cross-referencing.6.5 Cross ReferenceAn explicit semantic edge connecting one document/chunk/artifact to another, such as:“depends on”“implements”“constrains”“supersedes”“migrates”“explains”“references protocol field”“defines traversal invariant”6.6 LevelA stratification marker describing the abstraction level of a knowledge item.7. Level Stratification Model8. Rationale for Level StratificationWithout level stratification, a retrieval system operating over mixed architectural and implementation material tends to collapse the distinction between:“what the protocol means,”“how the DAG is represented,”“what code needs to change this week,”“why the migration strategy was chosen.”That leads to three recurring failures:Builders get too much theoryimplementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.Architects get too much local detailsubsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.Inspectors miss normative constraintsinvariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.A level field provides a stable, queryable abstraction boundary.9. Level DefinitionsThe first version of the level system usesfour levels.Level 1 — Execution / Build Detail (L1)Concrete implementation guidance and execution-facing material.Typical content:file-level implementation tasksendpoint contractsdataclass / schema detailsmethod signaturesSQL changesacceptance criteriatest casesmigration scriptsprecise repository change instructions“do this in package X” contentPrimary consumers:BuilderConduit executorimplementation-focused coding agentsLevel 2 — Subsystem Design (L2)Subsystem mechanics and technical design for a bounded domain.Typical content:DAG node/edge semanticscompilation pipeline structuretraversal algorithm designexecution receipt structurerole-specific service boundariesstorage mappings for a specific subsystemformal state transitions inside one bounded domainPrimary consumers:Builder (secondary)ArchitectInspectorLevel 3 — Architecture / Rationale (L3)Higher-order architectural reasoning, system relationships, and design justification.Typical content:why WRP existswhy DAG compilation is separate from traversalhow Conduit, Nebula, and LOSM relatemigration philosophy and rollout strategycross-subsystem responsibilitieslong-form tradeoff analysisarchitectural invariants spanning multiple packagesPrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerInspectorLevel 4 — Meta / Doctrine / Ontology (L4)Cross-cutting design doctrine, system philosophy, and ontology-level governance.Typical content:methodology rulesrole doctrinearchitectural constitution / invariants of invariantsontology rules for work, memory, or cognitionglobal modeling principlescross-project strategic doctrinePrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerstrategic planner10. Level Assignment Rules10.1 Canonical ruleLevel belongs primarily to the content node, not to the retrieval query and not to the edge.That means:documents have levels,chunks have levels,references may optionally have level metadata, but level is not primarily an edge property.10.2 Single-primary-level ruleEvery document and every chunk must haveone primary level.This avoids ambiguous retrieval behavior and keeps filtering deterministic.10.3 Mixed documentsA long document may contain sections at different abstraction levels. Therefore:thedocumentreceives a default or dominant level;chunksmay override the document level when section content clearly belongs to a different level.Example:a WRP migration document may be primarilyL3,but its implementation checklist section may be chunked asL1.10.4 Edge neutrality ruleCross-reference edges should belevel-neutral by default.The edge describes the relationship; the source and target nodes carry the abstraction level.11. Recommended Level Mapping for the Initial WRP Corpus11.1 WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefault document level:L2Reasoning:it defines subsystem protocol semantics and normative message shape;it is not merely implementation detail;it is narrower than whole-system doctrine.Typical chunk-level overrides:formal field definitions / JSON examples / schema tables →L1rationale for protocol boundaries →L311.2 WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:compilation algorithm pseudocode →L2concrete data structures / storage tables / code mapping →L1rationale for DAG compilation as separate phase →L311.3 WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:ExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceiptstructures →L1orL2depending on specificitytraversal invariants / isolation rules →L2rationale for deterministic traversal and experimental modes →L311.4 WRP Migration PlanDefault document level:L3Reasoning:migration is a cross-cutting architectural transition strategy;the document explains sequencing, compatibility, and rollout discipline.Typical chunk-level overrides:actual migration tasks and repo changes →L1compatibility matrix / rollout constraints →L2migration philosophy and sequencing rationale →L312. Nebula Data Model ExtensionsThis section defines the required schema extensions to Nebula’s markdown-derived corpus.13. Target Nebula EntitiesThe projection model assumes the following logical entities exist or will exist:nebula_documentsnebula_chunksnebula_cross_referencesOptionally:nebula_artifactsnebula_open_questionsnebula_execution_linksThis document does not require a specific SQL dialect, but examples assume a relational store.14. Required Additions tonebula_documents14.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_documentsADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8)NOTNULLDEFAULT'L2',ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNartifact_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNartifact_versionVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNconduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNconduit_project_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNsource_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNsupersedes_document_id BIGINTNULL;14.2 Field semanticslevelPrimary abstraction level of the document.Allowed values:L1L2L3L4artifact_typeStable WRP artifact family identifier, e.g.:wrp.protocolwrp.dag_modelwrp.execution_enginewrp.migration_planartifact_keyStable logical identifier for the artifact, e.g.:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planartifact_versionHuman-visible version identifier, e.g.:1.01.11.22026-06conduit_plan_idOptional link to the Conduit execution plan primarily associated with the document.conduit_project_keyOptional grouping key for Conduit project membership.source_kindDescribes origin:markdowngenerated_specconduit_projectionimported_transcriptmanual_notestatusDocument lifecycle:draftcandidateapprovedsupersededarchivedsupersedes_document_idOptional pointer to the prior document version.15. Required Additions tonebula_chunks15.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_chunksADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNchunk_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNnormative_strengthVARCHAR(32),ADDCOLUMNsection_keyVARCHAR(255);15.2 Field semanticslevelChunk-level override. If null, inherit from the parent document.artifact_typeOptional denormalized copy of the parent artifact type for faster filtering.chunk_kindClassifies the chunk’s semantic role. Recommended values:overviewdefinitionprotocol_ruledata_modelalgorithminvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriaopen_questionexamplerationaleimplementation_notenormative_strengthOptional normative marker for validation-oriented retrieval:informativerecommendedrequiredprohibitedsection_keyStable section identity, e.g.:wrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.compilation-invariantswrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.migration.phase-2-cutover16. Required Additions tonebula_cross_references16.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_cross_referencesADDCOLUMNrelation_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'references',ADDCOLUMNsource_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNtarget_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNweightDECIMAL(8,4),ADDCOLUMNevidence_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(32)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active';16.2 Why not a singlelevelon the edge?Because the edge itself is not the primary abstraction bearer. The useful information is usually:what level the source is,what level the target is,what relation binds them.Therefore, the preferred model is to carry:source_leveltarget_levelas denormalized convenience fields rather than treating the edge as an independently stratified knowledge unit.16.3 Field semanticsrelation_typeRecommended initial relation types:referencesdepends_onimplementsconstrainsdefinescompiled_intoexecutesmigratessupersedesvalidated_byraises_questionanswers_questionsource_level,target_levelOptional denormalized values copied from the linked nodes for efficient querying.weightOptional confidence or importance score.evidence_kindHow the edge was created:explicit_markdown_linkmanual_annotationartifact_projectionsemantic_matchreceipt_backlinkstatusactivesupersededtentative17. Optional New Table:nebula_artifactsIf WRP artifacts need to be treated as first-class entities independent of document versions, add a registry table.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_artifacts (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULLUNIQUE,artifact_typeVARCHAR(128)NOTNULL,current_versionVARCHAR(64),current_document_id BIGINT,statusVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active',created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL,updated_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Purpose:stable artifact identity across multiple document revisions,single lookup point for “the current WRP traversal spec,”easier version navigation and supersession tracking.18. Optional New Table:nebula_execution_linksThis table binds Nebula knowledge to execution artifacts and receipts.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_execution_links (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULL,document_id BIGINT,chunk_id BIGINT,conduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),wrp_work_request_idVARCHAR(255),receipt_idVARCHAR(255),link_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULL,created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Recommendedlink_typevalues:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planvalidated_by_receiptsuperseded_by_planmigrated_by_requestThis table is not required for the first pass, but it becomes useful as soon as execution receipts start flowing back into Nebula.19. WRP Artifact TaxonomyEach WRP artifact projected into Nebula must declare a stable type.19.1 Initial artifact typesArtifact TypeMeaningwrp.protocolFormal WRP protocol definitionwrp.dag_modelDAG representation and compilation pipelinewrp.execution_engineTraversal / execution engine semanticswrp.migration_planWRP migration and rollout strategy19.2 Future extension typesExamples of likely future additions:Artifact TypeMeaningwrp.validation_rulesCross-artifact validation and policy ruleswrp.compatibility_matrixVersion compatibility / migration compatibilitywrp.receipt_modelFormal execution receipt modelwrp.role_contractsRole-specific work request / execution constraints20. Canonical WRP Artifact KeysThe initial corpus should use stable artifact keys.Artifact KeyArtifact TypeVersionwrp-v1-protocolwrp.protocol1.0wrp-v1_1-dagwrp.dag_model1.1wrp-v1_2-traversalwrp.execution_engine1.2wrp-migration-planwrp.migration_plan2026-06These keys should remain stable even if the underlying document path changes.21. Projection ModelThis section defines how WRP material moves from authored docs / Conduit plans into Nebula entities.22. Projection SourcesA WRP artifact may enter Nebula from one of three sources.Source A — Markdown-authored specThe preferred source. A curated markdown spec exists under the repo and is imported into Nebula.Source B — Conduit plan projectionA Conduit plan or work packet is projected into Nebula as a lightweight execution-facing document when no richer Nebula document exists yet.Source C — Manual or generated synthesisA generated or manually synthesized architecture note is imported and later normalized.The preferred order is:Markdown specGenerated synthesisConduit projection fallback23. Projection Pipeline StagesEvery WRP artifact projection follows the same high-level pipeline.Source artifact→ artifact registration→ document ingestion→ section extraction→ chunk creation→ level assignment→ cross-reference extraction→ Conduit link registration→ optional open-question extraction24. Stage 1 — Artifact RegistrationInput:artifact keyartifact typeversionsource path or source identifierOutput:canonical artifact registration recordlink to the current Nebula document versionRules:artifact keys must be stable;new versions should supersede, not overwrite, old document rows;the current version should be discoverable by artifact key.25. Stage 2 — Document IngestionThe source markdown/spec is stored as a Nebula document.Required metadata:artifact_typeartifact_keyartifact_versionsource_kindstatusdefaultlevelDocument title should remain human-readable, e.g.:WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationWRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation PipelineWRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineWRP Migration Plan26. Stage 3 — Section ExtractionSections should be extracted from headings and stable heading anchors.Recommended section key convention:<artifact family>.<major section slug>[.<subsection slug>...]Examples:wrp.protocol.overviewwrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.node-typeswrp.dag.compilation-pipelinewrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.traversal.isolation-ruleswrp.migration.phase-1-parallel-support27. Stage 4 — Chunk CreationChunks should be created with semantic sensitivity rather than purely fixed token windows.Recommended chunk boundaries:section intro / overview paragraph groupsdata model definitionsinvariant blocksalgorithm descriptionsmigration phase stepsexamplesacceptance criteria sectionsopen questions sectionsA chunk should not mix:a high-level architectural rationale paragraph,a concrete SQL alteration block,and an execution acceptance checklist.Those should become separate chunks with different levels andchunk_kindvalues.28. Stage 5 — Level AssignmentLevel assignment occurs in two passes.Pass A — Document default levelAssign the document’s dominant level based on artifact type and overall intent.Pass B — Chunk override levelOverride chunk level when a section clearly belongs to another abstraction layer.Heuristic examplesAssignL1when the chunk contains:repository pathsmethod signaturesschema alteration stepsexplicit implementation task sequencesacceptance criteria / test instructionsfield-by-field code mappingAssignL2when the chunk contains:formal subsystem structuresexecution algorithmsgraph semanticsstate transition rulesnormative subsystem invariantsAssignL3when the chunk contains:design rationalecross-subsystem tradeoffsmigration sequencing rationalearchitectural positioning of WRP relative to Conduit/Nebula/LOSMAssignL4when the chunk contains:system-wide doctrineontology-level policymeta-rules for work modeling or architectural governance29. Stage 6 — Cross-Reference ExtractionCross-references should be created from explicit and inferred signals.29.1 Explicit signalsmarkdown linkssection references“depends on”, “see also”, “constrained by”manually annotated relationships29.2 Inferred signalsartifact-key mentionssection-key referencesprotocol field names reused in traversal or migration docsrepeated formal identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt,tenant_id,trace_id29.3 Required WRP reference classesThe first pass must at least support:protocol field ↔ DAG compilation ruleDAG node/edge semantics ↔ traversal behaviortraversal invariant ↔ migration constraintmigration step ↔ affected WRP artifactWRP artifact ↔ Conduit plan implementing it30. Stage 7 — Conduit Link RegistrationEach projected WRP artifact should retain a link to the Conduit execution packet(s) responsible for implementation.Minimum metadata to retain:conduit_plan_idconduit_project_keyoptional receipt trail / execution link rowIf one Nebula artifact maps to multiple Conduit plans, use:document-level link to the primary umbrella planexecution-link rows for subordinate plans31. Stage 8 — Open Question ExtractionIf a WRP document contains unresolved design questions, they should be extracted into either:dedicatedopen_questionchunks, ora separatenebula_open_questionstable.Recommended fields for open questions:artifact_keydocument_idchunk_idquestion_textstatuspriorityowner_roleThis is especially relevant for migration uncertainties, protocol compatibility questions, and unresolved traversal policy decisions.32. Conduit → Nebula Projection RulesThis section defines how Conduit work packets map into Nebula when a WRP artifact is tracked for implementation.33. Conduit as Execution Metadata, Not Architectural AuthorityA Conduit plan is not automatically a Nebula document. Conduit should only project enough information into Nebula to preserve execution traceability.That means:Conduit ownsactive execution plan rowsacceptance criteriafile listsdependenciesexecution receiptsNebula ownsthe meaning of the WRP artifactthe long-form architecturecross-artifact relationshipsrationalechunk-level retrievability34. Minimal Projection of a Conduit Plan into NebulaFor each Conduit WRP work packet, Nebula should store:conduit_plan_idartifact_keyartifact_typestatusa short execution summarylinks to the authoritative WRP spec documentlinks to receipt or migration status if availableThis can be represented either:as metadata on the authoritative WRP document, oras a small auxiliary Nebula document ofsource_kind = conduit_projection.The first option is preferred for the initial implementation.35. Example Projection of the Initial WRP PacketSuppose Conduit contains four plans:CDT-WRP-001— WRP v1.0 protocol formalizationCDT-WRP-002— WRP v1.1 DAG model and compilation pipelineCDT-WRP-003— WRP v1.2 traversal engineCDT-WRP-004— WRP migration planNebula should contain at least:Document Atitle:WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalizationartifact key:wrp-v1-protocolartifact type:wrp.protocollevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-001Document Btitle:WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation Pipelineartifact key:wrp-v1_1-dagartifact type:wrp.dag_modellevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-002Document Ctitle:WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal Engineartifact key:wrp-v1_2-traversalartifact type:wrp.execution_enginelevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-003Document Dtitle:WRP Migration Planartifact key:wrp-migration-planartifact type:wrp.migration_planlevel:L3conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-004And explicit cross-references such as:wrp-v1_1-dagdepends_onwrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_2-traversalexecuteswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1-protocolwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_2-traversal36. Required WRP Cross-Reference PatternsThe first implementation should explicitly emit the following relation families.36.1 Protocol → DAGExamples:protocol field or lifecycle state constrains DAG node constructionprotocol dependency semantics compiled into edge semanticsRelations:definesconstrainscompiled_into36.2 DAG → TraversalExamples:DAG node kinds determine traversal behaviorDAG execution order constraints are enforced by traversal rulesRelations:definesexecutesconstrains36.3 Traversal → Receipt / ValidationExamples:execution cursor produces execution receipt shapetraversal invariants determine receipt hierarchy or failure semanticsRelations:definesvalidated_by36.4 Migration → All WRP ArtifactsExamples:migration phases refer to protocol changes, DAG compatibility, traversal rolloutRelations:migratessupersedesconstrains36.5 WRP Artifact → Conduit PlanExamples:a Nebula artifact is being implemented by one or more Conduit plansRelations:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planThese may live innebula_execution_linksrather than the main cross-reference table if the execution linkage is operational rather than semantic.37. Role-Based Retrieval PolicyThis is the operational reason for level stratification.38. Builder Retrieval Profile38.1 GoalProvide concrete implementation guidance with only enough architectural context to avoid coding blind.38.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L1Secondary levels:L2ExcludeL3/L4unless:the retrievedL1/L2chunk explicitly references an architectural invariant, orthe prompt requests rationale or migration context38.3 Preferred chunk kindsimplementation_notedata_modelprotocol_rulealgorithmacceptance_criteriamigration_step38.4 Typical use casesimplement WRP protocol DTOsbuild DAG compiler classesadd traversal engine structureswrite migration scripts and tests39. Architect Retrieval Profile39.1 GoalProvide subsystem design and cross-artifact reasoning without drowning in file-level implementation noise.39.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3Optional expansion toL1for concrete examplesOptional expansion toL4for doctrine or ontology alignment39.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewdefinitiondata_modelalgorithminvariantrationaleopen_question39.4 Typical use casesrefine WRP semanticsunderstand why traversal is separated from DAG compilationreason about Conduit/Nebula/LOSM alignmentevaluate migration sequence40. Inspector / Validator Retrieval Profile40.1 GoalRetrieve normative constraints, invariants, and compatibility conditions.40.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3IncludeL1only when validation depends on concrete schema or implementation details40.3 Preferred chunk kindsprotocol_ruleinvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriadata_model40.4 Normative preferencePrefer chunks where:normative_strength = requirednormative_strength = prohibited40.5 Typical use casesverify WRP compatibility rulesvalidate migration sequencingenforce traversal invariantsdetect protocol / DAG / traversal mismatch41. Explorer Retrieval Profile41.1 GoalSupport open-ended investigation across architecture, rationale, and unresolved questions.41.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3,L4IncludeL1only if the search narrows to implementation mechanics41.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewrationaleopen_questiondefinitionexample42. Suggested Retrieval AlgorithmA role-aware retrieval query should combine:artifact filteringe.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')level filteringrole-dependent level setchunk kind weightingrole-specific preferred chunk kindsnormative weightingfor validator/inspector profilescross-reference expansionbounded traversal across explicit edgesexecution recency boostoptional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in ConduitPseudo-policy:candidate_chunks =filter by artifact family / lexical relevance / embedding relevance∩ filter by allowed levels for roleweighted by chunk_kind preferenceweighted by normative_strength where applicableexpanded by explicit cross-reference traversal depth <= NRecommended initial traversal depths:Builder:N = 1Architect:N = 2Inspector:N = 2Explorer:N = 343. Worked Example: Retrieval for WRP Traversal ImplementationUser intent:“Implement the traversal engine for WRP v1.2.”Builder profile should retrieve:WRP v1.2chunks describingExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceipttraversal order semanticsdeterministic traversal defaultisolation rule chunksmigration notes only if they affect implementation compatibilityArchitect profile should additionally retrieve:the WRP DAG document sections that define node and edge semanticsrationale for why traversal is a separate stagemigration constraints affecting rolloutInspector profile should emphasize:invariant chunks such as tenant isolation rulesfailure semanticsreceipt completeness rulescompatibility constraints in the migration plan44. Worked Example: WRP v1.2 Chunking and Level AssignmentConsider a traversal-engine document with these sections:OverviewExecutionContextExecutionCursorTraversal order and pending queue semanticsTenant isolationExperimental policy modeWhy traversal is separate from DAG compilationImplementation checklistRecommended chunking:SectionChunk KindLevelOverviewoverviewL2ExecutionContextdata_modelL2ExecutionCursordata_modelL2Traversal order and pending queue semanticsalgorithmL2Tenant isolationinvariantL2Experimental policy modedefinition/invariantL2Why traversal is separate from DAG compilationrationaleL3Implementation checklistimplementation_note/acceptance_criteriaL145. WRP-Specific Normative MarkingTo make validation retrieval effective, WRP chunks should mark normative strength where appropriate.Examples:requiredtraversal must enforce tenant isolation at execution timeprotocol version must be present in every WRP root requestDAG compilation must reject cycles if the WRP graph is defined as acyclicprohibitedtraversal must not execute a node under the wrong tenant contextmigration must not remove legacy compatibility before the designated cutover phaserecommendedbuilders should prefer deterministic traversal order unless explicitly in experimental modeinformativehistorical rationale and examples46. Back-Projection from Execution into NebulaOnce Conduit and runtime begin executing WRP work, Nebula should be updated with execution traceability.Examples:a Conduit plan completes implementation ofwrp-v1_2-traversalan execution receipt validates a traversal invarianta migration work request supersedes an older compatibility ruleThese should produce:document status updates,execution links,optional new cross-references,optional “implementation evidence” annotations.This should be append-only where possible; do not rewrite architectural history.47. Initial Migration Plan for the Existing WRP PacketThis section defines the first practical rollout for the four WRP artifacts already placed into Conduit.48. Phase 1 — Register the Four WRP ArtifactsCreate Nebula artifact/document records for:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planAt minimum, store:titleartifact typeartifact keyversiondefault levelconduit plan idsource kindstatus49. Phase 2 — Import the Authoritative WRP Markdown DocumentsFor each artifact, import the corresponding markdown spec into Nebula.If a markdown spec does not yet exist in repo form, use a temporary generated or manually curated document, but treat that as a stopgap. The target steady state is:WRP architectural material lives as markdown/spec documents in Nebula, not only as Conduit plan descriptions.50. Phase 3 — Chunk and Level the DocumentsRun the markdown importer with:section extractionsemantic chunkingchunk kind assignmentchunk-level level override assignmentnormative strength tagging for invariant sectionsDo not leave WRP material as giant undifferentiated chunks.51. Phase 4 — Emit Required Cross ReferencesAt minimum, emit:protocol → DAG edgesDAG → traversal edgesmigration → protocol/DAG/traversal edgesWRP artifact → Conduit plan links52. Phase 5 — Add Role-Aware Retrieval FiltersAdd query support for:allowed levelspreferred chunk kindsoptional normative strength weightingbounded cross-reference expansionThis is the point where “Builder sees implementation detail; Architect sees architecture” becomes real.53. Phase 6 — Backfill Execution LinksOnce Conduit begins implementing the packet, attach:plan IDsreceipt trailsstatus updatesimplementation evidence linksto the corresponding WRP artifacts in Nebula.54. InvariantsThe following invariants apply to the Conduit → Nebula WRP projection model.I1. Nebula is the authoritative long-form memory for WRPConduit may track execution, but architectural WRP meaning must remain represented in Nebula.I2. Every WRP artifact must have a stable artifact keyPaths may change; artifact identity must not.I3. Every Nebula document and chunk must have a deterministic effective levelA chunk either declares a level or inherits from its document.I4. Cross-reference edges are level-neutral by defaultThe source and target nodes carry the abstraction semantics.I5. The initial WRP packet must be explicitly cross-linkedProtocol, DAG, traversal, and migration documents must not exist as isolated documents.I6. Role-aware retrieval must filter by level before broad cross-reference expansionOtherwise the stratification model loses value.I7. Execution traceability must be additive, not destructiveImplementation evidence and receipts should enrich architectural records rather than overwrite them.58. What This Unlocks NextOnce this projection and stratification layer exists, the system can do all of the following coherently:Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.59. Bottom LineThe four WRP plans now sitting in Conduit should be treated as theexecution packetfor a broader WRP knowledge corpus. The missing piece is a projection layer that makes those artifacts durable and queryable inside Nebula.The core model is simple:Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledgeConduit stores the executable work packetWRP artifacts provide the stable identity between themlevelstratification controls who sees whatcross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graphThat is the foundation required before WRP can function as a real architectural substrate rather than just a set of implementation plans.---## What I’d do immediately after this oneSince those four WRP plans are now in Conduit and will take a bit to implement under your local Ollama/OpenCode/Qwen setup, the next companion spec I’d write is the **actual Nebula schema/ontology patch** for this document, not another prose architecture note.Specifically:# `schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonld`That doc should formalize, in machine-oriented ontology form:- `KnowledgeLevel`- `ArtifactType`- `ChunkKind`- `NormativeStrength`- `CrossReferenceRelationType`- `NebulaDocument`- `NebulaChunk`- `NebulaArtifact`- `NebulaExecutionLink`and the exact fields/relationships implied by the markdown spec above.If you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it **repo-ready JSON-LD** rather than another markdown doc.SourcesHelpjuice, Inc.SponsoredCompany Knowledge, Now Searchable by AIHelpjuice gives teams an AI-powered knowledge base built from their real documentation.You said:go onChatGPT said:Thought for 5sAbsolutely — the right next artifact is themachine-oriented ontology/schema companionfor the markdown spec we just pinned down.Given your own framing from earlier, I’m going to keep the JSON-LD side as theexternal graph/persistence targetfor Nebula/PEB rather than treating it like the authored source of truth. Purposethis JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links2. Canonical interpretation rulesNebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisionsNebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form contentNebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a documentNebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edgeNebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts3. Level rulesdocuments have default levelschunks may override levelscross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections4. WRP artifact registry obligationsartifact keys are stabledocument revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in placecurrentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision5. Retrieval implicationsBuilder → L1 + selective L2Architect → L2/L3Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunksExplorer → L2/L3/L4A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into Here’s the next piece as arepo-ready implementation specfor turning the WRP docs you just put into Conduit into structured Nebula artifacts, chunks, and cross-references.docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdMarkdown# WRP Document Projection Rules**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula / WRP integration**Purpose:** Define deterministic rules for projecting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, levels, and cross-references.---# 1. ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning13.2 Chunk IDsFormat:<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning/chunk/01Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.13.3 Re-import stabilityOn re-import:if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stableif a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new idsif a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported14. Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. Future ExtensionsThe following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)embedding generation and vector indexingrole-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itselfsupersession lineage across chunk revisionsbidirectional Conduit synchronizationLLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristicsconfidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments20. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is Here’s the next companion doc as the operational layer for the review-state schema.docs/nebula/review-workflow.mdMarkdown# Nebula Review Workflow**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula governance / corpus maintenance**Purpose:** Define how review state is assigned, updated, interpreted, and used to prioritize attention across Nebula artifacts, sections, and chunks.---# 1. PurposeNebula stores a growing corpus of architecture notes, specifications, migration plans, ontology documents, implementation plans, and execution-adjacent material. Not all corpus material is equally current, equally trustworthy, or equally relevant to active work.This document defines a **review workflow overlay** that allows Nebula users and roles to mark corpus material as:- needing review- under active review- reviewed- current focus- outdated- questioned- supersededThe review workflow exists to answer a different question than lifecycle status.## Lifecycle status answers:- Is this artifact active, draft, deprecated, or superseded in the corpus?## Review status answers:- What should we pay attention to right now?- What should be trusted by default?- What needs inspection before it influences implementation?- What should be deprioritized or excluded from normal retrieval?Review state is therefore a **triage and trust overlay** on top of the corpus, not a replacement for artifact lifecycle semantics.---# 2. Core Principles## 2.1 Review state is separate from artifact lifecycleAn item may be:- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`- `status = SUPERSEDED` and `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- `status = DRAFT` and `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Lifecycle describes what the artifact **is**.Review state describes what the team should **do about it**.## 2.2 Review state is primarily an attention and trust signalReview state is used to:- focus corpus maintenance- guide retrieval ranking- reduce accidental reliance on stale documents- identify blocking or suspect specs- surface active areas of architecture work## 2.3 Artifact-level review is the default starting pointNebula SHOULD support review state at:- artifact level- section level- chunk levelHowever, the initial operational workflow assumes:- **artifact-level review is primary**- section/chunk review is optional and targetedThe system MUST NOT require chunk-by-chunk review to be useful.## 2.4 Review state is allowed to be provisionalReview state is not a certification regime. It is acceptable to mark an item:- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`without yet knowing the final replacement or fix. The goal is to make uncertainty visible and actionable.---# 3. Review Scope LevelsNebula review annotations may apply at three scopes.## 3.1 Artifact scopeApplies to an entire document / artifact such as:- `wrp-v1-protocol`- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `wrp-v1_2-traversal`- `wrp-migration-plan`Artifact scope is the default and most common review target.## 3.2 Section scopeApplies to a specific section within an artifact when the document is mixed-quality.Example:- the WRP protocol document is generally current- but the `Execution Semantics / Receipts` section is outdatedSection review SHOULD be used when:- only one part of a large artifact is stale or questionable- the artifact should remain broadly retrievable without blanket demotion## 3.3 Chunk scopeApplies to a specific chunk when review needs to be precise.Chunk review SHOULD be used sparingly and mainly when:- a particular invariant is suspect- a specific migration step is obsolete- a specific rationale chunk remains valuable even inside an outdated section---# 4. Review Status VocabularyThe following review statuses are defined by `schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`.## 4.1 `UNREVIEWED`The item has not yet been reviewed for current validity or relevance.Use when:- a document was imported but not yet triaged- a new chunk has not been evaluated## 4.2 `NEEDS_REVIEW`The item should be reviewed soon because it may be stale, incomplete, or important to current work.Use when:- the document is likely relevant to current implementation- the document predates a major architectural shift- the document appears important but confidence is low## 4.3 `UNDER_REVIEW`The item is actively being reviewed, rewritten, or reconciled.Use when:- you are actively comparing it against current architecture or code- Builder/Architect/Inspector are working through it now## 4.4 `REVIEWED`The item has been reviewed and is believed to be usable in normal work.Use when:- the document is current enough for default retrieval- known issues are minor or already called out## 4.5 `CURRENT_FOCUS`The item is a current focus of architecture or implementation attention and should be surfaced prominently.Use when:- active work depends on this item now- the item is central to the current execution stream- the item is the present working center of a subsystem redesign## 4.6 `OUTDATED`The item is known to be out of date relative to the current architecture, runtime, or workflow.Use when:- the document predates a material redesign- its prescriptions are no longer safe defaults- it still has historical value but should be demoted## 4.7 `QUESTIONED`The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt.Use when:- parts of the document conflict with newer understanding- the model may be wrong, not merely old- the document should be examined before it is trusted## 4.8 `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval.Use when:- there is a clear replacement artifact or replacement chunk set- the supersession is intentional and not merely suspected---# 5. Review PriorityReview priority answers: **how urgently should this item be revisited?**Allowed values:- `CRITICAL`- `HIGH`- `MEDIUM`- `LOW`## 5.1 Priority guidance### `CRITICAL`Use when:- the item is blocking implementation- the item is actively misleading current work- the item governs current execution and is likely wrong or stale### `HIGH`Use when:- the item is central to near-term architecture or implementation- review delay would materially slow work or degrade decisions### `MEDIUM`Use when:- the item matters, but not immediately- it should be triaged in the near future### `LOW`Use when:- review is backlog hygiene- the item is historical or peripheral---# 6. Attention ReasonsAttention reasons explain **why** an item needs review or focus.The first review-state schema defines these reasons:- `BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIME`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE`- `CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODEL`- `REQUIRES_MIGRATION`- `DUPLICATED_ELSEWHERE`- `NEEDS_LEVEL_REVIEW`- `NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`Multiple reasons MAY be attached to the same item.## ExampleA migration document might be:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `reviewPriority = HIGH`- `attentionReason = [REQUIRES_MIGRATION, OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE]`---# 7. Who May Set Review State## 7.1 Human authority is primaryThe human operator is the authoritative source of review state.In practice, this means you may set review state manually based on reading, comparison, or implementation experience.## 7.2 Roles may propose review state, but not silently finalize itThe following roles may recommend review changes:- **Inspector**- flags contradictions, stale invariants, missing migration updates, or retrieval hazards- **Architect**- flags architectural obsolescence, boundary drift, or rationale conflicts- **Builder**- flags implementation-blocking ambiguity or mismatch with actual code- **Explorer**- flags duplicate or related documents that may need consolidationThese role recommendations SHOULD be recorded as annotations or proposals, but SHOULD NOT silently overwrite the effective review state unless explicitly authorized.## 7.3 Importers may initialize, not decideImporters and projectors MAY set initial values such as:- `UNREVIEWED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW` when the source predates a known migration boundary- `OUTDATED` when explicit source metadata says soHowever, importers SHOULD NOT autonomously mark an item `REVIEWED` or `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`.---# 8. Effective Review State ModelNebula may store multiple review annotations over time. The system therefore needs a rule for determining the **effective review state** used in retrieval and dashboards.## 8.1 Effective review state per scopeEach reviewable object (artifact, section, chunk) SHOULD expose a single **effective review state** for operational use.This effective state may be materialized directly on the object row or computed from annotations.## 8.2 Default precedence ruleIf multiple annotations exist for the same object, the effective review state SHOULD be determined by:1. most recent human-authored authoritative annotation2. otherwise most recent approved role recommendation3. otherwise importer-initialized default4. otherwise `UNREVIEWED`## 8.3 Status severity tie-breakIf multiple candidate annotations are equally authoritative and recent enough to conflict, use the following severity ordering to avoid false optimism:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `UNDER_REVIEW`- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `UNREVIEWED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`This severity ordering is for tie-breaking only and MUST NOT be interpreted as a universal ranking of importance.## 8.4 Why `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is not treated as “most severe”Superseded material is often safe to ignore rather than urgent to fix. It is not necessarily a live problem. Therefore it should not outrank `QUESTIONED` or `CURRENT_FOCUS` in attention logic.---# 9. Artifact / Section / Chunk Rollup RulesReview state may exist at multiple scopes simultaneously. The workflow needs rules for how lower-level review state influences higher-level summaries.## 9.1 Artifact effective review is primaryArtifact review status is the main corpus-level triage signal and SHOULD be set explicitly rather than inferred whenever possible.## 9.2 Section and chunk review do not automatically overwrite artifact reviewIf an artifact is marked `REVIEWED` but one chunk is marked `QUESTIONED`, the artifact does not automatically become `QUESTIONED`.Instead, the artifact SHOULD receive one or more rollup indicators such as:- `needsAttention = true`- `attentionReason += NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`- optional `focusScore` boost- optional “contains questioned chunk” derived flag## 9.3 Optional artifact rollup policyImplementations MAY define a rollup threshold such as:- if ≥ 30% of chunks are `OUTDATED` or `QUESTIONED`, artifact effective review becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`- if any chunk is `CURRENT_FOCUS`, artifact `focusScore` is boosted- if all chunks are `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`, artifact may be proposed as `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`But this rollup SHOULD be advisory until chunk review is common enough to trust statistically.---# 10. Review ActionsThe review workflow recognizes the following actions.## 10.1 Mark Needs ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- optionally priority and attention reasonsUse when an item should enter the review queue.## 10.2 Start ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Use when active review or rewrite has begun.## 10.3 Mark ReviewedSet:- `reviewStatus = REVIEWED`- `lastReviewedAt`- optional summaryUse when the item is current enough for normal use.## 10.4 Mark Current FocusSet:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`Use when the item is a live center of implementation or architecture work.## 10.5 Mark OutdatedSet:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`Use when the item is no longer a safe default but may still be historically useful.## 10.6 Mark QuestionedSet:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`Use when the item may be wrong, not merely old.## 10.7 Confirm SupersededSet:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- set `supersededBy` if knownUse when a replacement is clear and the old material should be demoted from normal retrieval.---# 11. Relationship Between Supersession and ReviewSupersession and review are related but distinct.## 11.1 Supersession is a semantic relationshipExample:- `wrp-v1-protocol-v0` is superseded by `wrp-v1-protocol`This is modeled as:- `supersededBy`- `supersedes`- lifecycle `status`## 11.2 Review supersession is an operational confirmationAn item becomes `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when the team has decided it should be treated as superseded for retrieval and attention purposes.## 11.3 Auto-promotion ruleIf `supersededBy` is set, the system MAY propose:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`but SHOULD NOT automatically finalize it unless configured to do so.Reason:- some superseded artifacts still matter during a migration period- some artifacts are partially superseded but still operationally relevant---# 12. Review Workflow for Corpus TriageThis section defines the simple human workflow the system is meant to support.## 12.1 Initial triage passAs you review the corpus, each artifact SHOULD be assigned one of:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`with optional:- priority- attention reasons- short review summaryThe goal is not perfection. The goal is to make the corpus sortable and navigable.## 12.2 Triage heuristics### Mark `CURRENT_FOCUS` when:- active implementation or redesign is centered on the artifact now### Mark `NEEDS_REVIEW` when:- the artifact is probably important but confidence is not high enough- the artifact predates a major design change- the artifact is about to become implementation-relevant again### Mark `REVIEWED` when:- the artifact is current enough to be used normally### Mark `OUTDATED` when:- the artifact still has historical value but should not be trusted as a default guide### Mark `QUESTIONED` when:- the artifact may encode wrong assumptions or contradictions### Mark `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when:- a replacement exists and default retrieval should normally prefer the replacement---# 13. Retrieval EffectsReview state MUST influence Nebula retrieval.## 13.1 Default retrieval behaviorUnless explicitly overridden:- `CURRENT_FOCUS` receives a strong ranking boost- `REVIEWED` receives a positive ranking boost- `NEEDS_REVIEW` remains retrievable but slightly demoted relative to reviewed/current material- `OUTDATED` is demoted- `QUESTIONED` is demoted for Builder/Architect defaults but may be boosted for Inspector- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is excluded or strongly demoted from default retrieval## 13.2 Role-specific review-state behavior### BuilderPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Demote:- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`Exclude by default:- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`### ArchitectPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Allow:- `QUESTIONED`- selected `OUTDATED` material when rationale still matters### InspectorPrefer:- `QUESTIONED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `OUTDATED`because those often indicate the places where validation and contradiction analysis are most needed.### ExplorerAllow broad inclusion, including:- `OUTDATED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`when historical lineage or unresolved questions matter.---# 14. Dashboard / Queue BehaviorNebula SHOULD support a review queue over artifacts.## 14.1 Default review queueThe default review queue SHOULD show artifacts where:- `reviewStatus IN (NEEDS_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW, CURRENT_FOCUS, OUTDATED, QUESTIONED)`- OR `needsAttention = true`ordered by:1. `reviewPriority`2. `focusScore`3. `updatedAt` or `lastReviewedAt`## 14.2 Suggested dashboard slicesUseful corpus views include:### Current FocusArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`### Needs ReviewArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`### Questioned / RiskyArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`### Outdated but not yet supersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`### SupersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`---# 15. Recommended Initial SQL ShapeFor the first operational implementation, Nebula SHOULD materialize current effective review state directly on `nebula_artifact`.Recommended columns:- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `needs_attention`- `last_reviewed_at`- `review_summary`- `focus_score`Optional on `nebula_chunk`:- same fields, nullableReview history SHOULD be stored separately in `nebula_review_annotation` with fields such as:- `id`- `target_type`- `target_id`- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `attention_reason_json`- `needs_attention`- `reviewed_by`- `review_summary`- `created_at`---# 16. Example Review Annotations## 16.1 Current focus artifact```json{"id": "review:annotation/wrp-v1_2-traversal/2026-06-21","type": "ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo": "wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal","reviewStatus": "review:CURRENT_FOCUS","reviewPriority": "review:CRITICAL","attentionReason": ["review:BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION"],"needsAttention": true,"lastReviewedAt": "2026-06-21T13:00:00Z","reviewedBy": "role:architect","reviewSummary": "Traversal engine spec is the current implementation center and should remain top-ranked for Builder and Architect retrieval."}16.2 Outdated migration sectionJSON{"id":"review:annotation/wrp-migration-plan/execution-cutover/2026-06-21","type":"ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo":"wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan/section/execution-cutover","reviewStatus":"review:OUTDATED","reviewPriority":"review:HIGH","attentionReason": ["review:OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE","review:REQUIRES_MIGRATION"],"needsAttention":true,"lastReviewedAt":"2026-06-21T13:10:00Z","reviewedBy":"role:inspector","reviewSummary":"This section predates the traversal split and should not be used as the default guide for execution cutover."}17. SummaryNebula review workflow exists to turn the corpus into a manageable attention system rather than a passive archive.The governing rule is:Lifecycle status tells us what an artifact is; review state tells us whether we should trust it, revisit it, focus on it, or route around it right now.The initial operational model is intentionally simple:review at artifact scope firstmark items as current focus / needs review / reviewed / outdated / questioned / supersededrecord priority and attention reasonlet retrieval and dashboards honor that stateonly descend to section/chunk review when precision is worth the effort---# Where we are nowWe’ve now inserted the review-governance pair:1. **`schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`**2. **`docs/nebula/review-workflow.md`**So we can go back
