This is the piece that turns everything you’ve built so far into something executable instead of just well-structured theory.This is youractual compiler spec.docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdMarkdown# WRP → Nebula Projection Pseudocode**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula ingestion / WRP compiler**Purpose:** Define deterministic algorithm for converting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, review overlays, and cross-reference graphs.---# 1. OverviewThis document specifies the **projection compiler pipeline** that transforms WRP markdown documents into structured Nebula graph data.Input:- WRP markdown documentsOutput:- NebulaArtifacts- NebulaSections- NebulaChunks- NebulaCrossReferences- Review overlays (optional but supported)- Conduit links (if present)The pipeline is deterministic, idempotent, and replay-safe.---# 2. High-Level Pipelineparse_markdown()→ build_ast()→ resolve_artifact()→ build_section_tree()→ segment_chunks()→ classify_chunks()→ assign_levels()→ assign_review_overlay()→ extract_cross_references()→ emit_graph()→ upsert_store()---# 3. Core Data Structures (Logical)## ArtifactArtifact {idkeysource_pathstatus}## SectionSection {idartifact_idparent_section_idheadingordinal}## ChunkChunk {idsection_idordinaltextchunk_kindlevelnormative_strength}## ReviewOverlay (optional)ReviewOverlay {target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason[]}## CrossReferenceCrossReference {source_idtarget_idrelation_type}---# 4. Step 1 — Parse Markdown```pseudofunction parse_markdown(source_text):ast = MarkdownParser.parse(source_text)return astRules:preserve heading hierarchypreserve code blocks as atomic nodespreserve tables as atomic nodespreserve block quotes as semantic units5. Step 2 — Artifact Resolutionpseudofunction resolve_artifact(file_path, registry):if registry.contains(file_path):return registry.get(file_path)if STRICT_MODE:throw Error("Unknown artifact in strict mode")return create_artifact_from_path(file_path)Artifact key mapping:derived from filenamenormalized slug6. Step 3 — Build Section Treepseudofunction build_section_tree(ast):root = new SectionTree()current_stack = []for node in ast:if node.type == HEADING:level = node.levelwhile current_stack.top.level >= level:current_stack.pop()section = new Section(heading=node.text,parent=current_stack.top)current_stack.push(section)root.add(section)return rootRules:##→ Section###→ child section####+→ either nested section or flatten depending on config7. Step 4 — Chunk Segmentationpseudofunction segment_chunks(section):chunks = []buffer = []for block in section.blocks:if is_boundary(block, buffer):chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))buffer = []buffer.append(block)if buffer not empty:chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))return chunks7.1 Boundary rulespseudofunction is_boundary(block, buffer):if buffer.empty:return falseif block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:return trueif block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:return trueif semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):return trueif buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:return truereturn false7.2 Semantic shift heuristicpseudofunction semantic_shift(a, b):if a.kind != b.kind:return trueif switches_between("RATIONALE","IMPLEMENTATION","PROTOCOL_RULE"):return truereturn false8. Step 5 — Chunk Classificationpseudofunction classify_chunk(chunk):text = chunk.textif contains("must not", text):chunk.normative = PROHIBITEDelse if contains("must", text):chunk.normative = REQUIREDelse if contains("should", text):chunk.normative = RECOMMENDEDelse:chunk.normative = INFORMATIVEchunk.kind = classify_kind(text)return chunk8.1 Chunk kind classifierpseudofunction classify_kind(text):if matches_definition_pattern(text):return DEFINITIONif contains_protocol_keywords(text):return PROTOCOL_RULEif contains_invariant_keywords(text):return INVARIANTif contains_algorithm_structure(text):return ALGORITHMif contains_schema_fields(text):return DATA_MODELif contains_migration_language(text):return MIGRATION_STEPif contains_open_question_markers(text):return OPEN_QUESTIONif contains_rationale_markers(text):return RATIONALEif contains_example_markers(text):return EXAMPLEreturn OVERVIEW9. Step 6 — Level Assignmentpseudofunction assign_level(chunk):if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:return L1if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:return L2if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:return L3return L210. Step 7 — Review Overlay Assignmentpseudofunction assign_review_overlay(entity, context):overlay = new ReviewOverlay()if entity.is_new:overlay.status = UNREVIEWEDif contains_staleness_signals(entity):overlay.status = NEEDS_REVIEWif matches_current_focus_tags(entity):overlay.status = CURRENT_FOCUSif contains_conflict_signals(entity):overlay.status = QUESTIONEDif superseded_by_exists(entity):overlay.status = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDreturn overlay11. Step 8 — Cross Reference Extractionpseudofunction extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):refs = []for token in chunk.text:if token matches artifact_key:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=artifact_id(token),type=DEPENDS_ON))if token matches section_heading:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=section_id(token),type=REFERENCES))if token matches known_concept:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=concept_id(token),type=MENTIONS))return refs12. Step 9 — Emit Graphpseudofunction emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):graph = NebulaGraph()graph.add(artifact)for section in sections:graph.add(section)for chunk in chunks:graph.add(chunk)for ref in refs:graph.add(ref)return graph13. Step 10 — Upsert Store (Idempotent)pseudofunction upsert_store(graph, db):for node in graph.nodes:db.upsert(node.id, node)for edge in graph.edges:db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)Rules:idempotent writesstable IDs requiredno duplicate edges unless explicitly allowedpreserve existing review annotations unless overridden14. Determinism RulesProjection MUST be deterministic:same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunksno LLM-based randomness in core pipelineonly heuristic classification allowedno sampling variabilityIf classifier improves:version bump requirednew projection run produces new revision lineage15. Failure Modes15.1 Unknown artifact→ fail in STRICT_MODE15.2 ambiguous chunk boundaries→ prefer splitting over merging15.3 classification uncertainty→ default to OVERVIEW + INFORMATIVE15.4 missing references→ ignore silently (do not fail pipeline)16. Minimal Implementation ContractA valid implementation MUST:parse markdown into structured ASTbuild deterministic section treesegment chunks deterministicallyclassify chunks without external LLM dependency (LLM optional later)assign level + kind to every chunkemit graph with stable IDssupport idempotent re-import17. SummaryThis pipeline defines Nebula’s core transformation:Markdown → structured semantic graphThe important shift is:documents are not storedsemantic nodes are storedEverything else (review, retrieval, roles, Conduit integration) operates on top of this graph, not the raw text.---# What you now have (important moment)You now have a complete **minimal compiler stack**:### 1. Review system (attention layer)- `nebula-review-state.jsonld`- `review-workflow.md`### 2. Semantic classification system- `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`### 3. Execution pipeline- `wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`---# What this unlocks nextAt this point, Nebula is structurally capable of:- ingesting your WRP corpus- chunking it deterministically- classifying semantics- tracking review state- building a queryable graph- feeding Conduit execution planning---# The next natural step (if you want to continue)There are two obvious upgrades:### A. Retrieval layer specHow Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer actually query this graph### B. This is where Nebula stops being “structured storage” and becomes an actualquery-driven cognitive system.We’re going to define how rolesthink over the graph.docs/nebula/retrieval-role-scoring-model.mdMarkdown# Nebula Retrieval & Role Scoring Model**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula query engine / cognitive runtime layer**Purpose:** Define how Nebula retrieves, ranks, and filters graph content based on role context, chunk semantics, review state, and task intent.---# 1. OverviewNebula does not retrieve documents.It retrieves a **ranked subgraph of semantic chunks**.Every query is evaluated through:- role profile (Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer / Conduit)- chunk kind (semantic intent)- level (L1–L4 abstraction)- review state (trust + attention overlay)- cross-reference density (graph connectivity)- task intent (implicit or explicit)The output is a **scored ranked set of chunks + their local graph neighborhood**.---# 2. Core Retrieval ObjectA retrieval result is not a document.It is:RetrievalResult {chunkscoreexplanationneighborhood[]}Neighborhood includes:- parent section- sibling chunks- referenced chunks- optionally upstream/downstream traversal nodes---# 3. Retrieval Pipelinequery→ intent_classification→ role_profile_resolution→ candidate_chunk_selection→ scoring→ graph_expansion→ reranking→ filtering→ return---# 4. Role ProfilesEach role defines **what “relevant” means**.---## 4.1 BuilderBuilder optimizes for implementation correctness.### Preferences:- L1 chunks strongly preferred- ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE- MIGRATION_STEP when executing transitions- REVIEWED and CURRENT_FOCUS### Demotions:- RATIONALE (unless directly tied to implementation)- OUTDATED- QUESTIONED### Boost factors:- normative chunks (REQUIRED > RECOMMENDED)- high retrievalBias chunks---## 4.2 ArchitectArchitect optimizes for system correctness and structure.### Preferences:- L2 chunks- PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DATA_MODEL- RATIONALE (strongly valued)- OPEN_QUESTION (for unresolved design space)### Demotions:- overly implementation-specific L1 noise- trivial EXAMPLE chunks---## 4.3 InspectorInspector optimizes for contradiction detection and system validation.### Preferences:- QUESTIONED- INVARIANT- OUTDATED- OPEN_QUESTION- cross-reference-heavy chunks### Behavior:- actively surfaces inconsistencies- boosts conflicting review states- prioritizes low-confidence or high-risk nodes---## 4.4 ExplorerExplorer optimizes for understanding and knowledge traversal.### Preferences:- OVERVIEW- RATIONALE- EXAMPLE- high connectivity chunks### Behavior:- expands neighborhoods aggressively- favors graph traversal depth over strict relevance- includes historical/superseded context when useful---## 4.5 Conduit (Execution Role)Conduit optimizes for executable transformation.### Preferences:- MIGRATION_STEP- ALGORITHM- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA- PROTOCOL_RULE- L1 chunks only### Behavior:- strips non-normative noise- prioritizes determinism- prefers minimal required graph for execution---# 5. Chunk Scoring FunctionEvery chunk receives a score:score =role_weightkind_weightlevel_weightreview_weightgraph_weightfreshness_weight---## 5.1 Role weightDefined per role profile preferences.Example:- Builder: +2 for L1- Architect: +2 for L2- Inspector: +3 for QUESTIONED- Explorer: +2 for OVERVIEW---## 5.2 Chunk kind weightFrom `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`:- PROTOCOL_RULE → +3 for Architect- ALGORITHM → +3 for Builder/Conduit- RATIONALE → +3 for Architect/Explorer- OPEN_QUESTION → +3 for Inspector/Architect- EXAMPLE → moderate boost for Explorer---## 5.3 Level weightL1: +3 for Builder/ConduitL2: +3 for ArchitectL3: +2 for ExplorerL4: +2 for all roles (meta awareness bonus)---## 5.4 Review weightCURRENT_FOCUS → +4REVIEWED → +2NEEDS_REVIEW → +1UNREVIEWED → 0OUTDATED → -2QUESTIONED → +2 for Inspector, -2 for BuilderSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED → -4 (default)---## 5.5 Graph weightChunks gain score from graph structure:- + connectivity (degree centrality)- + cross-reference richness- + being referenced by current focus nodes- + participation in migration chains---## 5.6 Freshness weightBased on:- last reviewed timestamp- recency of updates- proximity to current focus artifacts---# 6. Candidate SelectionBefore scoring, Nebula selects a candidate set:```pseudo id="c8xk1a"function select_candidates(query):if query.role_hint exists:seed = role_preferred_chunks(query.role)else:seed = semantic_search(query.text)expand seed using:- direct references- parent sections- sibling chunksreturn seed7. Graph Expansion PhaseAfter scoring top candidates:for chunk in top_results:expand:parent sectionreferenced chunksupstream dependenciesdownstream dependenciesThis produces alocal subgraph, not just a ranked list.8. Filtering RulesAfter scoring:removeSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDunless explicitly requestedremoveOUTDATEDfor Builder unless overriddenpreserveQUESTIONEDfor InspectorpreserveRATIONALEfor Architect/Explorerenforce role-level safety filters9. Explanation GenerationEvery retrieval result MUST include:explanation = {"why_selected": [],"role_alignment": "","chunk_kind_match": "","review_state_influence": "","graph_signals": []}``` id="v1k2zq"This is critical for debugging the system and for human trust calibration.---# 10. Retrieval Modes## 10.1 STRICT MODE- only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS- no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED- minimal graph expansionUsed for execution / Conduit---## 10.2 EXPLORATION MODE- broad inclusion- heavy graph traversal- includes OUTDATED + SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED if relevantUsed for learning / architecture discovery---## 10.3 DIAGNOSTIC MODE- Inspector role default mode- boosts QUESTIONED and conflicts- surfaces contradictions explicitly---## 10.4 EXECUTION MODE- Builder + Conduit hybrid- minimal graph- deterministic chunks only- excludes RATIONALE unless required---# 11. Conflict ResolutionIf two chunks compete:Priority resolution:1. CURRENT_FOCUS overrides all2. REVIEWED overrides NEARLY EVERYTHING except CURRENT_FOCUS3. QUESTIONED overrides OUTDATED for Inspector4. SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED loses by default5. graph centrality can override weak semantic differences---# 12. Key Design Principle> Nebula retrieval is not search. It is weighted cognitive reconstruction.The system is not trying to find documents.It is trying to reconstruct the **relevant slice of the system’s mental model for a role and intent**.---# 13. DAG Constructionpseudofunction build_execution_dag(nodes, edges):dag = DirectedAcyclicGraph()for node in nodes:dag.add_node(node)for edge in edges:dag.add_edge(edge)if dag.has_cycles():resolve_cycles(dag)return dag6.1 Cycle resolution strategyIf cycles exist:Priority resolution:break edges from LOWER level → HIGHER levelbreak edges from RATIONALE → ALGORITHMpreserve PROTOCOL_RULE dependencies over EXAMPLE linksif unresolved → mark as NEEDS_REVIEW in Nebula7. Execution Plan CompilationOnce DAG is constructed:pseudofunction compile_execution_plan(dag):topo_order = topological_sort(dag)plan = []for node in topo_order:step = ExecutionStep(node_id=node.id,action=resolve_executor(node),inputs=get_inputs(node),outputs=declare_outputs(node))plan.append(step)return plan8. Core Data Structures## Validation Report```json id="vr1"ValidationReport {dag_idstatus: PASS | FAIL | DEGRADEDstructural_issues[]semantic_issues[]invariant_violations[]warnings[]suggested_fixes[]}Invariant DefinitionJSONInvariant {iddescriptionscope: GLOBAL | ARTIFACT | CHUNK | EXECUTION_STEPseverity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUMcondition_expression}4. Structural ValidationEnsures DAG correctness independent of semantics.pseudofunction structural_validation(dag):assert dag.is_acyclic()assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)return PASSStructural rulesDAG MUST be acyclicall nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunksno dangling references allowedall edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs5. Semantic ValidationEnsures node meaning aligns with WRP + Nebula expectations.pseudofunction semantic_validation(dag):for node in dag.nodes:if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")if node.review_state == OUTDATED:mark_warning(node)if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")return reportSemantic constraints5.1 Protocol purity rulePROTOCOL_RULE nodes MUST NOT contain:side-effect logicmutation operationsexecution commandsThey define constraints only.5.2 Algorithm determinism ruleALGORITHM nodes MUST:be deterministicnot depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration5.3 Migration consistency ruleMIGRATION_STEP nodes MUST:reference a valid prior statedefine explicit transition target6. Invariant Verification EngineThis is the core of WRP correctness.6.1 Invariant evaluation looppseudofunction invariant_verification(dag, invariants):violations = []for invariant in invariants:for node in dag.nodes:if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):violations.append({"node": node.id,"invariant": invariant.id})return violations6.2 Example invariantsGlobal execution invariantsNo node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution pathAll PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chainNo cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chainsWRP-specific invariantsEvery ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULEEvery MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transitionEvery ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node7. Dependency Consistency CheckEnsures graph coherence across Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction dependency_consistency(dag):for edge in dag.edges:if edge.type == DEPENDS_ON:assert topological_order(edge.source) < topological_order(edge.target)if violates_level_constraints(edge):mark_error(edge)Level constraint rulesL1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logicL2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationaleL3 nodes MUST NOT define execution dependencies8. Execution Safety CheckThis step ensures the DAG is safe to run under Conduit.8.1 Safety rulespseudofunction execution_safety(dag):assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)return PASS8.2 Strict mode constraintsIn STRICT execution mode:only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowedQUESTIONED nodes forbiddenOUTDATED nodes forbiddenSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely9. Validation Severity ModelEach issue is classified:CRITICAL → blocks executionHIGH → requires interventionMEDIUM → warningLOW → informationalFailure policypseudoif CRITICAL exists:status = FAILhalt_execution()elif HIGH exists:status = DEGRADEDrequire_human_review()else:status = PASS10. Suggested Fix GeneratorFor each violation:pseudofunction suggest_fix(issue):switch issue.type:case OUTDATED_DEPENDENCY:suggest("Replace with superseding artifact")case INVALID_PROTOCOL_MUTATION:suggest("Move logic to ALGORITHM chunk")case MISSING_REFERENCE:suggest("Add cross-reference or dependency edge")case LEVEL_VIOLATION:suggest("Promote/demote chunk level or split chunk")return suggestion11. OverviewConduit is a deterministic execution runtime for validated Nebula-derived DAGs.It is responsible for:- scheduling execution steps- managing concurrency- tracking execution state- handling retries and failures- emitting execution receipts- ensuring deterministic replayability---# 2. Core Principle> Conduit does not “run code.” It executes validated semantic graphs under strict lifecycle control.Every execution is:- deterministic where possible- replayable- traceable to Nebula chunks- governed by WRP validation guarantees---# 3. Execution Lifecycle StatesEach node transitions through a lifecycle:PENDING→ READY→ RUNNING→ COMPLETED→ FAILED→ RETRYING→ SKIPPED→ COMPENSATED---## 3.1 State definitions### PENDINGNode is waiting for dependencies or scheduling.### READYAll dependencies satisfied; eligible for execution.### RUNNINGNode is actively executing.### COMPLETEDExecution succeeded and produced valid output.### FAILEDExecution failed irrecoverably for current attempt.### RETRYINGNode is scheduled for re-execution.### SKIPPEDNode is intentionally bypassed (policy or conditional logic).### COMPENSATEDNode failure has been resolved via compensating action (migration or rollback logic).---# 4. Scheduler ModelConduit uses a **dependency-aware priority scheduler**.---## 4.1 Scheduling loop```pseudo id="sched1"while true:ready_nodes = get_ready_nodes(dag)prioritized = rank(ready_nodes,priority_function)for node in prioritized:if can_run(node):dispatch(node)4.2 Priority functionpseudopriority(node) =role_priority_weight(node)+ review_priority_weight(node)+ chunk_kind_weight(node)+ dependency_depth_weight(node)- failure_penalty(node)4.3 Dependency depth weightNodes deeper in dependency chains may be prioritized to unlock downstream execution faster.depth_score = longest_path_from_root(node)5. Concurrency ModelConduit supports controlled parallel execution.5.1 Execution constraintsA node MAY execute in parallel if:pseudocan_parallelize(node) =node.has_no_shared_mutation_targetsAND node.dependencies_satisfiedAND not_conflicting_with_running_nodes(node)5.2 Conflict rulesTwo nodes conflict if:they modify same conceptual statethey depend on each other's outputsthey share non-isolated resource contexts5.3 Concurrency policydefault: conservative parallelismmigration mode: stricter (serial execution preferred)exploration mode: relaxed (higher parallelism allowed)6. Execution Dispatcherpseudofunction dispatch(node):mark(node, RUNNING)executor = resolve_executor(node.type)context = build_execution_context(node)try:result = executor.execute(node.payload, context)mark(node, COMPLETED)emit_receipt(node, result)except error:handle_failure(node, error)7. Execution Context BuilderEach node executes with a structured context:JSON{"node_id":"...","dag_id":"...","role":"Conduit","mode":"EXECUTION","strict_mode":true,"nebula_trace": [],"allowed_chunk_kinds": [],"validation_signature":"WRP_VALIDATED","determinism":true}8. Failure Handling System8.1 Failure classificationpseudofunction classify_failure(error):if transient(error):return RETRYABLEif dependency_missing(error):return BLOCKINGif semantic_violation(error):return INVALID_DAGreturn FATAL8.2 Retry policypseudoif RETRYABLE:if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:schedule_retry(node)else:mark(node, FAILED)8.3 Blocking failure propagationIf a node fails due to dependency:downstream nodes → SKIPPED or PENDINGupstream nodes unaffectedDAG remains valid but partially executable8.4 Compensation modelFor MIGRATION_STEP nodes:failures MAY trigger compensating stepsrollback DAG may be generated9. DAG Execution GuaranteesConduit guarantees:deterministic execution order for identical inputsidempotent retries (when possible)no execution without READY stateno execution of invalidated nodesstrict adherence to WRP validation outputs10. Execution ReceiptsEvery execution produces a receipt:JSONExecutionReceipt {node_iddag_idstatusstart_timeend_timeinputsoutputslogsvalidation_ref}Receipts are:immutablestored in Nebulaused for future graph refinementused for failure analysis and review updates11. Scheduling Policies11.1 STRICT POLICYUsed for production execution:no speculative executionno retry beyond limitno OUTDATED or QUESTIONED nodesminimal concurrency11.2 OPTIMIZED POLICYUsed for performance execution:moderate concurrencypredictive schedulingprioritizes unlocking downstream nodes11.3 EXPLORATION POLICYUsed for discovery:high concurrencyrelaxed ordering constraintsallows partial execution of graph branches12. Deadlock PreventionDeadlocks are prevented via:topological schedulingcycle detection (from WRP validation layer)fallback serial executionforced dependency resolution orderingIf deadlock is detected:1. pause execution2. emit diagnostic subgraph3. request inspector review13. System Integration13.1 Nebula integrationConduit reads:validated DAGschunk metadatareview overlayscross-reference structureConduit writes:ExecutionReceiptsfailure annotationsinferred review updates13.2 WRP integrationConduit only executes DAGs that:pass WRP validation enginesatisfy invariant checkscomply with strict mode rules13.3 Validation gate couplingpseudoif not WRPValidationReport.PASS:abort_execution()14. Feedback Loop (Critical)Execution results feed back into Nebula:failed nodes → QUESTIONEDrepeatedly failing nodes → OUTDATED candidatefrequently executed nodes → CURRENT_FOCUS candidatestable nodes → REVIEWEDThis closes theadaptive system loop.15. Key System PropertyConduit is not just an executor — it is a stateful runtime that evolves Nebula’s trust model over time.16. Final Architecture ViewWRP↓Nebula (semantic graph + review state)↓Retrieval (role-scored subgraph selection)↓WRP Validation Engine (pre-execution proof gate)↓Conduit Scheduler (this layer)↓Execution Nodes↓Receipts↓Nebula update cycle↓(continuous loop)``` id="loop2"---# 17. Control-flow driftExecution order violated expectations→ suggests DAG ordering issueD. Invariant driftInvariant violated during execution→ suggests WRP model mismatch7. Graph Update PlanningNebula does NOT mutate immediately.It generates amutation plan.7.1 Mutation plan structureJSONGraphMutationPlan {target_node_idmutation_typereasonconfidenceproposed_change}7.2 Mutation typesRECLASSIFY_CHUNK_KINDUPDATE_REVIEW_STATEMODIFY_EDGEADD_EDGEREMOVE_EDGEPROMOTE_LEVELDEMOTE_LEVELMARK_SUPERSEDEDSPLIT_CHUNKMERGE_CHUNK8. Cross-Reference AdjustmentExecution reveals incorrect or missing edges.9.1 Missing dependency discoveryIf runtime shows implicit dependency:pseudoif runtime_dependency_detected and no_edge_exists:add_edge(source, target, type=DEPENDS_ON)9.2 Broken dependency pruningIf dependency never used:downgrade to MENTIONSor remove edge entirely9.3 Over-constrained graph correctionIf SKIPPED nodes are frequent:dependency edges may be too strictdowngrade to soft references10. Chunk Reclassification EngineExecution results refine chunk taxonomy.10.1 Heuristic correction rulespseudoif ALGORITHM fails frequently:reconsider_chunk_kind(node)if PROTOCOL_RULE causes mutation logic:split_into(PROTOCOL_RULE, ALGORITHM)if RATIONALE is executed:likely misclassified → promote to PROTOCOL_RULE or DATA_MODEL11. Invariant LifecycleEvery invariant now has a lifecycle:PROPOSED→ TESTED→ VALIDATED→ STABLE→ DEPRECATED→ REPLACED---## 3.1 State definitions### PROPOSED- derived from observation or heuristic- not yet validated### TESTED- applied in simulation branches- evaluated under stress### VALIDATED- passes execution + simulation consistently### STABLE- holds across multiple branches and versions### DEPRECATED- fails under new system conditions### REPLACED- superseded by stronger invariant---# 4. Invariant SourcesWRP invariants are synthesized from:---## 4.1 Execution traces- repeated failure patterns- consistent success constraints- runtime invariants inferred from Conduit---## 4.2 Simulation divergence- invariants that hold across all stable branches- invariants that fail under specific mutations---## 4.3 Cross-agent agreement- invariants consistently inferred by Builder, Architect, Inspector---## 4.4 Governance decisions- human or L3-approved constraints- enforced structural rules---# 5. Invariant Synthesis Engine---## 5.1 Candidate generation```pseudo id="syn1"function generate_invariants(execution_data, simulation_data):candidates = []for pattern in extract_patterns(execution_data):if pattern.is_repeated():candidates.append(Invariant(candidate_from(pattern)))for divergence in simulation_data:if divergence.is_consistent_across_branches():candidates.append(Invariant(from_divergence(divergence)))return candidates5.2 Pattern typesdependency stability patternsexecution ordering constraintsfailure clustering patternsmutation resistance patterns6. Self-Representation ModelNebula introduces a canonical system node:SystemNode: NEBULA_COREThis node represents:- architecture- runtime components- governance structure- invariants (WRP)- agent fabric- execution system (Conduit)- temporal model- simulation engine---## 3.1 System Node Structure```json id="sysnode1"SystemNode {node_id: "NEBULA_CORE",components: ["WRP","Conduit","Nebula Graph","Multi-Agent Fabric","Governance Layer","Simulation Engine","Meta-Governance Layer"],version_alignment: GraphState.version_id,stability_score,drift_metrics,integrity_state}4. Introspection ModelNebula supports structured self-querying:4.1 Self-query typesA. Structural introspection“What am I made of?”returns system graph decompositionreturns dependency topology of core subsystemsB. Behavioral introspection“How do I behave under execution?”returns Conduit execution model applied to itselfreturns failure modes of system componentsC. Governance introspection“Who is allowed to change me?”returns L0–L4 authority mapreturns mutation constraints affecting itselfD. Stability introspection“Am I stable?”returns fixed-point compliance scorereturns drift metricsreturns invariant satisfaction distribution5. Self-Model Construction PipelineThe self-model is not manually defined.It is derived:SystemState↓Graph extraction↓Component clustering↓Role mapping↓Dependency inference↓SelfNode construction``` id="selfpipe1"---# 6. Bounded Recursion ConstraintSelf-modeling is restricted:---## 8.1 Allowed recursion depth- system → self-model → subcomponent model → bounded expansion onlyNo infinite expansion into:- “model of model of model …”---## 8.2 Forbidden operations- modifying WRP without L4 approval- redefining governance via self-model alone- collapsing self-model into execution logic- recursive self-modification without external validation---# 9. Self-Model as a Graph NodeThe SystemNode is part of Nebula:- it is queryable- it is versioned- it is included in simulation- it participates in structural validation (read-only)---## 9.1 Important constraint> The system cannot mutate itself via its self-model alone.Self-model is **observational**, not **authoritative**.---# 10. Drift Detection via Self-ModelSelf-model enables detection of:- hidden structural divergence- undocumented system behavior- governance bypass patterns- emergent behavior not reflected in design---## 10.1 Drift signal```pseudo id="drift2"drift =observed_system_state- self_model_stateIf drift exceeds threshold:trigger meta-governance reviewfreeze mutation pipelineregenerate self-model11. Self-Awareness Without AuthorityCritical separation:CapabilityAllowedAuthorityObserve selfYesL0–L3Model selfYesL1–L3Validate self-modelYesL2Modify system via self-modelNoL4 only14. Integration with Full SystemNebula Graph↓Multi-Agent Fabric↓Conduit Execution↓Validation Engine↓Self-Healing Layer↓Governance Layer↓Simulation Engine↓WRP Synthesizer↓Meta-Governance Layer↓Self-Model / Introspection Layer (this)↓SystemNode (NEBULA_CORE)↓feedback into all layers``` id="loop10"---# 15. Key System Property> The system contains a representation of itself, but that representation is always subordinate to observed execution reality.---# 16. Given that Conduit is execution-oriented and the real long-form knowledge belongs in Nebula, I’d treat this as thebridge specbetween the four WRP implementation plans now sitting in Conduit and the stratified knowledge corpus Nebula needs to become.Below is arepo-ready docin the style we’ve been using.docs/conduit/nebula-wrp-projection-and-level-stratification.mdMarkdown# Conduit → Nebula WRP Projection and Level Stratification**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Architecture / Nebula / Conduit**Last Updated:** 2026-06-21---# 1. PurposeThis document defines how **WRP artifacts managed through Conduit** are projected into the **Nebula knowledge graph / document corpus**, and how those artifacts are stratified by **abstraction level** so that different roles and agents can retrieve the right amount of context.The immediate goal is to support the first WRP work packet now tracked in Conduit:1. **WRP v1.0** — protocol formalization2. **WRP v1.1** — DAG data model & compilation pipeline3. **WRP v1.2** — execution traversal engine4. **WRP migration plan**These four artifacts must not remain isolated implementation plans. They must become **queryable architectural knowledge** inside Nebula so that:- builders can retrieve concrete implementation guidance,- architects can retrieve subsystem rationale and relationships,- inspectors/validators can retrieve invariants and migration constraints,- future harvests and work requests can cross-reference WRP material directly.This document therefore specifies:- the **projection model** from Conduit/WRP artifacts into Nebula;- the **`level` stratification model** for Nebula documents, chunks, and references;- the **artifact taxonomy** for WRP knowledge units;- the **retrieval policy** by role;- the **migration strategy** for the initial WRP corpus.---# 2. Context and Position in the StackThe working architectural chain is:```textNebula → WRP → Conduit → LOSM / runtime implementationwith the following responsibilities:Nebulalong-form architectural memorymarkdown-authored specificationschunked knowledge corpuscross-reference graphopen questions / unresolved decisionsretrieval substrate for planning and implementationWRP (Work Request Protocol / Work Request Package)canonical execution-facing representation of workprotocol, DAG model, traversal semantics, migration disciplinethe bridge between long-form intent and executable workConduitexecution-oriented work managerreceives concrete plans / work requeststracks dependencies, acceptance criteria, receipts, affected filesis not the authoritative home for large concept documentsLOSM / runtimeexecution engine, orchestration, persistence, validation, receiptsThe practical rule is:Nebula owns long-form architectural knowledge. Conduit owns executable work tracking. WRP is the formal bridge between the two.This document defines how that bridge is materialized in storage and retrieval.3. Design GoalsThe projection and stratification model must satisfy the following goals.G1. Preserve long-form WRP knowledge in NebulaThe WRP packet tracked in Conduit must be represented in Nebula as durable, queryable, versioned knowledge.G2. Preserve execution alignment with ConduitNebula entries must retain enough metadata to map back to the Conduit work packet(s) that implement them.G3. Support role-specific retrievalThe same corpus must serve multiple retrieval surfaces:Builder / implementerArchitect / plannerInspector / validatorExplorer / researcherG4. Separate abstraction levels cleanlyImplementation details should not drown architectural reasoning, and architectural rationale should not flood implementation prompts unless explicitly requested.G5. Preserve explicit cross-referencesProtocol rules, DAG semantics, traversal rules, migration tasks, invariants, and open questions must be linked explicitly rather than relying only on embedding similarity.G6. Remain compatible with the existing Nebula markdown-ingestion pipelineThis design should extend the existing markdown import / chunk / cross-reference model rather than replacing it.4. Core Decision4.1 Canonical ruleWRP artifacts are authored or curated as Nebula documents, then projected into Conduit as executable work packages.Conduit may hold the immediate execution plans, but Nebula remains the authoritative architectural memory for:protocol definitions,subsystem specs,migration rationale,invariants,open questions,design history.4.2 Projection directionThere are two distinct projection paths:A. Authoritative knowledge projectionNebula markdown/spec document→ Nebula document rows / chunks / cross references→ optional WRP artifact registration→ Conduit plan / work request generationB. Execution trace back-projectionConduit plan / execution receipt / implementation status→ WRP artifact linkage→ Nebula document metadata updates→ cross-linked execution referencesSo the system is not one-way. The long-form knowledge projects downward into executable work, and execution status projects upward into Nebula metadata and trace links.5. Scope of WRP Artifacts Covered by This SpecThis document covers the initial WRP corpus:WRP-1 — WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefines the formal work request protocol, message shape, identity, versioning, semantics, and lifecycle assumptions.WRP-2 — WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefines the DAG representation of work, node/edge semantics, compilation from protocol-level requests into executable graph structures, and compilation invariants.WRP-3 — WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefines the traversal/execution model over the WRP DAG, execution context, cursor/receipt semantics, deterministic traversal defaults, and isolation rules.WRP-4 — WRP Migration PlanDefines how existing work representations, legacy plans, or runtime workflows migrate into the WRP model with compatibility constraints and staged rollout.The schema and rules in this document are generic enough to apply to future WRP artifacts as well.6. Terminology6.1 Conduit PlanAn execution-oriented item managed by Conduit, typically containing:titleprojectaffected filesacceptance criteriadependenciesreceipt trail6.2 WRP ArtifactA versioned architectural / protocol artifact in the WRP family, such as:protocol specDAG model spectraversal engine specmigration planfuture validation / governance extensions6.3 Nebula DocumentA markdown-origin or spec-origin long-form document stored in Nebula.6.4 Nebula ChunkA chunked section or paragraph group extracted from a Nebula document for retrieval and cross-referencing.6.5 Cross ReferenceAn explicit semantic edge connecting one document/chunk/artifact to another, such as:“depends on”“implements”“constrains”“supersedes”“migrates”“explains”“references protocol field”“defines traversal invariant”6.6 LevelA stratification marker describing the abstraction level of a knowledge item.7. Level Stratification Model8. Rationale for Level StratificationWithout level stratification, a retrieval system operating over mixed architectural and implementation material tends to collapse the distinction between:“what the protocol means,”“how the DAG is represented,”“what code needs to change this week,”“why the migration strategy was chosen.”That leads to three recurring failures:Builders get too much theoryimplementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.Architects get too much local detailsubsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.Inspectors miss normative constraintsinvariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.A level field provides a stable, queryable abstraction boundary.9. Level DefinitionsThe first version of the level system usesfour levels.Level 1 — Execution / Build Detail (L1)Concrete implementation guidance and execution-facing material.Typical content:file-level implementation tasksendpoint contractsdataclass / schema detailsmethod signaturesSQL changesacceptance criteriatest casesmigration scriptsprecise repository change instructions“do this in package X” contentPrimary consumers:BuilderConduit executorimplementation-focused coding agentsLevel 2 — Subsystem Design (L2)Subsystem mechanics and technical design for a bounded domain.Typical content:DAG node/edge semanticscompilation pipeline structuretraversal algorithm designexecution receipt structurerole-specific service boundariesstorage mappings for a specific subsystemformal state transitions inside one bounded domainPrimary consumers:Builder (secondary)ArchitectInspectorLevel 3 — Architecture / Rationale (L3)Higher-order architectural reasoning, system relationships, and design justification.Typical content:why WRP existswhy DAG compilation is separate from traversalhow Conduit, Nebula, and LOSM relatemigration philosophy and rollout strategycross-subsystem responsibilitieslong-form tradeoff analysisarchitectural invariants spanning multiple packagesPrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerInspectorLevel 4 — Meta / Doctrine / Ontology (L4)Cross-cutting design doctrine, system philosophy, and ontology-level governance.Typical content:methodology rulesrole doctrinearchitectural constitution / invariants of invariantsontology rules for work, memory, or cognitionglobal modeling principlescross-project strategic doctrinePrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerstrategic planner10. Level Assignment Rules10.1 Canonical ruleLevel belongs primarily to the content node, not to the retrieval query and not to the edge.That means:documents have levels,chunks have levels,references may optionally have level metadata, but level is not primarily an edge property.10.2 Single-primary-level ruleEvery document and every chunk must haveone primary level.This avoids ambiguous retrieval behavior and keeps filtering deterministic.10.3 Mixed documentsA long document may contain sections at different abstraction levels. Therefore:thedocumentreceives a default or dominant level;chunksmay override the document level when section content clearly belongs to a different level.Example:a WRP migration document may be primarilyL3,but its implementation checklist section may be chunked asL1.10.4 Edge neutrality ruleCross-reference edges should belevel-neutral by default.The edge describes the relationship; the source and target nodes carry the abstraction level.11. Recommended Level Mapping for the Initial WRP Corpus11.1 WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefault document level:L2Reasoning:it defines subsystem protocol semantics and normative message shape;it is not merely implementation detail;it is narrower than whole-system doctrine.Typical chunk-level overrides:formal field definitions / JSON examples / schema tables →L1rationale for protocol boundaries →L311.2 WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:compilation algorithm pseudocode →L2concrete data structures / storage tables / code mapping →L1rationale for DAG compilation as separate phase →L311.3 WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:ExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceiptstructures →L1orL2depending on specificitytraversal invariants / isolation rules →L2rationale for deterministic traversal and experimental modes →L311.4 WRP Migration PlanDefault document level:L3Reasoning:migration is a cross-cutting architectural transition strategy;the document explains sequencing, compatibility, and rollout discipline.Typical chunk-level overrides:actual migration tasks and repo changes →L1compatibility matrix / rollout constraints →L2migration philosophy and sequencing rationale →L312. Nebula Data Model ExtensionsThis section defines the required schema extensions to Nebula’s markdown-derived corpus.13. Target Nebula EntitiesThe projection model assumes the following logical entities exist or will exist:nebula_documentsnebula_chunksnebula_cross_referencesOptionally:nebula_artifactsnebula_open_questionsnebula_execution_linksThis document does not require a specific SQL dialect, but examples assume a relational store.14. Required Additions tonebula_documents14.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_documentsADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8)NOTNULLDEFAULT'L2',ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNartifact_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNartifact_versionVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNconduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNconduit_project_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNsource_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNsupersedes_document_id BIGINTNULL;14.2 Field semanticslevelPrimary abstraction level of the document.Allowed values:L1L2L3L4artifact_typeStable WRP artifact family identifier, e.g.:wrp.protocolwrp.dag_modelwrp.execution_enginewrp.migration_planartifact_keyStable logical identifier for the artifact, e.g.:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planartifact_versionHuman-visible version identifier, e.g.:1.01.11.22026-06conduit_plan_idOptional link to the Conduit execution plan primarily associated with the document.conduit_project_keyOptional grouping key for Conduit project membership.source_kindDescribes origin:markdowngenerated_specconduit_projectionimported_transcriptmanual_notestatusDocument lifecycle:draftcandidateapprovedsupersededarchivedsupersedes_document_idOptional pointer to the prior document version.15. Required Additions tonebula_chunks15.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_chunksADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNchunk_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNnormative_strengthVARCHAR(32),ADDCOLUMNsection_keyVARCHAR(255);15.2 Field semanticslevelChunk-level override. If null, inherit from the parent document.artifact_typeOptional denormalized copy of the parent artifact type for faster filtering.chunk_kindClassifies the chunk’s semantic role. Recommended values:overviewdefinitionprotocol_ruledata_modelalgorithminvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriaopen_questionexamplerationaleimplementation_notenormative_strengthOptional normative marker for validation-oriented retrieval:informativerecommendedrequiredprohibitedsection_keyStable section identity, e.g.:wrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.compilation-invariantswrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.migration.phase-2-cutover16. Required Additions tonebula_cross_references16.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_cross_referencesADDCOLUMNrelation_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'references',ADDCOLUMNsource_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNtarget_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNweightDECIMAL(8,4),ADDCOLUMNevidence_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(32)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active';16.2 Why not a singlelevelon the edge?Because the edge itself is not the primary abstraction bearer. The useful information is usually:what level the source is,what level the target is,what relation binds them.Therefore, the preferred model is to carry:source_leveltarget_levelas denormalized convenience fields rather than treating the edge as an independently stratified knowledge unit.16.3 Field semanticsrelation_typeRecommended initial relation types:referencesdepends_onimplementsconstrainsdefinescompiled_intoexecutesmigratessupersedesvalidated_byraises_questionanswers_questionsource_level,target_levelOptional denormalized values copied from the linked nodes for efficient querying.weightOptional confidence or importance score.evidence_kindHow the edge was created:explicit_markdown_linkmanual_annotationartifact_projectionsemantic_matchreceipt_backlinkstatusactivesupersededtentative17. Optional New Table:nebula_artifactsIf WRP artifacts need to be treated as first-class entities independent of document versions, add a registry table.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_artifacts (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULLUNIQUE,artifact_typeVARCHAR(128)NOTNULL,current_versionVARCHAR(64),current_document_id BIGINT,statusVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active',created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL,updated_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Purpose:stable artifact identity across multiple document revisions,single lookup point for “the current WRP traversal spec,”easier version navigation and supersession tracking.18. Optional New Table:nebula_execution_linksThis table binds Nebula knowledge to execution artifacts and receipts.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_execution_links (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULL,document_id BIGINT,chunk_id BIGINT,conduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),wrp_work_request_idVARCHAR(255),receipt_idVARCHAR(255),link_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULL,created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Recommendedlink_typevalues:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planvalidated_by_receiptsuperseded_by_planmigrated_by_requestThis table is not required for the first pass, but it becomes useful as soon as execution receipts start flowing back into Nebula.19. WRP Artifact TaxonomyEach WRP artifact projected into Nebula must declare a stable type.19.1 Initial artifact typesArtifact TypeMeaningwrp.protocolFormal WRP protocol definitionwrp.dag_modelDAG representation and compilation pipelinewrp.execution_engineTraversal / execution engine semanticswrp.migration_planWRP migration and rollout strategy19.2 Future extension typesExamples of likely future additions:Artifact TypeMeaningwrp.validation_rulesCross-artifact validation and policy ruleswrp.compatibility_matrixVersion compatibility / migration compatibilitywrp.receipt_modelFormal execution receipt modelwrp.role_contractsRole-specific work request / execution constraints20. Canonical WRP Artifact KeysThe initial corpus should use stable artifact keys.Artifact KeyArtifact TypeVersionwrp-v1-protocolwrp.protocol1.0wrp-v1_1-dagwrp.dag_model1.1wrp-v1_2-traversalwrp.execution_engine1.2wrp-migration-planwrp.migration_plan2026-06These keys should remain stable even if the underlying document path changes.21. Projection ModelThis section defines how WRP material moves from authored docs / Conduit plans into Nebula entities.22. Projection SourcesA WRP artifact may enter Nebula from one of three sources.Source A — Markdown-authored specThe preferred source. A curated markdown spec exists under the repo and is imported into Nebula.Source B — Conduit plan projectionA Conduit plan or work packet is projected into Nebula as a lightweight execution-facing document when no richer Nebula document exists yet.Source C — Manual or generated synthesisA generated or manually synthesized architecture note is imported and later normalized.The preferred order is:Markdown specGenerated synthesisConduit projection fallback23. Projection Pipeline StagesEvery WRP artifact projection follows the same high-level pipeline.Source artifact→ artifact registration→ document ingestion→ section extraction→ chunk creation→ level assignment→ cross-reference extraction→ Conduit link registration→ optional open-question extraction24. Stage 1 — Artifact RegistrationInput:artifact keyartifact typeversionsource path or source identifierOutput:canonical artifact registration recordlink to the current Nebula document versionRules:artifact keys must be stable;new versions should supersede, not overwrite, old document rows;the current version should be discoverable by artifact key.25. Stage 2 — Document IngestionThe source markdown/spec is stored as a Nebula document.Required metadata:artifact_typeartifact_keyartifact_versionsource_kindstatusdefaultlevelDocument title should remain human-readable, e.g.:WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationWRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation PipelineWRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineWRP Migration Plan26. Stage 3 — Section ExtractionSections should be extracted from headings and stable heading anchors.Recommended section key convention:<artifact family>.<major section slug>[.<subsection slug>...]Examples:wrp.protocol.overviewwrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.node-typeswrp.dag.compilation-pipelinewrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.traversal.isolation-ruleswrp.migration.phase-1-parallel-support27. Stage 4 — Chunk CreationChunks should be created with semantic sensitivity rather than purely fixed token windows.Recommended chunk boundaries:section intro / overview paragraph groupsdata model definitionsinvariant blocksalgorithm descriptionsmigration phase stepsexamplesacceptance criteria sectionsopen questions sectionsA chunk should not mix:a high-level architectural rationale paragraph,a concrete SQL alteration block,and an execution acceptance checklist.Those should become separate chunks with different levels andchunk_kindvalues.28. Stage 5 — Level AssignmentLevel assignment occurs in two passes.Pass A — Document default levelAssign the document’s dominant level based on artifact type and overall intent.Pass B — Chunk override levelOverride chunk level when a section clearly belongs to another abstraction layer.Heuristic examplesAssignL1when the chunk contains:repository pathsmethod signaturesschema alteration stepsexplicit implementation task sequencesacceptance criteria / test instructionsfield-by-field code mappingAssignL2when the chunk contains:formal subsystem structuresexecution algorithmsgraph semanticsstate transition rulesnormative subsystem invariantsAssignL3when the chunk contains:design rationalecross-subsystem tradeoffsmigration sequencing rationalearchitectural positioning of WRP relative to Conduit/Nebula/LOSMAssignL4when the chunk contains:system-wide doctrineontology-level policymeta-rules for work modeling or architectural governance29. Stage 6 — Cross-Reference ExtractionCross-references should be created from explicit and inferred signals.29.1 Explicit signalsmarkdown linkssection references“depends on”, “see also”, “constrained by”manually annotated relationships29.2 Inferred signalsartifact-key mentionssection-key referencesprotocol field names reused in traversal or migration docsrepeated formal identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt,tenant_id,trace_id29.3 Required WRP reference classesThe first pass must at least support:protocol field ↔ DAG compilation ruleDAG node/edge semantics ↔ traversal behaviortraversal invariant ↔ migration constraintmigration step ↔ affected WRP artifactWRP artifact ↔ Conduit plan implementing it30. Stage 7 — Conduit Link RegistrationEach projected WRP artifact should retain a link to the Conduit execution packet(s) responsible for implementation.Minimum metadata to retain:conduit_plan_idconduit_project_keyoptional receipt trail / execution link rowIf one Nebula artifact maps to multiple Conduit plans, use:document-level link to the primary umbrella planexecution-link rows for subordinate plans31. Stage 8 — Open Question ExtractionIf a WRP document contains unresolved design questions, they should be extracted into either:dedicatedopen_questionchunks, ora separatenebula_open_questionstable.Recommended fields for open questions:artifact_keydocument_idchunk_idquestion_textstatuspriorityowner_roleThis is especially relevant for migration uncertainties, protocol compatibility questions, and unresolved traversal policy decisions.32. Conduit → Nebula Projection RulesThis section defines how Conduit work packets map into Nebula when a WRP artifact is tracked for implementation.33. Conduit as Execution Metadata, Not Architectural AuthorityA Conduit plan is not automatically a Nebula document. Conduit should only project enough information into Nebula to preserve execution traceability.That means:Conduit ownsactive execution plan rowsacceptance criteriafile listsdependenciesexecution receiptsNebula ownsthe meaning of the WRP artifactthe long-form architecturecross-artifact relationshipsrationalechunk-level retrievability34. Minimal Projection of a Conduit Plan into NebulaFor each Conduit WRP work packet, Nebula should store:conduit_plan_idartifact_keyartifact_typestatusa short execution summarylinks to the authoritative WRP spec documentlinks to receipt or migration status if availableThis can be represented either:as metadata on the authoritative WRP document, oras a small auxiliary Nebula document ofsource_kind = conduit_projection.The first option is preferred for the initial implementation.35. Example Projection of the Initial WRP PacketSuppose Conduit contains four plans:CDT-WRP-001— WRP v1.0 protocol formalizationCDT-WRP-002— WRP v1.1 DAG model and compilation pipelineCDT-WRP-003— WRP v1.2 traversal engineCDT-WRP-004— WRP migration planNebula should contain at least:Document Atitle:WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalizationartifact key:wrp-v1-protocolartifact type:wrp.protocollevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-001Document Btitle:WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation Pipelineartifact key:wrp-v1_1-dagartifact type:wrp.dag_modellevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-002Document Ctitle:WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal Engineartifact key:wrp-v1_2-traversalartifact type:wrp.execution_enginelevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-003Document Dtitle:WRP Migration Planartifact key:wrp-migration-planartifact type:wrp.migration_planlevel:L3conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-004And explicit cross-references such as:wrp-v1_1-dagdepends_onwrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_2-traversalexecuteswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1-protocolwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_2-traversal36. Required WRP Cross-Reference PatternsThe first implementation should explicitly emit the following relation families.36.1 Protocol → DAGExamples:protocol field or lifecycle state constrains DAG node constructionprotocol dependency semantics compiled into edge semanticsRelations:definesconstrainscompiled_into36.2 DAG → TraversalExamples:DAG node kinds determine traversal behaviorDAG execution order constraints are enforced by traversal rulesRelations:definesexecutesconstrains36.3 Traversal → Receipt / ValidationExamples:execution cursor produces execution receipt shapetraversal invariants determine receipt hierarchy or failure semanticsRelations:definesvalidated_by36.4 Migration → All WRP ArtifactsExamples:migration phases refer to protocol changes, DAG compatibility, traversal rolloutRelations:migratessupersedesconstrains36.5 WRP Artifact → Conduit PlanExamples:a Nebula artifact is being implemented by one or more Conduit plansRelations:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planThese may live innebula_execution_linksrather than the main cross-reference table if the execution linkage is operational rather than semantic.37. Role-Based Retrieval PolicyThis is the operational reason for level stratification.38. Builder Retrieval Profile38.1 GoalProvide concrete implementation guidance with only enough architectural context to avoid coding blind.38.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L1Secondary levels:L2ExcludeL3/L4unless:the retrievedL1/L2chunk explicitly references an architectural invariant, orthe prompt requests rationale or migration context38.3 Preferred chunk kindsimplementation_notedata_modelprotocol_rulealgorithmacceptance_criteriamigration_step38.4 Typical use casesimplement WRP protocol DTOsbuild DAG compiler classesadd traversal engine structureswrite migration scripts and tests39. Architect Retrieval Profile39.1 GoalProvide subsystem design and cross-artifact reasoning without drowning in file-level implementation noise.39.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3Optional expansion toL1for concrete examplesOptional expansion toL4for doctrine or ontology alignment39.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewdefinitiondata_modelalgorithminvariantrationaleopen_question39.4 Typical use casesrefine WRP semanticsunderstand why traversal is separated from DAG compilationreason about Conduit/Nebula/LOSM alignmentevaluate migration sequence40. Inspector / Validator Retrieval Profile40.1 GoalRetrieve normative constraints, invariants, and compatibility conditions.40.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3IncludeL1only when validation depends on concrete schema or implementation details40.3 Preferred chunk kindsprotocol_ruleinvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriadata_model40.4 Normative preferencePrefer chunks where:normative_strength = requirednormative_strength = prohibited40.5 Typical use casesverify WRP compatibility rulesvalidate migration sequencingenforce traversal invariantsdetect protocol / DAG / traversal mismatch41. Explorer Retrieval Profile41.1 GoalSupport open-ended investigation across architecture, rationale, and unresolved questions.41.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3,L4IncludeL1only if the search narrows to implementation mechanics41.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewrationaleopen_questiondefinitionexample42. Suggested Retrieval AlgorithmA role-aware retrieval query should combine:artifact filteringe.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')level filteringrole-dependent level setchunk kind weightingrole-specific preferred chunk kindsnormative weightingfor validator/inspector profilescross-reference expansionbounded traversal across explicit edgesexecution recency boostoptional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in ConduitPseudo-policy:candidate_chunks =filter by artifact family / lexical relevance / embedding relevance∩ filter by allowed levels for roleweighted by chunk_kind preferenceweighted by normative_strength where applicableexpanded by explicit cross-reference traversal depth <= NRecommended initial traversal depths:Builder:N = 1Architect:N = 2Inspector:N = 2Explorer:N = 343. Worked Example: Retrieval for WRP Traversal ImplementationUser intent:“Implement the traversal engine for WRP v1.2.”Builder profile should retrieve:WRP v1.2chunks describingExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceipttraversal order semanticsdeterministic traversal defaultisolation rule chunksmigration notes only if they affect implementation compatibilityArchitect profile should additionally retrieve:the WRP DAG document sections that define node and edge semanticsrationale for why traversal is a separate stagemigration constraints affecting rolloutInspector profile should emphasize:invariant chunks such as tenant isolation rulesfailure semanticsreceipt completeness rulescompatibility constraints in the migration plan44. Worked Example: WRP v1.2 Chunking and Level AssignmentConsider a traversal-engine document with these sections:OverviewExecutionContextExecutionCursorTraversal order and pending queue semanticsTenant isolationExperimental policy modeWhy traversal is separate from DAG compilationImplementation checklistRecommended chunking:SectionChunk KindLevelOverviewoverviewL2ExecutionContextdata_modelL2ExecutionCursordata_modelL2Traversal order and pending queue semanticsalgorithmL2Tenant isolationinvariantL2Experimental policy modedefinition/invariantL2Why traversal is separate from DAG compilationrationaleL3Implementation checklistimplementation_note/acceptance_criteriaL145. WRP-Specific Normative MarkingTo make validation retrieval effective, WRP chunks should mark normative strength where appropriate.Examples:requiredtraversal must enforce tenant isolation at execution timeprotocol version must be present in every WRP root requestDAG compilation must reject cycles if the WRP graph is defined as acyclicprohibitedtraversal must not execute a node under the wrong tenant contextmigration must not remove legacy compatibility before the designated cutover phaserecommendedbuilders should prefer deterministic traversal order unless explicitly in experimental modeinformativehistorical rationale and examples46. Back-Projection from Execution into NebulaOnce Conduit and runtime begin executing WRP work, Nebula should be updated with execution traceability.Examples:a Conduit plan completes implementation ofwrp-v1_2-traversalan execution receipt validates a traversal invarianta migration work request supersedes an older compatibility ruleThese should produce:document status updates,execution links,optional new cross-references,optional “implementation evidence” annotations.This should be append-only where possible; do not rewrite architectural history.47. Initial Migration Plan for the Existing WRP PacketThis section defines the first practical rollout for the four WRP artifacts already placed into Conduit.48. Phase 1 — Register the Four WRP ArtifactsCreate Nebula artifact/document records for:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planAt minimum, store:titleartifact typeartifact keyversiondefault levelconduit plan idsource kindstatus49. Phase 2 — Import the Authoritative WRP Markdown DocumentsFor each artifact, import the corresponding markdown spec into Nebula.If a markdown spec does not yet exist in repo form, use a temporary generated or manually curated document, but treat that as a stopgap. The target steady state is:WRP architectural material lives as markdown/spec documents in Nebula, not only as Conduit plan descriptions.50. Phase 3 — Chunk and Level the DocumentsRun the markdown importer with:section extractionsemantic chunkingchunk kind assignmentchunk-level level override assignmentnormative strength tagging for invariant sectionsDo not leave WRP material as giant undifferentiated chunks.51. Phase 4 — Emit Required Cross ReferencesAt minimum, emit:protocol → DAG edgesDAG → traversal edgesmigration → protocol/DAG/traversal edgesWRP artifact → Conduit plan links52. Phase 5 — Add Role-Aware Retrieval FiltersAdd query support for:allowed levelspreferred chunk kindsoptional normative strength weightingbounded cross-reference expansionThis is the point where “Builder sees implementation detail; Architect sees architecture” becomes real.53. Phase 6 — Backfill Execution LinksOnce Conduit begins implementing the packet, attach:plan IDsreceipt trailsstatus updatesimplementation evidence linksto the corresponding WRP artifacts in Nebula.54. InvariantsThe following invariants apply to the Conduit → Nebula WRP projection model.I1. Nebula is the authoritative long-form memory for WRPConduit may track execution, but architectural WRP meaning must remain represented in Nebula.I2. Every WRP artifact must have a stable artifact keyPaths may change; artifact identity must not.I3. Every Nebula document and chunk must have a deterministic effective levelA chunk either declares a level or inherits from its document.I4. Cross-reference edges are level-neutral by defaultThe source and target nodes carry the abstraction semantics.I5. The initial WRP packet must be explicitly cross-linkedProtocol, DAG, traversal, and migration documents must not exist as isolated documents.I6. Role-aware retrieval must filter by level before broad cross-reference expansionOtherwise the stratification model loses value.I7. Execution traceability must be additive, not destructiveImplementation evidence and receipts should enrich architectural records rather than overwrite them.58. What This Unlocks NextOnce this projection and stratification layer exists, the system can do all of the following coherently:Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.59. Bottom LineThe four WRP plans now sitting in Conduit should be treated as theexecution packetfor a broader WRP knowledge corpus. The missing piece is a projection layer that makes those artifacts durable and queryable inside Nebula.The core model is simple:Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledgeConduit stores the executable work packetWRP artifacts provide the stable identity between themlevelstratification controls who sees whatcross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graphThat is the foundation required before WRP can function as a real architectural substrate rather than just a set of implementation plans.---## What I’d do immediately after this oneSince those four WRP plans are now in Conduit and will take a bit to implement under your local Ollama/OpenCode/Qwen setup, the next companion spec I’d write is the **actual Nebula schema/ontology patch** for this document, not another prose architecture note.Specifically:# `schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonld`That doc should formalize, in machine-oriented ontology form:- `KnowledgeLevel`- `ArtifactType`- `ChunkKind`- `NormativeStrength`- `CrossReferenceRelationType`- `NebulaDocument`- `NebulaChunk`- `NebulaArtifact`- `NebulaExecutionLink`and the exact fields/relationships implied by the markdown spec above.If you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it **repo-ready JSON-LD** rather than another markdown doc.SourcesHelpjuice, Inc.SponsoredCompany Knowledge, Now Searchable by AIHelpjuice gives teams an AI-powered knowledge base built from their real documentation.You said:go onChatGPT said:Thought for 5sAbsolutely — the right next artifact is themachine-oriented ontology/schema companionfor the markdown spec we just pinned down.Given your own framing from earlier, I’m going to keep the JSON-LD side as theexternal graph/persistence targetfor Nebula/PEB rather than treating it like the authored source of truth. Purposethis JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links2. Canonical interpretation rulesNebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisionsNebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form contentNebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a documentNebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edgeNebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts3. Level rulesdocuments have default levelschunks may override levelscross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections4. WRP artifact registry obligationsartifact keys are stabledocument revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in placecurrentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision5. Retrieval implicationsBuilder → L1 + selective L2Architect → L2/L3Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunksExplorer → L2/L3/L4A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into
