Here’s the next piece as arepo-ready implementation specfor turning the WRP docs you just put into Conduit into structured Nebula artifacts, chunks, and cross-references.docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdMarkdown# WRP Document Projection Rules**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula / WRP integration**Purpose:** Define deterministic rules for projecting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, levels, and cross-references.---# 1. ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning13.2 Chunk IDsFormat:<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning/chunk/01Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.13.3 Re-import stabilityOn re-import:if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stableif a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new idsif a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported14. Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. Future ExtensionsThe following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)embedding generation and vector indexingrole-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itselfsupersession lineage across chunk revisionsbidirectional Conduit synchronizationLLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristicsconfidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments20. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is enough to start building the importer, but there are **two companion artifacts** that would make implementation much safer:## 1. `schemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`A proper ontology file for:- Here’s the next companion doc as the operational layer for the review-state schema.docs/nebula/review-workflow.mdMarkdown# Nebula Review Workflow**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula governance / corpus maintenance**Purpose:** Define how review state is assigned, updated, interpreted, and used to prioritize attention across Nebula artifacts, sections, and chunks.---# 1. PurposeNebula stores a growing corpus of architecture notes, specifications, migration plans, ontology documents, implementation plans, and execution-adjacent material. Not all corpus material is equally current, equally trustworthy, or equally relevant to active work.This document defines a **review workflow overlay** that allows Nebula users and roles to mark corpus material as:- needing review- under active review- reviewed- current focus- outdated- questioned- supersededThe review workflow exists to answer a different question than lifecycle status.## Lifecycle status answers:- Is this artifact active, draft, deprecated, or superseded in the corpus?## Review status answers:- What should we pay attention to right now?- What should be trusted by default?- What needs inspection before it influences implementation?- What should be deprioritized or excluded from normal retrieval?Review state is therefore a **triage and trust overlay** on top of the corpus, not a replacement for artifact lifecycle semantics.---# 2. Core Principles## 2.1 Review state is separate from artifact lifecycleAn item may be:- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`- `status = SUPERSEDED` and `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- `status = DRAFT` and `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Lifecycle describes what the artifact **is**.Review state describes what the team should **do about it**.## 2.2 Review state is primarily an attention and trust signalReview state is used to:- focus corpus maintenance- guide retrieval ranking- reduce accidental reliance on stale documents- identify blocking or suspect specs- surface active areas of architecture work## 2.3 Artifact-level review is the default starting pointNebula SHOULD support review state at:- artifact level- section level- chunk levelHowever, the initial operational workflow assumes:- **artifact-level review is primary**- section/chunk review is optional and targetedThe system MUST NOT require chunk-by-chunk review to be useful.## 2.4 Review state is allowed to be provisionalReview state is not a certification regime. It is acceptable to mark an item:- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`without yet knowing the final replacement or fix. The goal is to make uncertainty visible and actionable.---# 3. Review Scope LevelsNebula review annotations may apply at three scopes.## 3.1 Artifact scopeApplies to an entire document / artifact such as:- `wrp-v1-protocol`- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `wrp-v1_2-traversal`- `wrp-migration-plan`Artifact scope is the default and most common review target.## 3.2 Section scopeApplies to a specific section within an artifact when the document is mixed-quality.Example:- the WRP protocol document is generally current- but the `Execution Semantics / Receipts` section is outdatedSection review SHOULD be used when:- only one part of a large artifact is stale or questionable- the artifact should remain broadly retrievable without blanket demotion## 3.3 Chunk scopeApplies to a specific chunk when review needs to be precise.Chunk review SHOULD be used sparingly and mainly when:- a particular invariant is suspect- a specific migration step is obsolete- a specific rationale chunk remains valuable even inside an outdated section---# 4. Review Status VocabularyThe following review statuses are defined by `schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`.## 4.1 `UNREVIEWED`The item has not yet been reviewed for current validity or relevance.Use when:- a document was imported but not yet triaged- a new chunk has not been evaluated## 4.2 `NEEDS_REVIEW`The item should be reviewed soon because it may be stale, incomplete, or important to current work.Use when:- the document is likely relevant to current implementation- the document predates a major architectural shift- the document appears important but confidence is low## 4.3 `UNDER_REVIEW`The item is actively being reviewed, rewritten, or reconciled.Use when:- you are actively comparing it against current architecture or code- Builder/Architect/Inspector are working through it now## 4.4 `REVIEWED`The item has been reviewed and is believed to be usable in normal work.Use when:- the document is current enough for default retrieval- known issues are minor or already called out## 4.5 `CURRENT_FOCUS`The item is a current focus of architecture or implementation attention and should be surfaced prominently.Use when:- active work depends on this item now- the item is central to the current execution stream- the item is the present working center of a subsystem redesign## 4.6 `OUTDATED`The item is known to be out of date relative to the current architecture, runtime, or workflow.Use when:- the document predates a material redesign- its prescriptions are no longer safe defaults- it still has historical value but should be demoted## 4.7 `QUESTIONED`The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt.Use when:- parts of the document conflict with newer understanding- the model may be wrong, not merely old- the document should be examined before it is trusted## 4.8 `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval.Use when:- there is a clear replacement artifact or replacement chunk set- the supersession is intentional and not merely suspected---# 5. Review PriorityReview priority answers: **how urgently should this item be revisited?**Allowed values:- `CRITICAL`- `HIGH`- `MEDIUM`- `LOW`## 5.1 Priority guidance### `CRITICAL`Use when:- the item is blocking implementation- the item is actively misleading current work- the item governs current execution and is likely wrong or stale### `HIGH`Use when:- the item is central to near-term architecture or implementation- review delay would materially slow work or degrade decisions### `MEDIUM`Use when:- the item matters, but not immediately- it should be triaged in the near future### `LOW`Use when:- review is backlog hygiene- the item is historical or peripheral---# 6. Attention ReasonsAttention reasons explain **why** an item needs review or focus.The first review-state schema defines these reasons:- `BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIME`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE`- `CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODEL`- `REQUIRES_MIGRATION`- `DUPLICATED_ELSEWHERE`- `NEEDS_LEVEL_REVIEW`- `NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`Multiple reasons MAY be attached to the same item.## ExampleA migration document might be:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `reviewPriority = HIGH`- `attentionReason = [REQUIRES_MIGRATION, OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE]`---# 7. Who May Set Review State## 7.1 Human authority is primaryThe human operator is the authoritative source of review state.In practice, this means you may set review state manually based on reading, comparison, or implementation experience.## 7.2 Roles may propose review state, but not silently finalize itThe following roles may recommend review changes:- **Inspector**- flags contradictions, stale invariants, missing migration updates, or retrieval hazards- **Architect**- flags architectural obsolescence, boundary drift, or rationale conflicts- **Builder**- flags implementation-blocking ambiguity or mismatch with actual code- **Explorer**- flags duplicate or related documents that may need consolidationThese role recommendations SHOULD be recorded as annotations or proposals, but SHOULD NOT silently overwrite the effective review state unless explicitly authorized.## 7.3 Importers may initialize, not decideImporters and projectors MAY set initial values such as:- `UNREVIEWED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW` when the source predates a known migration boundary- `OUTDATED` when explicit source metadata says soHowever, importers SHOULD NOT autonomously mark an item `REVIEWED` or `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`.---# 8. Effective Review State ModelNebula may store multiple review annotations over time. The system therefore needs a rule for determining the **effective review state** used in retrieval and dashboards.## 8.1 Effective review state per scopeEach reviewable object (artifact, section, chunk) SHOULD expose a single **effective review state** for operational use.This effective state may be materialized directly on the object row or computed from annotations.## 8.2 Default precedence ruleIf multiple annotations exist for the same object, the effective review state SHOULD be determined by:1. most recent human-authored authoritative annotation2. otherwise most recent approved role recommendation3. otherwise importer-initialized default4. otherwise `UNREVIEWED`## 8.3 Status severity tie-breakIf multiple candidate annotations are equally authoritative and recent enough to conflict, use the following severity ordering to avoid false optimism:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `UNDER_REVIEW`- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `UNREVIEWED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`This severity ordering is for tie-breaking only and MUST NOT be interpreted as a universal ranking of importance.## 8.4 Why `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is not treated as “most severe”Superseded material is often safe to ignore rather than urgent to fix. It is not necessarily a live problem. Therefore it should not outrank `QUESTIONED` or `CURRENT_FOCUS` in attention logic.---# 9. Artifact / Section / Chunk Rollup RulesReview state may exist at multiple scopes simultaneously. The workflow needs rules for how lower-level review state influences higher-level summaries.## 9.1 Artifact effective review is primaryArtifact review status is the main corpus-level triage signal and SHOULD be set explicitly rather than inferred whenever possible.## 9.2 Section and chunk review do not automatically overwrite artifact reviewIf an artifact is marked `REVIEWED` but one chunk is marked `QUESTIONED`, the artifact does not automatically become `QUESTIONED`.Instead, the artifact SHOULD receive one or more rollup indicators such as:- `needsAttention = true`- `attentionReason += NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`- optional `focusScore` boost- optional “contains questioned chunk” derived flag## 9.3 Optional artifact rollup policyImplementations MAY define a rollup threshold such as:- if ≥ 30% of chunks are `OUTDATED` or `QUESTIONED`, artifact effective review becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`- if any chunk is `CURRENT_FOCUS`, artifact `focusScore` is boosted- if all chunks are `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`, artifact may be proposed as `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`But this rollup SHOULD be advisory until chunk review is common enough to trust statistically.---# 10. Review ActionsThe review workflow recognizes the following actions.## 10.1 Mark Needs ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- optionally priority and attention reasonsUse when an item should enter the review queue.## 10.2 Start ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Use when active review or rewrite has begun.## 10.3 Mark ReviewedSet:- `reviewStatus = REVIEWED`- `lastReviewedAt`- optional summaryUse when the item is current enough for normal use.## 10.4 Mark Current FocusSet:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`Use when the item is a live center of implementation or architecture work.## 10.5 Mark OutdatedSet:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`Use when the item is no longer a safe default but may still be historically useful.## 10.6 Mark QuestionedSet:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`Use when the item may be wrong, not merely old.## 10.7 Confirm SupersededSet:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- set `supersededBy` if knownUse when a replacement is clear and the old material should be demoted from normal retrieval.---# 11. Relationship Between Supersession and ReviewSupersession and review are related but distinct.## 11.1 Supersession is a semantic relationshipExample:- `wrp-v1-protocol-v0` is superseded by `wrp-v1-protocol`This is modeled as:- `supersededBy`- `supersedes`- lifecycle `status`## 11.2 Review supersession is an operational confirmationAn item becomes `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when the team has decided it should be treated as superseded for retrieval and attention purposes.## 11.3 Auto-promotion ruleIf `supersededBy` is set, the system MAY propose:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`but SHOULD NOT automatically finalize it unless configured to do so.Reason:- some superseded artifacts still matter during a migration period- some artifacts are partially superseded but still operationally relevant---# 12. Review Workflow for Corpus TriageThis section defines the simple human workflow the system is meant to support.## 12.1 Initial triage passAs you review the corpus, each artifact SHOULD be assigned one of:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`with optional:- priority- attention reasons- short review summaryThe goal is not perfection. The goal is to make the corpus sortable and navigable.## 12.2 Triage heuristics### Mark `CURRENT_FOCUS` when:- active implementation or redesign is centered on the artifact now### Mark `NEEDS_REVIEW` when:- the artifact is probably important but confidence is not high enough- the artifact predates a major design change- the artifact is about to become implementation-relevant again### Mark `REVIEWED` when:- the artifact is current enough to be used normally### Mark `OUTDATED` when:- the artifact still has historical value but should not be trusted as a default guide### Mark `QUESTIONED` when:- the artifact may encode wrong assumptions or contradictions### Mark `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when:- a replacement exists and default retrieval should normally prefer the replacement---# 13. Retrieval EffectsReview state MUST influence Nebula retrieval.## 13.1 Default retrieval behaviorUnless explicitly overridden:- `CURRENT_FOCUS` receives a strong ranking boost- `REVIEWED` receives a positive ranking boost- `NEEDS_REVIEW` remains retrievable but slightly demoted relative to reviewed/current material- `OUTDATED` is demoted- `QUESTIONED` is demoted for Builder/Architect defaults but may be boosted for Inspector- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is excluded or strongly demoted from default retrieval## 13.2 Role-specific review-state behavior### BuilderPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Demote:- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`Exclude by default:- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`### ArchitectPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Allow:- `QUESTIONED`- selected `OUTDATED` material when rationale still matters### InspectorPrefer:- `QUESTIONED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `OUTDATED`because those often indicate the places where validation and contradiction analysis are most needed.### ExplorerAllow broad inclusion, including:- `OUTDATED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`when historical lineage or unresolved questions matter.---# 14. Dashboard / Queue BehaviorNebula SHOULD support a review queue over artifacts.## 14.1 Default review queueThe default review queue SHOULD show artifacts where:- `reviewStatus IN (NEEDS_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW, CURRENT_FOCUS, OUTDATED, QUESTIONED)`- OR `needsAttention = true`ordered by:1. `reviewPriority`2. `focusScore`3. `updatedAt` or `lastReviewedAt`## 14.2 Suggested dashboard slicesUseful corpus views include:### Current FocusArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`### Needs ReviewArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`### Questioned / RiskyArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`### Outdated but not yet supersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`### SupersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`---# 15. Recommended Initial SQL ShapeFor the first operational implementation, Nebula SHOULD materialize current effective review state directly on `nebula_artifact`.Recommended columns:- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `needs_attention`- `last_reviewed_at`- `review_summary`- `focus_score`Optional on `nebula_chunk`:- same fields, nullableReview history SHOULD be stored separately in `nebula_review_annotation` with fields such as:- `id`- `target_type`- `target_id`- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `attention_reason_json`- `needs_attention`- `reviewed_by`- `review_summary`- `created_at`---# 16. Example Review Annotations## 16.1 Current focus artifact```json{"id": "review:annotation/wrp-v1_2-traversal/2026-06-21","type": "ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo": "wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal","reviewStatus": "review:CURRENT_FOCUS","reviewPriority": "review:CRITICAL","attentionReason": ["review:BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION"],"needsAttention": true,"lastReviewedAt": "2026-06-21T13:00:00Z","reviewedBy": "role:architect","reviewSummary": "Traversal engine spec is the current implementation center and should remain top-ranked for Builder and Architect retrieval."}16.2 Outdated migration sectionJSON{"id":"review:annotation/wrp-migration-plan/execution-cutover/2026-06-21","type":"ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo":"wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan/section/execution-cutover","reviewStatus":"review:OUTDATED","reviewPriority":"review:HIGH","attentionReason": ["review:OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE","review:REQUIRES_MIGRATION"],"needsAttention":true,"lastReviewedAt":"2026-06-21T13:10:00Z","reviewedBy":"role:inspector","reviewSummary":"This section predates the traversal split and should not be used as the default guide for execution cutover."}17. SummaryNebula review workflow exists to turn the corpus into a manageable attention system rather than a passive archive.The governing rule is:Lifecycle status tells us what an artifact is; review state tells us whether we should trust it, revisit it, focus on it, or route around it right now.The initial operational model is intentionally simple:review at artifact scope firstmark items as current focus / needs review / reviewed / outdated / questioned / supersededrecord priority and attention reasonlet retrieval and dashboards honor that stateonly descend to section/chunk review when precision is worth the effort---# Where we are nowWe’ve now inserted the review-governance pair:1. **`schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`**2. **`docs/nebula/review-workflow.md`**So we can go back This is the piece that turns everything you’ve built so far into something executable instead of just well-structured theory.This is youractual compiler spec.docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdMarkdown# WRP → Nebula Projection Pseudocode**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula ingestion / WRP compiler**Purpose:** Define deterministic algorithm for converting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, review overlays, and cross-reference graphs.---# 1. OverviewThis document specifies the **projection compiler pipeline** that transforms WRP markdown documents into structured Nebula graph data.Input:- WRP markdown documentsOutput:- NebulaArtifacts- NebulaSections- NebulaChunks- NebulaCrossReferences- Review overlays (optional but supported)- Conduit links (if present)The pipeline is deterministic, idempotent, and replay-safe.---# 2. High-Level Pipelineparse_markdown()→ build_ast()→ resolve_artifact()→ build_section_tree()→ segment_chunks()→ classify_chunks()→ assign_levels()→ assign_review_overlay()→ extract_cross_references()→ emit_graph()→ upsert_store()---# 3. Core Data Structures (Logical)## ArtifactArtifact {idkeysource_pathstatus}## SectionSection {idartifact_idparent_section_idheadingordinal}## ChunkChunk {idsection_idordinaltextchunk_kindlevelnormative_strength}## ReviewOverlay (optional)ReviewOverlay {target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason[]}## CrossReferenceCrossReference {source_idtarget_idrelation_type}---# 4. Step 1 — Parse Markdown```pseudofunction parse_markdown(source_text):ast = MarkdownParser.parse(source_text)return astRules:preserve heading hierarchypreserve code blocks as atomic nodespreserve tables as atomic nodespreserve block quotes as semantic units5. Step 2 — Artifact Resolutionpseudofunction resolve_artifact(file_path, registry):if registry.contains(file_path):return registry.get(file_path)if STRICT_MODE:throw Error("Unknown artifact in strict mode")return create_artifact_from_path(file_path)Artifact key mapping:derived from filenamenormalized slug6. Step 3 — Build Section Treepseudofunction build_section_tree(ast):root = new SectionTree()current_stack = []for node in ast:if node.type == HEADING:level = node.levelwhile current_stack.top.level >= level:current_stack.pop()section = new Section(heading=node.text,parent=current_stack.top)current_stack.push(section)root.add(section)return rootRules:##→ Section###→ child section####+→ either nested section or flatten depending on config7. Step 4 — Chunk Segmentationpseudofunction segment_chunks(section):chunks = []buffer = []for block in section.blocks:if is_boundary(block, buffer):chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))buffer = []buffer.append(block)if buffer not empty:chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))return chunks7.1 Boundary rulespseudofunction is_boundary(block, buffer):if buffer.empty:return falseif block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:return trueif block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:return trueif semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):return trueif buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:return truereturn false7.2 Semantic shift heuristicpseudofunction semantic_shift(a, b):if a.kind != b.kind:return trueif switches_between("RATIONALE","IMPLEMENTATION","PROTOCOL_RULE"):return truereturn false8. Step 5 — Chunk Classificationpseudofunction classify_chunk(chunk):text = chunk.textif contains("must not", text):chunk.normative = PROHIBITEDelse if contains("must", text):chunk.normative = REQUIREDelse if contains("should", text):chunk.normative = RECOMMENDEDelse:chunk.normative = INFORMATIVEchunk.kind = classify_kind(text)return chunk8.1 Chunk kind classifierpseudofunction classify_kind(text):if matches_definition_pattern(text):return DEFINITIONif contains_protocol_keywords(text):return PROTOCOL_RULEif contains_invariant_keywords(text):return INVARIANTif contains_algorithm_structure(text):return ALGORITHMif contains_schema_fields(text):return DATA_MODELif contains_migration_language(text):return MIGRATION_STEPif contains_open_question_markers(text):return OPEN_QUESTIONif contains_rationale_markers(text):return RATIONALEif contains_example_markers(text):return EXAMPLEreturn OVERVIEW9. Step 6 — Level Assignmentpseudofunction assign_level(chunk):if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:return L1if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:return L2if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:return L3return L210. Step 7 — Review Overlay Assignmentpseudofunction assign_review_overlay(entity, context):overlay = new ReviewOverlay()if entity.is_new:overlay.status = UNREVIEWEDif contains_staleness_signals(entity):overlay.status = NEEDS_REVIEWif matches_current_focus_tags(entity):overlay.status = CURRENT_FOCUSif contains_conflict_signals(entity):overlay.status = QUESTIONEDif superseded_by_exists(entity):overlay.status = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDreturn overlay11. Step 8 — Cross Reference Extractionpseudofunction extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):refs = []for token in chunk.text:if token matches artifact_key:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=artifact_id(token),type=DEPENDS_ON))if token matches section_heading:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=section_id(token),type=REFERENCES))if token matches known_concept:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=concept_id(token),type=MENTIONS))return refs12. Step 9 — Emit Graphpseudofunction emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):graph = NebulaGraph()graph.add(artifact)for section in sections:graph.add(section)for chunk in chunks:graph.add(chunk)for ref in refs:graph.add(ref)return graph13. Step 10 — Upsert Store (Idempotent)pseudofunction upsert_store(graph, db):for node in graph.nodes:db.upsert(node.id, node)for edge in graph.edges:db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)Rules:idempotent writesstable IDs requiredno duplicate edges unless explicitly allowedpreserve existing review annotations unless overridden14. Determinism RulesProjection MUST be deterministic:same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunksno LLM-based randomness in core pipelineonly heuristic classification allowedno sampling variabilityIf classifier improves:version bump requirednew projection run produces new revision lineage15. Failure Modes15.1 Unknown artifact→ fail in STRICT_MODE15.2 ambiguous chunk boundaries→ prefer splitting over merging15.3 classification uncertainty→ default to OVERVIEW + INFORMATIVE15.4 missing references→ ignore silently (do not fail pipeline)16. Minimal Implementation ContractA valid implementation MUST:parse markdown into structured ASTbuild deterministic section treesegment chunks deterministicallyclassify chunks without external LLM dependency (LLM optional later)assign level + kind to every chunkemit graph with stable IDssupport idempotent re-import17. SummaryThis pipeline defines Nebula’s core transformation:Markdown → structured semantic graphThe important shift is:documents are not storedsemantic nodes are storedEverything else (review, retrieval, roles, Conduit integration) operates on top of this graph, not the raw text.---# What you now have (important moment)You now have a complete **minimal compiler stack**:### 1. Review system (attention layer)- `nebula-review-state.jsonld`- `review-workflow.md`### 2. Semantic classification system- `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`### 3. Execution pipeline- `wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`---# What this unlocks nextAt this point, Nebula is structurally capable of:- ingesting your WRP corpus- chunking it deterministically- classifying semantics- tracking review state- building a queryable graph- feeding Conduit execution planning---# The next natural step (if you want to continue)There are two obvious upgrades:### A. Retrieval layer specHow Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer actually query this graph### B. This is where Nebula stops being “structured storage” and becomes an actualquery-driven cognitive system.We’re going to define how rolesthink over the graph.docs/nebula/retrieval-role-scoring-model.mdMarkdown# Nebula Retrieval & Role Scoring Model**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula query engine / cognitive runtime layer**Purpose:** Define how Nebula retrieves, ranks, and filters graph content based on role context, chunk semantics, review state, and task intent.---# 1. OverviewNebula does not retrieve documents.It retrieves a **ranked subgraph of semantic chunks**.Every query is evaluated through:- role profile (Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer / Conduit)- chunk kind (semantic intent)- level (L1–L4 abstraction)- review state (trust + attention overlay)- cross-reference density (graph connectivity)- task intent (implicit or explicit)The output is a **scored ranked set of chunks + their local graph neighborhood**.---# 2. Core Retrieval ObjectA retrieval result is not a document.It is:RetrievalResult {chunkscoreexplanationneighborhood[]}Neighborhood includes:- parent section- sibling chunks- referenced chunks- optionally upstream/downstream traversal nodes---# 3. Retrieval Pipelinequery→ intent_classification→ role_profile_resolution→ candidate_chunk_selection→ scoring→ graph_expansion→ reranking→ filtering→ return---# 4. Role ProfilesEach role defines **what “relevant” means**.---## 4.1 BuilderBuilder optimizes for implementation correctness.### Preferences:- L1 chunks strongly preferred- ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE- MIGRATION_STEP when executing transitions- REVIEWED and CURRENT_FOCUS### Demotions:- RATIONALE (unless directly tied to implementation)- OUTDATED- QUESTIONED### Boost factors:- normative chunks (REQUIRED > RECOMMENDED)- high retrievalBias chunks---## 4.2 ArchitectArchitect optimizes for system correctness and structure.### Preferences:- L2 chunks- PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DATA_MODEL- RATIONALE (strongly valued)- OPEN_QUESTION (for unresolved design space)### Demotions:- overly implementation-specific L1 noise- trivial EXAMPLE chunks---## 4.3 InspectorInspector optimizes for contradiction detection and system validation.### Preferences:- QUESTIONED- INVARIANT- OUTDATED- OPEN_QUESTION- cross-reference-heavy chunks### Behavior:- actively surfaces inconsistencies- boosts conflicting review states- prioritizes low-confidence or high-risk nodes---## 4.4 ExplorerExplorer optimizes for understanding and knowledge traversal.### Preferences:- OVERVIEW- RATIONALE- EXAMPLE- high connectivity chunks### Behavior:- expands neighborhoods aggressively- favors graph traversal depth over strict relevance- includes historical/superseded context when useful---## 4.5 Conduit (Execution Role)Conduit optimizes for executable transformation.### Preferences:- MIGRATION_STEP- ALGORITHM- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA- PROTOCOL_RULE- L1 chunks only### Behavior:- strips non-normative noise- prioritizes determinism- prefers minimal required graph for execution---# 5. Chunk Scoring FunctionEvery chunk receives a score:score =role_weightkind_weightlevel_weightreview_weightgraph_weightfreshness_weight---## 5.1 Role weightDefined per role profile preferences.Example:- Builder: +2 for L1- Architect: +2 for L2- Inspector: +3 for QUESTIONED- Explorer: +2 for OVERVIEW---## 5.2 Chunk kind weightFrom `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`:- PROTOCOL_RULE → +3 for Architect- ALGORITHM → +3 for Builder/Conduit- RATIONALE → +3 for Architect/Explorer- OPEN_QUESTION → +3 for Inspector/Architect- EXAMPLE → moderate boost for Explorer---## 5.3 Level weightL1: +3 for Builder/ConduitL2: +3 for ArchitectL3: +2 for ExplorerL4: +2 for all roles (meta awareness bonus)---## 5.4 Review weightCURRENT_FOCUS → +4REVIEWED → +2NEEDS_REVIEW → +1UNREVIEWED → 0OUTDATED → -2QUESTIONED → +2 for Inspector, -2 for BuilderSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED → -4 (default)---## 5.5 Graph weightChunks gain score from graph structure:- + connectivity (degree centrality)- + cross-reference richness- + being referenced by current focus nodes- + participation in migration chains---## 5.6 Freshness weightBased on:- last reviewed timestamp- recency of updates- proximity to current focus artifacts---# 6. Candidate SelectionBefore scoring, Nebula selects a candidate set:```pseudo id="c8xk1a"function select_candidates(query):if query.role_hint exists:seed = role_preferred_chunks(query.role)else:seed = semantic_search(query.text)expand seed using:- direct references- parent sections- sibling chunksreturn seed7. Graph Expansion PhaseAfter scoring top candidates:for chunk in top_results:expand:parent sectionreferenced chunksupstream dependenciesdownstream dependenciesThis produces alocal subgraph, not just a ranked list.8. Filtering RulesAfter scoring:removeSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDunless explicitly requestedremoveOUTDATEDfor Builder unless overriddenpreserveQUESTIONEDfor InspectorpreserveRATIONALEfor Architect/Explorerenforce role-level safety filters9. Explanation GenerationEvery retrieval result MUST include:explanation = {"why_selected": [],"role_alignment": "","chunk_kind_match": "","review_state_influence": "","graph_signals": []}``` id="v1k2zq"This is critical for debugging the system and for human trust calibration.---# 10. Retrieval Modes## 10.1 STRICT MODE- only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS- no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED- minimal graph expansionUsed for execution / Conduit---## 10.2 EXPLORATION MODE- broad inclusion- heavy graph traversal- includes OUTDATED + SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED if relevantUsed for learning / architecture discovery---## 10.3 DIAGNOSTIC MODE- Inspector role default mode- boosts QUESTIONED and conflicts- surfaces contradictions explicitly---## 10.4 EXECUTION MODE- Builder + Conduit hybrid- minimal graph- deterministic chunks only- excludes RATIONALE unless required---# 11. Conflict ResolutionIf two chunks compete:Priority resolution:1. CURRENT_FOCUS overrides all2. REVIEWED overrides NEARLY EVERYTHING except CURRENT_FOCUS3. QUESTIONED overrides OUTDATED for Inspector4. SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED loses by default5. graph centrality can override weak semantic differences---# 12. Key Design Principle> Nebula retrieval is not search. It is weighted cognitive reconstruction.The system is not trying to find documents.It is trying to reconstruct the **relevant slice of the system’s mental model for a role and intent**.---# 13. DAG Constructionpseudofunction build_execution_dag(nodes, edges):dag = DirectedAcyclicGraph()for node in nodes:dag.add_node(node)for edge in edges:dag.add_edge(edge)if dag.has_cycles():resolve_cycles(dag)return dag6.1 Cycle resolution strategyIf cycles exist:Priority resolution:break edges from LOWER level → HIGHER levelbreak edges from RATIONALE → ALGORITHMpreserve PROTOCOL_RULE dependencies over EXAMPLE linksif unresolved → mark as NEEDS_REVIEW in Nebula7. Execution Plan CompilationOnce DAG is constructed:pseudofunction compile_execution_plan(dag):topo_order = topological_sort(dag)plan = []for node in topo_order:step = ExecutionStep(node_id=node.id,action=resolve_executor(node),inputs=get_inputs(node),outputs=declare_outputs(node))plan.append(step)return plan8. Core Data Structures## Validation Report```json id="vr1"ValidationReport {dag_idstatus: PASS | FAIL | DEGRADEDstructural_issues[]semantic_issues[]invariant_violations[]warnings[]suggested_fixes[]}Invariant DefinitionJSONInvariant {iddescriptionscope: GLOBAL | ARTIFACT | CHUNK | EXECUTION_STEPseverity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUMcondition_expression}4. Structural ValidationEnsures DAG correctness independent of semantics.pseudofunction structural_validation(dag):assert dag.is_acyclic()assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)return PASSStructural rulesDAG MUST be acyclicall nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunksno dangling references allowedall edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs5. Semantic ValidationEnsures node meaning aligns with WRP + Nebula expectations.pseudofunction semantic_validation(dag):for node in dag.nodes:if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")if node.review_state == OUTDATED:mark_warning(node)if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")return reportSemantic constraints5.1 Protocol purity rulePROTOCOL_RULE nodes MUST NOT contain:side-effect logicmutation operationsexecution commandsThey define constraints only.5.2 Algorithm determinism ruleALGORITHM nodes MUST:be deterministicnot depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration5.3 Migration consistency ruleMIGRATION_STEP nodes MUST:reference a valid prior statedefine explicit transition target6. Invariant Verification EngineThis is the core of WRP correctness.6.1 Invariant evaluation looppseudofunction invariant_verification(dag, invariants):violations = []for invariant in invariants:for node in dag.nodes:if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):violations.append({"node": node.id,"invariant": invariant.id})return violations6.2 Example invariantsGlobal execution invariantsNo node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution pathAll PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chainNo cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chainsWRP-specific invariantsEvery ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULEEvery MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transitionEvery ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node7. Dependency Consistency CheckEnsures graph coherence across Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction dependency_consistency(dag):for edge in dag.edges:if edge.type == DEPENDS_ON:assert topological_order(edge.source) < topological_order(edge.target)if violates_level_constraints(edge):mark_error(edge)Level constraint rulesL1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logicL2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationaleL3 nodes MUST NOT define execution dependencies8. Execution Safety CheckThis step ensures the DAG is safe to run under Conduit.8.1 Safety rulespseudofunction execution_safety(dag):assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)return PASS8.2 Strict mode constraintsIn STRICT execution mode:only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowedQUESTIONED nodes forbiddenOUTDATED nodes forbiddenSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely9. Validation Severity ModelEach issue is classified:CRITICAL → blocks executionHIGH → requires interventionMEDIUM → warningLOW → informationalFailure policypseudoif CRITICAL exists:status = FAILhalt_execution()elif HIGH exists:status = DEGRADEDrequire_human_review()else:status = PASS10. Suggested Fix GeneratorFor each violation:pseudofunction suggest_fix(issue):switch issue.type:case OUTDATED_DEPENDENCY:suggest("Replace with superseding artifact")case INVALID_PROTOCOL_MUTATION:suggest("Move logic to ALGORITHM chunk")case MISSING_REFERENCE:suggest("Add cross-reference or dependency edge")case LEVEL_VIOLATION:suggest("Promote/demote chunk level or split chunk")return suggestion11. OverviewConduit is a deterministic execution runtime for validated Nebula-derived DAGs.It is responsible for:- scheduling execution steps- managing concurrency- tracking execution state- handling retries and failures- emitting execution receipts- ensuring deterministic replayability---# 2. Core Principle> Conduit does not “run code.” It executes validated semantic graphs under strict lifecycle control.Every execution is:- deterministic where possible- replayable- traceable to Nebula chunks- governed by WRP validation guarantees---# 3. Execution Lifecycle StatesEach node transitions through a lifecycle:PENDING→ READY→ RUNNING→ COMPLETED→ FAILED→ RETRYING→ SKIPPED→ COMPENSATED---## 3.1 State definitions### PENDINGNode is waiting for dependencies or scheduling.### READYAll dependencies satisfied; eligible for execution.### RUNNINGNode is actively executing.### COMPLETEDExecution succeeded and produced valid output.### FAILEDExecution failed irrecoverably for current attempt.### RETRYINGNode is scheduled for re-execution.### SKIPPEDNode is intentionally bypassed (policy or conditional logic).### COMPENSATEDNode failure has been resolved via compensating action (migration or rollback logic).---# 4. Scheduler ModelConduit uses a **dependency-aware priority scheduler**.---## 4.1 Scheduling loop```pseudo id="sched1"while true:ready_nodes = get_ready_nodes(dag)prioritized = rank(ready_nodes,priority_function)for node in prioritized:if can_run(node):dispatch(node)4.2 Priority functionpseudopriority(node) =role_priority_weight(node)+ review_priority_weight(node)+ chunk_kind_weight(node)+ dependency_depth_weight(node)- failure_penalty(node)4.3 Dependency depth weightNodes deeper in dependency chains may be prioritized to unlock downstream execution faster.depth_score = longest_path_from_root(node)5. Concurrency ModelConduit supports controlled parallel execution.5.1 Execution constraintsA node MAY execute in parallel if:pseudocan_parallelize(node) =node.has_no_shared_mutation_targetsAND node.dependencies_satisfiedAND not_conflicting_with_running_nodes(node)5.2 Conflict rulesTwo nodes conflict if:they modify same conceptual statethey depend on each other's outputsthey share non-isolated resource contexts5.3 Concurrency policydefault: conservative parallelismmigration mode: stricter (serial execution preferred)exploration mode: relaxed (higher parallelism allowed)6. Execution Dispatcherpseudofunction dispatch(node):mark(node, RUNNING)executor = resolve_executor(node.type)context = build_execution_context(node)try:result = executor.execute(node.payload, context)mark(node, COMPLETED)emit_receipt(node, result)except error:handle_failure(node, error)7. Execution Context BuilderEach node executes with a structured context:JSON{"node_id":"...","dag_id":"...","role":"Conduit","mode":"EXECUTION","strict_mode":true,"nebula_trace": [],"allowed_chunk_kinds": [],"validation_signature":"WRP_VALIDATED","determinism":true}8. Failure Handling System8.1 Failure classificationpseudofunction classify_failure(error):if transient(error):return RETRYABLEif dependency_missing(error):return BLOCKINGif semantic_violation(error):return INVALID_DAGreturn FATAL8.2 Retry policypseudoif RETRYABLE:if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:schedule_retry(node)else:mark(node, FAILED)8.3 Blocking failure propagationIf a node fails due to dependency:downstream nodes → SKIPPED or PENDINGupstream nodes unaffectedDAG remains valid but partially executable8.4 Compensation modelFor MIGRATION_STEP nodes:failures MAY trigger compensating stepsrollback DAG may be generated9. DAG Execution GuaranteesConduit guarantees:deterministic execution order for identical inputsidempotent retries (when possible)no execution without READY stateno execution of invalidated nodesstrict adherence to WRP validation outputs10. Execution ReceiptsEvery execution produces a receipt:JSONExecutionReceipt {node_iddag_idstatusstart_timeend_timeinputsoutputslogsvalidation_ref}Receipts are:immutablestored in Nebulaused for future graph refinementused for failure analysis and review updates11. Scheduling Policies11.1 STRICT POLICYUsed for production execution:no speculative executionno retry beyond limitno OUTDATED or QUESTIONED nodesminimal concurrency11.2 OPTIMIZED POLICYUsed for performance execution:moderate concurrencypredictive schedulingprioritizes unlocking downstream nodes11.3 EXPLORATION POLICYUsed for discovery:high concurrencyrelaxed ordering constraintsallows partial execution of graph branches12. Deadlock PreventionDeadlocks are prevented via:topological schedulingcycle detection (from WRP validation layer)fallback serial executionforced dependency resolution orderingIf deadlock is detected:1. pause execution2. emit diagnostic subgraph3. request inspector review13. System Integration13.1 Nebula integrationConduit reads:validated DAGschunk metadatareview overlayscross-reference structureConduit writes:ExecutionReceiptsfailure annotationsinferred review updates13.2 WRP integrationConduit only executes DAGs that:pass WRP validation enginesatisfy invariant checkscomply with strict mode rules13.3 Validation gate couplingpseudoif not WRPValidationReport.PASS:abort_execution()14. Feedback Loop (Critical)Execution results feed back into Nebula:failed nodes → QUESTIONEDrepeatedly failing nodes → OUTDATED candidatefrequently executed nodes → CURRENT_FOCUS candidatestable nodes → REVIEWEDThis closes theadaptive system loop.15. Key System PropertyConduit is not just an executor — it is a stateful runtime that evolves Nebula’s trust model over time.16. Final Architecture ViewWRP↓Nebula (semantic graph + review state)↓Retrieval (role-scored subgraph selection)↓WRP Validation Engine (pre-execution proof gate)↓Conduit Scheduler (this layer)↓Execution Nodes↓Receipts↓Nebula update cycle↓(continuous loop)``` id="loop2"---# 17. Control-flow driftExecution order violated expectations→ suggests DAG ordering issueD. Invariant driftInvariant violated during execution→ suggests WRP model mismatch7. Graph Update PlanningNebula does NOT mutate immediately.It generates amutation plan.7.1 Mutation plan structureJSONGraphMutationPlan {target_node_idmutation_typereasonconfidenceproposed_change}7.2 Mutation typesRECLASSIFY_CHUNK_KINDUPDATE_REVIEW_STATEMODIFY_EDGEADD_EDGEREMOVE_EDGEPROMOTE_LEVELDEMOTE_LEVELMARK_SUPERSEDEDSPLIT_CHUNKMERGE_CHUNK8. Cross-Reference AdjustmentExecution reveals incorrect or missing edges.9.1 Missing dependency discoveryIf runtime shows implicit dependency:pseudoif runtime_dependency_detected and no_edge_exists:add_edge(source, target, type=DEPENDS_ON)9.2 Broken dependency pruningIf dependency never used:downgrade to MENTIONSor remove edge entirely9.3 Over-constrained graph correctionIf SKIPPED nodes are frequent:dependency edges may be too strictdowngrade to soft references10. Chunk Reclassification EngineExecution results refine chunk taxonomy.10.1 Heuristic correction rulespseudoif ALGORITHM fails frequently:reconsider_chunk_kind(node)if PROTOCOL_RULE causes mutation logic:split_into(PROTOCOL_RULE, ALGORITHM)if RATIONALE is executed:likely misclassified → promote to PROTOCOL_RULE or DATA_MODEL11. Invariant LifecycleEvery invariant now has a lifecycle:PROPOSED→ TESTED→ VALIDATED→ STABLE→ DEPRECATED→ REPLACED---## 3.1 State definitions### PROPOSED- derived from observation or heuristic- not yet validated### TESTED- applied in simulation branches- evaluated under stress### VALIDATED- passes execution + simulation consistently### STABLE- holds across multiple branches and versions### DEPRECATED- fails under new system conditions### REPLACED- superseded by stronger invariant---# 4. Invariant SourcesWRP invariants are synthesized from:---## 4.1 Execution traces- repeated failure patterns- consistent success constraints- runtime invariants inferred from Conduit---## 4.2 Simulation divergence- invariants that hold across all stable branches- invariants that fail under specific mutations---## 4.3 Cross-agent agreement- invariants consistently inferred by Builder, Architect, Inspector---## 4.4 Governance decisions- human or L3-approved constraints- enforced structural rules---# 5. Invariant Synthesis Engine---## 5.1 Candidate generation```pseudo id="syn1"function generate_invariants(execution_data, simulation_data):candidates = []for pattern in extract_patterns(execution_data):if pattern.is_repeated():candidates.append(Invariant(candidate_from(pattern)))for divergence in simulation_data:if divergence.is_consistent_across_branches():candidates.append(Invariant(from_divergence(divergence)))return candidates5.2 Pattern typesdependency stability patternsexecution ordering constraintsfailure clustering patternsmutation resistance patterns6. Meta-Governance Layer (L4)A new layer is introduced:L4: Meta-Governance Layer``` id="lg4"---## 6.1 ResponsibilitiesL4 governs:- whether WRP itself can change- whether governance rules can evolve- whether simulation semantics can change- whether agent roles can be redefined---## 6.2 RestrictionsL4 CANNOT:- execute DAGs- directly mutate Nebula graphs- bypass L3 governance decisions without trace---## 6.3 Authority hierarchyL4 > L3 > L2 > L1 > L0But:> L4 changes are extremely rare and require full-system consistency validation.---# 7. Self-Representation ModelNebula introduces a canonical system node:SystemNode: NEBULA_COREThis node represents:- architecture- runtime components- governance structure- invariants (WRP)- agent fabric- execution system (Conduit)- temporal model- simulation engine---## 3.1 System Node Structure```json id="sysnode1"SystemNode {node_id: "NEBULA_CORE",components: ["WRP","Conduit","Nebula Graph","Multi-Agent Fabric","Governance Layer","Simulation Engine","Meta-Governance Layer"],version_alignment: GraphState.version_id,stability_score,drift_metrics,integrity_state}4. Introspection ModelNebula supports structured self-querying:4.1 Self-query typesA. Structural introspection“What am I made of?”returns system graph decompositionreturns dependency topology of core subsystemsB. Behavioral introspection“How do I behave under execution?”returns Conduit execution model applied to itselfreturns failure modes of system componentsC. Governance introspection“Who is allowed to change me?”returns L0–L4 authority mapreturns mutation constraints affecting itselfD. Stability introspection“Am I stable?”returns fixed-point compliance scorereturns drift metricsreturns invariant satisfaction distribution5. Self-Model Construction PipelineThe self-model is not manually defined.It is derived:SystemState↓Graph extraction↓Component clustering↓Role mapping↓Dependency inference↓SelfNode construction``` id="selfpipe1"---# 6. Self-Observation LoopNebula continuously observes itself:1. execute system operations2. record execution traces3. update SystemNode4. validate against invariants5. adjust self-model6. repeat``` id="selfloop1"---# 8. Bounded Recursion ConstraintSelf-modeling is restricted:---## 8.1 Allowed recursion depth- system → self-model → subcomponent model → bounded expansion onlyNo infinite expansion into:- “model of model of model …”---## 8.2 Forbidden operations- modifying WRP without L4 approval- redefining governance via self-model alone- collapsing self-model into execution logic- recursive self-modification without external validation---# 9. Self-Model as a Graph NodeThe SystemNode is part of Nebula:- it is queryable- it is versioned- it is included in simulation- it participates in structural validation (read-only)---## 9.1 Important constraint> The system cannot mutate itself via its self-model alone.Self-model is **observational**, not **authoritative**.---# 10. Drift Detection via Self-ModelSelf-model enables detection of:- hidden structural divergence- undocumented system behavior- governance bypass patterns- emergent behavior not reflected in design---## 10.1 Drift signal```pseudo id="drift2"drift =observed_system_state- self_model_stateIf drift exceeds threshold:trigger meta-governance reviewfreeze mutation pipelineregenerate self-model11. Simulation of SelfNebula can simulate itself:“What happens if Conduit fails?”“What if governance layer is removed?”“What if agent weights shift?”This is done via:simulation engineSystemNode as root graph seed12. System Integrity ConstraintThe self-model must always preserve:traceability to execution logsconsistency with WRP invariantsalignment with governance structurenon-circular validation grounding13. Self-Awareness Without AuthorityCritical separation:CapabilityAllowedAuthorityObserve selfYesL0–L3Model selfYesL1–L3Validate self-modelYesL2Modify system via self-modelNoL4 only14. Integration with Full SystemNebula Graph↓Multi-Agent Fabric↓Conduit Execution↓Validation Engine↓Self-Healing Layer↓Governance Layer↓Simulation Engine↓WRP Synthesizer↓Meta-Governance Layer↓Self-Model / Introspection Layer (this)↓SystemNode (NEBULA_CORE)↓feedback into all layers``` id="loop10"---# 15. Key System Property> The system contains a representation of itself, but that representation is always subordinate to observed execution reality.---# 16. Final Principle> True self-awareness in a system is not the ability to change itself, but the ability to correctly model itself without losing grounding in execution reality.---# 17. retrieve fromL2/L3

allow traversal across cross-references

emphasize invariants, state transitions, schema rules, migration constraints
