Suggested Application-Level TypesThe following are reference shapes for the application layer.55.1 Document level enumJavapublicenumKnowledgeLevel{L1,// execution/build detailL2,// subsystem designL3,// architecture/rationaleL4// doctrine/ontology}55.2 Artifact type enumJavapublicenumArtifactType{WRP_PROTOCOL,WRP_DAG_MODEL,WRP_EXECUTION_ENGINE,WRP_MIGRATION_PLAN}55.3 Chunk kind enumJavapublicenumChunkKind{OVERVIEW,DEFINITION,PROTOCOL_RULE,DATA_MODEL,ALGORITHM,INVARIANT,MIGRATION_STEP,ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA,OPEN_QUESTION,EXAMPLE,RATIONALE,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE}55.4 Normative strength enumJavapublicenumNormativeStrength{INFORMATIVE,RECOMMENDED,REQUIRED,PROHIBITED}56. Suggested Projection DTOsJavapublicrecordNebulaArtifactRegistration(StringartifactKey,ArtifactTypeartifactType,StringartifactVersion,StringsourcePath,StringsourceKind,StringconduitPlanId,StringconduitProjectKey,KnowledgeLeveldefaultLevel) {}JavapublicrecordNebulaChunkProjection(LongdocumentId,StringsectionKey,ChunkKindchunkKind,KnowledgeLevellevel,NormativeStrengthnormativeStrength,Stringcontent) {}JavapublicrecordNebulaCrossReferenceProjection(StringsourceSectionKey,StringtargetSectionKey,StringrelationType,KnowledgeLevelsourceLevel,KnowledgeLeveltargetLevel,StringevidenceKind,Doubleweight) {}57. InvariantsThe following invariants apply to the Conduit → Nebula WRP projection model.I1. Nebula is the authoritative long-form memory for WRPConduit may track execution, but architectural WRP meaning must remain represented in Nebula.I2. Every WRP artifact must have a stable artifact keyPaths may change; artifact identity must not.I3. Every Nebula document and chunk must have a deterministic effective levelA chunk either declares a level or inherits from its document.I4. Cross-reference edges are level-neutral by defaultThe source and target nodes carry the abstraction semantics.I5. The initial WRP packet must be explicitly cross-linkedProtocol, DAG, traversal, and migration documents must not exist as isolated documents.I6. Role-aware retrieval must filter by level before broad cross-reference expansionOtherwise the stratification model loses value.I7. Execution traceability must be additive, not destructiveImplementation evidence and receipts should enrich architectural records rather than overwrite them.58. What This Unlocks NextOnce this projection and stratification layer exists, the system can do all of the following coherently:Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.59. Bottom LineThe four WRP plans now sitting in Conduit should be treated as theexecution packetfor a broader WRP knowledge corpus. The missing piece is a projection layer that makes those artifacts durable and queryable inside Nebula.The core model is simple:Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledgeConduit stores the executable work packetWRP artifacts provide the stable identity between themlevelstratification controls who sees whatcross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graphThat is the foundation required before WRP can function as a real architectural substrate rather than just a set of implementation plans.---## What I’d do immediately after this oneSince those four WRP plans are now in Conduit and will take a bit to implement under your local Ollama/OpenCode/Qwen setup, the next companion spec I’d write is the **actual Nebula schema/ontology patch** for this document, not another prose architecture note.Specifically:# `schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonld`That doc should formalize, in machine-oriented ontology form:- `KnowledgeLevel`- `ArtifactType`- `ChunkKind`- `NormativeStrength`- `CrossReferenceRelationType`- `NebulaDocument`- `NebulaChunk`- `NebulaArtifact`- `NebulaExecutionLink`and the exact fields/relationships implied by the markdown spec above.If you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it **repo-ready JSON-LD** rather than another markdown doc.

Absolutely. Given that Conduit is execution-oriented and the real long-form knowledge belongs in Nebula, I’d treat this as thebridge specbetween the four WRP implementation plans now sitting in Conduit and the stratified knowledge corpus Nebula needs to become.Below is arepo-ready docin the style we’ve been using.docs/conduit/nebula-wrp-projection-and-level-stratification.mdMarkdown# Conduit → Nebula WRP Projection and Level Stratification**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Architecture / Nebula / Conduit**Last Updated:** 2026-06-21---# 1. PurposeThis document defines how **WRP artifacts managed through Conduit** are projected into the **Nebula knowledge graph / document corpus**, and how those artifacts are stratified by **abstraction level** so that different roles and agents can retrieve the right amount of context.The immediate goal is to support the first WRP work packet now tracked in Conduit:1. **WRP v1.0** — protocol formalization2. **WRP v1.1** — DAG data model & compilation pipeline3. **WRP v1.2** — execution traversal engine4. **WRP migration plan**These four artifacts must not remain isolated implementation plans. They must become **queryable architectural knowledge** inside Nebula so that:- builders can retrieve concrete implementation guidance,- architects can retrieve subsystem rationale and relationships,- inspectors/validators can retrieve invariants and migration constraints,- future harvests and work requests can cross-reference WRP material directly.This document therefore specifies:- the **projection model** from Conduit/WRP artifacts into Nebula;- the **`level` stratification model** for Nebula documents, chunks, and references;- the **artifact taxonomy** for WRP knowledge units;- the **retrieval policy** by role;- the **migration strategy** for the initial WRP corpus.---# 2. Context and Position in the StackThe working architectural chain is:```textNebula → WRP → Conduit → LOSM / runtime implementationwith the following responsibilities:Nebulalong-form architectural memorymarkdown-authored specificationschunked knowledge corpuscross-reference graphopen questions / unresolved decisionsretrieval substrate for planning and implementationWRP (Work Request Protocol / Work Request Package)canonical execution-facing representation of workprotocol, DAG model, traversal semantics, migration disciplinethe bridge between long-form intent and executable workConduitexecution-oriented work managerreceives concrete plans / work requeststracks dependencies, acceptance criteria, receipts, affected filesis not the authoritative home for large concept documentsLOSM / runtimeexecution engine, orchestration, persistence, validation, receiptsThe practical rule is:Nebula owns long-form architectural knowledge. Conduit owns executable work tracking. WRP is the formal bridge between the two.This document defines how that bridge is materialized in storage and retrieval.3. Design GoalsThe projection and stratification model must satisfy the following goals.G1. Preserve long-form WRP knowledge in NebulaThe WRP packet tracked in Conduit must be represented in Nebula as durable, queryable, versioned knowledge.G2. Preserve execution alignment with ConduitNebula entries must retain enough metadata to map back to the Conduit work packet(s) that implement them.G3. Support role-specific retrievalThe same corpus must serve multiple retrieval surfaces:Builder / implementerArchitect / plannerInspector / validatorExplorer / researcherG4. Separate abstraction levels cleanlyImplementation details should not drown architectural reasoning, and architectural rationale should not flood implementation prompts unless explicitly requested.G5. Preserve explicit cross-referencesProtocol rules, DAG semantics, traversal rules, migration tasks, invariants, and open questions must be linked explicitly rather than relying only on embedding similarity.G6. Remain compatible with the existing Nebula markdown-ingestion pipelineThis design should extend the existing markdown import / chunk / cross-reference model rather than replacing it.4. Core Decision4.1 Canonical ruleWRP artifacts are authored or curated as Nebula documents, then projected into Conduit as executable work packages.Conduit may hold the immediate execution plans, but Nebula remains the authoritative architectural memory for:protocol definitions,subsystem specs,migration rationale,invariants,open questions,design history.4.2 Projection directionThere are two distinct projection paths:A. Authoritative knowledge projectionNebula markdown/spec document→ Nebula document rows / chunks / cross references→ optional WRP artifact registration→ Conduit plan / work request generationB. Execution trace back-projectionConduit plan / execution receipt / implementation status→ WRP artifact linkage→ Nebula document metadata updates→ cross-linked execution referencesSo the system is not one-way. The long-form knowledge projects downward into executable work, and execution status projects upward into Nebula metadata and trace links.5. Scope of WRP Artifacts Covered by This SpecThis document covers the initial WRP corpus:WRP-1 — WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefines the formal work request protocol, message shape, identity, versioning, semantics, and lifecycle assumptions.WRP-2 — WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefines the DAG representation of work, node/edge semantics, compilation from protocol-level requests into executable graph structures, and compilation invariants.WRP-3 — WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefines the traversal/execution model over the WRP DAG, execution context, cursor/receipt semantics, deterministic traversal defaults, and isolation rules.WRP-4 — WRP Migration PlanDefines how existing work representations, legacy plans, or runtime workflows migrate into the WRP model with compatibility constraints and staged rollout.The schema and rules in this document are generic enough to apply to future WRP artifacts as well.6. Terminology6.1 Conduit PlanAn execution-oriented item managed by Conduit, typically containing:titleprojectaffected filesacceptance criteriadependenciesreceipt trail6.2 WRP ArtifactA versioned architectural / protocol artifact in the WRP family, such as:protocol specDAG model spectraversal engine specmigration planfuture validation / governance extensions6.3 Nebula DocumentA markdown-origin or spec-origin long-form document stored in Nebula.6.4 Nebula ChunkA chunked section or paragraph group extracted from a Nebula document for retrieval and cross-referencing.6.5 Cross ReferenceAn explicit semantic edge connecting one document/chunk/artifact to another, such as:“depends on”“implements”“constrains”“supersedes”“migrates”“explains”“references protocol field”“defines traversal invariant”6.6 LevelA stratification marker describing the abstraction level of a knowledge item.7. Level Stratification Model8. Rationale for Level StratificationWithout level stratification, a retrieval system operating over mixed architectural and implementation material tends to collapse the distinction between:“what the protocol means,”“how the DAG is represented,”“what code needs to change this week,”“why the migration strategy was chosen.”That leads to three recurring failures:Builders get too much theoryimplementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.Architects get too much local detailsubsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.Inspectors miss normative constraintsinvariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.A level field provides a stable, queryable abstraction boundary.9. Level DefinitionsThe first version of the level system usesfour levels.Level 1 — Execution / Build Detail (L1)Concrete implementation guidance and execution-facing material.Typical content:file-level implementation tasksendpoint contractsdataclass / schema detailsmethod signaturesSQL changesacceptance criteriatest casesmigration scriptsprecise repository change instructions“do this in package X” contentPrimary consumers:BuilderConduit executorimplementation-focused coding agentsLevel 2 — Subsystem Design (L2)Subsystem mechanics and technical design for a bounded domain.Typical content:DAG node/edge semanticscompilation pipeline structuretraversal algorithm designexecution receipt structurerole-specific service boundariesstorage mappings for a specific subsystemformal state transitions inside one bounded domainPrimary consumers:Builder (secondary)ArchitectInspectorLevel 3 — Architecture / Rationale (L3)Higher-order architectural reasoning, system relationships, and design justification.Typical content:why WRP existswhy DAG compilation is separate from traversalhow Conduit, Nebula, and LOSM relatemigration philosophy and rollout strategycross-subsystem responsibilitieslong-form tradeoff analysisarchitectural invariants spanning multiple packagesPrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerInspectorLevel 4 — Meta / Doctrine / Ontology (L4)Cross-cutting design doctrine, system philosophy, and ontology-level governance.Typical content:methodology rulesrole doctrinearchitectural constitution / invariants of invariantsontology rules for work, memory, or cognitionglobal modeling principlescross-project strategic doctrinePrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerstrategic planner10. Level Assignment Rules10.1 Canonical ruleLevel belongs primarily to the content node, not to the retrieval query and not to the edge.That means:documents have levels,chunks have levels,references may optionally have level metadata, but level is not primarily an edge property.10.2 Single-primary-level ruleEvery document and every chunk must haveone primary level.This avoids ambiguous retrieval behavior and keeps filtering deterministic.10.3 Mixed documentsA long document may contain sections at different abstraction levels. Therefore:thedocumentreceives a default or dominant level;chunksmay override the document level when section content clearly belongs to a different level.Example:a WRP migration document may be primarilyL3,but its implementation checklist section may be chunked asL1.10.4 Edge neutrality ruleCross-reference edges should belevel-neutral by default.The edge describes the relationship; the source and target nodes carry the abstraction level.11. Recommended Level Mapping for the Initial WRP Corpus11.1 WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefault document level:L2Reasoning:it defines subsystem protocol semantics and normative message shape;it is not merely implementation detail;it is narrower than whole-system doctrine.Typical chunk-level overrides:formal field definitions / JSON examples / schema tables →L1rationale for protocol boundaries →L311.2 WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:compilation algorithm pseudocode →L2concrete data structures / storage tables / code mapping →L1rationale for DAG compilation as separate phase →L311.3 WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:ExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceiptstructures →L1orL2depending on specificitytraversal invariants / isolation rules →L2rationale for deterministic traversal and experimental modes →L311.4 WRP Migration PlanDefault document level:L3Reasoning:migration is a cross-cutting architectural transition strategy;the document explains sequencing, compatibility, and rollout discipline.Typical chunk-level overrides:actual migration tasks and repo changes →L1compatibility matrix / rollout constraints →L2migration philosophy and sequencing rationale →L312. Nebula Data Model ExtensionsThis section defines the required schema extensions to Nebula’s markdown-derived corpus.13. Target Nebula EntitiesThe projection model assumes the following logical entities exist or will exist:nebula_documentsnebula_chunksnebula_cross_referencesOptionally:nebula_artifactsnebula_open_questionsnebula_execution_linksThis document does not require a specific SQL dialect, but examples assume a relational store.14. Required Additions tonebula_documents14.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_documentsADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8)NOTNULLDEFAULT'L2',ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNartifact_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNartifact_versionVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNconduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNconduit_project_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNsource_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNsupersedes_document_id BIGINTNULL;14.2 Field semanticslevelPrimary abstraction level of the document.Allowed values:L1L2L3L4artifact_typeStable WRP artifact family identifier, e.g.:wrp.protocolwrp.dag_modelwrp.execution_enginewrp.migration_planartifact_keyStable logical identifier for the artifact, e.g.:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planartifact_versionHuman-visible version identifier, e.g.:1.01.11.22026-06conduit_plan_idOptional link to the Conduit execution plan primarily associated with the document.conduit_project_keyOptional grouping key for Conduit project membership.source_kindDescribes origin:markdowngenerated_specconduit_projectionimported_transcriptmanual_notestatusDocument lifecycle:draftcandidateapprovedsupersededarchivedsupersedes_document_idOptional pointer to the prior document version.15. Required Additions tonebula_chunks15.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_chunksADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNchunk_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNnormative_strengthVARCHAR(32),ADDCOLUMNsection_keyVARCHAR(255);15.2 Field semanticslevelChunk-level override. If null, inherit from the parent document.artifact_typeOptional denormalized copy of the parent artifact type for faster filtering.chunk_kindClassifies the chunk’s semantic role. Recommended values:overviewdefinitionprotocol_ruledata_modelalgorithminvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriaopen_questionexamplerationaleimplementation_notenormative_strengthOptional normative marker for validation-oriented retrieval:informativerecommendedrequiredprohibitedsection_keyStable section identity, e.g.:wrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.compilation-invariantswrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.migration.phase-2-cutover16. Required Additions tonebula_cross_references16.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_cross_referencesADDCOLUMNrelation_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'references',ADDCOLUMNsource_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNtarget_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNweightDECIMAL(8,4),ADDCOLUMNevidence_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(32)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active';16.2 Why not a singlelevelon the edge?Because the edge itself is not the primary abstraction bearer. The useful information is usually:what level the source is,what level the target is,what relation binds them.Therefore, the preferred model is to carry:source_leveltarget_levelas denormalized convenience fields rather than treating the edge as an independently stratified knowledge unit.16.3 Field semanticsrelation_typeRecommended initial relation types:referencesdepends_onimplementsconstrainsdefinescompiled_intoexecutesmigratessupersedesvalidated_byraises_questionanswers_questionsource_level,target_levelOptional denormalized values copied from the linked nodes for efficient querying.weightOptional confidence or importance score.evidence_kindHow the edge was created:explicit_markdown_linkmanual_annotationartifact_projectionsemantic_matchreceipt_backlinkstatusactivesupersededtentative17. Optional New Table:nebula_artifactsIf WRP artifacts need to be treated as first-class entities independent of document versions, add a registry table.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_artifacts (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULLUNIQUE,artifact_typeVARCHAR(128)NOTNULL,current_versionVARCHAR(64),current_document_id BIGINT,statusVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active',created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL,updated_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Purpose:stable artifact identity across multiple document revisions,single lookup point for “the current WRP traversal spec,”easier version navigation and supersession tracking.18. Optional New Table:nebula_execution_linksThis table binds Nebula knowledge to execution artifacts and receipts.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_execution_links (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULL,document_id BIGINT,chunk_id BIGINT,conduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),wrp_work_request_idVARCHAR(255),receipt_idVARCHAR(255),link_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULL,created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Recommendedlink_typevalues:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planvalidated_by_receiptsuperseded_by_planmigrated_by_requestThis table is not required for the first pass, but it becomes useful as soon as execution receipts start flowing back into Nebula.19. WRP Artifact TaxonomyEach WRP artifact projected into Nebula must declare a stable type.19.1 Initial artifact typesArtifact TypeMeaningwrp.protocolFormal WRP protocol definitionwrp.dag_modelDAG representation and compilation pipelinewrp.execution_engineTraversal / execution engine semanticswrp.migration_planWRP migration and rollout strategy19.2 Future extension typesExamples of likely future additions:Artifact TypeMeaningwrp.validation_rulesCross-artifact validation and policy ruleswrp.compatibility_matrixVersion compatibility / migration compatibilitywrp.receipt_modelFormal execution receipt modelwrp.role_contractsRole-specific work request / execution constraints20. Canonical WRP Artifact KeysThe initial corpus should use stable artifact keys.Artifact KeyArtifact TypeVersionwrp-v1-protocolwrp.protocol1.0wrp-v1_1-dagwrp.dag_model1.1wrp-v1_2-traversalwrp.execution_engine1.2wrp-migration-planwrp.migration_plan2026-06These keys should remain stable even if the underlying document path changes.21. Projection ModelThis section defines how WRP material moves from authored docs / Conduit plans into Nebula entities.22. Projection SourcesA WRP artifact may enter Nebula from one of three sources.Source A — Markdown-authored specThe preferred source. A curated markdown spec exists under the repo and is imported into Nebula.Source B — Conduit plan projectionA Conduit plan or work packet is projected into Nebula as a lightweight execution-facing document when no richer Nebula document exists yet.Source C — Manual or generated synthesisA generated or manually synthesized architecture note is imported and later normalized.The preferred order is:Markdown specGenerated synthesisConduit projection fallback23. Projection Pipeline StagesEvery WRP artifact projection follows the same high-level pipeline.Source artifact→ artifact registration→ document ingestion→ section extraction→ chunk creation→ level assignment→ cross-reference extraction→ Conduit link registration→ optional open-question extraction24. Stage 1 — Artifact RegistrationInput:artifact keyartifact typeversionsource path or source identifierOutput:canonical artifact registration recordlink to the current Nebula document versionRules:artifact keys must be stable;new versions should supersede, not overwrite, old document rows;the current version should be discoverable by artifact key.25. Stage 2 — Document IngestionThe source markdown/spec is stored as a Nebula document.Required metadata:artifact_typeartifact_keyartifact_versionsource_kindstatusdefaultlevelDocument title should remain human-readable, e.g.:WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationWRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation PipelineWRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineWRP Migration Plan26. Stage 3 — Section ExtractionSections should be extracted from headings and stable heading anchors.Recommended section key convention:<artifact family>.<major section slug>[.<subsection slug>...]Examples:wrp.protocol.overviewwrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.node-typeswrp.dag.compilation-pipelinewrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.traversal.isolation-ruleswrp.migration.phase-1-parallel-support27. Stage 4 — Chunk CreationChunks should be created with semantic sensitivity rather than purely fixed token windows.Recommended chunk boundaries:section intro / overview paragraph groupsdata model definitionsinvariant blocksalgorithm descriptionsmigration phase stepsexamplesacceptance criteria sectionsopen questions sectionsA chunk should not mix:a high-level architectural rationale paragraph,a concrete SQL alteration block,and an execution acceptance checklist.Those should become separate chunks with different levels andchunk_kindvalues.28. Stage 5 — Level AssignmentLevel assignment occurs in two passes.Pass A — Document default levelAssign the document’s dominant level based on artifact type and overall intent.Pass B — Chunk override levelOverride chunk level when a section clearly belongs to another abstraction layer.Heuristic examplesAssignL1when the chunk contains:repository pathsmethod signaturesschema alteration stepsexplicit implementation task sequencesacceptance criteria / test instructionsfield-by-field code mappingAssignL2when the chunk contains:formal subsystem structuresexecution algorithmsgraph semanticsstate transition rulesnormative subsystem invariantsAssignL3when the chunk contains:design rationalecross-subsystem tradeoffsmigration sequencing rationalearchitectural positioning of WRP relative to Conduit/Nebula/LOSMAssignL4when the chunk contains:system-wide doctrineontology-level policymeta-rules for work modeling or architectural governance29. Stage 6 — Cross-Reference ExtractionCross-references should be created from explicit and inferred signals.29.1 Explicit signalsmarkdown linkssection references“depends on”, “see also”, “constrained by”manually annotated relationships29.2 Inferred signalsartifact-key mentionssection-key referencesprotocol field names reused in traversal or migration docsrepeated formal identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt,tenant_id,trace_id29.3 Required WRP reference classesThe first pass must at least support:protocol field ↔ DAG compilation ruleDAG node/edge semantics ↔ traversal behaviortraversal invariant ↔ migration constraintmigration step ↔ affected WRP artifactWRP artifact ↔ Conduit plan implementing it30. Stage 7 — Conduit Link RegistrationEach projected WRP artifact should retain a link to the Conduit execution packet(s) responsible for implementation.Minimum metadata to retain:conduit_plan_idconduit_project_keyoptional receipt trail / execution link rowIf one Nebula artifact maps to multiple Conduit plans, use:document-level link to the primary umbrella planexecution-link rows for subordinate plans31. Stage 8 — Open Question ExtractionIf a WRP document contains unresolved design questions, they should be extracted into either:dedicatedopen_questionchunks, ora separatenebula_open_questionstable.Recommended fields for open questions:artifact_keydocument_idchunk_idquestion_textstatuspriorityowner_roleThis is especially relevant for migration uncertainties, protocol compatibility questions, and unresolved traversal policy decisions.32. Conduit → Nebula Projection RulesThis section defines how Conduit work packets map into Nebula when a WRP artifact is tracked for implementation.33. Conduit as Execution Metadata, Not Architectural AuthorityA Conduit plan is not automatically a Nebula document. Conduit should only project enough information into Nebula to preserve execution traceability.That means:Conduit ownsactive execution plan rowsacceptance criteriafile listsdependenciesexecution receiptsNebula ownsthe meaning of the WRP artifactthe long-form architecturecross-artifact relationshipsrationalechunk-level retrievability34. Minimal Projection of a Conduit Plan into NebulaFor each Conduit WRP work packet, Nebula should store:conduit_plan_idartifact_keyartifact_typestatusa short execution summarylinks to the authoritative WRP spec documentlinks to receipt or migration status if availableThis can be represented either:as metadata on the authoritative WRP document, oras a small auxiliary Nebula document ofsource_kind = conduit_projection.The first option is preferred for the initial implementation.35. Example Projection of the Initial WRP PacketSuppose Conduit contains four plans:CDT-WRP-001— WRP v1.0 protocol formalizationCDT-WRP-002— WRP v1.1 DAG model and compilation pipelineCDT-WRP-003— WRP v1.2 traversal engineCDT-WRP-004— WRP migration planNebula should contain at least:Document Atitle:WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalizationartifact key:wrp-v1-protocolartifact type:wrp.protocollevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-001Document Btitle:WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation Pipelineartifact key:wrp-v1_1-dagartifact type:wrp.dag_modellevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-002Document Ctitle:WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal Engineartifact key:wrp-v1_2-traversalartifact type:wrp.execution_enginelevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-003Document Dtitle:WRP Migration Planartifact key:wrp-migration-planartifact type:wrp.migration_planlevel:L3conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-004And explicit cross-references such as:wrp-v1_1-dagdepends_onwrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_2-traversalexecuteswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1-protocolwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_2-traversal36. Required WRP Cross-Reference PatternsThe first implementation should explicitly emit the following relation families.36.1 Protocol → DAGExamples:protocol field or lifecycle state constrains DAG node constructionprotocol dependency semantics compiled into edge semanticsRelations:definesconstrainscompiled_into36.2 DAG → TraversalExamples:DAG node kinds determine traversal behaviorDAG execution order constraints are enforced by traversal rulesRelations:definesexecutesconstrains36.3 Traversal → Receipt / ValidationExamples:execution cursor produces execution receipt shapetraversal invariants determine receipt hierarchy or failure semanticsRelations:definesvalidated_by36.4 Migration → All WRP ArtifactsExamples:migration phases refer to protocol changes, DAG compatibility, traversal rolloutRelations:migratessupersedesconstrains36.5 WRP Artifact → Conduit PlanExamples:a Nebula artifact is being implemented by one or more Conduit plansRelations:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planThese may live innebula_execution_linksrather than the main cross-reference table if the execution linkage is operational rather than semantic.37. Role-Based Retrieval PolicyThis is the operational reason for level stratification.38. Builder Retrieval Profile38.1 GoalProvide concrete implementation guidance with only enough architectural context to avoid coding blind.38.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L1Secondary levels:L2ExcludeL3/L4unless:the retrievedL1/L2chunk explicitly references an architectural invariant, orthe prompt requests rationale or migration context38.3 Preferred chunk kindsimplementation_notedata_modelprotocol_rulealgorithmacceptance_criteriamigration_step38.4 Typical use casesimplement WRP protocol DTOsbuild DAG compiler classesadd traversal engine structureswrite migration scripts and tests39. Architect Retrieval Profile39.1 GoalProvide subsystem design and cross-artifact reasoning without drowning in file-level implementation noise.39.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3Optional expansion toL1for concrete examplesOptional expansion toL4for doctrine or ontology alignment39.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewdefinitiondata_modelalgorithminvariantrationaleopen_question39.4 Typical use casesrefine WRP semanticsunderstand why traversal is separated from DAG compilationreason about Conduit/Nebula/LOSM alignmentevaluate migration sequence40. Inspector / Validator Retrieval Profile40.1 GoalRetrieve normative constraints, invariants, and compatibility conditions.40.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3IncludeL1only when validation depends on concrete schema or implementation details40.3 Preferred chunk kindsprotocol_ruleinvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriadata_model40.4 Normative preferencePrefer chunks where:normative_strength = requirednormative_strength = prohibited40.5 Typical use casesverify WRP compatibility rulesvalidate migration sequencingenforce traversal invariantsdetect protocol / DAG / traversal mismatch41. Explorer Retrieval Profile41.1 GoalSupport open-ended investigation across architecture, rationale, and unresolved questions.41.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3,L4IncludeL1only if the search narrows to implementation mechanics41.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewrationaleopen_questiondefinitionexample42. Suggested Retrieval AlgorithmA role-aware retrieval query should combine:artifact filteringe.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')level filteringrole-dependent level setchunk kind weightingrole-specific preferred chunk kindsnormative weightingfor validator/inspector profilescross-reference expansionbounded traversal across explicit edgesexecution recency boostoptional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in ConduitPseudo-policy:candidate_chunks =filter by artifact family / lexical relevance / embedding relevance∩ filter by allowed levels for roleweighted by chunk_kind preferenceweighted by normative_strength where applicableexpanded by explicit cross-reference traversal depth <= NRecommended initial traversal depths:Builder:N = 1Architect:N = 2Inspector:N = 2Explorer:N = 343. Worked Example: Retrieval for WRP Traversal ImplementationUser intent:“Implement the traversal engine for WRP v1.2.”Builder profile should retrieve:WRP v1.2chunks describingExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceipttraversal order semanticsdeterministic traversal defaultisolation rule chunksmigration notes only if they affect implementation compatibilityArchitect profile should additionally retrieve:the WRP DAG document sections that define node and edge semanticsrationale for why traversal is a separate stagemigration constraints affecting rolloutInspector profile should emphasize:invariant chunks such as tenant isolation rulesfailure semanticsreceipt completeness rulescompatibility constraints in the migration plan44. Worked Example: WRP v1.2 Chunking and Level AssignmentConsider a traversal-engine document with these sections:OverviewExecutionContextExecutionCursorTraversal order and pending queue semanticsTenant isolationExperimental policy modeWhy traversal is separate from DAG compilationImplementation checklistRecommended chunking:SectionChunk KindLevelOverviewoverviewL2ExecutionContextdata_modelL2ExecutionCursordata_modelL2Traversal order and pending queue semanticsalgorithmL2Tenant isolationinvariantL2Experimental policy modedefinition/invariantL2Why traversal is separate from DAG compilationrationaleL3Implementation checklistimplementation_note/acceptance_criteriaL145. WRP-Specific Normative MarkingTo make validation retrieval effective, WRP chunks should mark normative strength where appropriate.Examples:requiredtraversal must enforce tenant isolation at execution timeprotocol version must be present in every WRP root requestDAG compilation must reject cycles if the WRP graph is defined as acyclicprohibitedtraversal must not execute a node under the wrong tenant contextmigration must not remove legacy compatibility before the designated cutover phaserecommendedbuilders should prefer deterministic traversal order unless explicitly in experimental modeinformativehistorical rationale and examples46. Back-Projection from Execution into NebulaOnce Conduit and runtime begin executing WRP work, Nebula should be updated with execution traceability.Examples:a Conduit plan completes implementation ofwrp-v1_2-traversalan execution receipt validates a traversal invarianta migration work request supersedes an older compatibility ruleThese should produce:document status updates,execution links,optional new cross-references,optional “implementation evidence” annotations.This should be append-only where possible; do not rewrite architectural history.47. Initial Migration Plan for the Existing WRP PacketThis section defines the first practical rollout for the four WRP artifacts already placed into Conduit.48. Phase 1 — Register the Four WRP ArtifactsCreate Nebula artifact/document records for:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planAt minimum, store:titleartifact typeartifact keyversiondefault levelconduit plan idsource kindstatus49. Phase 2 — Import the Authoritative WRP Markdown DocumentsFor each artifact, import the corresponding markdown spec into Nebula.If a markdown spec does not yet exist in repo form, use a temporary generated or manually curated document, but treat that as a stopgap. The target steady state is:WRP architectural material lives as markdown/spec documents in Nebula, not only as Conduit plan descriptions.50. Phase 3 — Chunk and Level the DocumentsRun the markdown importer with:section extractionsemantic chunkingchunk kind assignmentchunk-level level override assignmentnormative strength tagging for invariant sectionsDo not leave WRP material as giant undifferentiated chunks.51. Phase 4 — Emit Required Cross ReferencesAt minimum, emit:protocol → DAG edgesDAG → traversal edgesmigration → protocol/DAG/traversal edgesWRP artifact → Conduit plan links52. Phase 5 — Add Role-Aware Retrieval FiltersAdd query support for:allowed levelspreferred chunk kindsoptional normative strength weightingbounded cross-reference expansionThis is the point where “Builder sees implementation detail; Architect sees architecture” becomes real.53. Phase 6 — Backfill Execution LinksOnce Conduit begins implementing the packet, attach:plan IDsreceipt trailsstatus updatesimplementation evidence linksto the corresponding WRP artifacts in Nebula.54. Suggested Application-Level TypesThe following are reference shapes for the application layer.55.1 Document level enumJavapublicenumKnowledgeLevel{L1,// execution/build detailL2,// subsystem designL3,// architecture/rationaleL4// doctrine/ontology}55.2 Artifact type enumJavapublicenumArtifactType{WRP_PROTOCOL,WRP_DAG_MODEL,WRP_EXECUTION_ENGINE,WRP_MIGRATION_PLAN}55.3 Chunk kind enumJavapublicenumChunkKind{OVERVIEW,DEFINITION,PROTOCOL_RULE,DATA_MODEL,ALGORITHM,INVARIANT,MIGRATION_STEP,ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA,OPEN_QUESTION,EXAMPLE,RATIONALE,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE}55.4 Normative strength enumJavapublicenumNormativeStrength{INFORMATIVE,RECOMMENDED,REQUIRED,PROHIBITED}56. Suggested Projection DTOsJavapublicrecordNebulaArtifactRegistration(StringartifactKey,ArtifactTypeartifactType,StringartifactVersion,StringsourcePath,StringsourceKind,StringconduitPlanId,StringconduitProjectKey,KnowledgeLeveldefaultLevel) {}JavapublicrecordNebulaChunkProjection(LongdocumentId,StringsectionKey,ChunkKindchunkKind,KnowledgeLevellevel,NormativeStrengthnormativeStrength,Stringcontent) {}JavapublicrecordNebulaCrossReferenceProjection(StringsourceSectionKey,StringtargetSectionKey,StringrelationType,KnowledgeLevelsourceLevel,KnowledgeLeveltargetLevel,StringevidenceKind,Doubleweight) {}57. InvariantsThe following invariants apply to the Conduit → Nebula WRP projection model.I1. Nebula is the authoritative long-form memory for WRPConduit may track execution, but architectural WRP meaning must remain represented in Nebula.I2. Every WRP artifact must have a stable artifact keyPaths may change; artifact identity must not.I3. Every Nebula document and chunk must have a deterministic effective levelA chunk either declares a level or inherits from its document.I4. Cross-reference edges are level-neutral by defaultThe source and target nodes carry the abstraction semantics.I5. The initial WRP packet must be explicitly cross-linkedProtocol, DAG, traversal, and migration documents must not exist as isolated documents.I6. Role-aware retrieval must filter by level before broad cross-reference expansionOtherwise the stratification model loses value.I7. Execution traceability must be additive, not destructiveImplementation evidence and receipts should enrich architectural records rather than overwrite them.58. What This Unlocks NextOnce this projection and stratification layer exists, the system can do all of the following coherently:Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.59. Bottom LineThe four WRP plans now sitting in Conduit should be treated as theexecution packetfor a broader WRP knowledge corpus. The missing piece is a projection layer that makes those artifacts durable and queryable inside Nebula.The core model is simple:Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledgeConduit stores the executable work packetWRP artifacts provide the stable identity between themlevelstratification controls who sees whatcross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graphThat is the foundation required before WRP can function as a real architectural substrate rather than just a set of implementation plans.---## What I’d do immediately after this oneSince those four WRP plans are now in Conduit and will take a bit to implement under your local Ollama/OpenCode/Qwen setup, the next companion spec I’d write is the **actual Nebula schema/ontology patch** for this document, not another prose architecture note.Specifically:# `schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonld`That doc should formalize, in machine-oriented ontology form:- `KnowledgeLevel`- `ArtifactType`- `ChunkKind`- `NormativeStrength`- `CrossReferenceRelationType`- `NebulaDocument`- `NebulaChunk`- `NebulaArtifact`- `NebulaExecutionLink`and the exact fields/relationships implied by the markdown spec above.If you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it **repo-ready JSON-LD** rather than another markdown doc.

Absolutely. Given that Conduit is execution-oriented and the real long-form knowledge belongs in Nebula, I’d treat this as thebridge specbetween the four WRP implementation plans now sitting in Conduit and the stratified knowledge corpus Nebula needs to become.Below is arepo-ready docin the style we’ve been using.docs/conduit/nebula-wrp-projection-and-level-stratification.mdMarkdown# Conduit → Nebula WRP Projection and Level Stratification**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Architecture / Nebula / Conduit**Last Updated:** 2026-06-21---# 1. PurposeThis document defines how **WRP artifacts managed through Conduit** are projected into the **Nebula knowledge graph / document corpus**, and how those artifacts are stratified by **abstraction level** so that different roles and agents can retrieve the right amount of context.The immediate goal is to support the first WRP work packet now tracked in Conduit:1. **WRP v1.0** — protocol formalization2. **WRP v1.1** — DAG data model & compilation pipeline3. **WRP v1.2** — execution traversal engine4. **WRP migration plan**These four artifacts must not remain isolated implementation plans. They must become **queryable architectural knowledge** inside Nebula so that:- builders can retrieve concrete implementation guidance,- architects can retrieve subsystem rationale and relationships,- inspectors/validators can retrieve invariants and migration constraints,- future harvests and work requests can cross-reference WRP material directly.This document therefore specifies:- the **projection model** from Conduit/WRP artifacts into Nebula;- the **`level` stratification model** for Nebula documents, chunks, and references;- the **artifact taxonomy** for WRP knowledge units;- the **retrieval policy** by role;- the **migration strategy** for the initial WRP corpus.---# 2. Context and Position in the StackThe working architectural chain is:```textNebula → WRP → Conduit → LOSM / runtime implementationwith the following responsibilities:Nebulalong-form architectural memorymarkdown-authored specificationschunked knowledge corpuscross-reference graphopen questions / unresolved decisionsretrieval substrate for planning and implementationWRP (Work Request Protocol / Work Request Package)canonical execution-facing representation of workprotocol, DAG model, traversal semantics, migration disciplinethe bridge between long-form intent and executable workConduitexecution-oriented work managerreceives concrete plans / work requeststracks dependencies, acceptance criteria, receipts, affected filesis not the authoritative home for large concept documentsLOSM / runtimeexecution engine, orchestration, persistence, validation, receiptsThe practical rule is:Nebula owns long-form architectural knowledge. Conduit owns executable work tracking. WRP is the formal bridge between the two.This document defines how that bridge is materialized in storage and retrieval.3. Design GoalsThe projection and stratification model must satisfy the following goals.G1. Preserve long-form WRP knowledge in NebulaThe WRP packet tracked in Conduit must be represented in Nebula as durable, queryable, versioned knowledge.G2. Preserve execution alignment with ConduitNebula entries must retain enough metadata to map back to the Conduit work packet(s) that implement them.G3. Support role-specific retrievalThe same corpus must serve multiple retrieval surfaces:Builder / implementerArchitect / plannerInspector / validatorExplorer / researcherG4. Separate abstraction levels cleanlyImplementation details should not drown architectural reasoning, and architectural rationale should not flood implementation prompts unless explicitly requested.G5. Preserve explicit cross-referencesProtocol rules, DAG semantics, traversal rules, migration tasks, invariants, and open questions must be linked explicitly rather than relying only on embedding similarity.G6. Remain compatible with the existing Nebula markdown-ingestion pipelineThis design should extend the existing markdown import / chunk / cross-reference model rather than replacing it.4. Core Decision4.1 Canonical ruleWRP artifacts are authored or curated as Nebula documents, then projected into Conduit as executable work packages.Conduit may hold the immediate execution plans, but Nebula remains the authoritative architectural memory for:protocol definitions,subsystem specs,migration rationale,invariants,open questions,design history.4.2 Projection directionThere are two distinct projection paths:A. Authoritative knowledge projectionNebula markdown/spec document→ Nebula document rows / chunks / cross references→ optional WRP artifact registration→ Conduit plan / work request generationB. Execution trace back-projectionConduit plan / execution receipt / implementation status→ WRP artifact linkage→ Nebula document metadata updates→ cross-linked execution referencesSo the system is not one-way. The long-form knowledge projects downward into executable work, and execution status projects upward into Nebula metadata and trace links.5. Scope of WRP Artifacts Covered by This SpecThis document covers the initial WRP corpus:WRP-1 — WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefines the formal work request protocol, message shape, identity, versioning, semantics, and lifecycle assumptions.WRP-2 — WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefines the DAG representation of work, node/edge semantics, compilation from protocol-level requests into executable graph structures, and compilation invariants.WRP-3 — WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefines the traversal/execution model over the WRP DAG, execution context, cursor/receipt semantics, deterministic traversal defaults, and isolation rules.WRP-4 — WRP Migration PlanDefines how existing work representations, legacy plans, or runtime workflows migrate into the WRP model with compatibility constraints and staged rollout.The schema and rules in this document are generic enough to apply to future WRP artifacts as well.6. Terminology6.1 Conduit PlanAn execution-oriented item managed by Conduit, typically containing:titleprojectaffected filesacceptance criteriadependenciesreceipt trail6.2 WRP ArtifactA versioned architectural / protocol artifact in the WRP family, such as:protocol specDAG model spectraversal engine specmigration planfuture validation / governance extensions6.3 Nebula DocumentA markdown-origin or spec-origin long-form document stored in Nebula.6.4 Nebula ChunkA chunked section or paragraph group extracted from a Nebula document for retrieval and cross-referencing.6.5 Cross ReferenceAn explicit semantic edge connecting one document/chunk/artifact to another, such as:“depends on”“implements”“constrains”“supersedes”“migrates”“explains”“references protocol field”“defines traversal invariant”6.6 LevelA stratification marker describing the abstraction level of a knowledge item.7. Level Stratification Model8. Rationale for Level StratificationWithout level stratification, a retrieval system operating over mixed architectural and implementation material tends to collapse the distinction between:“what the protocol means,”“how the DAG is represented,”“what code needs to change this week,”“why the migration strategy was chosen.”That leads to three recurring failures:Builders get too much theoryimplementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.Architects get too much local detailsubsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.Inspectors miss normative constraintsinvariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.A level field provides a stable, queryable abstraction boundary.9. Level DefinitionsThe first version of the level system usesfour levels.Level 1 — Execution / Build Detail (L1)Concrete implementation guidance and execution-facing material.Typical content:file-level implementation tasksendpoint contractsdataclass / schema detailsmethod signaturesSQL changesacceptance criteriatest casesmigration scriptsprecise repository change instructions“do this in package X” contentPrimary consumers:BuilderConduit executorimplementation-focused coding agentsLevel 2 — Subsystem Design (L2)Subsystem mechanics and technical design for a bounded domain.Typical content:DAG node/edge semanticscompilation pipeline structuretraversal algorithm designexecution receipt structurerole-specific service boundariesstorage mappings for a specific subsystemformal state transitions inside one bounded domainPrimary consumers:Builder (secondary)ArchitectInspectorLevel 3 — Architecture / Rationale (L3)Higher-order architectural reasoning, system relationships, and design justification.Typical content:why WRP existswhy DAG compilation is separate from traversalhow Conduit, Nebula, and LOSM relatemigration philosophy and rollout strategycross-subsystem responsibilitieslong-form tradeoff analysisarchitectural invariants spanning multiple packagesPrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerInspectorLevel 4 — Meta / Doctrine / Ontology (L4)Cross-cutting design doctrine, system philosophy, and ontology-level governance.Typical content:methodology rulesrole doctrinearchitectural constitution / invariants of invariantsontology rules for work, memory, or cognitionglobal modeling principlescross-project strategic doctrinePrimary consumers:ArchitectExplorerstrategic planner10. Level Assignment Rules10.1 Canonical ruleLevel belongs primarily to the content node, not to the retrieval query and not to the edge.That means:documents have levels,chunks have levels,references may optionally have level metadata, but level is not primarily an edge property.10.2 Single-primary-level ruleEvery document and every chunk must haveone primary level.This avoids ambiguous retrieval behavior and keeps filtering deterministic.10.3 Mixed documentsA long document may contain sections at different abstraction levels. Therefore:thedocumentreceives a default or dominant level;chunksmay override the document level when section content clearly belongs to a different level.Example:a WRP migration document may be primarilyL3,but its implementation checklist section may be chunked asL1.10.4 Edge neutrality ruleCross-reference edges should belevel-neutral by default.The edge describes the relationship; the source and target nodes carry the abstraction level.11. Recommended Level Mapping for the Initial WRP Corpus11.1 WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationDefault document level:L2Reasoning:it defines subsystem protocol semantics and normative message shape;it is not merely implementation detail;it is narrower than whole-system doctrine.Typical chunk-level overrides:formal field definitions / JSON examples / schema tables →L1rationale for protocol boundaries →L311.2 WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation PipelineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:compilation algorithm pseudocode →L2concrete data structures / storage tables / code mapping →L1rationale for DAG compilation as separate phase →L311.3 WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineDefault document level:L2Typical chunk-level overrides:ExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceiptstructures →L1orL2depending on specificitytraversal invariants / isolation rules →L2rationale for deterministic traversal and experimental modes →L311.4 WRP Migration PlanDefault document level:L3Reasoning:migration is a cross-cutting architectural transition strategy;the document explains sequencing, compatibility, and rollout discipline.Typical chunk-level overrides:actual migration tasks and repo changes →L1compatibility matrix / rollout constraints →L2migration philosophy and sequencing rationale →L312. Nebula Data Model ExtensionsThis section defines the required schema extensions to Nebula’s markdown-derived corpus.13. Target Nebula EntitiesThe projection model assumes the following logical entities exist or will exist:nebula_documentsnebula_chunksnebula_cross_referencesOptionally:nebula_artifactsnebula_open_questionsnebula_execution_linksThis document does not require a specific SQL dialect, but examples assume a relational store.14. Required Additions tonebula_documents14.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_documentsADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8)NOTNULLDEFAULT'L2',ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNartifact_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNartifact_versionVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNconduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNconduit_project_keyVARCHAR(255),ADDCOLUMNsource_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNsupersedes_document_id BIGINTNULL;14.2 Field semanticslevelPrimary abstraction level of the document.Allowed values:L1L2L3L4artifact_typeStable WRP artifact family identifier, e.g.:wrp.protocolwrp.dag_modelwrp.execution_enginewrp.migration_planartifact_keyStable logical identifier for the artifact, e.g.:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planartifact_versionHuman-visible version identifier, e.g.:1.01.11.22026-06conduit_plan_idOptional link to the Conduit execution plan primarily associated with the document.conduit_project_keyOptional grouping key for Conduit project membership.source_kindDescribes origin:markdowngenerated_specconduit_projectionimported_transcriptmanual_notestatusDocument lifecycle:draftcandidateapprovedsupersededarchivedsupersedes_document_idOptional pointer to the prior document version.15. Required Additions tonebula_chunks15.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_chunksADDCOLUMNlevelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNartifact_typeVARCHAR(128),ADDCOLUMNchunk_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNnormative_strengthVARCHAR(32),ADDCOLUMNsection_keyVARCHAR(255);15.2 Field semanticslevelChunk-level override. If null, inherit from the parent document.artifact_typeOptional denormalized copy of the parent artifact type for faster filtering.chunk_kindClassifies the chunk’s semantic role. Recommended values:overviewdefinitionprotocol_ruledata_modelalgorithminvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriaopen_questionexamplerationaleimplementation_notenormative_strengthOptional normative marker for validation-oriented retrieval:informativerecommendedrequiredprohibitedsection_keyStable section identity, e.g.:wrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.compilation-invariantswrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.migration.phase-2-cutover16. Required Additions tonebula_cross_references16.1 New fieldsSQLALTERTABLEnebula_cross_referencesADDCOLUMNrelation_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'references',ADDCOLUMNsource_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNtarget_levelVARCHAR(8),ADDCOLUMNweightDECIMAL(8,4),ADDCOLUMNevidence_kindVARCHAR(64),ADDCOLUMNstatusVARCHAR(32)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active';16.2 Why not a singlelevelon the edge?Because the edge itself is not the primary abstraction bearer. The useful information is usually:what level the source is,what level the target is,what relation binds them.Therefore, the preferred model is to carry:source_leveltarget_levelas denormalized convenience fields rather than treating the edge as an independently stratified knowledge unit.16.3 Field semanticsrelation_typeRecommended initial relation types:referencesdepends_onimplementsconstrainsdefinescompiled_intoexecutesmigratessupersedesvalidated_byraises_questionanswers_questionsource_level,target_levelOptional denormalized values copied from the linked nodes for efficient querying.weightOptional confidence or importance score.evidence_kindHow the edge was created:explicit_markdown_linkmanual_annotationartifact_projectionsemantic_matchreceipt_backlinkstatusactivesupersededtentative17. Optional New Table:nebula_artifactsIf WRP artifacts need to be treated as first-class entities independent of document versions, add a registry table.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_artifacts (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULLUNIQUE,artifact_typeVARCHAR(128)NOTNULL,current_versionVARCHAR(64),current_document_id BIGINT,statusVARCHAR(64)NOTNULLDEFAULT'active',created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL,updated_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Purpose:stable artifact identity across multiple document revisions,single lookup point for “the current WRP traversal spec,”easier version navigation and supersession tracking.18. Optional New Table:nebula_execution_linksThis table binds Nebula knowledge to execution artifacts and receipts.SQLCREATETABLEnebula_execution_links (id BIGINTPRIMARYKEYGENERATED ALWAYSASIDENTITY,artifact_keyVARCHAR(255)NOTNULL,document_id BIGINT,chunk_id BIGINT,conduit_plan_idVARCHAR(255),wrp_work_request_idVARCHAR(255),receipt_idVARCHAR(255),link_typeVARCHAR(64)NOTNULL,created_atTIMESTAMPNOTNULL);Recommendedlink_typevalues:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planvalidated_by_receiptsuperseded_by_planmigrated_by_requestThis table is not required for the first pass, but it becomes useful as soon as execution receipts start flowing back into Nebula.19. WRP Artifact TaxonomyEach WRP artifact projected into Nebula must declare a stable type.19.1 Initial artifact typesArtifact TypeMeaningwrp.protocolFormal WRP protocol definitionwrp.dag_modelDAG representation and compilation pipelinewrp.execution_engineTraversal / execution engine semanticswrp.migration_planWRP migration and rollout strategy19.2 Future extension typesExamples of likely future additions:Artifact TypeMeaningwrp.validation_rulesCross-artifact validation and policy ruleswrp.compatibility_matrixVersion compatibility / migration compatibilitywrp.receipt_modelFormal execution receipt modelwrp.role_contractsRole-specific work request / execution constraints20. Canonical WRP Artifact KeysThe initial corpus should use stable artifact keys.Artifact KeyArtifact TypeVersionwrp-v1-protocolwrp.protocol1.0wrp-v1_1-dagwrp.dag_model1.1wrp-v1_2-traversalwrp.execution_engine1.2wrp-migration-planwrp.migration_plan2026-06These keys should remain stable even if the underlying document path changes.21. Projection ModelThis section defines how WRP material moves from authored docs / Conduit plans into Nebula entities.22. Projection SourcesA WRP artifact may enter Nebula from one of three sources.Source A — Markdown-authored specThe preferred source. A curated markdown spec exists under the repo and is imported into Nebula.Source B — Conduit plan projectionA Conduit plan or work packet is projected into Nebula as a lightweight execution-facing document when no richer Nebula document exists yet.Source C — Manual or generated synthesisA generated or manually synthesized architecture note is imported and later normalized.The preferred order is:Markdown specGenerated synthesisConduit projection fallback23. Projection Pipeline StagesEvery WRP artifact projection follows the same high-level pipeline.Source artifact→ artifact registration→ document ingestion→ section extraction→ chunk creation→ level assignment→ cross-reference extraction→ Conduit link registration→ optional open-question extraction24. Stage 1 — Artifact RegistrationInput:artifact keyartifact typeversionsource path or source identifierOutput:canonical artifact registration recordlink to the current Nebula document versionRules:artifact keys must be stable;new versions should supersede, not overwrite, old document rows;the current version should be discoverable by artifact key.25. Stage 2 — Document IngestionThe source markdown/spec is stored as a Nebula document.Required metadata:artifact_typeartifact_keyartifact_versionsource_kindstatusdefaultlevelDocument title should remain human-readable, e.g.:WRP v1.0 Protocol FormalizationWRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation PipelineWRP v1.2 Execution Traversal EngineWRP Migration Plan26. Stage 3 — Section ExtractionSections should be extracted from headings and stable heading anchors.Recommended section key convention:<artifact family>.<major section slug>[.<subsection slug>...]Examples:wrp.protocol.overviewwrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningwrp.dag.node-typeswrp.dag.compilation-pipelinewrp.traversal.execution-contextwrp.traversal.isolation-ruleswrp.migration.phase-1-parallel-support27. Stage 4 — Chunk CreationChunks should be created with semantic sensitivity rather than purely fixed token windows.Recommended chunk boundaries:section intro / overview paragraph groupsdata model definitionsinvariant blocksalgorithm descriptionsmigration phase stepsexamplesacceptance criteria sectionsopen questions sectionsA chunk should not mix:a high-level architectural rationale paragraph,a concrete SQL alteration block,and an execution acceptance checklist.Those should become separate chunks with different levels andchunk_kindvalues.28. Stage 5 — Level AssignmentLevel assignment occurs in two passes.Pass A — Document default levelAssign the document’s dominant level based on artifact type and overall intent.Pass B — Chunk override levelOverride chunk level when a section clearly belongs to another abstraction layer.Heuristic examplesAssignL1when the chunk contains:repository pathsmethod signaturesschema alteration stepsexplicit implementation task sequencesacceptance criteria / test instructionsfield-by-field code mappingAssignL2when the chunk contains:formal subsystem structuresexecution algorithmsgraph semanticsstate transition rulesnormative subsystem invariantsAssignL3when the chunk contains:design rationalecross-subsystem tradeoffsmigration sequencing rationalearchitectural positioning of WRP relative to Conduit/Nebula/LOSMAssignL4when the chunk contains:system-wide doctrineontology-level policymeta-rules for work modeling or architectural governance29. Stage 6 — Cross-Reference ExtractionCross-references should be created from explicit and inferred signals.29.1 Explicit signalsmarkdown linkssection references“depends on”, “see also”, “constrained by”manually annotated relationships29.2 Inferred signalsartifact-key mentionssection-key referencesprotocol field names reused in traversal or migration docsrepeated formal identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt,tenant_id,trace_id29.3 Required WRP reference classesThe first pass must at least support:protocol field ↔ DAG compilation ruleDAG node/edge semantics ↔ traversal behaviortraversal invariant ↔ migration constraintmigration step ↔ affected WRP artifactWRP artifact ↔ Conduit plan implementing it30. Stage 7 — Conduit Link RegistrationEach projected WRP artifact should retain a link to the Conduit execution packet(s) responsible for implementation.Minimum metadata to retain:conduit_plan_idconduit_project_keyoptional receipt trail / execution link rowIf one Nebula artifact maps to multiple Conduit plans, use:document-level link to the primary umbrella planexecution-link rows for subordinate plans31. Stage 8 — Open Question ExtractionIf a WRP document contains unresolved design questions, they should be extracted into either:dedicatedopen_questionchunks, ora separatenebula_open_questionstable.Recommended fields for open questions:artifact_keydocument_idchunk_idquestion_textstatuspriorityowner_roleThis is especially relevant for migration uncertainties, protocol compatibility questions, and unresolved traversal policy decisions.32. Conduit → Nebula Projection RulesThis section defines how Conduit work packets map into Nebula when a WRP artifact is tracked for implementation.33. Conduit as Execution Metadata, Not Architectural AuthorityA Conduit plan is not automatically a Nebula document. Conduit should only project enough information into Nebula to preserve execution traceability.That means:Conduit ownsactive execution plan rowsacceptance criteriafile listsdependenciesexecution receiptsNebula ownsthe meaning of the WRP artifactthe long-form architecturecross-artifact relationshipsrationalechunk-level retrievability34. Minimal Projection of a Conduit Plan into NebulaFor each Conduit WRP work packet, Nebula should store:conduit_plan_idartifact_keyartifact_typestatusa short execution summarylinks to the authoritative WRP spec documentlinks to receipt or migration status if availableThis can be represented either:as metadata on the authoritative WRP document, oras a small auxiliary Nebula document ofsource_kind = conduit_projection.The first option is preferred for the initial implementation.35. Example Projection of the Initial WRP PacketSuppose Conduit contains four plans:CDT-WRP-001— WRP v1.0 protocol formalizationCDT-WRP-002— WRP v1.1 DAG model and compilation pipelineCDT-WRP-003— WRP v1.2 traversal engineCDT-WRP-004— WRP migration planNebula should contain at least:Document Atitle:WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalizationartifact key:wrp-v1-protocolartifact type:wrp.protocollevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-001Document Btitle:WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model and Compilation Pipelineartifact key:wrp-v1_1-dagartifact type:wrp.dag_modellevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-002Document Ctitle:WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal Engineartifact key:wrp-v1_2-traversalartifact type:wrp.execution_enginelevel:L2conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-003Document Dtitle:WRP Migration Planartifact key:wrp-migration-planartifact type:wrp.migration_planlevel:L3conduit_plan_id:CDT-WRP-004And explicit cross-references such as:wrp-v1_1-dagdepends_onwrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_2-traversalexecuteswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1-protocolwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_1-dagwrp-migration-planmigrateswrp-v1_2-traversal36. Required WRP Cross-Reference PatternsThe first implementation should explicitly emit the following relation families.36.1 Protocol → DAGExamples:protocol field or lifecycle state constrains DAG node constructionprotocol dependency semantics compiled into edge semanticsRelations:definesconstrainscompiled_into36.2 DAG → TraversalExamples:DAG node kinds determine traversal behaviorDAG execution order constraints are enforced by traversal rulesRelations:definesexecutesconstrains36.3 Traversal → Receipt / ValidationExamples:execution cursor produces execution receipt shapetraversal invariants determine receipt hierarchy or failure semanticsRelations:definesvalidated_by36.4 Migration → All WRP ArtifactsExamples:migration phases refer to protocol changes, DAG compatibility, traversal rolloutRelations:migratessupersedesconstrains36.5 WRP Artifact → Conduit PlanExamples:a Nebula artifact is being implemented by one or more Conduit plansRelations:implemented_by_plantracked_by_planThese may live innebula_execution_linksrather than the main cross-reference table if the execution linkage is operational rather than semantic.37. Role-Based Retrieval PolicyThis is the operational reason for level stratification.38. Builder Retrieval Profile38.1 GoalProvide concrete implementation guidance with only enough architectural context to avoid coding blind.38.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L1Secondary levels:L2ExcludeL3/L4unless:the retrievedL1/L2chunk explicitly references an architectural invariant, orthe prompt requests rationale or migration context38.3 Preferred chunk kindsimplementation_notedata_modelprotocol_rulealgorithmacceptance_criteriamigration_step38.4 Typical use casesimplement WRP protocol DTOsbuild DAG compiler classesadd traversal engine structureswrite migration scripts and tests39. Architect Retrieval Profile39.1 GoalProvide subsystem design and cross-artifact reasoning without drowning in file-level implementation noise.39.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3Optional expansion toL1for concrete examplesOptional expansion toL4for doctrine or ontology alignment39.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewdefinitiondata_modelalgorithminvariantrationaleopen_question39.4 Typical use casesrefine WRP semanticsunderstand why traversal is separated from DAG compilationreason about Conduit/Nebula/LOSM alignmentevaluate migration sequence40. Inspector / Validator Retrieval Profile40.1 GoalRetrieve normative constraints, invariants, and compatibility conditions.40.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3IncludeL1only when validation depends on concrete schema or implementation details40.3 Preferred chunk kindsprotocol_ruleinvariantmigration_stepacceptance_criteriadata_model40.4 Normative preferencePrefer chunks where:normative_strength = requirednormative_strength = prohibited40.5 Typical use casesverify WRP compatibility rulesvalidate migration sequencingenforce traversal invariantsdetect protocol / DAG / traversal mismatch41. Explorer Retrieval Profile41.1 GoalSupport open-ended investigation across architecture, rationale, and unresolved questions.41.2 Default retrieval policyPrimary levels:L2,L3,L4IncludeL1only if the search narrows to implementation mechanics41.3 Preferred chunk kindsoverviewrationaleopen_questiondefinitionexample42. Suggested Retrieval AlgorithmA role-aware retrieval query should combine:artifact filteringe.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')level filteringrole-dependent level setchunk kind weightingrole-specific preferred chunk kindsnormative weightingfor validator/inspector profilescross-reference expansionbounded traversal across explicit edgesexecution recency boostoptional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in ConduitPseudo-policy:candidate_chunks =filter by artifact family / lexical relevance / embedding relevance∩ filter by allowed levels for roleweighted by chunk_kind preferenceweighted by normative_strength where applicableexpanded by explicit cross-reference traversal depth <= NRecommended initial traversal depths:Builder:N = 1Architect:N = 2Inspector:N = 2Explorer:N = 343. Worked Example: Retrieval for WRP Traversal ImplementationUser intent:“Implement the traversal engine for WRP v1.2.”Builder profile should retrieve:WRP v1.2chunks describingExecutionContext,ExecutionCursor,ExecutionReceipttraversal order semanticsdeterministic traversal defaultisolation rule chunksmigration notes only if they affect implementation compatibilityArchitect profile should additionally retrieve:the WRP DAG document sections that define node and edge semanticsrationale for why traversal is a separate stagemigration constraints affecting rolloutInspector profile should emphasize:invariant chunks such as tenant isolation rulesfailure semanticsreceipt completeness rulescompatibility constraints in the migration plan44. Worked Example: WRP v1.2 Chunking and Level AssignmentConsider a traversal-engine document with these sections:OverviewExecutionContextExecutionCursorTraversal order and pending queue semanticsTenant isolationExperimental policy modeWhy traversal is separate from DAG compilationImplementation checklistRecommended chunking:SectionChunk KindLevelOverviewoverviewL2ExecutionContextdata_modelL2ExecutionCursordata_modelL2Traversal order and pending queue semanticsalgorithmL2Tenant isolationinvariantL2Experimental policy modedefinition/invariantL2Why traversal is separate from DAG compilationrationaleL3Implementation checklistimplementation_note/acceptance_criteriaL145. WRP-Specific Normative MarkingTo make validation retrieval effective, WRP chunks should mark normative strength where appropriate.Examples:requiredtraversal must enforce tenant isolation at execution timeprotocol version must be present in every WRP root requestDAG compilation must reject cycles if the WRP graph is defined as acyclicprohibitedtraversal must not execute a node under the wrong tenant contextmigration must not remove legacy compatibility before the designated cutover phaserecommendedbuilders should prefer deterministic traversal order unless explicitly in experimental modeinformativehistorical rationale and examples46. Back-Projection from Execution into NebulaOnce Conduit and runtime begin executing WRP work, Nebula should be updated with execution traceability.Examples:a Conduit plan completes implementation ofwrp-v1_2-traversalan execution receipt validates a traversal invarianta migration work request supersedes an older compatibility ruleThese should produce:document status updates,execution links,optional new cross-references,optional “implementation evidence” annotations.This should be append-only where possible; do not rewrite architectural history.47. Initial Migration Plan for the Existing WRP PacketThis section defines the first practical rollout for the four WRP artifacts already placed into Conduit.48. Phase 1 — Register the Four WRP ArtifactsCreate Nebula artifact/document records for:wrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planAt minimum, store:titleartifact typeartifact keyversiondefault levelconduit plan idsource kindstatus49. Phase 2 — Import the Authoritative WRP Markdown DocumentsFor each artifact, import the corresponding markdown spec into Nebula.If a markdown spec does not yet exist in repo form, use a temporary generated or manually curated document, but treat that as a stopgap. The target steady state is:WRP architectural material lives as markdown/spec documents in Nebula, not only as Conduit plan descriptions.50. Phase 3 — Chunk and Level the DocumentsRun the markdown importer with:section extractionsemantic chunkingchunk kind assignmentchunk-level level override assignmentnormative strength tagging for invariant sectionsDo not leave WRP material as giant undifferentiated chunks.51. Phase 4 — Emit Required Cross ReferencesAt minimum, emit:protocol → DAG edgesDAG → traversal edgesmigration → protocol/DAG/traversal edgesWRP artifact → Conduit plan links52. Phase 5 — Add Role-Aware Retrieval FiltersAdd query support for:allowed levelspreferred chunk kindsoptional normative strength weightingbounded cross-reference expansionThis is the point where “Builder sees implementation detail; Architect sees architecture” becomes real.53. Phase 6 — Backfill Execution LinksOnce Conduit begins implementing the packet, attach:plan IDsreceipt trailsstatus updatesimplementation evidence linksto the corresponding WRP artifacts in Nebula.54.
