Suggested Application-Level TypesThe following are reference shapes for the application layer.55.1 Document level enumJavapublicenumKnowledgeLevel{L1,// execution/build detailL2,// subsystem designL3,// architecture/rationaleL4// doctrine/ontology}55.2 Artifact type enumJavapublicenumArtifactType{WRP_PROTOCOL,WRP_DAG_MODEL,WRP_EXECUTION_ENGINE,WRP_MIGRATION_PLAN}55.3 Chunk kind enumJavapublicenumChunkKind{OVERVIEW,DEFINITION,PROTOCOL_RULE,DATA_MODEL,ALGORITHM,INVARIANT,MIGRATION_STEP,ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA,OPEN_QUESTION,EXAMPLE,RATIONALE,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE}55.4 Normative strength enumJavapublicenumNormativeStrength{INFORMATIVE,RECOMMENDED,REQUIRED,PROHIBITED}56. Suggested Projection DTOsJavapublicrecordNebulaArtifactRegistration(StringartifactKey,ArtifactTypeartifactType,StringartifactVersion,StringsourcePath,StringsourceKind,StringconduitPlanId,StringconduitProjectKey,KnowledgeLeveldefaultLevel) {}JavapublicrecordNebulaChunkProjection(LongdocumentId,StringsectionKey,ChunkKindchunkKind,KnowledgeLevellevel,NormativeStrengthnormativeStrength,Stringcontent) {}JavapublicrecordNebulaCrossReferenceProjection(StringsourceSectionKey,StringtargetSectionKey,StringrelationType,KnowledgeLevelsourceLevel,KnowledgeLeveltargetLevel,StringevidenceKind,Doubleweight) {}57. InvariantsThe following invariants apply to the Conduit → Nebula WRP projection model.I1. Nebula is the authoritative long-form memory for WRPConduit may track execution, but architectural WRP meaning must remain represented in Nebula.I2. Every WRP artifact must have a stable artifact keyPaths may change; artifact identity must not.I3. Every Nebula document and chunk must have a deterministic effective levelA chunk either declares a level or inherits from its document.I4. Cross-reference edges are level-neutral by defaultThe source and target nodes carry the abstraction semantics.I5. The initial WRP packet must be explicitly cross-linkedProtocol, DAG, traversal, and migration documents must not exist as isolated documents.I6. Role-aware retrieval must filter by level before broad cross-reference expansionOtherwise the stratification model loses value.I7. Execution traceability must be additive, not destructiveImplementation evidence and receipts should enrich architectural records rather than overwrite them.58. What This Unlocks NextOnce this projection and stratification layer exists, the system can do all of the following coherently:Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.59. Bottom LineThe four WRP plans now sitting in Conduit should be treated as theexecution packetfor a broader WRP knowledge corpus. The missing piece is a projection layer that makes those artifacts durable and queryable inside Nebula.The core model is simple:Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledgeConduit stores the executable work packetWRP artifacts provide the stable identity between themlevelstratification controls who sees whatcross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graphThat is the foundation required before WRP can function as a real architectural substrate rather than just a set of implementation plans.---## What I’d do immediately after this oneSince those four WRP plans are now in Conduit and will take a bit to implement under your local Ollama/OpenCode/Qwen setup, the next companion spec I’d write is the **actual Nebula schema/ontology patch** for this document, not another prose architecture note.Specifically:# `schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonld`That doc should formalize, in machine-oriented ontology form:- `KnowledgeLevel`- `ArtifactType`- `ChunkKind`- `NormativeStrength`- `CrossReferenceRelationType`- `NebulaDocument`- `NebulaChunk`- `NebulaArtifact`- `NebulaExecutionLink`and the exact fields/relationships implied by the markdown spec above.If you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it **repo-ready JSON-LD** rather than another markdown doc.

Absolutely. Given that Conduit is execution-oriented and the real long-form knowledge belongs in Nebula, I’d treat this as thebridge specbetween the four WRP implementation plans now sitting in Conduit and the stratified knowledge corpus Nebula needs to become.

# 3. Design Goals

The projection and stratification model must satisfy the following goals.

## G1. Preserve long-form WRP knowledge in Nebula

The WRP packet tracked in Conduit must be represented in Nebula as durable, queryable, versioned knowledge.

## G2. Preserve execution alignment with Conduit

Nebula entries must retain enough metadata to map back to the Conduit work packet(s) that implement them.

## G3. Support role-specific retrieval

The same corpus must serve multiple retrieval surfaces:

- Builder / implementer
Builder / implementer

- Architect / planner
Architect / planner

- Inspector / validator
Inspector / validator

- Explorer / researcher
Explorer / researcher

## G4. Separate abstraction levels cleanly

Implementation details should not drown architectural reasoning, and architectural rationale should not flood implementation prompts unless explicitly requested.

## G5. Preserve explicit cross-references

Protocol rules, DAG semantics, traversal rules, migration tasks, invariants, and open questions must be linked explicitly rather than relying only on embedding similarity.

## G6. Remain compatible with the existing Nebula markdown-ingestion pipeline

This design should extend the existing markdown import / chunk / cross-reference model rather than replacing it.

---

# 4. Core Decision

## 4.1 Canonical rule

WRP artifacts are authored or curated as Nebula documents, then projected into Conduit as executable work packages.

Conduit may hold the immediate execution plans, but Nebula remains the authoritative architectural memory for:

- protocol definitions,
protocol definitions,

- subsystem specs,
subsystem specs,

- migration rationale,
migration rationale,

- invariants,
invariants,

- open questions,
open questions,

- design history.
design history.

## 4.2 Projection direction

There are two distinct projection paths:

### A. Authoritative knowledge projection

```
Nebula markdown/spec document    → Nebula document rows / chunks / cross references    → optional WRP artifact registration    → Conduit plan / work request generation
```

```
Nebula markdown/spec document    → Nebula document rows / chunks / cross references    → optional WRP artifact registration    → Conduit plan / work request generation
```

### B. Execution trace back-projection

```
Conduit plan / execution receipt / implementation status    → WRP artifact linkage    → Nebula document metadata updates    → cross-linked execution references
```

```
Conduit plan / execution receipt / implementation status    → WRP artifact linkage    → Nebula document metadata updates    → cross-linked execution references
```

So the system is not one-way. The long-form knowledge projects downward into executable work, and execution status projects upward into Nebula metadata and trace links.

---

# 5. Scope of WRP Artifacts Covered by This Spec

This document covers the initial WRP corpus:

## WRP-1 — WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization

Defines the formal work request protocol, message shape, identity, versioning, semantics, and lifecycle assumptions.

## WRP-2 — WRP v1.1 DAG Data Model & Compilation Pipeline

Defines the DAG representation of work, node/edge semantics, compilation from protocol-level requests into executable graph structures, and compilation invariants.

## WRP-3 — WRP v1.2 Execution Traversal Engine

Defines the traversal/execution model over the WRP DAG, execution context, cursor/receipt semantics, deterministic traversal defaults, and isolation rules.

## WRP-4 — WRP Migration Plan

Defines how existing work representations, legacy plans, or runtime workflows migrate into the WRP model with compatibility constraints and staged rollout.

The schema and rules in this document are generic enough to apply to future WRP artifacts as well.

# 7. Level Stratification Model

---

# 8. Rationale for Level Stratification

Without level stratification, a retrieval system operating over mixed architectural and implementation material tends to collapse the distinction between:

- “what the protocol means,”
“what the protocol means,”

- “how the DAG is represented,”
“how the DAG is represented,”

- “what code needs to change this week,”
“what code needs to change this week,”

- “why the migration strategy was chosen.”
“why the migration strategy was chosen.”

That leads to three recurring failures:

- Builders get too much theoryimplementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.
Builders get too much theory

- implementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.
implementation prompts fill with architecture prose and migration history.

- Architects get too much local detailsubsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.
Architects get too much local detail

- subsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.
subsystem reasoning is polluted by file-level implementation instructions.

- Inspectors miss normative constraintsinvariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.
Inspectors miss normative constraints

- invariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.
invariants and compatibility rules are not distinguished from general descriptive prose.

A level field provides a stable, queryable abstraction boundary.

---

# 10. Level Assignment Rules

## 10.1 Canonical rule

Level belongs primarily to the content node, not to the retrieval query and not to the edge.

That means:

- documents have levels,
documents have levels,

- chunks have levels,
chunks have levels,

- references may optionally have level metadata, but level is not primarily an edge property.
references may optionally have level metadata, but level is not primarily an edge property.

## 10.2 Single-primary-level rule

Every document and every chunk must haveone primary level.

This avoids ambiguous retrieval behavior and keeps filtering deterministic.

## 10.3 Mixed documents

A long document may contain sections at different abstraction levels. Therefore:

- thedocumentreceives a default or dominant level;
thedocumentreceives a default or dominant level;

- chunksmay override the document level when section content clearly belongs to a different level.
chunksmay override the document level when section content clearly belongs to a different level.

Example:

- a WRP migration document may be primarilyL3,
a WRP migration document may be primarilyL3,

- but its implementation checklist section may be chunked asL1.
but its implementation checklist section may be chunked asL1.

## 10.4 Edge neutrality rule

Cross-reference edges should belevel-neutral by default.The edge describes the relationship; the source and target nodes carry the abstraction level.

Default document level:L2

Reasoning:

- it defines subsystem protocol semantics and normative message shape;
it defines subsystem protocol semantics and normative message shape;

- it is not merely implementation detail;
it is not merely implementation detail;

it is narrower than whole-system doctrine.

Typical chunk-level overrides:

- formal field definitions / JSON examples / schema tables →L1
formal field definitions / JSON examples / schema tables →L1

rationale for protocol boundaries →L3

Default document level:L2

Typical chunk-level overrides:

- compilation algorithm pseudocode →L2
compilation algorithm pseudocode →L2

- concrete data structures / storage tables / code mapping →L1
concrete data structures / storage tables / code mapping →L1

rationale for DAG compilation as separate phase →L3

Default document level:L2

- traversal invariants / isolation rules →L2
traversal invariants / isolation rules →L2

rationale for deterministic traversal and experimental modes →L3

## 11.4 WRP Migration Plan

Default document level:L3

Reasoning:

- migration is a cross-cutting architectural transition strategy;
migration is a cross-cutting architectural transition strategy;

- the document explains sequencing, compatibility, and rollout discipline.
the document explains sequencing, compatibility, and rollout discipline.

Typical chunk-level overrides:

actual migration tasks and repo changes →L1

Because the edge itself is not the primary abstraction bearer. The useful information is usually:

- what level the source is,

- what level the target is,

- what relation binds them.
what relation binds them.

Therefore, the preferred model is to carry:

- source_level
source_level

- target_level
target_level

as denormalized convenience fields rather than treating the edge as an independently stratified knowledge unit.

# 21. Projection Model

This section defines how WRP material moves from authored docs / Conduit plans into Nebula entities.

---

# 22. Projection Sources

A WRP artifact may enter Nebula from one of three sources.

## Source A — Markdown-authored spec

The preferred source. A curated markdown spec exists under the repo and is imported into Nebula.

## Source B — Conduit plan projection

A Conduit plan or work packet is projected into Nebula as a lightweight execution-facing document when no richer Nebula document exists yet.

## Source C — Manual or generated synthesis

A generated or manually synthesized architecture note is imported and later normalized.

The preferred order is:

- Markdown spec
Markdown spec

- Generated synthesis
Generated synthesis

# 23. Projection Pipeline Stages

Every WRP artifact projection follows the same high-level pipeline.

```
Source artifact  → artifact registration  → document ingestion  → section extraction  → chunk creation  → level assignment  → cross-reference extraction  → Conduit link registration  → optional open-question extraction
```

```
Source artifact  → artifact registration  → document ingestion  → section extraction  → chunk creation  → level assignment  → cross-reference extraction  → Conduit link registration  → optional open-question extraction
```

- link to the current Nebula document version
link to the current Nebula document version

- artifact keys must be stable;
artifact keys must be stable;

new versions should supersede, not overwrite, old document rows;

# 42. Suggested Retrieval Algorithm

A role-aware retrieval query should combine:

- artifact filteringe.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')
artifact filtering

- e.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')
e.g.artifact_type in ('wrp.protocol','wrp.dag_model')

- level filteringrole-dependent level set
level filtering

- role-dependent level set
role-dependent level set

- chunk kind weightingrole-specific preferred chunk kinds
chunk kind weighting

- role-specific preferred chunk kinds
role-specific preferred chunk kinds

- normative weightingfor validator/inspector profiles
normative weighting

- for validator/inspector profiles
for validator/inspector profiles

- cross-reference expansionbounded traversal across explicit edges
cross-reference expansion

- bounded traversal across explicit edges
bounded traversal across explicit edges

- execution recency boostoptional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in Conduit
execution recency boost

- optional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in Conduit
optional boost for artifacts actively being implemented in Conduit

Pseudo-policy:

```
candidate_chunks =    filter by artifact family / lexical relevance / embedding relevance    ∩ filter by allowed levels for role    weighted by chunk_kind preference    weighted by normative_strength where applicable    expanded by explicit cross-reference traversal depth <= N
```

```
candidate_chunks =    filter by artifact family / lexical relevance / embedding relevance    ∩ filter by allowed levels for role    weighted by chunk_kind preference    weighted by normative_strength where applicable    expanded by explicit cross-reference traversal depth <= N
```

Recommended initial traversal depths:

- Builder:N = 1

- Architect:N = 2

- Inspector:N = 2
Inspector:N = 2

- Explorer:N = 3
Explorer:N = 3

# 45. WRP-Specific Normative Marking

To make validation retrieval effective, WRP chunks should mark normative strength where appropriate.

Examples:

## required

- traversal must enforce tenant isolation at execution time
traversal must enforce tenant isolation at execution time

- protocol version must be present in every WRP root request
protocol version must be present in every WRP root request

- DAG compilation must reject cycles if the WRP graph is defined as acyclic
DAG compilation must reject cycles if the WRP graph is defined as acyclic

## prohibited

- traversal must not execute a node under the wrong tenant context
traversal must not execute a node under the wrong tenant context

- migration must not remove legacy compatibility before the designated cutover phase
migration must not remove legacy compatibility before the designated cutover phase

## recommended

- builders should prefer deterministic traversal order unless explicitly in experimental mode
builders should prefer deterministic traversal order unless explicitly in experimental mode

## informative

- historical rationale and examples
historical rationale and examples

- an execution receipt validates a traversal invariant
an execution receipt validates a traversal invariant

- a migration work request supersedes an older compatibility rule
a migration work request supersedes an older compatibility rule

- document status updates,
document status updates,

execution links,

optional new cross-references,

optional “implementation evidence” annotations.

# 57. Invariants

The following invariants apply to the Conduit → Nebula WRP projection model.

## I1. Nebula is the authoritative long-form memory for WRP

Conduit may track execution, but architectural WRP meaning must remain represented in Nebula.

## I2. Every WRP artifact must have a stable artifact key

Paths may change; artifact identity must not.

## I3. Every Nebula document and chunk must have a deterministic effective level

A chunk either declares a level or inherits from its document.

## I4. Cross-reference edges are level-neutral by default

The source and target nodes carry the abstraction semantics.

## I5. The initial WRP packet must be explicitly cross-linked

Protocol, DAG, traversal, and migration documents must not exist as isolated documents.

## I6. Role-aware retrieval must filter by level before broad cross-reference expansion

Otherwise the stratification model loses value.

## I7. Execution traceability must be additive, not destructive

Implementation evidence and receipts should enrich architectural records rather than overwrite them.

---

# 58. What This Unlocks Next

Once this projection and stratification layer exists, the system can do all of the following coherently:

- Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.
Treat the WRP packet in Conduit as first-class Nebula knowledgerather than four disconnected implementation tasks.

- Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.
Retrieve different WRP context for different rolesso Builder, Architect, and Inspector stop stepping on each other.

- Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.
Project future WRP work automaticallyfrom Nebula-authored docs into execution-facing Conduit work requests.

- Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.
Back-link implementation evidenceso WRP architectural docs can show what has actually been built.

- Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.
Use Nebula as the long-term architectural substratewhile Conduit remains focused on execution.

# 59. Bottom Line

The four WRP plans now sitting in Conduit should be treated as theexecution packetfor a broader WRP knowledge corpus. The missing piece is a projection layer that makes those artifacts durable and queryable inside Nebula.

The core model is simple:

- Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledge
Nebula stores the long-form WRP knowledge

- Conduit stores the executable work packet
Conduit stores the executable work packet

- WRP artifacts provide the stable identity between them
WRP artifacts provide the stable identity between them

- levelstratification controls who sees what
levelstratification controls who sees what

- cross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graph
cross-references turn the four documents into a navigable WRP knowledge graph

That is the foundation required before WRP can function as a real architectural substrate rather than just a set of implementation plans.

the repoI’d put a short companion markdown right next to it, because the JSON-LD should be aformal graph contract, not the only place where the rules are explained.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.mdAnd I’d keep that doc very focused onprojection semantics and implementation obligations:1. Purposethis JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links2. Canonical interpretation rulesNebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisionsNebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form contentNebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a documentNebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edgeNebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts3. Level rulesdocuments have default levelschunks may override levelscross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections4. WRP artifact registry obligationsartifact keys are stabledocument revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in placecurrentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision5. Retrieval implicationsBuilder → L1 + selective L2Architect → L2/L3Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunksExplorer → L2/L3/L4A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into codeThere aretwo immediate refinementsI’d make, because they’ll matter once you start projecting real WRP docs into Nebula.1) Split ontology classes from seed instancesRight now, for convenience, I included both:theschema vocabularyand theinitial four WRP artifact instancesin one file.For the actual repo, I’d split that into:A.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonldOnly classes + properties + enumsand thenB.data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldThe four seeded artifact instanceswrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planThat separation is cleaner because the schema remains stable while the bootstrap artifact registry evolves.2) Add an explicit retrieval-profile ontologyBecause you’ve now got a real level model, the next useful machine-readable layer is therole/query projection surface.I would make the next schema:schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldwith classes like:RetrievalProfileBuilderProfileArchitectProfileInspectorProfileExplorerProfileand properties like:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthcrossReferenceExpansionDepthallowExecutionRecencyBoostallowOpenQuestionsallowRationaleChunksThat would let the “Inspector cares about JSON-LD” instinct become concrete: not just a role in prose, but a formal retrieval/projection contract over Nebula.My recommended next sequence from hereSince you’ve already got the four WRP plans cooking in Conduit, I’d keep the companion artifacts tightly scoped and move in this order:Next 1data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldSeed the four WRP artifact instances separately from the ontology.Next 2schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldFormalize Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer retrieval profiles.Next 3docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdA concrete importer spec:markdown heading →sectionKeychunking ruleslevel assignment heuristicsnormative strength extractioncross-reference extraction rulesNext 4schemas/core/nebula-cross-reference-relations.jsonldIf you want the relation system to grow beyond WRP, pull relation types into their own ontology file.If you want, I’ll go straight to the next one and writedata/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldfirst, then the retrieval profile ontology after that.SourcesApryseSponsoredPreprocess Documents for RAG PipelinesTurn PDFs into clean structured data for retrieval-augmented generation pipelines.

Thought for 5sAbsolutely — the right next artifact is themachine-oriented ontology/schema companionfor the markdown spec we just pinned down.Given your own framing from earlier, I’m going to keep the JSON-LD side as theexternal graph/persistence targetfor Nebula/PEB rather than treating it like the authored source of truth. So this file is theprojection contract / ontology shapefor WRP-aware Nebula knowledge, not an invitation to author the system directly in JSON-LD.Below is arepo-ready first the repoI’d put a short companion markdown right next to it, because the JSON-LD should be aformal graph contract, not the only place where the rules are explained.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.mdAnd I’d keep that doc very focused onprojection semantics and implementation obligations:1. Purposethis JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links2. Canonical interpretation rulesNebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisionsNebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form contentNebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a documentNebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edgeNebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts3. Level rulesdocuments have default levelschunks may override levelscross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections4. WRP artifact registry obligationsartifact keys are stabledocument revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in placecurrentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision5. Retrieval implicationsBuilder → L1 + selective L2Architect → L2/L3Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunksExplorer → L2/L3/L4A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into codeThere aretwo immediate refinementsI’d make, because they’ll matter once you start projecting real WRP docs into Nebula.1) Split ontology classes from seed instancesRight now, for convenience, I included both:theschema vocabularyand theinitial four WRP artifact instancesin one file.For the actual repo, I’d split that into:A.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonldOnly classes + properties + enumsand thenB.data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldThe four seeded artifact instanceswrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planThat separation is cleaner because the schema remains stable while the bootstrap artifact registry evolves.2) Add an explicit retrieval-profile ontologyBecause you’ve now got a real level model, the next useful machine-readable layer is therole/query projection surface.I would make the next schema:schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldwith classes like:RetrievalProfileBuilderProfileArchitectProfileInspectorProfileExplorerProfileand properties like:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthcrossReferenceExpansionDepthallowExecutionRecencyBoostallowOpenQuestionsallowRationaleChunksThat would let the “Inspector cares about JSON-LD” instinct become concrete: not just a role in prose, but a formal retrieval/projection contract over Nebula.My recommended next sequence from hereSince you’ve already got the four WRP plans cooking in Conduit, I’d keep the companion artifacts tightly scoped and move in this order:Next 1data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldSeed the four WRP artifact instances separately from the ontology.Next 2schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldFormalize Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer retrieval profiles.Next 3docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdA concrete importer spec:markdown heading →sectionKeychunking ruleslevel assignment heuristicsnormative strength extractioncross-reference extraction rulesNext 4schemas/core/nebula-cross-reference-relations.jsonldIf you want the relation system to grow beyond WRP, pull relation types into their own ontology file.If you want, I’ll go straight to the next one and writedata/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldfirst, then the retrieval profile ontology after that.SourcesApryseSponsoredPreprocess Documents for RAG PipelinesTurn PDFs into clean structured data for retrieval-augmented generation pipelines.

Thought for 5sAbsolutely — the right next artifact is themachine-oriented ontology/schema companionfor the markdown spec we just pinned down.Given your own framing from earlier, I’m going to keep the JSON-LD side as theexternal graph/persistence targetfor Nebula/PEB rather than treating it like the authored source of truth. So this file is theprojection contract / ontology shapefor WRP-aware Nebula knowledge, not an invitation to author the system directly in JSON-LD.Below is arepo-ready first included both:theschema vocabularyand theinitial four WRP artifact instancesin one file.For the actual repo, I’d split that into:A.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonldOnly classes + properties + enumsand thenB.data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldThe four seeded artifact instanceswrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planThat separation is the repoI’d put a short companion markdown right next to it, because the JSON-LD should be aformal graph contract, not the only place where the rules are explained.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.mdAnd I’d keep that doc very focused onprojection semantics and implementation obligations:1. Purposethis JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links2. Canonical interpretation rulesNebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisionsNebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form contentNebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a documentNebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edgeNebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts3. Level rulesdocuments have default levelschunks may override levelscross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections4. WRP artifact registry obligationsartifact keys are stabledocument revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in placecurrentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision5. Retrieval implicationsBuilder → L1 + selective L2Architect → L2/L3Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunksExplorer → L2/L3/L4A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into codeThere aretwo immediate refinementsI’d make, because they’ll matter once you start projecting real WRP docs into Nebula.1) Split ontology classes from seed instancesRight now, for convenience, I included both:theschema vocabularyand theinitial four WRP artifact instancesin one file.For the actual repo, I’d split that into:A.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonldOnly classes + properties + enumsand thenB.data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldThe four seeded artifact instanceswrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planThat separation is cleaner because the schema remains stable while the bootstrap artifact registry evolves.2) Add an explicit retrieval-profile ontologyBecause you’ve now got a real level model, the next useful machine-readable layer is therole/query projection surface.I would make the next schema:schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldwith classes like:RetrievalProfileBuilderProfileArchitectProfileInspectorProfileExplorerProfileand properties like:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthcrossReferenceExpansionDepthallowExecutionRecencyBoostallowOpenQuestionsallowRationaleChunksThat would let the “Inspector cares about JSON-LD” instinct become concrete: not just a role in prose, but a formal retrieval/projection contract over Nebula.My recommended next sequence from hereSince you’ve already got the four WRP plans cooking in Conduit, I’d keep the companion artifacts tightly scoped and move in this order:Next 1data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldSeed the four WRP artifact instances separately from the ontology.Next 2schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldFormalize Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer retrieval profiles.Next 3docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdA concrete importer spec:markdown heading →sectionKeychunking ruleslevel assignment heuristicsnormative strength extractioncross-reference extraction rulesNext 4schemas/core/nebula-cross-reference-relations.jsonldIf you want the relation system to grow beyond WRP, pull relation types into their own ontology file.If you want, I’ll go straight to the next one and writedata/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldfirst, then the retrieval profile ontology after that.

Absolutely — the right next artifact is themachine-oriented ontology/schema companionfor the markdown spec we just pinned down.Given your own framing from earlier, I’m going to keep the JSON-LD side as theexternal graph/persistence targetfor Nebula/PEB rather than treating it like the authored source of truth. So this file is theprojection contract / ontology shapefor WRP-aware Nebula knowledge, not an invitation to author the system directly in JSON-LD.Below is arepo-ready first explained.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.mdAnd I’d keep that doc very focused onprojection semantics and implementation obligations:1. Purposethis JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links2. Canonical interpretation rulesNebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisionsNebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form contentNebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a documentNebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edgeNebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts3. Level rulesdocuments have default levelschunks may override levelscross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections4. WRP artifact registry obligationsartifact keys are stabledocument revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in placecurrentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision5. Retrieval implicationsBuilder → L1 + selective L2Architect → L2/L3Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunksExplorer → L2/L3/L4A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into codeThere aretwo immediate refinementsI’d make, because they’ll matter once you start projecting real WRP docs into Nebula.1) Split ontology classes from seed instancesRight now, for convenience, I included both:theschema vocabularyand theinitial four WRP artifact instancesin one file.For the actual repo, I’d split that into:A.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonldOnly classes + properties + enumsand thenB.data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonldThe four seeded artifact instanceswrp-v1-protocolwrp-v1_1-dagwrp-v1_2-traversalwrp-migration-planThat separation is cleaner because the schema remains stable while the bootstrap artifact registry evolves.2) Add an explicit retrieval-profile ontologyBecause you’ve now got a real level model, the next useful machine-readable layer is therole/query projection surface.I would make the next schema:schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldwith classes like:RetrievalProfileBuilderProfileArchitectProfileInspectorProfileExplorerProfileand properties like:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthcrossReferenceExpansionDepthallowExecutionRecencyBoostallowOpenQuestionsallowRationaleChunksThat would let the “Inspector cares about Given your own framing from earlier, I’m going to keep the JSON-LD side as theexternal graph/persistence targetfor Nebula/PEB rather than treating it like the authored source of truth. So this file is theprojection contract / ontology shapefor WRP-aware Nebula knowledge, not an invitation to author the system directly in JSON-LD.

# Companion notes for the repo

I’d put a short companion markdown right next to it, because the JSON-LD should be aformal graph contract, not the only place where the rules are explained.

## schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.md

And I’d keep that doc very focused onprojection semantics and implementation obligations:

### 1. Purpose

- this JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:level stratificationWRP artifact identitychunk classificationnormative strengthcross-reference relation typesexecution links
this JSON-LD defines the Nebula graph vocabulary for:

- level stratification
level stratification

- WRP artifact identity
WRP artifact identity

- chunk classification
chunk classification

- normative strength
normative strength

- cross-reference relation types
cross-reference relation types

- execution links
execution links

### 2. Canonical interpretation rules

- NebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisions
NebulaArtifact= stable logical identity across document revisions

- NebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form content
NebulaDocument= versioned authored/ingested long-form content

- NebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a document
NebulaChunk= retrievable semantic subdivision of a document

- NebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edge
NebulaCrossReference= explicit semantic edge

- NebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts
NebulaExecutionLink= operational backlink into Conduit / receipts

### 3. Level rules

- documents have default levels
documents have default levels

- chunks may override levels
chunks may override levels

- cross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections
cross-reference edges donotown abstraction level semantically;sourceLevel/targetLevelare denormalized convenience projections

### 4. WRP artifact registry obligations

- artifact keys are stable
artifact keys are stable

- document revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in place
document revisions supersede prior documents rather than mutating them in place

- currentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision
currentDocumentonNebulaArtifactpoints to the active canonical doc revision

### 5. Retrieval implications

- Builder → L1 + selective L2
Builder → L1 + selective L2

- Architect → L2/L3
Architect → L2/L3

- Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunks
Inspector → L2/L3 + normative chunks

- Explorer → L2/L3/L4
Explorer → L2/L3/L4

# A couple of things I would tighten in this JSON-LD before you wire it into code

There aretwo immediate refinementsI’d make, because they’ll matter once you start projecting real WRP docs into Nebula.

# 1) Split ontology classes from seed instances

Right now, for convenience, I included both:

- theschema vocabulary
theschema vocabulary

- and theinitial four WRP artifact instances
and theinitial four WRP artifact instances

in one file.

For the actual repo, I’d split that into:

## A.schemas/core/nebula-level-stratification-and-wrp-artifacts.jsonld

Only classes + properties + enums

and then

## B.data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifacts.jsonld

The four seeded artifact instances

- wrp-v1-protocol

- wrp-v1_1-dag

- wrp-v1_2-traversal
wrp-v1_2-traversal

- wrp-migration-plan
wrp-migration-plan

That separation is cleaner because the schema remains stable while the bootstrap artifact registry evolves.

with classes like:

- RetrievalProfile
RetrievalProfile

- InspectorProfile

ExplorerProfile

and properties like:

- allowedLevel
allowedLevel

preferredChunkKind

preferredNormativeStrength

crossReferenceExpansionDepth

allowExecutionRecencyBoost

allowOpenQuestions

allowRationaleChunks

importerThis seed file is good enough as abootstrap registry, but I’d makethree concrete adjustmentsbefore you treat it as durable input to the Nebula projector.1) Stop treatingconduitPlanIdas singularRight now I used:conduitPlanId: "CDT-WRP-001"That’s fine for the current four-plan packet, but it will age badly because one artifact will almost certainly end up being implemented bymultiple Conduit plans.For example:the traversal engine may split intotraversal corereceipt emissionvalidator hooksmigration shimsSo I would change the ontology and the bootstrap data to supportplural plan links:replaceJSON"conduitPlanId":"CDT-WRP-003"with something likeJSON"conduitPlanIds": ["CDT-WRP-003"]or, even better, keepartifact seed data free of execution multiplicityand push execution bindings intoNebulaExecutionLinkinstances.My preference is:artifact registry = stable artifact metadataexecution links = operational Conduit/receipt bindingsSo the more future-proof shape is:removeconduitPlanIdfrom the artifact registry entirelyortreat it only as an initial “primary seed plan” field2) AddartifactFamilyandversionLineYou’re already thinking in terms of WRPas a living protocol family, not just one-off documents. So I’d make that explicit.I’d add fields like:JSON"artifactFamily":"wrp","versionLine":"v1"That gives you a clean grouping dimension for:all WRP artifactsall WRP v1 artifactsfuture WRP v2 work if the protocol or execution model evolvesSo an artifact instance might become:JSON{"artifactKey":"wrp-v1_2-traversal","artifactFamily":"wrp","versionLine":"v1","artifactVersion":"1.2"}That is much easier to query than inferring family/version-line by parsing keys.3) Seed explicit artifact-to-artifact dependency edges tooRight now this file only seeds the four artifacts as isolated nodes. But the relationships between them are already known and stable enough that I’d probably seed those at bootstrap time too.I would either:Option A — keep this file node-onlyand add a second file:data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifact-cross-references.jsonldwith edges like:DAGdepends_onProtocolTraversalexecutes / constrains / depends_onDAGMigrationmigratesProtocolMigrationmigratesDAGMigrationmigratesTraversalorOption B — includeNebulaCrossReferenceseed instances in this same fileI preferOption A, because it keeps:artifact registry= stable node identitiesrelationship registry= explicit edge graphThat separation will make importer logic cleaner too.So the next artifact I’d produce is this:data/nebula/bootstrap/wrp-artifact-cross-references.jsonldIt should seed the initial WRP graph edges such as:wrp-v1_1-dag→wrp-v1-protocol(depends_on)wrp-v1_2-traversal→wrp-v1_1-dag(executes)wrp-v1_2-traversal→wrp-v1-protocol(constrainsordepends_on, depending on how tight you want that coupling modeled)wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1-protocol(migrates)wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_1-dag(migrates)wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_2-traversal(migrates)and I’d probably also add:edge-levelnotesstatusevidenceKind = artifact_projectionoptionalsourceLevel/targetLevelIf you want, I’ll go straight into that file next.

# What I would tighten before wiring this into the importer

This seed file is good enough as abootstrap registry, but I’d makethree concrete adjustmentsbefore you treat it as durable input to the Nebula projector.

---

# 1) Stop treatingconduitPlanIdas singular

Right now I used:

- conduitPlanId: "CDT-WRP-001"
conduitPlanId: "CDT-WRP-001"

That’s fine for the current four-plan packet, but it will age badly because one artifact will almost certainly end up being implemented bymultiple Conduit plans.

For example:

- the traversal engine may split intotraversal corereceipt emissionvalidator hooksmigration shims
the traversal engine may split into

- traversal core
traversal core

- receipt emission
receipt emission

- validator hooks
validator hooks

- migration shims
migration shims

```

or, even better, keepartifact seed data free of execution multiplicityand push execution bindings intoNebulaExecutionLinkinstances.

My preference is:

- artifact registry = stable artifact metadata
artifact registry = stable artifact metadata

- execution links = operational Conduit/receipt bindings
execution links = operational Conduit/receipt bindings

- removeconduitPlanIdfrom the artifact registry entirelyor

# 2) AddartifactFamilyandversionLine

You’re already thinking in terms of WRPas a living protocol family, not just one-off documents. So I’d make that explicit.

I’d add fields like:

```
"artifactFamily": "wrp","versionLine": "v1"
```

```
"artifactFamily": "wrp","versionLine": "v1"
```

That gives you a clean grouping dimension for:

- all WRP artifacts
all WRP artifacts

- all WRP v1 artifacts

- future WRP v2 work if the protocol or execution model evolves
future WRP v2 work if the protocol or execution model evolves

```

thisThis is the rightshape, but before you treat it as the stable bootstrap graph, I’d makethree modeling decisions explicitly.1) Decide whetherEXECUTESis the right relation from Traversal → DAGRight now I modeled:wrp-v1_2-traversalEXECUTESwrp-v1_1-dagThat is directionally sensible if you read it as:“the traversal engine executes graphs defined by the DAG model.”But there are reallythree different semantic relationshipshiding in there:A. structural dependencyTraversaldepends onthe DAG representation.B. runtime operationTraversalexecutesgraph instances that conform to the DAG model.C. representation pressureTraversalconstrainswhat metadata the DAG must expose.So if you want the bootstrap graph to stay conceptually crisp, I’d keepall threebut treat them differently:Recommended minimal stable setTraversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ONTraversal → DAG =CONSTRAINSOptional if you want runtime semantics in the knowledge graphTraversal → DAG =EXECUTESMy instinct is:keepEXECUTESifNebula is going to model operational semantics and not just design dependencydrop itifyou want the bootstrap graph to stay mostly architectural and staticIf I were normalizing this for long-term use, I’d probably keep:DEPENDS_ONCONSTRAINSand reserveEXECUTESfor either:chunk-level references, oractual runtime execution-link semantics later.2) Add edge identifiers that are independent of English phrasingThe current IDs are readable, but they’re basically sentence fragments:wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal-constrains-wrp-v1_1-dagThat’s fine for bootstrap, but if you want them to stay stable across wording changes, I’d introduce a more structured ID convention like:wrp:xref/<source-artifact-key>/<relation>/<target-artifact-key>So for example:wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/depends_on/wrp-v1_1-dagwrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/constrains/wrp-v1_1-dagwrp:xref/wrp-migration-plan/migrates/wrp-v1_2-traversalThat makes parsing and deduplication easier.3) Add one more edge: Migration Plan → TraversalCONSTRAINSRight now the migration plan onlymigratesthe traversal artifact. But in practice the migration plan will almost certainly alsoconstrainthe traversal engine design, because rollout compatibility affects:fallback behaviordual-mode executionlegacy request adaptersreceipt compatibilitycutover toggles / feature flagsSo I would probably add:wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_2-traversal=CONSTRAINSand maybe also:wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_1-dag=CONSTRAINSbecause migration can force temporary DAG compatibility shims too.That gives you a cleaner distinction:MIGRATES= “this artifact is part of the migration target set”CONSTRAINS= “the migration strategy places design limits on this artifact”My recommended normalized bootstrap edge setIf I were turning this into the first stable graph, I’d probably normalize it to something like:Protocol / DAGDAG → Protocol =DEPENDS_ONTraversal / DAG / ProtocolTraversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ONTraversal → DAG =CONSTRAINSTraversal → Protocol =DEPENDS_ONMigration → all WRP artifactsMigration → Protocol =MIGRATESMigration → DAG =MIGRATESMigration → Traversal =MIGRATESMigration as design pressureMigration → DAG =CONSTRAINSMigration → Traversal =CONSTRAINSThat’s a pretty good initial semantic skeleton.So the next artifact I’d write is the one you flagged a moment ago as the real operational prize:schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldThat’s where the level system stops being passive metadata and starts drivingBuilder / Architect / Inspector / Explorerretrieval behavior.I’d make it define:RetrievalProfileBuilderRetrievalProfileArchitectRetrievalProfileInspectorRetrievalProfileExplorerRetrievalProfilewith fields like:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthcrossReferenceExpansionDepthincludeRationaleincludeOpenQuestionspreferActiveArtifactsallowExecutionLinksIf you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it repo-ready JSON-LD plus the initial four seeded retrieval profiles.SourcesKanaries Data Inc.SponsoredAI Agent in JupyterEdit cells, run code, inspect outputs, and debug notebooks directly inside JupyterLab.

thisThis is the rightshape, but before you treat it as the stable bootstrap graph, I’d makethree modeling decisions explicitly.1) Decide whetherEXECUTESis the right relation from Traversal → DAGRight now I modeled:wrp-v1_2-traversalEXECUTESwrp-v1_1-dagThat is directionally sensible if you read it as:“the traversal engine executes graphs defined by the DAG model.”But there are reallythree different semantic relationshipshiding in there:A. structural dependencyTraversaldepends onthe DAG representation.B. runtime operationTraversalexecutesgraph instances that conform to the DAG model.C. representation pressureTraversalconstrainswhat metadata the DAG must expose.So if you want the bootstrap graph to stay conceptually crisp, I’d keepall threebut treat them differently:Recommended minimal stable setTraversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ONTraversal → DAG =CONSTRAINSOptional if you want runtime semantics in the knowledge graphTraversal → DAG =EXECUTESMy instinct is:keepEXECUTESifNebula is going to model operational semantics and not just design dependencydrop itifyou want the bootstrap graph to stay mostly architectural and staticIf I were normalizing this for long-term use, I’d probably keep:DEPENDS_ONCONSTRAINSand reserveEXECUTESfor either:chunk-level references, oractual runtime execution-link semantics later.2) Add edge identifiers that are independent of English phrasingThe current IDs are readable, but they’re basically sentence fragments:wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal-constrains-wrp-v1_1-dagThat’s fine for bootstrap, but if you want them to stay stable across wording changes, I’d introduce a more structured ID convention like:wrp:xref/<source-artifact-key>/<relation>/<target-artifact-key>So for example:wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/depends_on/wrp-v1_1-dagwrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/constrains/wrp-v1_1-dagwrp:xref/wrp-migration-plan/migrates/wrp-v1_2-traversalThat makes parsing and deduplication easier.3) Add one more edge: Migration Plan → TraversalCONSTRAINSRight now the migration plan onlymigratesthe traversal artifact. But in practice the migration plan will almost certainly alsoconstrainthe traversal engine design, because rollout compatibility affects:fallback behaviordual-mode executionlegacy request adaptersreceipt compatibilitycutover toggles / feature flagsSo I would probably add:wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_2-traversal=CONSTRAINSand maybe also:wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_1-dag=CONSTRAINSbecause migration can force temporary DAG compatibility shims too.That gives you a cleaner distinction:MIGRATES= “this artifact is part of the migration target set”CONSTRAINS= “the migration strategy places design limits on this artifact”My recommended normalized bootstrap edge setIf I were turning this into the first stable graph, I’d probably normalize it to something like:Protocol / DAGDAG → Protocol =DEPENDS_ONTraversal / DAG / ProtocolTraversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ONTraversal → DAG =CONSTRAINSTraversal → Protocol =DEPENDS_ONMigration → all WRP artifactsMigration → Protocol =MIGRATESMigration → DAG =MIGRATESMigration → Traversal =MIGRATESMigration as design pressureMigration → DAG =CONSTRAINSMigration → Traversal =CONSTRAINSThat’s a pretty good initial semantic skeleton.So the next artifact I’d write is the one you flagged a moment ago as the real operational prize:schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonldThat’s where the level system stops being passive metadata and starts drivingBuilder / Architect / Inspector / Explorerretrieval behavior.I’d make it define:RetrievalProfileBuilderRetrievalProfileArchitectRetrievalProfileInspectorRetrievalProfileExplorerRetrievalProfilewith fields like:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthcrossReferenceExpansionDepthincludeRationaleincludeOpenQuestionspreferActiveArtifactsallowExecutionLinksIf you want, I’ll go straight into that next and make it repo-ready JSON-LD plus the initial four seeded retrieval profiles.

# What I’d refine before freezing this

This is the rightshape, but before you treat it as the stable bootstrap graph, I’d makethree modeling decisions explicitly.

---

# 1) Decide whetherEXECUTESis the right relation from Traversal → DAG

Right now I modeled:

- wrp-v1_2-traversalEXECUTESwrp-v1_1-dag
wrp-v1_2-traversalEXECUTESwrp-v1_1-dag

That is directionally sensible if you read it as:

> “the traversal engine executes graphs defined by the DAG model.”

“the traversal engine executes graphs defined by the DAG model.”

But there are reallythree different semantic relationshipshiding in there:

## A. structural dependency

Traversaldepends onthe DAG representation.

## B. runtime operation

Traversalexecutesgraph instances that conform to the DAG model.

## C. representation pressure

Traversalconstrainswhat metadata the DAG must expose.

So if you want the bootstrap graph to stay conceptually crisp, I’d keepall threebut treat them differently:

### Recommended minimal stable set

- Traversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ON
Traversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ON

- Traversal → DAG =CONSTRAINS
Traversal → DAG =CONSTRAINS

### Optional if you want runtime semantics in the knowledge graph

- Traversal → DAG =EXECUTES
Traversal → DAG =EXECUTES

My instinct is:

- keepEXECUTESifNebula is going to model operational semantics and not just design dependency
keepEXECUTESifNebula is going to model operational semantics and not just design dependency

- drop itifyou want the bootstrap graph to stay mostly architectural and static
drop itifyou want the bootstrap graph to stay mostly architectural and static

If I were normalizing this for long-term use, I’d probably keep:

- DEPENDS_ON
DEPENDS_ON

- CONSTRAINS
CONSTRAINS

and reserveEXECUTESfor either:

- chunk-level references, or
chunk-level references, or

- actual runtime execution-link semantics later.
actual runtime execution-link semantics later.

---

# 2) Add edge identifiers that are independent of English phrasing

The current IDs are readable, but they’re basically sentence fragments:

- wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal-constrains-wrp-v1_1-dag
wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal-constrains-wrp-v1_1-dag

That’s fine for bootstrap, but if you want them to stay stable across wording changes, I’d introduce a more structured ID convention like:

```
wrp:xref/<source-artifact-key>/<relation>/<target-artifact-key>
```

```
wrp:xref/<source-artifact-key>/<relation>/<target-artifact-key>
```

So for example:

- wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/depends_on/wrp-v1_1-dag
wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/depends_on/wrp-v1_1-dag

- wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/constrains/wrp-v1_1-dag
wrp:xref/wrp-v1_2-traversal/constrains/wrp-v1_1-dag

- wrp:xref/wrp-migration-plan/migrates/wrp-v1_2-traversal
wrp:xref/wrp-migration-plan/migrates/wrp-v1_2-traversal

That makes parsing and deduplication easier.

---

# 3) Add one more edge: Migration Plan → TraversalCONSTRAINS

Right now the migration plan onlymigratesthe traversal artifact. But in practice the migration plan will almost certainly alsoconstrainthe traversal engine design, because rollout compatibility affects:

- fallback behavior
fallback behavior

- dual-mode execution
dual-mode execution

- legacy request adapters
legacy request adapters

- receipt compatibility
receipt compatibility

- cutover toggles / feature flags
cutover toggles / feature flags

So I would probably add:

- wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_2-traversal=CONSTRAINS
wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_2-traversal=CONSTRAINS

and maybe also:

- wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_1-dag=CONSTRAINS
wrp-migration-plan→wrp-v1_1-dag=CONSTRAINS

because migration can force temporary DAG compatibility shims too.

That gives you a cleaner distinction:

- MIGRATES= “this artifact is part of the migration target set”
MIGRATES= “this artifact is part of the migration target set”

- CONSTRAINS= “the migration strategy places design limits on this artifact”
CONSTRAINS= “the migration strategy places design limits on this artifact”

Traversal → DAG =DEPENDS_ON

Migration → Protocol =MIGRATES

Migration → DAG =MIGRATES

Migration → Traversal =MIGRATES

Migration → DAG =CONSTRAINS

- Migration → Traversal =CONSTRAINS
Migration → Traversal =CONSTRAINS

Allows broader cross-reference traversal and inclusion of superseded material when historically relevant."}]}What this gives you immediatelyThis schema turns the level model into aretrieval contractrather than just a tagging scheme.So instead of having some vague rule like:“Builder should mostly see implementation detail”“Architect should see subsystem design and rationale”you now have a machine-readable policy surface that can drive:Nebula retrievalrole-specific prompt assemblycontext expansion limitsweighting of normative vs descriptive chunkswhether Conduit execution links are relevantThe core shape I think is right hereThere arethree things in this schemathat I think are exactly the right axis for your system.1)allowedLevelas a hard filter, not just a score hintThis is important.For example,Builderis defined as:L1L2not “prefer L1/L2 but maybe let L3 flood in if embeddings happen to like it.”That means your retrieval pipeline can do:phase 1retrieve candidate chunks by lexical / embedding relevancephase 2hard filterto allowed levels for the active profilephase 3apply ranking boosts for:preferred chunk kindsnormative strengthactive artifactsexecution recency if allowedThat preserves the whole point of stratification.2)preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevelThis looks minor, but I think it matters a lot.You explicitly want documents like the WRP migration plan to contain:L3migration rationaleL2compatibility rulesL1concrete migration tasksIf retrieval only respected document-level classification, you’d lose that nuance. So the retrieval profile making this explicit is good: it tells the retrieval engine to trustchunk-level overridesas the primary abstraction signal.3)includeExecutionLinksas a role-level toggleThis is a very good dividing line between Nebula-as-knowledge and Conduit-as-execution.For example:Buildershould usually see execution links because “what plan is implementing this?” is relevant.Inspectoroften should too, because “what actually got run / what receipt exists?” matters.Architectusually doesn’t need that in default retrieval.Explorerprobably doesn’t either.That’s exactly the kind of separation that stops every role from dragging execution metadata into every context window.What I would change before I treat this as stableThere arefour concrete refinementsI’d make next.1) Add a distinction betweenhard filtersandsoft preferencesRight now the schema has:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthThat’s good, but in practice you’ll want some preferences to behard exclusionsand some to beranking weights.So I’d add fields like:JSON"requiredChunkKind": {"@id":"retrieval:requiredChunkKind","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"excludedChunkKind": {"@id":"retrieval:excludedChunkKind","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"excludedLevel": {"@id":"retrieval:excludedLevel","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That would let you express things like:Builderallowed levels =L1,L2excluded chunk kinds = maybeOPEN_QUESTIONby defaultInspectorrequired chunk kinds = at least one ofINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,MIGRATION_STEPif availablewhich is more precise than “preference only.”2) Addartifact-family scopingso a role can be specialized per domainRight now the profiles are generic:BuilderArchitectInspectorExplorerBut in practice you’ll wantrole + domainvariants, e.g.:Builder for WRPBuilder for NebulaBuilder for LOSMInspector for JSON-LD / ontologyArchitect for ConduitSo I’d add an optional field like:JSON"appliesToArtifactType": {"@id":"retrieval:appliesToArtifactType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}or maybe:JSON"appliesToArtifactFamily": {"@id":"retrieval:appliesToArtifactFamily"}Then later you can have:retrieval:profile/inspector-jsonldretrieval:profile/builder-wrpretrieval:profile/architect-nebulawithout inventing a totally separate mechanism.That lines up very closely with the way you keep noticing that certain roles “care about” specific domains.3) Addopen-question policyinstead of just a booleanRight now you’ve got:includeOpenQuestions: true/falseThat’s a good start, but I think you’ll eventually wanthowopen questions are used, not just whether they’re allowed.Something like:JSON"openQuestionMode": {"@id":"retrieval:openQuestionMode"}with values like:excludeappendprioritizeonly_if_blockedWhy this matters:Architectmight want open questions appended after stable material.Explorermight want them actively surfaced.Buildermight want them only if the implementation target is blocked or underspecified.That would be a very useful knob once the open-question harvest starts growing.4) Addcross-reference relation filtering, not just depthRight now the profile can say:how deep to traversebut notwhich relation types are allowed/preferredThat’s going to matter.Example:Builder probably wants:DEPENDS_ONIMPLEMENTSmaybeCONSTRAINSbut not necessarily broadRAISES_QUESTIONorSUPERSEDEShistory.Whereas Explorer may absolutely want:RAISES_QUESTIONANSWERS_QUESTIONSUPERSEDESSo I’d add:JSON"allowedRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:allowedRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"preferredRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:preferredRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That’s one of the most important missing pieces.My recommendation for the very next artifactAt this point we have:Conduit → Nebula WRP projection docNebula level / WRP artifact ontologyWRP artifact bootstrap nodesWRP artifact bootstrap cross-referencesNebula retrieval profiles ontologyThe next thing I would write is the firstprocedural importer spec, because that’s what actually turns your markdown and plans into the graph you’ve just modeled.Next doc:docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdThat doc should be extremely concrete and implementation-facing. It should specify:A. markdown heading →sectionKeyFor example:## Identity and Versioninginwrp-v1-protocol.mdbecomeswrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningB. chunking rulessplit by heading block firstthen by semantic subtype within a sectiondon’t mix rationale + code checklist + invariants in one chunkC. level assignment heuristicsif a chunk contains file paths / schema diffs / implementation checklists →L1if it contains protocol semantics / graph rules / invariants →L2if it contains tradeoffs / migration rationale / system positioning →L3if it contains doctrine / ontology rules →L4D. chunk kind classification rulesHow to tag:PROTOCOL_RULEDATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTRATIONALEMIGRATION_STEPOPEN_QUESTIONE. normative strength extractionHeuristics for:“must” →REQUIRED“must not” / “shall not” →PROHIBITED“should” →RECOMMENDEDdescriptive prose →INFORMATIVEF. cross-reference extractionRules for emitting edges from:explicit markdown linksartifactKeymentionssection referencesrecognized WRP identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt, etc.G. back-projection of Conduit metadataHowconduitPlanId, receipts, and implementation status get attached to documents/chunks/artifacts.That’s the piece that would let the local Qwen/OpenCode work eventually land in Nebula without hand-curating every chunk.If you want, I’ll writedocs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdnext as a full repo-ready spec.SourcesPeople Data LabsSponsoredMillions of recordsOne clean API for people and company data

It should specify:A. markdown heading →sectionKeyFor example:## Identity and Versioninginwrp-v1-protocol.mdbecomeswrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningB. chunking rulessplit by heading block firstthen by semantic subtype within a sectiondon’t mix rationale + code checklist + invariants in one chunkC. level assignment heuristicsif a chunk contains file paths / schema diffs / implementation checklists →L1if it contains protocol semantics / graph rules / invariants →L2if it contains tradeoffs / migration rationale / system positioning →L3if it contains doctrine / ontology rules →L4D. chunk kind classification rulesHow to tag:PROTOCOL_RULEDATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTRATIONALEMIGRATION_STEPOPEN_QUESTIONE. normative strength extractionHeuristics for:“must” →REQUIRED“must not” / “shall not” →PROHIBITED“should” →RECOMMENDEDdescriptive prose →INFORMATIVEF. cross-reference extractionRules for emitting edges from:explicit markdown linksartifactKeymentionssection referencesrecognized WRP identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt, etc.G. back-projection of Conduit metadataHowconduitPlanId, receipts, and implementation status get attached to documents/chunks/artifacts.That’s the piece that would let the local Qwen/OpenCode work eventually land in Nebula without hand-curating every chunk.If you want, I’ll writedocs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdnext as a full repo-ready spec.SourcesPeople Data LabsSponsoredMillions of recordsOne clean API for people and company data

Allows broader cross-reference traversal and inclusion of superseded material when historically relevant."}]}What this gives you immediatelyThis schema turns the level model into aretrieval contractrather than just a tagging scheme.So instead of having some vague rule like:“Builder should mostly see implementation detail”“Architect should see subsystem design and rationale”you now have a machine-readable policy surface that can drive:Nebula retrievalrole-specific prompt assemblycontext expansion limitsweighting of normative vs descriptive chunkswhether Conduit execution links are relevantThe core shape I think is right hereThere arethree things in this schemathat I think are exactly the right axis for your system.1)allowedLevelas a hard filter, not just a score hintThis is important.For example,Builderis defined as:L1L2not “prefer L1/L2 but maybe let L3 flood in if embeddings happen to like it.”That means your retrieval pipeline can do:phase 1retrieve candidate chunks by lexical / embedding relevancephase 2hard filterto allowed levels for the active profilephase 3apply ranking boosts for:preferred chunk kindsnormative strengthactive artifactsexecution recency if allowedThat preserves the whole point of stratification.2)preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevelThis looks minor, but I think it matters a lot.You explicitly want documents like the WRP migration plan to contain:L3migration rationaleL2compatibility rulesL1concrete migration tasksIf retrieval only respected document-level classification, you’d lose that nuance. So the retrieval profile making this explicit is good: it tells the retrieval engine to trustchunk-level overridesas the primary abstraction signal.3)includeExecutionLinksas a role-level toggleThis is a very good dividing line between Nebula-as-knowledge and Conduit-as-execution.For example:Buildershould usually see execution links because “what plan is implementing this?” is relevant.Inspectoroften should too, because “what actually got run / what receipt exists?” matters.Architectusually doesn’t need that in default retrieval.Explorerprobably doesn’t either.That’s exactly the kind of separation that stops every role from dragging execution metadata into every context window.What I would change before I treat this as stableThere arefour concrete refinementsI’d make next.1) Add a distinction betweenhard filtersandsoft preferencesRight now the schema has:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthThat’s good, but in practice you’ll want some preferences to behard exclusionsand some to beranking weights.So I’d add fields like:JSON"requiredChunkKind": {"@id":"retrieval:requiredChunkKind","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"excludedChunkKind": {"@id":"retrieval:excludedChunkKind","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"excludedLevel": {"@id":"retrieval:excludedLevel","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That would let you express things like:Builderallowed levels =L1,L2excluded chunk kinds = maybeOPEN_QUESTIONby defaultInspectorrequired chunk kinds = at least one ofINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,MIGRATION_STEPif availablewhich is more precise than “preference only.”2) Addartifact-family scopingso a role can be specialized per domainRight now the profiles are generic:BuilderArchitectInspectorExplorerBut in practice you’ll wantrole + domainvariants, e.g.:Builder for WRPBuilder for NebulaBuilder for LOSMInspector for JSON-LD / ontologyArchitect for ConduitSo I’d add an optional field like:JSON"appliesToArtifactType": {"@id":"retrieval:appliesToArtifactType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}or maybe:JSON"appliesToArtifactFamily": {"@id":"retrieval:appliesToArtifactFamily"}Then later you can have:retrieval:profile/inspector-jsonldretrieval:profile/builder-wrpretrieval:profile/architect-nebulawithout inventing a totally separate mechanism.That lines up very closely with the way you keep noticing that certain roles “care about” specific domains.3) Addopen-question policyinstead of just a booleanRight now you’ve got:includeOpenQuestions: true/falseThat’s a good start, but I think you’ll eventually wanthowopen questions are used, not just whether they’re allowed.Something like:JSON"openQuestionMode": {"@id":"retrieval:openQuestionMode"}with values like:excludeappendprioritizeonly_if_blockedWhy this matters:Architectmight want open questions appended after stable material.Explorermight want them actively surfaced.Buildermight want them only if the implementation target is blocked or underspecified.That would be a very useful knob once the open-question harvest starts growing.4) Addcross-reference relation filtering, not just depthRight now the profile can say:how deep to traversebut notwhich relation types are allowed/preferredThat’s going to matter.Example:Builder probably wants:DEPENDS_ONIMPLEMENTSmaybeCONSTRAINSbut not necessarily broadRAISES_QUESTIONorSUPERSEDEShistory.Whereas Explorer may absolutely want:RAISES_QUESTIONANSWERS_QUESTIONSUPERSEDESSo I’d add:JSON"allowedRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:allowedRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"preferredRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:preferredRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That’s one of the most important missing pieces.My recommendation for the very next artifactAt this point we have:Conduit → Nebula WRP projection docNebula level / WRP artifact ontologyWRP artifact bootstrap nodesWRP exactly the kind of separation that stops every role from dragging execution metadata into every context window.What I would change before I treat this as stableThere arefour concrete refinementsI’d noticing that certain roles “care about” specific domains.3) Addopen-question policyinstead of just a booleanRight now you’ve got:includeOpenQuestions: true/falseThat’s a good start, but I think like:excludeappendprioritizeonly_if_blockedWhy this matters:Architectmight want open questions appended after stable material.Explorermight want them actively surfaced.Buildermight want them only if {"@id":"retrieval:allowedRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"preferredRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:preferredRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That’s one of the most important missing pieces.My recommendation for the very next artifactAt this point we have:Conduit → Nebula WRP projection docNebula level / WRP artifact ontologyWRP artifact bootstrap nodesWRP artifact bootstrap cross-referencesNebula retrieval profiles ontologyThe next thing I would write is the firstprocedural importer spec, because that’s what actually turns your markdown and plans into the graph you’ve just modeled.Next doc:docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdThat doc should be extremely concrete and implementation-facing. It should specify:A. markdown heading →sectionKeyFor example:## Identity and Versioninginwrp-v1-protocol.mdbecomeswrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningB. chunking rulessplit by heading block firstthen by semantic subtype within a sectiondon’t mix rationale + code checklist + invariants in one chunkC. level assignment heuristicsif a chunk contains file paths / schema diffs / implementation checklists →L1if it contains protocol semantics / graph rules / invariants →L2if it contains tradeoffs / migration rationale / system positioning →L3if it contains doctrine / ontology rules →L4D. chunk kind classification rulesHow to tag:PROTOCOL_RULEDATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTRATIONALEMIGRATION_STEPOPEN_QUESTIONE. normative strength extractionHeuristics for:“must” →REQUIRED“must not” / “shall not” →PROHIBITED“should” →RECOMMENDEDdescriptive prose →INFORMATIVEF. cross-reference extractionRules for emitting edges from:explicit markdown linksartifactKeymentionssection referencesrecognized WRP identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt, etc.G. back-projection of Conduit metadataHowconduitPlanId, receipts, and implementation status get attached to documents/chunks/artifacts.That’s the piece that would let the local Qwen/OpenCode work eventually land in Nebula without hand-curating every chunk.If you want, I’ll writedocs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdnext as a full repo-ready spec.
