Favors execution/build detail and bounded subsystem design, with minimal architectural expansion unless explicitly requested."},{"id":"retrieval:profile/architect","type":"ArchitectRetrievalProfile","title":"Architect Retrieval Profile","allowedLevel": ["nebula:L2","nebula:L3"],"preferredChunkKind": ["nebula:OVERVIEW","nebula:DEFINITION","nebula:DATA_MODEL","nebula:ALGORITHM","nebula:INVARIANT","nebula:RATIONALE","nebula:OPEN_QUESTION"],"preferredNormativeStrength": ["nebula:REQUIRED","nebula:RECOMMENDED","nebula:INFORMATIVE"],"crossReferenceExpansionDepth":2,"maxChunks":16,"includeRationale":true,"includeOpenQuestions":true,"includeExamples":true,"includeExecutionLinks":false,"includeSupersededArtifacts":false,"preferActiveArtifacts":true,"preferNormativeChunks":false,"preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevel":true,"allowExecutionRecencyBoost":false,"allowCrossArtifactExpansion":true,"notes":"Optimized for subsystem design and architectural reasoning. Favors L2/L3 material, explicit invariants, and rationale-rich cross-artifact context."},{"id":"retrieval:profile/inspector","type":"InspectorRetrievalProfile","title":"Inspector Retrieval Profile","allowedLevel": ["nebula:L2","nebula:L3"],"preferredChunkKind": ["nebula:PROTOCOL_RULE","nebula:INVARIANT","nebula:MIGRATION_STEP","nebula:ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA","nebula:DATA_MODEL"],"preferredNormativeStrength": ["nebula:REQUIRED","nebula:PROHIBITED","nebula:RECOMMENDED"],"crossReferenceExpansionDepth":2,"maxChunks":14,"includeRationale":true,"includeOpenQuestions":false,"includeExamples":false,"includeExecutionLinks":true,"includeSupersededArtifacts":false,"preferActiveArtifacts":true,"preferNormativeChunks":true,"preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevel":true,"allowExecutionRecencyBoost":false,"allowCrossArtifactExpansion":true,"notes":"Optimized for invariants, validation, compatibility analysis, and rule enforcement. Strongly favors normative chunks and explicit migration/protocol constraints."},{"id":"retrieval:profile/explorer","type":"ExplorerRetrievalProfile","title":"Explorer Retrieval Profile","allowedLevel": ["nebula:L2","nebula:L3","nebula:L4"],"preferredChunkKind": ["nebula:OVERVIEW","nebula:RATIONALE","nebula:OPEN_QUESTION","nebula:DEFINITION","nebula:EXAMPLE"],"preferredNormativeStrength": ["nebula:INFORMATIVE","nebula:RECOMMENDED","nebula:REQUIRED"],"crossReferenceExpansionDepth":3,"maxChunks":18,"includeRationale":true,"includeOpenQuestions":true,"includeExamples":true,"includeExecutionLinks":false,"includeSupersededArtifacts":true,"preferActiveArtifacts":true,"preferNormativeChunks":false,"preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevel":true,"allowExecutionRecencyBoost":false,"allowCrossArtifactExpansion":true,"notes":"Optimized for exploratory reasoning across architecture, doctrine, and unresolved questions. Allows broader cross-reference traversal and inclusion of superseded material when historically relevant."}]}What this gives you immediatelyThis schema turns the level model into aretrieval contractrather than just a tagging scheme.So instead of having some vague rule like:“Builder should mostly see implementation detail”“Architect should see subsystem design and rationale”you now have a machine-readable policy surface that can drive:Nebula retrievalrole-specific prompt assemblycontext expansion limitsweighting of normative vs descriptive chunkswhether Conduit execution links are relevantThe core shape I think is right hereThere arethree things in this schemathat I think are exactly the right axis for your system.1)allowedLevelas a hard filter, not just a score hintThis is important.For example,Builderis defined as:L1L2not “prefer L1/L2 but maybe let L3 flood in if embeddings happen to like it.”That means your retrieval pipeline can do:phase 1retrieve candidate chunks by lexical / embedding relevancephase 2hard filterto allowed levels for the active profilephase 3apply ranking boosts for:preferred chunk kindsnormative strengthactive artifactsexecution recency if allowedThat preserves the whole point of stratification.2)preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevelThis looks minor, but I think it matters a lot.You explicitly want documents like the WRP migration plan to contain:L3migration rationaleL2compatibility rulesL1concrete migration tasksIf retrieval only respected document-level classification, you’d lose that nuance. So the retrieval profile making this explicit is good: it tells the retrieval engine to trustchunk-level overridesas the primary abstraction signal.3)includeExecutionLinksas a role-level toggleThis is a very good dividing line between Nebula-as-knowledge and Conduit-as-execution.For example:Buildershould usually see execution links because “what plan is implementing this?” is relevant.Inspectoroften should too, because “what actually got run / what receipt exists?” matters.Architectusually doesn’t need that in default retrieval.Explorerprobably doesn’t either.That’s exactly the kind of separation that stops every role from dragging execution metadata into every context window.What I would change before I treat this as stableThere arefour concrete refinementsI’d make next.1) Add a distinction betweenhard filtersandsoft preferencesRight now the schema has:allowedLevelpreferredChunkKindpreferredNormativeStrengthThat’s good, but in practice you’ll want some preferences to behard exclusionsand some to beranking weights.So I’d add fields like:JSON"requiredChunkKind": {"@id":"retrieval:requiredChunkKind","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"excludedChunkKind": {"@id":"retrieval:excludedChunkKind","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"excludedLevel": {"@id":"retrieval:excludedLevel","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That would let you express things like:Builderallowed levels =L1,L2excluded chunk kinds = maybeOPEN_QUESTIONby defaultInspectorrequired chunk kinds = at least one ofINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,MIGRATION_STEPif availablewhich is more precise than “preference only.”2) Addartifact-family scopingso a role can be specialized per domainRight now the profiles are generic:BuilderArchitectInspectorExplorerBut in practice you’ll wantrole + domainvariants, e.g.:Builder for WRPBuilder for NebulaBuilder for LOSMInspector for JSON-LD / ontologyArchitect for ConduitSo I’d add an optional field like:JSON"appliesToArtifactType": {"@id":"retrieval:appliesToArtifactType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}or maybe:JSON"appliesToArtifactFamily": {"@id":"retrieval:appliesToArtifactFamily"}Then later you can have:retrieval:profile/inspector-jsonldretrieval:profile/builder-wrpretrieval:profile/architect-nebulawithout inventing a totally separate mechanism.That lines up very closely with the way you keep noticing that certain roles “care about” specific domains.3) Addopen-question policyinstead of just a booleanRight now you’ve got:includeOpenQuestions: true/falseThat’s a good start, but I think you’ll eventually wanthowopen questions are used, not just whether they’re allowed.Something like:JSON"openQuestionMode": {"@id":"retrieval:openQuestionMode"}with values like:excludeappendprioritizeonly_if_blockedWhy this matters:Architectmight want open questions appended after stable material.Explorermight want them actively surfaced.Buildermight want them only if the implementation target is blocked or underspecified.That would be a very useful knob once the open-question harvest starts growing.4) Addcross-reference relation filtering, not just depthRight now the profile can say:how deep to traversebut notwhich relation types are allowed/preferredThat’s going to matter.Example:Builder probably wants:DEPENDS_ONIMPLEMENTSmaybeCONSTRAINSbut not necessarily broadRAISES_QUESTIONorSUPERSEDEShistory.Whereas Explorer may absolutely want:RAISES_QUESTIONANSWERS_QUESTIONSUPERSEDESSo I’d add:JSON"allowedRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:allowedRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"},"preferredRelationType": {"@id":"retrieval:preferredRelationType","@type":"@id","@container":"@set"}That’s one of the most important missing pieces.My recommendation for the very next artifactAt this point we have:Conduit → Nebula WRP projection docNebula level / WRP artifact ontologyWRP artifact bootstrap nodesWRP artifact bootstrap cross-referencesNebula retrieval profiles ontologyThe next thing I would write is the firstprocedural importer spec, because that’s what actually turns your markdown and plans into the graph you’ve just modeled.Next doc:docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdThat doc should be extremely concrete and implementation-facing. It should specify:A. markdown heading →sectionKeyFor example:## Identity and Versioninginwrp-v1-protocol.mdbecomeswrp.protocol.identity-and-versioningB. chunking rulessplit by heading block firstthen by semantic subtype within a sectiondon’t mix rationale + code checklist + invariants in one chunkC. level assignment heuristicsif a chunk contains file paths / schema diffs / implementation checklists →L1if it contains protocol semantics / graph rules / invariants →L2if it contains tradeoffs / migration rationale / system positioning →L3if it contains doctrine / ontology rules →L4D. chunk kind classification rulesHow to tag:PROTOCOL_RULEDATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTRATIONALEMIGRATION_STEPOPEN_QUESTIONE. normative strength extractionHeuristics for:“must” →REQUIRED“must not” / “shall not” →PROHIBITED“should” →RECOMMENDEDdescriptive prose →INFORMATIVEF. cross-reference extractionRules for emitting edges from:explicit markdown linksartifactKeymentionssection referencesrecognized WRP identifiers likeExecutionContext,ExecutionReceipt, etc.G. back-projection of Conduit metadataHowconduitPlanId, receipts, and implementation status get attached to documents/chunks/artifacts.That’s the piece that would let the local Qwen/OpenCode work eventually land in Nebula without hand-curating every chunk.If you want, I’ll writedocs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdnext as a full repo-ready spec.

Absolutely. This is the point where the level system becomes operational instead of just descriptive metadata.

Below is arepo-ready first passfor:

# schemas/core/nebula-retrieval-profiles.jsonld

The intent of this schema is to formalizerole-shaped retrieval policyover Nebula so that “Builder”, “Architect”, “Inspector”, and “Explorer” stop being just narrative roles and become concrete retrieval surfaces with explicit defaults.

# What this gives you immediately

This schema turns the level model into aretrieval contractrather than just a tagging scheme.

So instead of having some vague rule like:

- “Builder should mostly see implementation detail”
“Builder should mostly see implementation detail”

- “Architect should see subsystem design and rationale”
“Architect should see subsystem design and rationale”

you now have a machine-readable policy surface that can drive:

- Nebula retrieval
Nebula retrieval

- role-specific prompt assembly
role-specific prompt assembly

- context expansion limits
context expansion limits

- weighting of normative vs descriptive chunks
weighting of normative vs descriptive chunks

- whether Conduit execution links are relevant
whether Conduit execution links are relevant

---

# The core shape I think is right here

There arethree things in this schemathat I think are exactly the right axis for your system.

---

# 1)allowedLevelas a hard filter, not just a score hint

This is important.

For example,Builderis defined as:

- L1
L1

- L2
L2

not “prefer L1/L2 but maybe let L3 flood in if embeddings happen to like it.”

That means your retrieval pipeline can do:

## phase 1

retrieve candidate chunks by lexical / embedding relevance

## phase 2

hard filterto allowed levels for the active profile

## phase 3

apply ranking boosts for:

- preferred chunk kinds
preferred chunk kinds

- normative strength
normative strength

- active artifacts
active artifacts

- execution recency if allowed
execution recency if allowed

That preserves the whole point of stratification.

---

# 2)preferChunkLevelOverDocumentLevel

This looks minor, but I think it matters a lot.

You explicitly want documents like the WRP migration plan to contain:

- L3migration rationale
L3migration rationale

- L2compatibility rules
L2compatibility rules

- L1concrete migration tasks
L1concrete migration tasks

If retrieval only respected document-level classification, you’d lose that nuance. So the retrieval profile making this explicit is good: it tells the retrieval engine to trustchunk-level overridesas the primary abstraction signal.

---

# 3)includeExecutionLinksas a role-level toggle

This is a very good dividing line between Nebula-as-knowledge and Conduit-as-execution.

For example:

- Buildershould usually see execution links because “what plan is implementing this?” is relevant.
Buildershould usually see execution links because “what plan is implementing this?” is relevant.

- Inspectoroften should too, because “what actually got run / what receipt exists?” matters.
Inspectoroften should too, because “what actually got run / what receipt exists?” matters.

- Architectusually doesn’t need that in default retrieval.
Architectusually doesn’t need that in default retrieval.

- Explorerprobably doesn’t either.
Explorerprobably doesn’t either.

That’s exactly the kind of separation that stops every role from dragging execution metadata into every context window.

---

# What I would change before I treat this as stable

There arefour concrete refinementsI’d make next.

---

# 1) Add a distinction betweenhard filtersandsoft preferences

Right now the schema has:

- allowedLevel
allowedLevel

- preferredChunkKind
preferredChunkKind

- preferredNormativeStrength
preferredNormativeStrength

That’s good, but in practice you’ll want some preferences to behard exclusionsand some to beranking weights.

So I’d add fields like:

```
"requiredChunkKind": {  "@id": "retrieval:requiredChunkKind",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"},"excludedChunkKind": {  "@id": "retrieval:excludedChunkKind",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"},"excludedLevel": {  "@id": "retrieval:excludedLevel",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"}
```

```
"requiredChunkKind": {  "@id": "retrieval:requiredChunkKind",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"},"excludedChunkKind": {  "@id": "retrieval:excludedChunkKind",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"},"excludedLevel": {  "@id": "retrieval:excludedLevel",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"}
```

That would let you express things like:

## Builder

- allowed levels =L1,L2
allowed levels =L1,L2

- excluded chunk kinds = maybeOPEN_QUESTIONby default
excluded chunk kinds = maybeOPEN_QUESTIONby default

## Inspector

- required chunk kinds = at least one ofINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,MIGRATION_STEPif available
required chunk kinds = at least one ofINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,MIGRATION_STEPif available

which is more precise than “preference only.”

---

# 2) Addartifact-family scopingso a role can be specialized per domain

Right now the profiles are generic:

- Builder
Builder

- Architect
Architect

- Inspector
Inspector

- Explorer
Explorer

But in practice you’ll wantrole + domainvariants, e.g.:

- Builder for WRP
Builder for WRP

- Builder for Nebula
Builder for Nebula

- Builder for LOSM
Builder for LOSM

- Inspector for JSON-LD / ontology
Inspector for JSON-LD / ontology

- Architect for Conduit
Architect for Conduit

So I’d add an optional field like:

```
"appliesToArtifactType": {  "@id": "retrieval:appliesToArtifactType",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"}
```

```
"appliesToArtifactType": {  "@id": "retrieval:appliesToArtifactType",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"}
```

or maybe:

"appliesToArtifactFamily": {  "@id": "retrieval:appliesToArtifactFamily"}

- retrieval:profile/inspector-jsonld
retrieval:profile/inspector-jsonld

retrieval:profile/builder-wrp

retrieval:profile/architect-nebula

without inventing a totally separate mechanism.

That lines up very closely with the way you keep noticing that certain roles “care about” specific domains.

# 3) Addopen-question policyinstead of just a boolean

Right now you’ve got:

- includeOpenQuestions: true/false
includeOpenQuestions: true/false

That’s a good start, but I think you’ll eventually wanthowopen questions are used, not just whether they’re allowed.

Something like:

```
"openQuestionMode": {  "@id": "retrieval:openQuestionMode"}
```

```
"openQuestionMode": {  "@id": "retrieval:openQuestionMode"}
```

with values like:

- exclude
exclude

- append
append

- prioritize
prioritize

- only_if_blocked
only_if_blocked

Why this matters:

- Architectmight want open questions appended after stable material.
Architectmight want open questions appended after stable material.

- Explorermight want them actively surfaced.
Explorermight want them actively surfaced.

- Buildermight want them only if the implementation target is blocked or underspecified.
Buildermight want them only if the implementation target is blocked or underspecified.

That would be a very useful knob once the open-question harvest starts growing.

# 4) Addcross-reference relation filtering, not just depth

Right now the profile can say:

- how deep to traverse
how deep to traverse

but not

- which relation types are allowed/preferred
which relation types are allowed/preferred

That’s going to matter.

Example:

- Builder probably wants:DEPENDS_ONIMPLEMENTSmaybeCONSTRAINS

- DEPENDS_ON
DEPENDS_ON

- IMPLEMENTS
IMPLEMENTS

- maybeCONSTRAINS
maybeCONSTRAINS

but not necessarily broadRAISES_QUESTIONorSUPERSEDEShistory.

Whereas Explorer may absolutely want:

- RAISES_QUESTION
RAISES_QUESTION

- ANSWERS_QUESTION
ANSWERS_QUESTION

- SUPERSEDES
SUPERSEDES

So I’d add:

"allowedRelationType": {  "@id": "retrieval:allowedRelationType",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"},"preferredRelationType": {  "@id": "retrieval:preferredRelationType",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"}

"allowedRelationType": {  "@id": "retrieval:allowedRelationType",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"},"preferredRelationType": {  "@id": "retrieval:preferredRelationType",  "@type": "@id",  "@container": "@set"}

Here’s the next piece as arepo-ready implementation specfor turning the WRP docs you just put into Conduit into structured Nebula artifacts, chunks, and cross-references.docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.mdMarkdown# WRP Document Projection Rules**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula / WRP integration**Purpose:** Define deterministic rules for projecting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, levels, and cross-references.---# 1. ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning13.2 Chunk IDsFormat:<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning/chunk/01Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.13.3 Re-import stabilityOn re-import:if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stableif a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new idsif a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported14. Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning13.2 Chunk IDsFormat:<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning/chunk/01Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.13.3 Re-import stabilityOn re-import:if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stableif a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new idsif a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported14. Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. Future ExtensionsThe following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)embedding generation and vector indexingrole-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itselfsupersession lineage across chunk revisionsbidirectional Conduit synchronizationLLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristicsconfidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments20. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is enough to start building the importer, but there are **two companion artifacts** that would make implementation much safer:## 1. `schemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`A proper ontology file for:- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- etc.and probably:- which retrieval profiles prefer them- whether they are normative by default- whether they’re expected at L1/L2/L3/L4## 2. `docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`A literal importer algorithm doc:- parse markdown AST- build section tree- segment blocks into chunk candidates- classify chunk- infer cross refs- upsert SQL rows / graph rowsThat second one would be especially good for your current “Conduit + local Qwen coder” setup because it’s exactly the kind of thing you can hand to the model as an implementation scaffold.---Go ahead with the question.SourcesFivetranSponsoredOpen Data ArchitecturePower your AI with the adaptability of ODI.

Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. Future ExtensionsThe following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)embedding generation and vector indexingrole-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itselfsupersession lineage across chunk revisionsbidirectional Conduit synchronizationLLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristicsconfidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments20. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is enough to start building the importer, but there are **two companion artifacts** that would make implementation much safer:## 1. `schemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`A proper ontology file for:- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- etc.and probably:- which retrieval profiles prefer them- whether they are normative by default- whether they’re expected at L1/L2/L3/L4## 2. `docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`A literal importer algorithm doc:- parse markdown AST- build section tree- segment blocks into chunk candidates- classify chunk- infer cross refs- upsert SQL rows / graph rowsThat second one would be especially good for your current “Conduit + local Qwen coder” setup because it’s exactly the kind of thing you can hand to the model as an implementation scaffold.---Go ahead with the question.
