ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:- artifact family can be inferred- artifact key is stable- a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**- descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements- requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**- protocol semantics → data model- data model → algorithm- rationale → open questions- migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**- fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern- numbered migration checklist- table encoding a model or mapping- quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**- paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning13.2 Chunk IDsFormat:<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>Example:wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol/section/identity-and-versioning/chunk/01Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.13.3 Re-import stabilityOn re-import:if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stableif a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new idsif a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported14. Conduit Metadata Back-ProjectionThe projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.14.1 Artifact-level linksAn artifact MAY link to:Conduit plan idsplan statusimplementation branch / task identifiersmigration work package identifiers14.2 Chunk-level linksA chunk MAY link to:a Conduit plan implementing the chunkexecution receipts demonstrating realizationmigration steps or validation results14.3 Source precedenceIf Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identityConduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation linksconflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten15. Importer Determinism RequirementsProjection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.Determinism requirements:stable heading normalizationstable chunk orderingstable chunk boundary rulesstable level and chunkKind heuristicsstable relation inference defaultsAny projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.16. Validation RulesThe importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:16.1 Artifact integritysource document mapped to unknown artifact in strict modeduplicate artifact key projection in one import batch16.2 Section integrityduplicatesectionKeywithin an artifactinvalid parent-child heading hierarchy16.3 Chunk integrityempty chunk body after trimmingmissing levelmissing chunkKindmissing normativeStrengthduplicate chunk id in one import batch16.4 Cross-reference integritysource or target id missingrelation type missingself-loop edges unless explicitly allowedduplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic DefaultsUntil a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:wrp-v1-protocolBias toward:L2PROTOCOL_RULEDEFINITIONINVARIANTwrp-v1_1-dagBias toward:L2DATA_MODELALGORITHMINVARIANTwrp-v1_2-traversalBias toward:L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semanticALGORITHMIMPLEMENTATION_NOTEINVARIANTwrp-migration-planBias toward:L1for concrete rollout stepsL3for migration rationale / sequencingMIGRATION_STEPRATIONALEACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA18. Recommended Import Output ShapeFor each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)NebulaSectionrows for heading structureNebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic unitsNebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from referencesoptional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is presentimport receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures19. Future ExtensionsThe following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)embedding generation and vector indexingrole-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itselfsupersession lineage across chunk revisionsbidirectional Conduit synchronizationLLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristicsconfidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments20. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is enough to start building the importer, but there are **two companion artifacts** that would make implementation much safer:## 1. `schemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`A proper ontology file for:- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- etc.and probably:- which retrieval profiles prefer them- whether they are normative by default- whether they’re expected at L1/L2/L3/L4## 2. `docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`A literal importer algorithm doc:- parse markdown AST- build section tree- segment blocks into chunk candidates- classify chunk- infer cross refs- upsert SQL rows / graph rowsThat second one would be especially good for your current “Conduit + local Qwen coder” setup because it’s exactly the kind of thing you can hand to the model as an implementation scaffold.---Go ahead with the question.

ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**- Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks- Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks- Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints- Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**- each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`- each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**- level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level- a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**- explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**- artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**- map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`- create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**- parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**- create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**- split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**- assign:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**- emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**- attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**- write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. SummaryThe WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:artifact identitysection structuresemantically coherent chunkingchunk-level level stratificationchunk kind and normative classificationcross-artifact referencesoptional execution links back to ConduitThe first-pass rule is simple:project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.---# What I’d do next, before your questionThis doc is enough to start building the importer, but there are **two companion artifacts** that would make implementation much safer:## 1. `schemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`A proper ontology file for:- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- etc.and probably:- which retrieval profiles prefer them- whether they are normative by default- whether they’re expected at L1/L2/L3/L4## 2. `docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`A literal importer algorithm doc:- parse markdown AST- build section tree- segment blocks into chunk candidates- classify chunk- infer cross refs- upsert SQL rows / graph rowsThat second one would be especially good for your current “Conduit + local Qwen coder” setup because it’s exactly the kind of thing you can hand to the model as an implementation scaffold.---Go ahead with the question.

# docs/nebula/wrp-document-projection-rules.md

# WRP Document Projection Rules**Status:** Draft  **Owner:** Nebula / WRP integration  **Purpose:** Define deterministic rules for projecting WRP markdown artifacts into Nebula artifacts, sections, chunks, levels, and cross-references.---# 1. ScopeThis document defines how the initial WRP artifact set is ingested into Nebula:- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md`- `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md`The projection pipeline transforms those markdown documents into:- `NebulaArtifact` records- `NebulaSection` records- `NebulaChunk` records- `NebulaCrossReference` records- optional execution links to Conduit plans and receiptsThis document governs **projection behavior**, not authoring style. It specifies how Nebula should interpret WRP documents that already exist.---# 2. Projection ObjectivesThe projection pipeline MUST produce a graph that supports:1. **role-shaped retrieval**   - Builder sees implementation-oriented chunks   - Architect sees subsystem and rationale chunks   - Inspector sees invariants, migration rules, and protocol constraints   - Explorer sees rationale, open questions, and broader cross-artifact context2. **artifact-level identity**   - each WRP document projects to a stable `NebulaArtifact`   - each section and chunk receives stable identifiers3. **chunk-level stratification**   - level assignment is done at chunk level, not only document level   - a single document may yield L1, L2, and L3 chunks4. **cross-reference graph construction**   - explicit and inferred relationships between chunks, sections, and artifacts are materialized into Nebula edges5. **Conduit interoperability**   - artifacts and chunks may link to Conduit plans, execution receipts, or migration records where applicable---# 3. Projection Pipeline OverviewProjection MUST proceed in the following stages:1. **Artifact Resolution**   - map source markdown file to known `NebulaArtifact`   - create artifact if missing and bootstrap mode permits creation2. **Markdown Parsing**   - parse headings, lists, paragraphs, tables, fenced code blocks, block quotes3. **Section Construction**   - create ordered `NebulaSection` records from heading hierarchy4. **Chunk Segmentation**   - split section bodies into semantically coherent `NebulaChunk` units5. **Chunk Classification**   - assign:     - `level`     - `chunkKind`     - `normativeStrength`     - `status`     - optional tags / concepts6. **Cross-Reference Extraction**   - emit explicit and inferred edges among artifacts, sections, and chunks7. **Execution Link Attachment**   - attach Conduit plan or receipt links where metadata exists8. **Persistence / Upsert**   - write artifact/section/chunk/xref records using stable ids and idempotent upsert semantics---# 4. Source Artifact Mapping## 4.1 Canonical artifact bindingsThe following markdown files MUST map to these canonical artifacts:| Source file | Artifact ID | Artifact Key ||---|---|---|| `docs/wrp/wrp-v1-protocol.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol` | `wrp-v1-protocol` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_1-dag-model-and-compilation-pipeline.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_1-dag` | `wrp-v1_1-dag` || `docs/wrp/wrp-v1_2-execution-traversal-engine.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal` | `wrp-v1_2-traversal` || `docs/wrp/wrp-migration-plan.md` | `wrp:artifact/wrp-migration-plan` | `wrp-migration-plan` |## 4.2 Artifact creation policyIf a source document is encountered that is not already present in the bootstrap registry:- projection MUST fail by default in strict mode- projection MAY create a new `NebulaArtifact` in permissive mode if:  - artifact family can be inferred  - artifact key is stable  - a document path is availableStrict mode is the default for WRP v1 bootstrap ingestion.---# 5. Section Construction Rules## 5.1 Heading-based section boundariesMarkdown headings define section boundaries.- `#` = document root title (not a `NebulaSection` unless explicitly configured)- `##` = top-level section- `###` = child section of nearest preceding `##`- `####` and below = nested section nodes OR local substructure depending on depth policyDefault policy:- persist `##` and `###` as `NebulaSection`- treat `####+` as internal segmentation hints unless a document is unusually deep and preservation is requested## 5.2 Stable section identifiersEach section MUST receive a stable `sectionKey` derived from:- artifact key- normalized heading path### normalization rules- lowercase- spaces → `-`- strip punctuation except internal hyphen separators- collapse repeated separators- include ancestry path for nested sections### examplesDocument:- `wrp-v1-protocol`Heading:- `## Identity and Versioning`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.identity-and-versioning`Nested heading:- `## Execution Semantics`- `### Receipts`Section key:- `wrp-v1-protocol.execution-semantics.receipts`## 5.3 Section orderingEach section MUST store:- `ordinal` within artifact- `headingLevel`- `parentSectionId` if nestedOrder is derived from source markdown order and MUST be stable across re-import if heading order is unchanged.---# 6. Chunk Segmentation RulesSections are often too coarse to retrieve effectively. Each section MUST be segmented into one or more `NebulaChunk` units.## 6.1 Chunking principleA chunk MUST represent **one dominant semantic purpose**.Do not mix the following in a single chunk unless they are inseparable and short:- protocol rule + migration checklist- rationale + normative invariant- algorithm + historical commentary- open question + implementation task list## 6.2 Primary chunk boundariesWithin a section, start a new chunk when any of the following occurs:1. **normative mode switch**   - descriptive exposition changes into explicit requirements   - requirements change into rationale or migration guidance2. **semantic subtype switch**   - protocol semantics → data model   - data model → algorithm   - rationale → open questions   - migration steps → compatibility constraints3. **structural block boundary**   - fenced code block introducing a new implementation concern   - numbered migration checklist   - table encoding a model or mapping   - quoted rule / invariant block4. **topic pivot**   - paragraph group changes subject materially even within same heading## 6.3 Secondary chunk boundariesThe projector SHOULD split large chunks when:- chunk text exceeds configured token threshold- chunk contains more than one independent invariant- chunk contains more than one migration step cluster- chunk interleaves prose and code examples in a way that harms retrieval specificity## 6.4 Default chunk size guidanceTarget chunk size:- **preferred:** 150–450 tokens- **acceptable:** 80–700 tokensThe projector SHOULD avoid:- micro-chunks that contain only one sentence unless it is a high-value invariant- mega-chunks that contain an entire section with mixed concerns---# 7. Chunk ClassificationEach chunk MUST be assigned:- `level`- `chunkKind`- `normativeStrength`- `status`- optional concept tags---# 8. Level Assignment RulesLevels represent the abstraction stratum of the chunk itself, not the artifact as a whole.## 8.1 L1 — implementation / operational detailAssign `nebula:L1` when a chunk is primarily about:- file/module/class layout- API signatures or field-level request/response shapes- schema fields and exact JSON examples- traversal step logic in implementation form- migration task checklists- compatibility adapters and rollout steps- concrete validation checks- code-generation or compilation pass details- exact Conduit integration mechanics### examples- “add `level` to `nebula_artifact` and `nebula_cross_reference`”- “compiler emits `ExecutionReceipt` nodes with parent cursor ids”- “Phase 2 migration sequence: dual-write old plan registry and WRP graph”## 8.2 L2 — subsystem semantics / formal system behaviorAssign `nebula:L2` when a chunk is primarily about:- protocol semantics- DAG semantics- traversal semantics- formal lifecycle rules- graph invariants- execution contracts- state transition rules- artifact relationship semantics- chunk schema semantics### examples- “a WRP request compiles into a DAG whose nodes are execution units”- “receipts are immutable records of execution outcomes”- “Traversal must not execute a node whose predecessors are incomplete”## 8.3 L3 — architectural rationale / migration strategy / design tradeoffAssign `nebula:L3` when a chunk is primarily about:- why the protocol is structured this way- tradeoffs among alternative models- migration sequencing and rollout strategy- compatibility philosophy- boundary decisions between Nebula / Conduit / runtime- architectural decomposition rationale### examples- “Migration is staged so legacy workflows can coexist during cutover”- “Traversal remains separate from protocol formalization to preserve replaceability”- “Chunk-level levels are necessary because one document mixes implementation and rationale”## 8.4 L4 — doctrine / meta-ontology / worldviewAssign `nebula:L4` when a chunk is primarily about:- universal methodology- ontology-first doctrine- role philosophy- persistent engineering brain rules- meta-rules governing how artifacts should be interpreted across domainsWRP documents will rarely contain L4 chunks, but the projector MUST allow them if they appear.## 8.5 Tie-breaking ruleIf a chunk mixes levels, assign the level of the **dominant actionable purpose**.Tie-break priority:- if implementation instructions are present and operationally central → `L1`- else if formal subsystem semantics dominate → `L2`- else if rationale/tradeoff dominates → `L3`- else doctrine/meta → `L4`---# 9. Chunk Kind Classification RulesEach chunk MUST be assigned a `chunkKind`.## 9.1 Core chunk kindsThe WRP projector MUST support at least the following kinds:- `OVERVIEW`- `DEFINITION`- `PROTOCOL_RULE`- `DATA_MODEL`- `ALGORITHM`- `INVARIANT`- `RATIONALE`- `MIGRATION_STEP`- `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`- `OPEN_QUESTION`- `EXAMPLE`- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`## 9.2 Classification heuristics### `OVERVIEW`Use for:- section introductions- high-level summaries of a subsystem or artifact### `DEFINITION`Use for:- explicit term definitions- identity/lifecycle terminology- conceptual type descriptions not yet prescribing behavior### `PROTOCOL_RULE`Use for:- request/response semantics- protocol-level must/should rules- lifecycle constraints expressed as protocol behavior### `DATA_MODEL`Use for:- node/edge structures- fields, schemas, object model mappings- compilation or receipt data shapes### `ALGORITHM`Use for:- traversal order- graph compilation passes- validation procedures- deterministic execution logic### `INVARIANT`Use for:- statements that must always hold across valid WRP state- acyclicity, immutability, uniqueness, ordering guarantees### `RATIONALE`Use for:- “why” explanations- architectural tradeoffs- boundary explanations- decomposition reasoning### `MIGRATION_STEP`Use for:- rollout sequencing- compatibility tasks- backfill / cutover steps- staged adoption instructions### `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA`Use for:- explicit conditions for completion or correctness- verification checklist items### `OPEN_QUESTION`Use for:- unresolved design questions- TODO architecture decisions- future investigation points### `EXAMPLE`Use for:- worked examples- sample requests / DAG shapes / traversal traces### `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE`Use for:- code-facing notes- file layout guidance- “do this in the importer/compiler/runtime” instructions## 9.3 Multi-label ruleA chunk SHOULD have one primary `chunkKind`.A secondary tag list MAY be attached separately if a chunk straddles multiple concerns, but retrieval ranking MUST use the primary kind.---# 10. Normative Strength ExtractionEach chunk MUST be assigned a `normativeStrength`.## 10.1 Allowed strengths- `REQUIRED`- `PROHIBITED`- `RECOMMENDED`- `INFORMATIVE`## 10.2 Extraction rules### `REQUIRED`Use when the chunk contains language such as:- must- shall- is required to- cannot be valid unless- always### `PROHIBITED`Use when the chunk contains:- must not- shall not- never- prohibited- invalid if### `RECOMMENDED`Use when the chunk contains:- should- recommended- ordinarily- preferred- expected to### `INFORMATIVE`Use when the chunk is primarily descriptive, explanatory, or exploratory and does not prescribe behavior.## 10.3 Mixed normative languageIf a chunk contains both informative explanation and a clear normative rule, the chunk SHOULD be split if possible.If not split, normative strength follows the strongest explicit rule present:- `PROHIBITED` > `REQUIRED` > `RECOMMENDED` > `INFORMATIVE`---# 11. Status AssignmentProjected chunks MUST default to `nebula:ACTIVE` unless source metadata indicates otherwise.The projector SHOULD support future status extraction for:- `DRAFT`- `ACTIVE`- `SUPERSEDED`- `DEPRECATED`Possible signals:- explicit frontmatter- “superseded by” text- migration plan status tables- artifact registry metadata---# 12. Cross-Reference ExtractionThe projector MUST extract cross-references at artifact, section, and chunk level where possible.## 12.1 Explicit artifact referencesEmit a cross-reference when a chunk explicitly mentions a known artifact key or canonical artifact title.### examples- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `WRP Migration Plan`- `WRP v1.0 Protocol Formalization`## 12.2 Section referencesEmit a section-level cross-reference when a chunk references another section by heading name or stable section key.### examples- “see Identity and Versioning”- “as described in Execution Semantics / Receipts”## 12.3 Known concept referencesThe projector SHOULD maintain a concept lexicon for high-value WRP terms such as:- `ExecutionContext`- `ExecutionReceipt`- `WorkRequest`- `TraversalCursor`- `CompiledDag`- `MigrationPhase`- `ProtocolVersion`Mentions of these MAY emit:- concept tags- chunk-to-chunk inferred references- future concept nodes if concept projection is enabled## 12.4 Link-derived referencesMarkdown links MUST be interpreted as references and MAY become:- chunk → chunk edges if target is internal- chunk → artifact edges if target is another artifact- chunk → external source edges if external references are permitted## 12.5 Relation type inferenceDefault inferred relation types:- mentions protocol artifact semantics → `DEPENDS_ON`- migration instructions targeting another artifact → `MIGRATES`- rationale explaining why another structure must exist → `CONSTRAINS`- worked example illustrating another chunk → `EXEMPLIFIES`- open question about another artifact/section → `RAISES_QUESTION`If relation type is ambiguous, default to `REFERENCES` unless stricter inference rules are configured.---# 13. Section and Chunk ID Construction## 13.1 Section IDsFormat:```text<artifact-id>/section/<section-key-suffix>
```

## 13.2 Chunk IDs

Format:

```
<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>
```

```
<section-id>/chunk/<ordinal>
```

```

```

```

Chunk ordinals MUST be stable relative to section-local chunk order.

## 13.3 Re-import stability

On re-import:

- if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stable
if heading path and chunk boundary remain stable, ids MUST remain stable

- if a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new ids
if a section is renamed, projector SHOULD attempt fuzzy continuity mapping before issuing new ids

- if a chunk splits, the original id MAY be superseded by child chunk ids with lineage metadata if supported

# 14. Conduit Metadata Back-Projection

The projector SHOULD attach Conduit metadata when available.

## 14.1 Artifact-level links

An artifact MAY link to:

- Conduit plan ids
Conduit plan ids

- plan status
plan status

- implementation branch / task identifiers
implementation branch / task identifiers

- migration work package identifiers
migration work package identifiers

## 14.2 Chunk-level links

A chunk MAY link to:

- a Conduit plan implementing the chunk
a Conduit plan implementing the chunk

- execution receipts demonstrating realization
execution receipts demonstrating realization

- migration steps or validation results
migration steps or validation results

## 14.3 Source precedence

If Conduit metadata conflicts with artifact bootstrap metadata:

- explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identity
explicit artifact bootstrap metadata wins for artifact identity

- Conduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation links
Conduit metadata may augment operational status and implementation links

- conflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten
conflicting plan bindings MUST be preserved for review rather than silently overwritten

---

# 15. Importer Determinism Requirements

Projection MUST be deterministic for the same source inputs and same projector version.

Determinism requirements:

- stable heading normalization
stable heading normalization

- stable chunk ordering
stable chunk ordering

- stable chunk boundary rules
stable chunk boundary rules

- stable level and chunkKind heuristics
stable level and chunkKind heuristics

- stable relation inference defaults
stable relation inference defaults

Any projector version change that can alter emitted chunk ids or classifications SHOULD increment a projector version stamp stored on emitted records.

---

# 16. Validation Rules

The importer MUST reject or flag projection results that violate the following:

## 16.1 Artifact integrity

- source document mapped to unknown artifact in strict mode
source document mapped to unknown artifact in strict mode

- duplicate artifact key projection in one import batch
duplicate artifact key projection in one import batch

## 16.2 Section integrity

- duplicatesectionKeywithin an artifact
duplicatesectionKeywithin an artifact

- invalid parent-child heading hierarchy
invalid parent-child heading hierarchy

## 16.3 Chunk integrity

- empty chunk body after trimming
empty chunk body after trimming

- missing level
missing level

- missing chunkKind
missing chunkKind

- missing normativeStrength
missing normativeStrength

- duplicate chunk id in one import batch
duplicate chunk id in one import batch

## 16.4 Cross-reference integrity

- source or target id missing
source or target id missing

- relation type missing
relation type missing

- self-loop edges unless explicitly allowed
self-loop edges unless explicitly allowed

- duplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge
duplicate identical edges unless deduplication policy permits weighted merge

---

# 17. Initial WRP-Specific Heuristic Defaults

Until a richer classifier exists, the projector SHOULD apply these WRP-specific priors:

## wrp-v1-protocol

Bias toward:

- L2
L2

- PROTOCOL_RULE
PROTOCOL_RULE

- DEFINITION
DEFINITION

- INVARIANT
INVARIANT

## wrp-v1_1-dag

Bias toward:

- L2
L2

- DATA_MODEL
DATA_MODEL

- ALGORITHM
ALGORITHM

- INVARIANT
INVARIANT

## wrp-v1_2-traversal

Bias toward:

- L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semantic
L1orL2depending on whether content is implementation-facing or semantic

- ALGORITHM
ALGORITHM

- IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE
IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE

- INVARIANT
INVARIANT

## wrp-migration-plan

Bias toward:

- L1for concrete rollout steps
L1for concrete rollout steps

- L3for migration rationale / sequencing
L3for migration rationale / sequencing

- MIGRATION_STEP
MIGRATION_STEP

- RATIONALE
RATIONALE

- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA

---

# 18. Recommended Import Output Shape

For each source document, the importer SHOULD emit:

- oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)
oneNebulaArtifactbinding (or verification of existing binding)

- NebulaSectionrows for heading structure
NebulaSectionrows for heading structure

- NebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic units
NebulaChunkrows for chunked semantic units

- NebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from references
NebulaCrossReferencerows inferred from references

- optional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is present
optional execution-link rows if Conduit metadata is present

- import receipt / projector report containing:artifact idsource pathprojector versionsection countchunk countxref countwarningsvalidation failures
import receipt / projector report containing:

- artifact id
artifact id

- source path
source path

- projector version
projector version

- section count
section count

- chunk count
chunk count

- xref count
xref count

- warnings
warnings

- validation failures
validation failures

---

# 19. Future Extensions

The following are intentionally out of scope for the first WRP projection pass but expected later:

- concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)
concept node projection (ExecutionReceipt,TraversalCursor, etc.)

- embedding generation and vector indexing
embedding generation and vector indexing

- role-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itself
role-specific retrieval scoring weights in the importer itself

- supersession lineage across chunk revisions
supersession lineage across chunk revisions

- bidirectional Conduit synchronization
bidirectional Conduit synchronization

- LLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristics
LLM-assisted chunk classification as a fallback after deterministic heuristics

- confidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments
confidence scoring for level / chunk kind assignments

---

# 20. Summary

The WRP document projection pipeline exists to transform a small set of high-value markdown artifacts into a stable Nebula graph with:

- artifact identity
artifact identity

- section structure
section structure

- semantically coherent chunking
semantically coherent chunking

- chunk-level level stratification
chunk-level level stratification

- chunk kind and normative classification
chunk kind and normative classification

- cross-artifact references
cross-artifact references

- optional execution links back to Conduit
optional execution links back to Conduit

The first-pass rule is simple:

> project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.

project by heading, split by semantic purpose, classify at chunk level, preserve stable ids, and emit explicit graph structure rather than storing markdown as opaque blobs.

be kept out of default retrieval until repairedI would model this as adocument/artifact review-governance layerthat sits alongside the WRP artifact/chunk projection, not inside it.The simplest thing I think you should addAdd areview state / lifecycle overlayto Nebula artifacts and optionally sections/chunks.At minimum, every projected document/artifact should be able to carry fields like:reviewStatusreviewPrioritylastReviewedAtreviewNotessupersededByneedsAttentionattentionReasonThat gives you the very simple workflow you want:“As I’m reading through the corpus, I can mark this spec as needs review / outdated / superseded / authoritative / draft, and then retrieval and dashboards can prioritize accordingly.”I would separate this from the existingstatusRight now in the projection docs we’ve usedstatusfor things like:ACTIVEDRAFTSUPERSEDEDDEPRECATEDThat’s useful, but it mixesartifact lifecyclewithhuman review workflow.Those are related, but they are not the same thing.For example:a doc can beACTIVEbut stillNEEDS_REVIEWa doc can beSUPERSEDEDand yetREVIEWEDa doc can beDRAFTbutCURRENT_FOCUSa doc can beACTIVEandTRUSTED, but some chunks inside it may beQUESTIONEDSo I would keep two separate axes:Axis 1 — artifact lifecycle / semantic statusThis is about what the documentisin the system.Examples:DRAFTACTIVESUPERSEDEDDEPRECATEDARCHIVEDThis is the ontology / corpus truth axis.Axis 2 — review / attention workflowThis is about whatyou want people to do with it now.Examples:UNREVIEWEDNEEDS_REVIEWUNDER_REVIEWREVIEWEDOUTDATEDQUESTIONEDCURRENT_FOCUSBLOCKEDREADY_TO_SUPERSEDEThis is the operational prioritization axis.That split is the key thing.My recommendation: add a Nebula “review state” schema nowI’d add a new schema file:schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonldand use it to define:ClassesReviewStateReviewAnnotationmaybeAttentionReasonProperties on artifacts / sections / chunksreviewStatusreviewPrioritylastReviewedAtreviewedByreviewSummaryattentionReasonsupersededBysupersedesneedsAttentionfocusScoreThe minimum viable model I’d use1)reviewStatusThis is the main thing you’ll set by hand as you walk the corpus.Suggested values:UNREVIEWEDNEEDS_REVIEWUNDER_REVIEWREVIEWEDOUTDATEDSUPERSEDED_CANDIDATESUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDQUESTIONEDCURRENT_FOCUSI would not worry yet about making these perfect. The important part is that they let you sort the pile.2)reviewPriorityA simple ranking field so you can filter your queue.Example values:P0P1P2P3or numeric0..100.I’d probably use a simple enum first:CRITICALHIGHMEDIUMLOW3)attentionReasonThis is what makes the review state useful rather than just decorative.Examples:OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_CODECONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_ARCHITECTUREBLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATIONNEEDS_NORMALIZATIONDUPLICATE_OF_NEWER_DOCUNCLEAR_OWNERSHIPPENDING_MIGRATIONNEEDS_LEVEL_TAGGINGREQUIRES_CHUNK_REVIEWThis gives you something much better than a generic “needs review.”4)lastReviewedAtThis lets you see whether “reviewed” means yesterday or six months ago.5)reviewSummaryA short free-text note like:“WRP protocol is mostly current, but the execution section predates the traversal split.”“Migration plan assumes legacy WorkRequest shape; needs rewrite against WRP DAG.”“Good architecture rationale, but operational details moved to Conduit.”That note will be disproportionately valuable.Where I would attach review stateI’d support it atthree levels, but onlyuse one heavily at first.A. Artifact-level review stateThis is the big one.You mark the whole doc/spec as:needs reviewoutdatedcurrent focussupersededThis is the simplest and probably 80% of the value.B. Section-level review stateUseful when:the protocol doc is mostly goodbut the “Execution Semantics” section is outdatedC. Chunk-level review stateUseful later for:one invariant is still goodone migration step is obsoleteone rationale chunk is still worth surfacingBut I would not start by trying to review every chunk by hand.The workflow I’d actually implement firstI’d make the first pass dead simple:Step 1: add review columns to artifactsOnnebula_artifactadd:review_statusreview_prioritylast_reviewed_atreview_summaryneeds_attentionattention_reasonStep 2: optionally mirror on cross-reference table laterNot necessary at first, but eventually you may want to flag edges too.Step 3: build a “review queue” querySomething like:show me all artifacts where:review_status IN ('NEEDS_REVIEW', 'OUTDATED', 'QUESTIONED', 'CURRENT_FOCUS')ordered by priority desc, then updated_at descStep 4: make retrieval honor itThis is where it gets powerful.For example:Builder retrieval shouldpreferACTIVEREVIEWEDCURRENT_FOCUSExplorer may includeOUTDATEDandSUPERSEDEDif explicitly askeddefault retrieval should probablydemoteOUTDATEDandQUESTIONEDSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDshould only show up when historical context is requestedHow I’d integrate this with the retrieval profiles we just definedI would extend the retrieval profiles with review-state behavior.Add fields like:allowedReviewStatuspreferredReviewStatusdemotedReviewStatusincludeOutdatedArtifactsincludeSupersededArtifactsSo for example:Builderprefer:REVIEWED,CURRENT_FOCUSdemote:OUTDATED,QUESTIONEDexclude superseded by defaultArchitectprefer:REVIEWED,CURRENT_FOCUSallowQUESTIONEDallowOUTDATEDif it still carries rationaleExplorerallow almost everythingespeciallySUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDandOUTDATEDwhen tracing lineageInspectorpreferQUESTIONED,OUTDATED,NEEDS_REVIEW, because those are often exactly the problem areasThat last one is important:Inspector probably wants the trouble spots.The smallest ontology I’d write nextIf you want the simplest thing that still fits the Nebula direction, I’d writetwo companion artifacts nextbefore anything else:1)schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonldThis defines the vocabulary for:review statusesprioritiesattention reasonsreview annotationsI’d make it cover both artifacts and chunks, even if you only use artifact-level initially.2)data/nebula/bootstrap/review-queue-seed.jsonldThis is optional, but useful if you want to start immediately by hand-tagging the WRP docs you just created.For example, you could seed something like:wrp-v1-protocol→CURRENT_FOCUSwrp-v1_1-dag→CURRENT_FOCUSwrp-v1_2-traversal→CURRENT_FOCUSwrp-migration-plan→NEEDS_REVIEWor whatever is true for you.That would give you a live queue right away.My recommended concrete statusesIf you want a clean first set, I’d use exactly these:Review statusesUNREVIEWEDNEEDS_REVIEWUNDER_REVIEWREVIEWEDCURRENT_FOCUSOUTDATEDQUESTIONEDSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDPrioritiesCRITICALHIGHMEDIUMLOWAttention reasonsBLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATIONOUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIMEOUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURECONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODELREQUIRES_MIGRATIONDUPLICATED_ELSEWHERENEEDS_LEVEL_REVIEWNEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEWThat’s enough to be useful immediately.My answer to the core questionis it possible for me to do the simplest thing: as I review the corpus of specs and documentation, categorize them as needing review, outdated, superseded, etc., to focus everyone’s attention on priorities?Yes — and I think you should do itbeforethe rest of Nebula gets much more elaborate.Because without that layer, Nebula can tell you what exists, but notwhat deserves attention now.With it, Nebula becomes not just a knowledge graph but aliving engineering review board.What I suggest we do nextI’d change the order of the next docs.Before the chunk-kinds ontology and importer pseudocode, I would write thesetwo:schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonlddocs/nebula/review-workflow.mdThe workflow doc would specify exactly how you, Builder, Architect, Inspector, Explorer, and Conduit interact with review status:who can set itwhat it meanshow it affects retrievalhow supersession is markedhow review state rolls from artifact → section → chunkThen after that, we do the two we parked:3.schemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld4.docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdIf you want, I’ll go straight intoschemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonldnext and make it repo-ready.Helpjuice, Inc.SponsoredCompany Knowledge, Now Searchable by AIHelpjuice gives teams an AI-powered knowledge base built from their real documentation.

Yes — and I think you should make that afirst-class Nebula feature immediately, not an afterthought.

What you’re describing is simpler than retrieval profiles and importer semantics, but it’s operationally more important because it gives you a way totriage the corpus itself:

- what needs review now
what needs review now

- what is stale
what is stale

- what has been superseded
what has been superseded

- what is authoritative
what is authoritative

- what is still just a draft
what is still just a draft

- what should be kept out of default retrieval until repaired
what should be kept out of default retrieval until repaired

I would model this as adocument/artifact review-governance layerthat sits alongside the WRP artifact/chunk projection, not inside it.

---

# The simplest thing I think you should add

Add areview state / lifecycle overlayto Nebula artifacts and optionally sections/chunks.

At minimum, every projected document/artifact should be able to carry fields like:

- reviewStatus
reviewStatus

- reviewPriority
reviewPriority

- lastReviewedAt
lastReviewedAt

- reviewNotes
reviewNotes

- supersededBy
supersededBy

- needsAttention
needsAttention

- attentionReason
attentionReason

That gives you the very simple workflow you want:

> “As I’m reading through the corpus, I can mark this spec as needs review / outdated / superseded / authoritative / draft, and then retrieval and dashboards can prioritize accordingly.”

“As I’m reading through the corpus, I can mark this spec as needs review / outdated / superseded / authoritative / draft, and then retrieval and dashboards can prioritize accordingly.”

---

# I would separate this from the existingstatus

Right now in the projection docs we’ve usedstatusfor things like:

- ACTIVE
ACTIVE

- DRAFT
DRAFT

- SUPERSEDED
SUPERSEDED

- DEPRECATED
DEPRECATED

That’s useful, but it mixesartifact lifecyclewithhuman review workflow.

Those are related, but they are not the same thing.

For example:

- a doc can beACTIVEbut stillNEEDS_REVIEW
a doc can beACTIVEbut stillNEEDS_REVIEW

- a doc can beSUPERSEDEDand yetREVIEWED
a doc can beSUPERSEDEDand yetREVIEWED

- a doc can beDRAFTbutCURRENT_FOCUS
a doc can beDRAFTbutCURRENT_FOCUS

- a doc can beACTIVEandTRUSTED, but some chunks inside it may beQUESTIONED
a doc can beACTIVEandTRUSTED, but some chunks inside it may beQUESTIONED

So I would keep two separate axes:

---

# Axis 1 — artifact lifecycle / semantic status

This is about what the documentisin the system.

Examples:

- DRAFT
DRAFT

- ACTIVE
ACTIVE

- SUPERSEDED
SUPERSEDED

- DEPRECATED
DEPRECATED

- ARCHIVED
ARCHIVED

This is the ontology / corpus truth axis.

---

# Axis 2 — review / attention workflow

This is about whatyou want people to do with it now.

Examples:

- UNREVIEWED
UNREVIEWED

- NEEDS_REVIEW
NEEDS_REVIEW

- UNDER_REVIEW
UNDER_REVIEW

- REVIEWED
REVIEWED

- OUTDATED
OUTDATED

- QUESTIONED
QUESTIONED

- CURRENT_FOCUS
CURRENT_FOCUS

- BLOCKED
BLOCKED

- READY_TO_SUPERSEDE
READY_TO_SUPERSEDE

This is the operational prioritization axis.

That split is the key thing.

---

I’d add a new schema file:

and use it to define:

## Classes

- ReviewState
ReviewState

- ReviewAnnotation
ReviewAnnotation

- maybeAttentionReason
maybeAttentionReason

## Properties on artifacts / sections / chunks

- reviewStatus
reviewStatus

- reviewPriority
reviewPriority

- lastReviewedAt
lastReviewedAt

- reviewedBy
reviewedBy

- reviewSummary
reviewSummary

- attentionReason
attentionReason

- supersededBy
supersededBy

- supersedes
supersedes

- needsAttention
needsAttention

- focusScore
focusScore

# The minimum viable model I’d use

## 1)reviewStatus

This is the main thing you’ll set by hand as you walk the corpus.

Suggested values:

- UNREVIEWED
UNREVIEWED

- NEEDS_REVIEW
NEEDS_REVIEW

- UNDER_REVIEW
UNDER_REVIEW

- REVIEWED
REVIEWED

- OUTDATED
OUTDATED

- SUPERSEDED_CANDIDATE
SUPERSEDED_CANDIDATE

- SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED
SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED

- QUESTIONED
QUESTIONED

- CURRENT_FOCUS
CURRENT_FOCUS

I would not worry yet about making these perfect. The important part is that they let you sort the pile.

---

## 2)reviewPriority

A simple ranking field so you can filter your queue.

Example values:

- P0
P0

- P1
P1

- P2
P2

- P3
P3

or numeric0..100.

I’d probably use a simple enum first:

- CRITICAL
CRITICAL

- HIGH
HIGH

- MEDIUM
MEDIUM

- LOW
LOW

---

## 3)attentionReason

This is what makes the review state useful rather than just decorative.

Examples:

- OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_CODE
OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_CODE

- CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_ARCHITECTURE
CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_ARCHITECTURE

- BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION
BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION

- NEEDS_NORMALIZATION
NEEDS_NORMALIZATION

- DUPLICATE_OF_NEWER_DOC
DUPLICATE_OF_NEWER_DOC

- UNCLEAR_OWNERSHIP
UNCLEAR_OWNERSHIP

- PENDING_MIGRATION
PENDING_MIGRATION

- NEEDS_LEVEL_TAGGING
NEEDS_LEVEL_TAGGING

- REQUIRES_CHUNK_REVIEW
REQUIRES_CHUNK_REVIEW

This gives you something much better than a generic “needs review.”

---

## 4)lastReviewedAt

This lets you see whether “reviewed” means yesterday or six months ago.

---

## 5)reviewSummary

A short free-text note like:

- “WRP protocol is mostly current, but the execution section predates the traversal split.”
“WRP protocol is mostly current, but the execution section predates the traversal split.”

- “Migration plan assumes legacy WorkRequest shape; needs rewrite against WRP DAG.”
“Migration plan assumes legacy WorkRequest shape; needs rewrite against WRP DAG.”

- “Good architecture rationale, but operational details moved to Conduit.”
“Good architecture rationale, but operational details moved to Conduit.”

That note will be disproportionately valuable.

---

# Where I would attach review state

I’d support it atthree levels, but onlyuse one heavily at first.

## A. Artifact-level review state

This is the big one.You mark the whole doc/spec as:

- needs review
needs review

- outdated
outdated

- current focus
current focus

- superseded
superseded

This is the simplest and probably 80% of the value.

## B. Section-level review state

Useful when:

- the protocol doc is mostly good
the protocol doc is mostly good

- but the “Execution Semantics” section is outdated
but the “Execution Semantics” section is outdated

## C. Chunk-level review state

Useful later for:

- one invariant is still good
one invariant is still good

- one migration step is obsolete
one migration step is obsolete

- one rationale chunk is still worth surfacing
one rationale chunk is still worth surfacing

But I would not start by trying to review every chunk by hand.

# The workflow I’d actually implement first

I’d make the first pass dead simple:

## Step 1: add review columns to artifacts

Onnebula_artifactadd:

- review_status
review_status

- review_priority
review_priority

- last_reviewed_at
last_reviewed_at

- review_summary
review_summary

- needs_attention
needs_attention

- attention_reason
attention_reason

## Step 2: optionally mirror on cross-reference table later

Not necessary at first, but eventually you may want to flag edges too.

## Step 3: build a “review queue” query

Something like:

## show me all artifacts where:

- review_status IN ('NEEDS_REVIEW', 'OUTDATED', 'QUESTIONED', 'CURRENT_FOCUS')
review_status IN ('NEEDS_REVIEW', 'OUTDATED', 'QUESTIONED', 'CURRENT_FOCUS')

- ordered by priority desc, then updated_at desc
ordered by priority desc, then updated_at desc

## Step 4: make retrieval honor it

This is where it gets powerful.

For example:

- Builder retrieval shouldpreferACTIVEREVIEWEDCURRENT_FOCUS
Builder retrieval shouldprefer

- ACTIVE
ACTIVE

- REVIEWED
REVIEWED

- CURRENT_FOCUS
CURRENT_FOCUS

- Explorer may includeOUTDATEDandSUPERSEDEDif explicitly asked
Explorer may includeOUTDATEDandSUPERSEDEDif explicitly asked

- default retrieval should probablydemoteOUTDATEDandQUESTIONED
default retrieval should probablydemoteOUTDATEDandQUESTIONED

- SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDshould only show up when historical context is requested
SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDshould only show up when historical context is requested

# How I’d integrate this with the retrieval profiles we just defined

I would extend the retrieval profiles with review-state behavior.

Add fields like:

- allowedReviewStatus
allowedReviewStatus

- preferredReviewStatus
preferredReviewStatus

- demotedReviewStatus
demotedReviewStatus

- includeOutdatedArtifacts
includeOutdatedArtifacts

- includeSupersededArtifacts
includeSupersededArtifacts

So for example:

## Builder

- prefer:REVIEWED,CURRENT_FOCUS
prefer:REVIEWED,CURRENT_FOCUS

- demote:OUTDATED,QUESTIONED
demote:OUTDATED,QUESTIONED

- exclude superseded by default
exclude superseded by default

## Architect

- prefer:REVIEWED,CURRENT_FOCUS
prefer:REVIEWED,CURRENT_FOCUS

- allowQUESTIONED
allowQUESTIONED

- allowOUTDATEDif it still carries rationale
allowOUTDATEDif it still carries rationale

## Explorer

- allow almost everything
allow almost everything

- especiallySUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDandOUTDATEDwhen tracing lineage
especiallySUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDandOUTDATEDwhen tracing lineage

## Inspector

- preferQUESTIONED,OUTDATED,NEEDS_REVIEW, because those are often exactly the problem areas
preferQUESTIONED,OUTDATED,NEEDS_REVIEW, because those are often exactly the problem areas

That last one is important:Inspector probably wants the trouble spots.

process."},{"id":"review:QUESTIONED","type":"ReviewStatus","label":"Questioned","comment":"The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt."},{"id":"review:SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED","type":"ReviewStatus","label":"Superseded Confirmed","comment":"The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval."},// -----------------------------// Priority vocabulary// -----------------------------{"id":"review:CRITICAL","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"Critical","comment":"Immediate attention required because the item blocks implementation, risks incorrect work, or is central to current execution."},{"id":"review:HIGH","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"High","comment":"Important review work that should be addressed soon."},{"id":"review:MEDIUM","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"Medium","comment":"Useful review work, but not urgent."},{"id":"review:LOW","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"Low","comment":"Backlog review work with low immediate operational impact."},// -----------------------------// Attention reasons// implementation work."},{"id":"review:OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIME","type":"AttentionReason","label":"Out of Date with Runtime","comment":"The item no longer matches the current runtime behavior or execution model."},{"id":"review:OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE","type":"AttentionReason","label":"Out of Date with Architecture","comment":"The item no longer reflects the current architectural decomposition, boundaries, or design intent."},{"id":"review:CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODEL","type":"AttentionReason","label":"Conflicts with New Model","comment":"The item conflicts with a newer ontology, reviewed."},{"id":"review:NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW","type":"AttentionReason","label":"Needs Chunking Review","comment":"The item’s section or chunk segmentation should be revisited."},// Scope"},{"id":"review:SECTION_SCOPE","type":"schema:DefinedTerm","label":"Section Scope"},{"id":"review:CHUNK_SCOPE","type":"schema:DefinedTerm","label":"Chunk Scope"}]}What this schema is doing conceptuallyIt gives Nebula areview overlaythat isindependent of lifecycle status.That means an artifact can simultaneously be:status = nebula:ACTIVEreviewStatus = review:NEEDS_REVIEWor:status = nebula:SUPERSEDEDreviewStatus = review:SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDThose are not redundant; they answer different questions:status→ what is this artifact in the corpus lifecycle?reviewStatus→ what attention should we pay to it right now?That split is the core reason to do this as a separate schema instead of just stuffing more enum values intostatus.The one modeling change I would make immediatelyThe JSON-LD above defines review properties in the vocabulary, but I would also makeReviewAnnotationa first-class node pattern, not just “extra columns on artifacts.”In other words, I’d supportbothof these:A. denormalized convenience fields onnebula_artifactreview_statusreview_prioritylast_reviewed_atreview_summaryneeds_attentionB. normalized review annotation recordsSomething like:JSON{"id":"review:annotation/wrp-v1-protocol/2026-06-21","type":"ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo":"wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol","reviewStatus":"review:CURRENT_FOCUS","reviewPriority":"review:HIGH","attentionReason": ["review:BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION"],"needsAttention":true,"lastReviewedAt":"2026-06-21T13:00:00Z","reviewedBy":"role:architect","reviewSummary":"Protocol remains active and central, but execution-related sections should be checked against the traversal split."}Why I think you want both:artifact columnsmake filtering and dashboards easyannotation nodespreserve review history, multiple opinions, and section/chunk review laterSo my rule would be:the artifact table stores thecurrent effective review statereview annotations store thehistory / evidence / per-scope detailHow I’d wire this into the SQL side immediatelyIf you want the simplest operational thing, I’d add these columns toboth:nebula_artifactreview_statusreview_priorityneeds_attentionlast_reviewed_atreview_summaryfocus_scorenebula_chunksame fields, nullableI wouldnotbother withnebula_sectionon day one unless you know you want section-level review in the UI immediately.Then add a new table:nebula_review_annotationwith fields like:idtarget_type(artifact,chunk, maybesection)target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason_jsonneeds_attentionreviewed_byreview_summarycreated_atThat gives you both the cheap operational path and the richer future path.What the next doc should doThe schema above gives the vocabulary, but thebehaviorstill needs to be pinned down. So the next document should be:docs/nebula/review-workflow.mdThat doc should define:1. who can set review stateFor example:you manuallyInspector role recommendationsBuilder/Architect proposalsConduit import hooks maybe, but not as final authority2. effective-state precedenceIf:artifact saysREVIEWEDbut one chunk saysQUESTIONEDand a newer annotation saysCURRENT_FOCUSwhat wins?3. how review state affects retrievalFor example:default retrieval demotesOUTDATEDExplorer can include superseded materialInspector may boostQUESTIONED4. how supersession interacts with reviewExamples:ifsupersededByis set, shouldreviewStatusauto-flip toSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED?or only after manual confirmation?5. how “current focus” is maintainedBecause you probably don’t want 40 things marked current focus forever.After that, we return to the two deferred docsSo the updated sequence is now:Review-governance insertionschemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld← done abovedocs/nebula/review-workflow.mdThen the two deferred docsschemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonlddocs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdIf you want, I’ll go straight intodocs/nebula/review-workflow.mdnext.Read AI, Inc.SponsoredMeeting Notes in ChatGPTAI meeting notes with integrated ChatGPT app

these:A. denormalized convenience fields onnebula_artifactreview_statusreview_prioritylast_reviewed_atreview_summaryneeds_attentionB. normalized review annotation recordsSomething like:JSON{"id":"review:annotation/wrp-v1-protocol/2026-06-21","type":"ReviewAnnotation","appliesTo":"wrp:artifact/wrp-v1-protocol","reviewStatus":"review:CURRENT_FOCUS","reviewPriority":"review:HIGH","attentionReason": ["review:BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION"],"needsAttention":true,"lastReviewedAt":"2026-06-21T13:00:00Z","reviewedBy":"role:architect","reviewSummary":"Protocol remains active and central, but execution-related sections should be checked against the traversal split."}Why I think you want both:artifact columnsmake filtering and dashboards easyannotation nodespreserve review history, multiple opinions, and section/chunk review laterSo my rule would be:the artifact table stores thecurrent effective review statereview annotations store thehistory / evidence / per-scope detailHow I’d wire this into the SQL side immediatelyIf you want the simplest operational thing, I’d add these columns toboth:nebula_artifactreview_statusreview_priorityneeds_attentionlast_reviewed_atreview_summaryfocus_scorenebula_chunksame fields, nullableI wouldnotbother withnebula_sectionon day one unless you know you want section-level review in the UI immediately.Then add a new table:nebula_review_annotationwith fields like:idtarget_type(artifact,chunk, maybesection)target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason_jsonneeds_attentionreviewed_byreview_summarycreated_atThat gives you both the cheap operational path and the richer future path.What the next doc should doThe schema above gives the vocabulary, but thebehaviorstill needs to be pinned down. So the next document should be:docs/nebula/review-workflow.mdThat doc should define:1. who can set review stateFor example:you manuallyInspector role recommendationsBuilder/Architect proposalsConduit import hooks maybe, but not as final authority2. effective-state precedenceIf:artifact saysREVIEWEDbut one chunk saysQUESTIONEDand a newer annotation saysCURRENT_FOCUSwhat wins?3. how review state affects retrievalFor example:default retrieval demotesOUTDATEDExplorer can include superseded materialInspector may boostQUESTIONED4. how supersession interacts with reviewExamples:ifsupersededByis set, shouldreviewStatusauto-flip toSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED?or only after manual confirmation?5. how “current focus” is maintainedBecause you probably don’t want 40 things marked current focus forever.After that, we return to the two deferred docsSo the updated sequence is now:Review-governance insertionschemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld← done abovedocs/nebula/review-workflow.mdThen the two deferred docsschemas/core/nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonlddocs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdIf you want, I’ll go straight intodocs/nebula/review-workflow.mdnext.Read AI, Inc.SponsoredMeeting Notes in ChatGPTAI meeting notes with integrated ChatGPT app

dashboards."},{"id":"review:OUTDATED","type":"ReviewStatus","label":"Outdated","comment":"The item contains material that is known to be out of date relative to the current architecture, code, or process."},{"id":"review:QUESTIONED","type":"ReviewStatus","label":"Questioned","comment":"The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt."},{"id":"review:SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED","type":"ReviewStatus","label":"Superseded Confirmed","comment":"The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval."},// -----------------------------// Priority vocabulary// -----------------------------{"id":"review:CRITICAL","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"Critical","comment":"Immediate attention required because the item blocks implementation, risks incorrect work, or is central to current execution."},{"id":"review:HIGH","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"High","comment":"Important review work that should be addressed soon."},{"id":"review:MEDIUM","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"Medium","comment":"Useful review work, but not urgent."},{"id":"review:LOW","type":"ReviewPriority","label":"Low","comment":"Backlog review work with low immediate operational impact."},// -----------------------------// Attention reasons//
