Here’s the next companion doc as the operational layer for the review-state schema.docs/nebula/review-workflow.mdMarkdown# Nebula Review Workflow**Status:** Draft**Owner:** Nebula governance / corpus maintenance**Purpose:** Define how review state is assigned, updated, interpreted, and used to prioritize attention across Nebula artifacts, sections, and chunks.---# 1. PurposeNebula stores a growing corpus of architecture notes, specifications, migration plans, ontology documents, implementation plans, and execution-adjacent material. Not all corpus material is equally current, equally trustworthy, or equally relevant to active work.This document defines a **review workflow overlay** that allows Nebula users and roles to mark corpus material as:- needing review- under active review- reviewed- current focus- outdated- questioned- supersededThe review workflow exists to answer a different question than lifecycle status.## Lifecycle status answers:- Is this artifact active, draft, deprecated, or superseded in the corpus?## Review status answers:- What should we pay attention to right now?- What should be trusted by default?- What needs inspection before it influences implementation?- What should be deprioritized or excluded from normal retrieval?Review state is therefore a **triage and trust overlay** on top of the corpus, not a replacement for artifact lifecycle semantics.---# 2. Core Principles## 2.1 Review state is separate from artifact lifecycleAn item may be:- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`- `status = SUPERSEDED` and `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- `status = DRAFT` and `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Lifecycle describes what the artifact **is**.Review state describes what the team should **do about it**.## 2.2 Review state is primarily an attention and trust signalReview state is used to:- focus corpus maintenance- guide retrieval ranking- reduce accidental reliance on stale documents- identify blocking or suspect specs- surface active areas of architecture work## 2.3 Artifact-level review is the default starting pointNebula SHOULD support review state at:- artifact level- section level- chunk levelHowever, the initial operational workflow assumes:- **artifact-level review is primary**- section/chunk review is optional and targetedThe system MUST NOT require chunk-by-chunk review to be useful.## 2.4 Review state is allowed to be provisionalReview state is not a certification regime. It is acceptable to mark an item:- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`without yet knowing the final replacement or fix. The goal is to make uncertainty visible and actionable.---# 3. Review Scope LevelsNebula review annotations may apply at three scopes.## 3.1 Artifact scopeApplies to an entire document / artifact such as:- `wrp-v1-protocol`- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `wrp-v1_2-traversal`- `wrp-migration-plan`Artifact scope is the default and most common review target.## 3.2 Section scopeApplies to a specific section within an artifact when the document is mixed-quality.Example:- the WRP protocol document is generally current- but the `Execution Semantics / Receipts` section is outdatedSection review SHOULD be used when:- only one part of a large artifact is stale or questionable- the artifact should remain broadly retrievable without blanket demotion## 3.3 Chunk scopeApplies to a specific chunk when review needs to be precise.Chunk review SHOULD be used sparingly and mainly when:- a particular invariant is suspect- a specific migration step is obsolete- a specific rationale chunk remains valuable even inside an outdated section---# 4. Review Status VocabularyThe following review statuses are defined by `schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`.## 4.1 `UNREVIEWED`The item has not yet been reviewed for current validity or relevance.Use when:- a document was imported but not yet triaged- a new chunk has not been evaluated## 4.2 `NEEDS_REVIEW`The item should be reviewed soon because it may be stale, incomplete, or important to current work.Use when:- the document is likely relevant to current implementation- the document predates a major architectural shift- the document appears important but confidence is low## 4.3 `UNDER_REVIEW`The item is actively being reviewed, rewritten, or reconciled.Use when:- you are actively comparing it against current architecture or code- Builder/Architect/Inspector are working through it now## 4.4 `REVIEWED`The item has been reviewed and is believed to be usable in normal work.Use when:- the document is current enough for default retrieval- known issues are minor or already called out## 4.5 `CURRENT_FOCUS`The item is a current focus of architecture or implementation attention and should be surfaced prominently.Use when:- active work depends on this item now- the item is central to the current execution stream- the item is the present working center of a subsystem redesign## 4.6 `OUTDATED`The item is known to be out of date relative to the current architecture, runtime, or workflow.Use when:- the document predates a material redesign- its prescriptions are no longer safe defaults- it still has historical value but should be demoted## 4.7 `QUESTIONED`The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt.Use when:- parts of the document conflict with newer understanding- the model may be wrong, not merely old- the document should be examined before it is trusted## 4.8 `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval.Use when:- there is a clear replacement artifact or replacement chunk set- the supersession is intentional and not merely suspected---# 5. Review PriorityReview priority answers: **how urgently should this item be revisited?**Allowed values:- `CRITICAL`- `HIGH`- `MEDIUM`- `LOW`## 5.1 Priority guidance### `CRITICAL`Use when:- the item is blocking implementation- the item is actively misleading current work- the item governs current execution and is likely wrong or stale### `HIGH`Use when:- the item is central to near-term architecture or implementation- review delay would materially slow work or degrade decisions### `MEDIUM`Use when:- the item matters, but not immediately- it should be triaged in the near future### `LOW`Use when:- review is backlog hygiene- the item is historical or peripheral---# 6. Attention ReasonsAttention reasons explain **why** an item needs review or focus.The first review-state schema defines these reasons:- `BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIME`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE`- `CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODEL`- `REQUIRES_MIGRATION`- `DUPLICATED_ELSEWHERE`- `NEEDS_LEVEL_REVIEW`- `NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`Multiple reasons MAY be attached to the same item.## ExampleA migration document might be:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `reviewPriority = HIGH`- `attentionReason = [REQUIRES_MIGRATION, OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE]`---# 7. Who May Set Review State## 7.1 Human authority is primaryThe human operator is the authoritative source of review state.In practice, this means you may set review state manually based on reading, comparison, or implementation experience.## 7.2 Roles may propose review state, but not silently finalize itThe following roles may recommend review changes:- **Inspector**- flags contradictions, stale invariants, missing migration updates, or retrieval hazards- **Architect**- flags architectural obsolescence, boundary drift, or rationale conflicts- **Builder**- flags implementation-blocking ambiguity or mismatch with actual code- **Explorer**- flags duplicate or related documents that may need consolidationThese role recommendations SHOULD be recorded as annotations or proposals, but SHOULD NOT silently overwrite the effective review state unless explicitly authorized.## 7.3 Importers may initialize, not decideImporters and projectors MAY set initial values such as:- `UNREVIEWED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW` when the source predates a known migration boundary- `OUTDATED` when explicit source metadata says soHowever, importers SHOULD NOT autonomously mark an item `REVIEWED` or `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`.---# 8. Effective Review State ModelNebula may store multiple review annotations over time. The system therefore needs a rule for determining the **effective review state** used in retrieval and dashboards.## 8.1 Effective review state per scopeEach reviewable object (artifact, section, chunk) SHOULD expose a single **effective review state** for operational use.This effective state may be materialized directly on the object row or computed from annotations.## 8.2 Default precedence ruleIf multiple annotations exist for the same object, the effective review state SHOULD be determined by:1. most recent human-authored authoritative annotation2. otherwise most recent approved role recommendation3. otherwise importer-initialized default4. otherwise `UNREVIEWED`## 8.3 Status severity tie-breakIf multiple candidate annotations are equally authoritative and recent enough to conflict, use the following severity ordering to avoid false optimism:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `UNDER_REVIEW`- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `UNREVIEWED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`This severity ordering is for tie-breaking only and MUST NOT be interpreted as a universal ranking of importance.## 8.4 Why `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is not treated as “most severe”Superseded material is often safe to ignore rather than urgent to fix. It is not necessarily a live problem. Therefore it should not outrank `QUESTIONED` or `CURRENT_FOCUS` in attention logic.---# 9. Artifact / Section / Chunk Rollup RulesReview state may exist at multiple scopes simultaneously. The workflow needs rules for how lower-level review state influences higher-level summaries.## 9.1 Artifact effective review is primaryArtifact review status is the main corpus-level triage signal and SHOULD be set explicitly rather than inferred whenever possible.## 9.2 Section and chunk review do not automatically overwrite artifact reviewIf an artifact is marked `REVIEWED` but one chunk is marked `QUESTIONED`, the artifact does not automatically become `QUESTIONED`.Instead, the artifact SHOULD receive one or more rollup indicators such as:- `needsAttention = true`- `attentionReason += NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`- optional `focusScore` boost- optional “contains questioned chunk” derived flag## 9.3 Optional artifact rollup policyImplementations MAY define a rollup threshold such as:- if ≥ 30% of chunks are `OUTDATED` or `QUESTIONED`, artifact effective review becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`- if any chunk is `CURRENT_FOCUS`, artifact `focusScore` is boosted- if all chunks are `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`, artifact may be proposed as `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`But this rollup SHOULD be advisory until chunk review is common enough to trust statistically.---# 10. Review ActionsThe review workflow recognizes the following actions.## 10.1 Mark Needs ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- optionally priority and attention reasonsUse when an item should enter the review queue.## 10.2 Start ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Use when active review or rewrite has begun.## 10.3 Mark ReviewedSet:- `reviewStatus = REVIEWED`- `lastReviewedAt`- optional summaryUse when the item is current enough for normal use.## 10.4 Mark Current FocusSet:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`Use when the item is a live center of implementation or architecture work.## 10.5 Mark OutdatedSet:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`Use when the item is no longer a safe default but may still be historically useful.## 10.6 Mark QuestionedSet:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`Use when the item may be wrong, not merely old.## 10.7 Confirm SupersededSet:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- set `supersededBy` if knownUse when a replacement is clear and the old material should be demoted from normal retrieval.---# 11. Relationship Between Supersession and ReviewSupersession and review are related but distinct.## 11.1 Supersession is a semantic relationshipExample:- `wrp-v1-protocol-v0` is superseded by `wrp-v1-protocol`This is modeled as:- `supersededBy`- `supersedes`- lifecycle `status`## 11.2 Review supersession is an operational confirmationAn item becomes `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when the team has decided it should be treated as superseded for retrieval and attention purposes.## 11.3 Auto-promotion ruleIf `supersededBy` is set, the system MAY propose:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`but SHOULD NOT automatically finalize it unless configured to do so.Reason:- some superseded artifacts still matter during a migration period- some artifacts are partially superseded but still operationally relevant---# 12. Review Workflow for Corpus TriageThis section defines the simple human workflow the system is meant to support.## 12.1 Initial triage passAs you review the corpus, each artifact SHOULD be assigned one of:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`with optional:- priority- attention reasons- short review summaryThe goal is not perfection. The goal is to make the corpus sortable and navigable.## 12.2 Triage heuristics### Mark `CURRENT_FOCUS` when:- active implementation or redesign is centered on the artifact now### Mark `NEEDS_REVIEW` when:- the artifact is probably important but confidence is not high enough- the artifact predates a major design change- the artifact is about to become implementation-relevant again### Mark `REVIEWED` when:- the artifact is current enough to be used normally### Mark `OUTDATED` when:- the artifact still has historical value but should not be trusted as a default guide### Mark `QUESTIONED` when:- the artifact may encode wrong assumptions or contradictions### Mark `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when:- a replacement exists and default retrieval should normally prefer the replacement---# 13. Retrieval EffectsReview state MUST influence Nebula retrieval.## 13.1 Default retrieval behaviorUnless explicitly overridden:- `CURRENT_FOCUS` receives a strong ranking boost- `REVIEWED` receives a positive ranking boost- `NEEDS_REVIEW` remains retrievable but slightly demoted relative to reviewed/current material- `OUTDATED` is demoted- `QUESTIONED` is demoted for Builder/Architect defaults but may be boosted for Inspector- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is excluded or strongly demoted from default retrieval## 13.2 Role-specific review-state behavior### BuilderPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Demote:- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`Exclude by default:- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`### ArchitectPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Allow:- `QUESTIONED`- selected `OUTDATED` material when rationale still matters### InspectorPrefer:- `QUESTIONED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `OUTDATED`because those often indicate the places where validation and contradiction analysis are most needed.### ExplorerAllow broad inclusion, including:- `OUTDATED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`when historical lineage or unresolved questions matter.---# 14. Dashboard / Queue BehaviorNebula SHOULD support a review queue over artifacts.## 14.1 Default review queueThe default review queue SHOULD show artifacts where:- `reviewStatus IN (NEEDS_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW, CURRENT_FOCUS, OUTDATED, QUESTIONED)`- OR `needsAttention = true`ordered by:1. `reviewPriority`2. `focusScore`3. `updatedAt` or `lastReviewedAt`## 14.2 Suggested dashboard slicesUseful corpus views include:### Current FocusArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`### Needs ReviewArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`### Questioned / RiskyArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`### Outdated but not yet supersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`### SupersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`---# 15. Attention ReasonsAttention reasons explain **why** an item needs review or focus.The first review-state schema defines these reasons:- `BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_RUNTIME`- `OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE`- `CONFLICTS_WITH_NEW_MODEL`- `REQUIRES_MIGRATION`- `DUPLICATED_ELSEWHERE`- `NEEDS_LEVEL_REVIEW`- `NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`Multiple reasons MAY be attached to the same item.## ExampleA migration document might be:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `reviewPriority = HIGH`- `attentionReason = [REQUIRES_MIGRATION, OUT_OF_DATE_WITH_ARCHITECTURE]`---# 7. Who May Set Review State## 7.1 Human authority is primaryThe human operator is the authoritative source of review state.In practice, this means you may set review state manually based on reading, comparison, or implementation experience.## 7.2 Roles may propose review state, but not silently finalize itThe following roles may recommend review changes:- **Inspector**  - flags contradictions, stale invariants, missing migration updates, or retrieval hazards- **Architect**  - flags architectural obsolescence, boundary drift, or rationale conflicts- **Builder**  - flags implementation-blocking ambiguity or mismatch with actual code- **Explorer**  - flags duplicate or related documents that may need consolidationThese role recommendations SHOULD be recorded as annotations or proposals, but SHOULD NOT silently overwrite the effective review state unless explicitly authorized.## 7.3 Importers may initialize, not decideImporters and projectors MAY set initial values such as:- `UNREVIEWED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW` when the source predates a known migration boundary- `OUTDATED` when explicit source metadata says soHowever, importers SHOULD NOT autonomously mark an item `REVIEWED` or `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`.---# 8. Effective Review State ModelNebula may store multiple review annotations over time. The system therefore needs a rule for determining the **effective review state** used in retrieval and dashboards.## 8.1 Effective review state per scopeEach reviewable object (artifact, section, chunk) SHOULD expose a single **effective review state** for operational use.This effective state may be materialized directly on the object row or computed from annotations.## 8.2 Default precedence ruleIf multiple annotations exist for the same object, the effective review state SHOULD be determined by:1. most recent human-authored authoritative annotation2. otherwise most recent approved role recommendation3. otherwise importer-initialized default4. otherwise `UNREVIEWED`## 8.3 Status severity tie-breakIf multiple candidate annotations are equally authoritative and recent enough to conflict, use the following severity ordering to avoid false optimism:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `UNDER_REVIEW`- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `UNREVIEWED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`This severity ordering is for tie-breaking only and MUST NOT be interpreted as a universal ranking of importance.## 8.4 Why `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is not treated as “most severe”Superseded material is often safe to ignore rather than urgent to fix. It is not necessarily a live problem. Therefore it should not outrank `QUESTIONED` or `CURRENT_FOCUS` in attention logic.---# 9. Artifact / Section / Chunk Rollup RulesReview state may exist at multiple scopes simultaneously. The workflow needs rules for how lower-level review state influences higher-level summaries.## 9.1 Artifact effective review is primaryArtifact review status is the main corpus-level triage signal and SHOULD be set explicitly rather than inferred whenever possible.## 9.2 Section and chunk review do not automatically overwrite artifact reviewIf an artifact is marked `REVIEWED` but one chunk is marked `QUESTIONED`, the artifact does not automatically become `QUESTIONED`.Instead, the artifact SHOULD receive one or more rollup indicators such as:- `needsAttention = true`- `attentionReason += NEEDS_CHUNKING_REVIEW`- optional `focusScore` boost- optional “contains questioned chunk” derived flag## 9.3 Optional artifact rollup policyImplementations MAY define a rollup threshold such as:- if ≥ 30% of chunks are `OUTDATED` or `QUESTIONED`, artifact effective review becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`- if any chunk is `CURRENT_FOCUS`, artifact `focusScore` is boosted- if all chunks are `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`, artifact may be proposed as `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`But this rollup SHOULD be advisory until chunk review is common enough to trust statistically.---# 10. Review ActionsThe review workflow recognizes the following actions.## 10.1 Mark Needs ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- optionally priority and attention reasonsUse when an item should enter the review queue.## 10.2 Start ReviewSet:- `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Use when active review or rewrite has begun.## 10.3 Mark ReviewedSet:- `reviewStatus = REVIEWED`- `lastReviewedAt`- optional summaryUse when the item is current enough for normal use.## 10.4 Mark Current FocusSet:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`Use when the item is a live center of implementation or architecture work.## 10.5 Mark OutdatedSet:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`Use when the item is no longer a safe default but may still be historically useful.## 10.6 Mark QuestionedSet:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`Use when the item may be wrong, not merely old.## 10.7 Confirm SupersededSet:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- set `supersededBy` if knownUse when a replacement is clear and the old material should be demoted from normal retrieval.---# 11. Relationship Between Supersession and ReviewSupersession and review are related but distinct.## 11.1 Supersession is a semantic relationshipExample:- `wrp-v1-protocol-v0` is superseded by `wrp-v1-protocol`This is modeled as:- `supersededBy`- `supersedes`- lifecycle `status`## 11.2 Review supersession is an operational confirmationAn item becomes `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when the team has decided it should be treated as superseded for retrieval and attention purposes.## 11.3 Auto-promotion ruleIf `supersededBy` is set, the system MAY propose:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`but SHOULD NOT automatically finalize it unless configured to do so.Reason:- some superseded artifacts still matter during a migration period- some artifacts are partially superseded but still operationally relevant---# 12. Review Workflow for Corpus TriageThis section defines the simple human workflow the system is meant to support.## 12.1 Initial triage passAs you review the corpus, each artifact SHOULD be assigned one of:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `REVIEWED`- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`with optional:- priority- attention reasons- short review summaryThe goal is not perfection. The goal is to make the corpus sortable and navigable.## 12.2 Triage heuristics### Mark `CURRENT_FOCUS` when:- active implementation or redesign is centered on the artifact now### Mark `NEEDS_REVIEW` when:- the artifact is probably important but confidence is not high enough- the artifact predates a major design change- the artifact is about to become implementation-relevant again### Mark `REVIEWED` when:- the artifact is current enough to be used normally### Mark `OUTDATED` when:- the artifact still has historical value but should not be trusted as a default guide### Mark `QUESTIONED` when:- the artifact may encode wrong assumptions or contradictions### Mark `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` when:- a replacement exists and default retrieval should normally prefer the replacement---# 13. Retrieval EffectsReview state MUST influence Nebula retrieval.## 13.1 Default retrieval behaviorUnless explicitly overridden:- `CURRENT_FOCUS` receives a strong ranking boost- `REVIEWED` receives a positive ranking boost- `NEEDS_REVIEW` remains retrievable but slightly demoted relative to reviewed/current material- `OUTDATED` is demoted- `QUESTIONED` is demoted for Builder/Architect defaults but may be boosted for Inspector- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED` is excluded or strongly demoted from default retrieval## 13.2 Role-specific review-state behavior### BuilderPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Demote:- `OUTDATED`- `QUESTIONED`Exclude by default:- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`### ArchitectPrefer:- `CURRENT_FOCUS`- `REVIEWED`Allow:- `QUESTIONED`- selected `OUTDATED` material when rationale still matters### InspectorPrefer:- `QUESTIONED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`- `OUTDATED`because those often indicate the places where validation and contradiction analysis are most needed.### ExplorerAllow broad inclusion, including:- `OUTDATED`- `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`when historical lineage or unresolved questions matter.---# 14. Dashboard / Queue BehaviorNebula SHOULD support a review queue over artifacts.## 14.1 Default review queueThe default review queue SHOULD show artifacts where:- `reviewStatus IN (NEEDS_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW, CURRENT_FOCUS, OUTDATED, QUESTIONED)`- OR `needsAttention = true`ordered by:1. `reviewPriority`2. `focusScore`3. `updatedAt` or `lastReviewedAt`## 14.2 Suggested dashboard slicesUseful corpus views include:### Current FocusArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`### Needs ReviewArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`### Questioned / RiskyArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = QUESTIONED`### Outdated but not yet supersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = OUTDATED`### SupersededArtifacts with:- `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`---# 15. Recommended Initial SQL ShapeFor the first operational implementation, Nebula SHOULD materialize current effective review state directly on `nebula_artifact`.Recommended columns:- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `needs_attention`- `last_reviewed_at`- `review_summary`- `focus_score`Optional on `nebula_chunk`:- same fields, nullableReview history SHOULD be stored separately in `nebula_review_annotation` with fields such as:- `id`- `target_type`- `target_id`- `review_status`- `review_priority`- `attention_reason_json`- `needs_attention`- `reviewed_by`- `review_summary`- `created_at`---# 16. Example Review Annotations## 16.1 Current focus artifact```json{  "id": "review:annotation/wrp-v1_2-traversal/2026-06-21",  "type": "ReviewAnnotation",  "appliesTo": "wrp:artifact/wrp-v1_2-traversal",  "reviewStatus": "review:CURRENT_FOCUS",  "reviewPriority": "review:CRITICAL",  "attentionReason": [    "review:BLOCKING_IMPLEMENTATION"  ],  "needsAttention": true,  "lastReviewedAt": "2026-06-21T13:00:00Z",  "reviewedBy": "role:architect",  "reviewSummary": "Traversal engine spec is the current implementation center and should remain top-ranked for Builder and Architect retrieval."}
```

# Nebula Review Workflow**Status:** Draft  **Owner:** Nebula governance / corpus maintenance  **Purpose:** Define how review state is assigned, updated, interpreted, and used to prioritize attention across Nebula artifacts, sections, and chunks.---# 1. PurposeNebula stores a growing corpus of architecture notes, specifications, migration plans, ontology documents, implementation plans, and execution-adjacent material. Not all corpus material is equally current, equally trustworthy, or equally relevant to active work.This document defines a **review workflow overlay** that allows Nebula users and roles to mark corpus material as:- needing review- under active review- reviewed- current focus- outdated- questioned- supersededThe review workflow exists to answer a different question than lifecycle status.## Lifecycle status answers:- Is this artifact active, draft, deprecated, or superseded in the corpus?## Review status answers:- What should we pay attention to right now?- What should be trusted by default?- What needs inspection before it influences implementation?- What should be deprioritized or excluded from normal retrieval?Review state is therefore a **triage and trust overlay** on top of the corpus, not a replacement for artifact lifecycle semantics.---# 2. Core Principles## 2.1 Review state is separate from artifact lifecycleAn item may be:- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = NEEDS_REVIEW`- `status = ACTIVE` and `reviewStatus = CURRENT_FOCUS`- `status = SUPERSEDED` and `reviewStatus = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`- `status = DRAFT` and `reviewStatus = UNDER_REVIEW`Lifecycle describes what the artifact **is**.  Review state describes what the team should **do about it**.## 2.2 Review state is primarily an attention and trust signalReview state is used to:- focus corpus maintenance- guide retrieval ranking- reduce accidental reliance on stale documents- identify blocking or suspect specs- surface active areas of architecture work## 2.3 Artifact-level review is the default starting pointNebula SHOULD support review state at:- artifact level- section level- chunk levelHowever, the initial operational workflow assumes:- **artifact-level review is primary**- section/chunk review is optional and targetedThe system MUST NOT require chunk-by-chunk review to be useful.## 2.4 Review state is allowed to be provisionalReview state is not a certification regime. It is acceptable to mark an item:- `QUESTIONED`- `OUTDATED`- `NEEDS_REVIEW`without yet knowing the final replacement or fix. The goal is to make uncertainty visible and actionable.---# 3. Review Scope LevelsNebula review annotations may apply at three scopes.## 3.1 Artifact scopeApplies to an entire document / artifact such as:- `wrp-v1-protocol`- `wrp-v1_1-dag`- `wrp-v1_2-traversal`- `wrp-migration-plan`Artifact scope is the default and most common review target.## 3.2 Section scopeApplies to a specific section within an artifact when the document is mixed-quality.Example:- the WRP protocol document is generally current- but the `Execution Semantics / Receipts` section is outdatedSection review SHOULD be used when:- only one part of a large artifact is stale or questionable- the artifact should remain broadly retrievable without blanket demotion## 3.3 Chunk scopeApplies to a specific chunk when review needs to be precise.Chunk review SHOULD be used sparingly and mainly when:- a particular invariant is suspect- a specific migration step is obsolete- a specific rationale chunk remains valuable even inside an outdated section---# 4. Review Status VocabularyThe following review statuses are defined by `schemas/core/nebula-review-state.jsonld`.## 4.1 `UNREVIEWED`The item has not yet been reviewed for current validity or relevance.Use when:- a document was imported but not yet triaged- a new chunk has not been evaluated## 4.2 `NEEDS_REVIEW`The item should be reviewed soon because it may be stale, incomplete, or important to current work.Use when:- the document is likely relevant to current implementation- the document predates a major architectural shift- the document appears important but confidence is low## 4.3 `UNDER_REVIEW`The item is actively being reviewed, rewritten, or reconciled.Use when:- you are actively comparing it against current architecture or code- Builder/Architect/Inspector are working through it now## 4.4 `REVIEWED`The item has been reviewed and is believed to be usable in normal work.Use when:- the document is current enough for default retrieval- known issues are minor or already called out## 4.5 `CURRENT_FOCUS`The item is a current focus of architecture or implementation attention and should be surfaced prominently.Use when:- active work depends on this item now- the item is central to the current execution stream- the item is the present working center of a subsystem redesign## 4.6 `OUTDATED`The item is known to be out of date relative to the current architecture, runtime, or workflow.Use when:- the document predates a material redesign- its prescriptions are no longer safe defaults- it still has historical value but should be demoted## 4.7 `QUESTIONED`The item contains claims, assumptions, or structure whose correctness is in doubt.Use when:- parts of the document conflict with newer understanding- the model may be wrong, not merely old- the document should be examined before it is trusted## 4.8 `SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED`The item has been superseded by a newer artifact or chunk and should normally be excluded from default retrieval.Use when:- there is a clear replacement artifact or replacement chunk set- the supersession is intentional and not merely suspected---# 5. # 17. Summary

Nebula review workflow exists to turn the corpus into a manageable attention system rather than a passive archive.

The governing rule is:

> Lifecycle status tells us what an artifact is; review state tells us whether we should trust it, revisit it, focus on it, or route around it right now.

Lifecycle status tells us what an artifact is; review state tells us whether we should trust it, revisit it, focus on it, or route around it right now.

The initial operational model is intentionally simple:

- review at artifact scope first
review at artifact scope first

- mark items as current focus / needs review / reviewed / outdated / questioned / superseded
mark items as current focus / needs review / reviewed / outdated / questioned / superseded

- record priority and attention reason
record priority and attention reason

- let retrieval and dashboards honor that state
let retrieval and dashboards honor that state

- only descend to section/chunk review when precision is worth the effort
only descend to section/chunk review when precision is worth the effort

actually does (important)This is not just classification metadata — it gives Nebula threecontrol surfaces:1. Retrieval shaping (the big win)Each chunk kind has:retrievalBiaspreferredLevelisNormativeSo now you can do things like:Builder → boostALGORITHM,DATA_MODEL,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTEArchitect → boostINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,RATIONALEInspector → boostOPEN_QUESTION,INVARIANT, low-confidenceDEFINITIONWithout hardcoding roles into every query.2. Level coherence enforcementBecause each chunk kind declares:expectedpreferredLevelYou can now detect:L3 chunk leaking implementation detail → smells wrongL1 chunk containing pure rationale → likely misclassifiedinvariant appearing in L3 → probably needs tighteningThis becomes yourautomatic ontology consistency checkerlater.3. Normative surface separationYou now have a clean distinction between:isNormative: truenormativeDefault: REQUIRED / RECOMMENDEDThis matters because it lets you do:“show me all REQUIRED rules in WRP”“ignore non-normative chunks in execution reasoning”“highlight normative drift between versions”This is what eventually makes Nebula behave like aspec compiler rather than a wiki.Important design choice you just locked in (quietly)This schema implicitly enforces:Chunk kind is not cosmetic — it is a semantic contract.That matters because it means:chunking decisions are part of the system correctness modelnot just UI or indexing heuristicsThat’s exactly what you want for WRP + Conduit + execution graph systems.Next step (last deferred artifact)Now the final missing piece in the sequence is:docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdThat will connect everything:markdown → sectionssections → chunkschunks → kinds (this schema)chunks → levelschunks → review state overlaychunks → cross-reference graphchunks → Conduit linkageIt’s thecompiler function for everything we just defined.If you say “go”, I’llproduce it as a single coherent projection algorithmthat you can literally hand to:Ollama / Qwen2.5-CoderConduit ingestion pipelineor a Spring/Python hybrid workerand it will behave like a deterministic WRP → Nebula compiler.SourcesQodoSponsoredQodo: code review that knows your codebaseFull codebase context across services and repos. Works for monorepos, multi-repo, and microservices.

Retrieval shaping (the big win)Each chunk kind has:retrievalBiaspreferredLevelisNormativeSo now you can do things like:Builder → boostALGORITHM,DATA_MODEL,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTEArchitect → boostINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,RATIONALEInspector → boostOPEN_QUESTION,INVARIANT, low-confidenceDEFINITIONWithout hardcoding roles into every query.2. Level coherence enforcementBecause each chunk kind declares:expectedpreferredLevelYou can now detect:L3 chunk leaking implementation detail → smells wrongL1 chunk containing pure rationale → likely misclassifiedinvariant appearing in L3 → probably needs tighteningThis becomes yourautomatic ontology consistency checkerlater.3. Normative surface separationYou now have a clean distinction between:isNormative: truenormativeDefault: REQUIRED / RECOMMENDEDThis matters because it lets you do:“show me all REQUIRED rules in WRP”“ignore non-normative chunks in execution reasoning”“highlight normative drift between versions”This is what eventually makes Nebula behave like aspec compiler rather than a wiki.Important design choice you just locked in (quietly)This schema implicitly enforces:Chunk kind is not cosmetic — it is a semantic contract.That matters because it means:chunking decisions are part of the system correctness modelnot just UI or indexing heuristicsThat’s exactly what you want for WRP + Conduit + execution graph systems.Next step (last deferred artifact)Now the final missing piece in the sequence is:docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.mdThat will connect everything:markdown → sectionssections → chunkschunks → kinds (this schema)chunks → levelschunks → review state overlaychunks → cross-reference graphchunks → Conduit linkageIt’s thecompiler function for everything we just defined.If you say “go”, I’llproduce it as a single coherent projection algorithmthat you can literally hand to:Ollama / Qwen2.5-CoderConduit ingestion pipelineor a Spring/Python hybrid workerand it will behave like a deterministic WRP → Nebula compiler.

exists.",      "preferredLevel": "nebula:L3",      "isNormative": false,      "retrievalBias": 0.7    },    {      "id": "chunk:OPEN_QUESTION",      "type": "ChunkKind",      "label": "Open Question",      "comment": "An unresolved question or ambiguity in system design or interpretation.",      "preferredLevel": "nebula:L3",      "isNormative": false,      "retrievalBias": 0.8    },    // ----------------------------    // Examples + validation    // ----------------------------    {      "id": "chunk:EXAMPLE",      "type": "ChunkKind",      "label": "Example",      "comment": "Illustrative example showing how a system, model, or protocol behaves.",      "preferredLevel": "nebula:L2",      "isNormative": false,      "retrievalBias": 0.75    },    {      "id": "chunk:ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA",      "type": "ChunkKind",      "label": "Acceptance Criteria",      "comment": "Conditions that must be satisfied for a feature, migration, or system behavior to be considered correct.",      "preferredLevel": "nebula:L1",      "isNormative": true,      "normativeDefault": "REQUIRED",      "retrievalBias": 0.95    }  ]}
```

---

# What this actually does (important)

This is not just classification metadata — it gives Nebula threecontrol surfaces:

## 1. Retrieval shaping (the big win)

Each chunk kind has:

- retrievalBias
retrievalBias

- preferredLevel
preferredLevel

- isNormative
isNormative

So now you can do things like:

- Builder → boostALGORITHM,DATA_MODEL,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE
Builder → boostALGORITHM,DATA_MODEL,IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE

- Architect → boostINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,RATIONALE
Architect → boostINVARIANT,PROTOCOL_RULE,RATIONALE

- Inspector → boostOPEN_QUESTION,INVARIANT, low-confidenceDEFINITION
Inspector → boostOPEN_QUESTION,INVARIANT, low-confidenceDEFINITION

Without hardcoding roles into every query.

---

## 2. Level coherence enforcement

Because each chunk kind declares:

- expectedpreferredLevel
expectedpreferredLevel

You can now detect:

- L3 chunk leaking implementation detail → smells wrong
L3 chunk leaking implementation detail → smells wrong

- L1 chunk containing pure rationale → likely misclassified
L1 chunk containing pure rationale → likely misclassified

- invariant appearing in L3 → probably needs tightening
invariant appearing in L3 → probably needs tightening

This becomes yourautomatic ontology consistency checkerlater.

---

## 3. Normative surface separation

You now have a clean distinction between:

- isNormative: true
isNormative: true

- normativeDefault: REQUIRED / RECOMMENDED
normativeDefault: REQUIRED / RECOMMENDED

This matters because it lets you do:

- “show me all REQUIRED rules in WRP”
“show me all REQUIRED rules in WRP”

- “ignore non-normative chunks in execution reasoning”
“ignore non-normative chunks in execution reasoning”

- “highlight normative drift between versions”
“highlight normative drift between versions”

This is what eventually makes Nebula behave like aspec compiler rather than a wiki.

---

# Important design choice you just locked in (quietly)

This schema implicitly enforces:

> Chunk kind is not cosmetic — it is a semantic contract.

Chunk kind is not cosmetic — it is a semantic contract.

That matters because it means:

- chunking decisions are part of the system correctness model
chunking decisions are part of the system correctness model

- not just UI or indexing heuristics
not just UI or indexing heuristics

That’s exactly what you want for WRP + Conduit + execution graph systems.

---

# Next step (last deferred artifact)

Now the final missing piece in the sequence is:

# docs/nebula/wrp-projection-pseudocode.md

That will connect everything:

- markdown → sections
markdown → sections

- sections → chunks
sections → chunks

- chunks → kinds (this schema)
chunks → kinds (this schema)

- chunks → levels
chunks → levels

- chunks → review state overlay
chunks → review state overlay

- chunks → cross-reference graph
chunks → cross-reference graph

- chunks → Conduit linkage
chunks → Conduit linkage

It’s thecompiler function for everything we just defined.

---

If you say “go”, I’llproduce it as a single coherent projection algorithmthat you can literally hand to:

- Ollama / Qwen2.5-Coder
Ollama / Qwen2.5-Coder

- Conduit ingestion pipeline
Conduit ingestion pipeline

- or a Spring/Python hybrid worker
or a Spring/Python hybrid worker

and it will behave like a deterministic WRP → Nebula compiler.

OverviewThis document specifies the **projection compiler pipeline** that transforms WRP markdown documents into structured Nebula graph data.Input:- WRP markdown documentsOutput:- NebulaArtifacts- NebulaSections- NebulaChunks- NebulaCrossReferences- Review overlays (optional but supported)- Conduit links (if present)The pipeline is deterministic, idempotent, and replay-safe.---# 2. High-Level Pipelineparse_markdown()→ build_ast()→ resolve_artifact()→ build_section_tree()→ segment_chunks()→ classify_chunks()→ assign_levels()→ assign_review_overlay()→ extract_cross_references()→ emit_graph()→ upsert_store()---# 3. Core Data Structures (Logical)## ArtifactArtifact {idkeysource_pathstatus}## SectionSection {idartifact_idparent_section_idheadingordinal}## ChunkChunk {idsection_idordinaltextchunk_kindlevelnormative_strength}## ReviewOverlay (optional)ReviewOverlay {target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason[]}## CrossReferenceCrossReference {source_idtarget_idrelation_type}---# 4. Step 1 — Parse Markdown```pseudofunction parse_markdown(source_text):ast = MarkdownParser.parse(source_text)return astRules:preserve heading hierarchypreserve code blocks as atomic nodespreserve tables as atomic nodespreserve block quotes as semantic units5. Step 2 — Artifact Resolutionpseudofunction resolve_artifact(file_path, registry):if registry.contains(file_path):return registry.get(file_path)if STRICT_MODE:throw Error("Unknown artifact in strict mode")return create_artifact_from_path(file_path)Artifact key mapping:derived from filenamenormalized slug6. Step 3 — Build Section Treepseudofunction build_section_tree(ast):root = new SectionTree()current_stack = []for node in ast:if node.type == HEADING:level = node.levelwhile current_stack.top.level >= level:current_stack.pop()section = new Section(heading=node.text,parent=current_stack.top)current_stack.push(section)root.add(section)return rootRules:##→ Section###→ child section####+→ either nested section or flatten depending on config7. Step 4 — Chunk Segmentationpseudofunction segment_chunks(section):chunks = []buffer = []for block in section.blocks:if is_boundary(block, buffer):chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))buffer = []buffer.append(block)if buffer not empty:chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))return chunks7.1 Boundary rulespseudofunction is_boundary(block, buffer):if buffer.empty:return falseif block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:return trueif block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:return trueif semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):return trueif buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:return truereturn false7.2 Semantic shift heuristicpseudofunction semantic_shift(a, b):if a.kind != b.kind:return trueif switches_between("RATIONALE","IMPLEMENTATION","PROTOCOL_RULE"):return truereturn false8. Step 5 — Chunk Classificationpseudofunction classify_chunk(chunk):text = chunk.textif contains("must not", text):chunk.normative = PROHIBITEDelse if contains("must", text):chunk.normative = REQUIREDelse if contains("should", text):chunk.normative = RECOMMENDEDelse:chunk.normative = INFORMATIVEchunk.kind = classify_kind(text)return chunk8.1 Chunk kind classifierpseudofunction classify_kind(text):if matches_definition_pattern(text):return DEFINITIONif contains_protocol_keywords(text):return PROTOCOL_RULEif contains_invariant_keywords(text):return INVARIANTif contains_algorithm_structure(text):return ALGORITHMif contains_schema_fields(text):return DATA_MODELif contains_migration_language(text):return MIGRATION_STEPif contains_open_question_markers(text):return OPEN_QUESTIONif contains_rationale_markers(text):return RATIONALEif contains_example_markers(text):return EXAMPLEreturn OVERVIEW9. Step 6 — Level Assignmentpseudofunction assign_level(chunk):if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:return L1if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:return L2if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:return L3return L210. Step 7 — Review Overlay Assignmentpseudofunction assign_review_overlay(entity, context):overlay = new ReviewOverlay()if entity.is_new:overlay.status = UNREVIEWEDif contains_staleness_signals(entity):overlay.status = NEEDS_REVIEWif matches_current_focus_tags(entity):overlay.status = CURRENT_FOCUSif contains_conflict_signals(entity):overlay.status = QUESTIONEDif superseded_by_exists(entity):overlay.status = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDreturn overlay11. Step 8 — Cross Reference Extractionpseudofunction extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):refs = []for token in chunk.text:if token matches artifact_key:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=artifact_id(token),type=DEPENDS_ON))if token matches section_heading:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=section_id(token),type=REFERENCES))if token matches known_concept:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=concept_id(token),type=MENTIONS))return refs12. Step 9 — Emit Graphpseudofunction emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):graph = NebulaGraph()graph.add(artifact)for section in sections:graph.add(section)for chunk in chunks:graph.add(chunk)for ref in refs:graph.add(ref)return graph13. Step 10 — Upsert Store (Idempotent)pseudofunction upsert_store(graph, db):for node in graph.nodes:db.upsert(node.id, node)for edge in graph.edges:db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)Rules:idempotent writesstable IDs requiredno duplicate edges unless explicitly allowedpreserve existing review annotations unless overridden14. Determinism RulesProjection MUST be deterministic:same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunksno LLM-based randomness in core pipelineonly heuristic classification allowedno sampling variabilityIf classifier improves:version bump requirednew projection run produces new revision lineage15. Failure Modes15.1 Unknown artifact→ fail in STRICT_MODE15.2 ambiguous chunk boundaries→ prefer splitting over merging15.3 classification uncertainty→ default to OVERVIEW + INFORMATIVE15.4 missing references→ ignore silently (do not fail pipeline)16. Minimal Implementation ContractA valid implementation MUST:parse markdown into structured ASTbuild deterministic section treesegment chunks deterministicallyclassify chunks without external LLM dependency (LLM optional later)assign level + kind to every chunkemit graph with stable IDssupport idempotent re-import17. SummaryThis pipeline defines Nebula’s core transformation:Markdown → structured semantic graphThe important shift is:documents are not storedsemantic nodes are storedEverything else (review, retrieval, roles, Conduit integration) operates on top of this graph, not the raw text.---# What you now have (important moment)You now have a complete **minimal compiler stack**:### 1. Review system (attention layer)- `nebula-review-state.jsonld`- `review-workflow.md`### 2. Semantic classification system- `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`### 3. Execution pipeline- `wrp-projection-pseudocode.md`---# What this unlocks nextAt this point, Nebula is structurally capable of:- ingesting your WRP corpus- chunking it deterministically- classifying semantics- tracking review state- building a queryable graph- feeding Conduit execution planning---# The next natural step (if you want to continue)There are two obvious upgrades:### A. Retrieval layer specHow Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer actually query this graph### B. Conduit ↔ Nebula execution bindingHow WRP chunks become executable plans or DAG nodes---If you want to keep going, I’d recommend next:> “Nebula Retrieval & Role Scoring Model”That’s where the system starts behaving like a cognitive runtime instead of just a compiler.SourcesApryseSponsoredPDFjs Alternative | Out of the box solutionBring accurate PDF viewing, annotating, editing to any web, mobile, desktop or framework.

OverviewThis document specifies the **projection compiler pipeline** that transforms WRP markdown documents into structured Nebula graph data.Input:- WRP markdown documentsOutput:- NebulaArtifacts- NebulaSections- NebulaChunks- NebulaCrossReferences- Review overlays (optional but supported)- Conduit links (if present)The pipeline is deterministic, idempotent, and replay-safe.---# 2. High-Level Pipelineparse_markdown()→ build_ast()→ resolve_artifact()→ build_section_tree()→ segment_chunks()→ classify_chunks()→ assign_levels()→ assign_review_overlay()→ extract_cross_references()→ emit_graph()→ upsert_store()---# 3. Core Data Structures (Logical)## ArtifactArtifact {idkeysource_pathstatus}## SectionSection {idartifact_idparent_section_idheadingordinal}## ChunkChunk {idsection_idordinaltextchunk_kindlevelnormative_strength}## ReviewOverlay (optional)ReviewOverlay {target_idreview_statusreview_priorityattention_reason[]}## CrossReferenceCrossReference {source_idtarget_idrelation_type}---# 4. Step 1 — Parse Markdown```pseudofunction parse_markdown(source_text):ast = MarkdownParser.parse(source_text)return astRules:preserve heading hierarchypreserve code blocks as atomic nodespreserve tables as atomic nodespreserve block quotes as semantic units5. Step 2 — Artifact Resolutionpseudofunction resolve_artifact(file_path, registry):if registry.contains(file_path):return registry.get(file_path)if STRICT_MODE:throw Error("Unknown artifact in strict mode")return create_artifact_from_path(file_path)Artifact key mapping:derived from filenamenormalized slug6. Step 3 — Build Section Treepseudofunction build_section_tree(ast):root = new SectionTree()current_stack = []for node in ast:if node.type == HEADING:level = node.levelwhile current_stack.top.level >= level:current_stack.pop()section = new Section(heading=node.text,parent=current_stack.top)current_stack.push(section)root.add(section)return rootRules:##→ Section###→ child section####+→ either nested section or flatten depending on config7. Step 4 — Chunk Segmentationpseudofunction segment_chunks(section):chunks = []buffer = []for block in section.blocks:if is_boundary(block, buffer):chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))buffer = []buffer.append(block)if buffer not empty:chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))return chunks7.1 Boundary rulespseudofunction is_boundary(block, buffer):if buffer.empty:return falseif block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:return trueif block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:return trueif semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):return trueif buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:return truereturn false7.2 Semantic shift heuristicpseudofunction semantic_shift(a, b):if a.kind != b.kind:return trueif switches_between("RATIONALE","IMPLEMENTATION","PROTOCOL_RULE"):return truereturn false8. Step 5 — Chunk Classificationpseudofunction classify_chunk(chunk):text = chunk.textif contains("must not", text):chunk.normative = PROHIBITEDelse if contains("must", text):chunk.normative = REQUIREDelse if contains("should", text):chunk.normative = RECOMMENDEDelse:chunk.normative = INFORMATIVEchunk.kind = classify_kind(text)return chunk8.1 Chunk kind classifierpseudofunction classify_kind(text):if matches_definition_pattern(text):return DEFINITIONif contains_protocol_keywords(text):return PROTOCOL_RULEif contains_invariant_keywords(text):return INVARIANTif contains_algorithm_structure(text):return ALGORITHMif contains_schema_fields(text):return DATA_MODELif contains_migration_language(text):return MIGRATION_STEPif contains_open_question_markers(text):return OPEN_QUESTIONif contains_rationale_markers(text):return RATIONALEif contains_example_markers(text):return EXAMPLEreturn OVERVIEW9. Step 6 — Level Assignmentpseudofunction assign_level(chunk):if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:return L1if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:return L2if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:return L3return L210. Step 7 — Review Overlay Assignmentpseudofunction assign_review_overlay(entity, context):overlay = new ReviewOverlay()if entity.is_new:overlay.status = UNREVIEWEDif contains_staleness_signals(entity):overlay.status = NEEDS_REVIEWif matches_current_focus_tags(entity):overlay.status = CURRENT_FOCUSif contains_conflict_signals(entity):overlay.status = QUESTIONEDif superseded_by_exists(entity):overlay.status = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDreturn overlay11. Step 8 — Cross Reference Extractionpseudofunction extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):refs = []for token in chunk.text:if token matches artifact_key:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=artifact_id(token),type=DEPENDS_ON))if token matches section_heading:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=section_id(token),type=REFERENCES))if token matches known_concept:refs.append(CrossReference(source=chunk.id,target=concept_id(token),type=MENTIONS))return refs12. Step 9 — Emit Graphpseudofunction emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):graph = NebulaGraph()graph.add(artifact)for section in sections:graph.add(section)for chunk in chunks:graph.add(chunk)for ref in refs:graph.add(ref)return graph13. Step 10 — Upsert Store (Idempotent)pseudofunction upsert_store(graph, db):for node in graph.nodes:db.upsert(node.id, node)for edge in graph.edges:db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)Rules:idempotent writesstable IDs requiredno duplicate edges unless explicitly allowedpreserve existing review annotations unless overridden14. Determinism RulesProjection MUST be deterministic:same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunksno LLM-based randomness in core pipelineonly heuristic classification allowedno sampling variabilityIf classifier improves:version bump requirednew projection run produces new revision lineage15. Failure Modes15.1 Unknown artifact→ fail in STRICT_MODE15.2 ambiguous chunk boundaries→ prefer splitting over merging15.3 classification uncertainty→ default to OVERVIEW + INFORMATIVE15.4 missing references→ ignore silently (do not fail pipeline)16. Minimal Implementation ContractA valid implementation MUST:parse markdown into structured ASTbuild deterministic section treesegment chunks deterministicallyclassify chunks without external LLM dependency (LLM optional later)assign level + kind to every chunkemit graph with stable IDssupport idempotent re-import17. SummaryThis pipeline defines Nebula’s core transformation:Markdown → structured semantic graphThe important shift is:documents are not storedsemantic nodes are storedEverything else (review, retrieval, roles, Conduit integration) operates on top of this graph, not the raw text.---# What you now have (important moment)You now have a complete **minimal compiler stack**:### 1. Review system (attention layer)- `nebula-review-state.jsonld`- `review-workflow.md`### 2. Semantic classification system- `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`### 3. # 5. Step 2 — Artifact Resolution

```
function resolve_artifact(file_path, registry):    if registry.contains(file_path):        return registry.get(file_path)    if STRICT_MODE:        throw Error("Unknown artifact in strict mode")    return create_artifact_from_path(file_path)
```

# 6. Step 3 — Build Section Tree

```
function build_section_tree(ast):    root = new SectionTree()    current_stack = []    for node in ast:        if node.type == HEADING:            level = node.level            while current_stack.top.level >= level:                current_stack.pop()            section = new Section(                heading=node.text,                parent=current_stack.top            )            current_stack.push(section)            root.add(section)    return root
```

```
function build_section_tree(ast):    root = new SectionTree()    current_stack = []    for node in ast:        if node.type == HEADING:            level = node.level            while current_stack.top.level >= level:                current_stack.pop()            section = new Section(                heading=node.text,                parent=current_stack.top            )            current_stack.push(section)            root.add(section)    return root
```

# 7. Step 4 — Chunk Segmentation

```
function segment_chunks(section):    chunks = []    buffer = []    for block in section.blocks:        if is_boundary(block, buffer):            chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))            buffer = []        buffer.append(block)    if buffer not empty:        chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))    return chunks
```

function segment_chunks(section):    chunks = []    buffer = []    for block in section.blocks:        if is_boundary(block, buffer):            chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))            buffer = []        buffer.append(block)    if buffer not empty:        chunks.append(create_chunk(buffer))    return chunks
```

---

## 7.1 Boundary rules

```
function is_boundary(block, buffer):    if buffer.empty:        return false    if block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:        return true    if block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:        return true    if semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):        return true    if buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:        return true    return false
```

```
function is_boundary(block, buffer):    if buffer.empty:        return false    if block.type == HEADING_CHANGE:        return true    if block.type == CODE_BLOCK and buffer.contains_non_code:        return true    if semantic_shift(buffer.last, block):        return true    if buffer.token_count > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE:        return true    return false
```

---

## 7.2 Semantic shift heuristic

```
function semantic_shift(a, b):    if a.kind != b.kind:        return true    if switches_between(        "RATIONALE",        "IMPLEMENTATION",        "PROTOCOL_RULE"    ):        return true    return false
```

```
function semantic_shift(a, b):    if a.kind != b.kind:        return true    if switches_between(        "RATIONALE",        "IMPLEMENTATION",        "PROTOCOL_RULE"    ):        return true    return false
```

# 8. Step 5 — Chunk Classification

```
function classify_chunk(chunk):    text = chunk.text    if contains("must not", text):        chunk.normative = PROHIBITED    else if contains("must", text):        chunk.normative = REQUIRED    else if contains("should", text):        chunk.normative = RECOMMENDED    else:        chunk.normative = INFORMATIVE    chunk.kind = classify_kind(text)    return chunk
```

```
function classify_chunk(chunk):    text = chunk.text    if contains("must not", text):        chunk.normative = PROHIBITED    else if contains("must", text):        chunk.normative = REQUIRED    else if contains("should", text):        chunk.normative = RECOMMENDED    else:        chunk.normative = INFORMATIVE    chunk.kind = classify_kind(text)    return chunk
```

---

## 8.1 Chunk kind classifier

```
function classify_kind(text):    if matches_definition_pattern(text):        return DEFINITION    if contains_protocol_keywords(text):        return PROTOCOL_RULE    if contains_invariant_keywords(text):        return INVARIANT    if contains_algorithm_structure(text):        return ALGORITHM    if contains_schema_fields(text):        return DATA_MODEL    if contains_migration_language(text):        return MIGRATION_STEP    if contains_open_question_markers(text):        return OPEN_QUESTION    if contains_rationale_markers(text):        return RATIONALE    if contains_example_markers(text):        return EXAMPLE    return OVERVIEW
```

```
function classify_kind(text):    if matches_definition_pattern(text):        return DEFINITION    if contains_protocol_keywords(text):        return PROTOCOL_RULE    if contains_invariant_keywords(text):        return INVARIANT    if contains_algorithm_structure(text):        return ALGORITHM    if contains_schema_fields(text):        return DATA_MODEL    if contains_migration_language(text):        return MIGRATION_STEP    if contains_open_question_markers(text):        return OPEN_QUESTION    if contains_rationale_markers(text):        return RATIONALE    if contains_example_markers(text):        return EXAMPLE    return OVERVIEW
```

---

# 9. Step 6 — Level Assignment

```
function assign_level(chunk):    if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:        return L1    if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:        return L2    if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:        return L3    return L2
```

```
function assign_level(chunk):    if chunk.kind in [ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA]:        return L1    if chunk.kind in [PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DEFINITION, EXAMPLE]:        return L2    if chunk.kind in [OVERVIEW, RATIONALE, OPEN_QUESTION]:        return L3    return L2
```

# 10. Step 7 — Review Overlay Assignment

```
function assign_review_overlay(entity, context):    overlay = new ReviewOverlay()    if entity.is_new:        overlay.status = UNREVIEWED    if contains_staleness_signals(entity):        overlay.status = NEEDS_REVIEW    if matches_current_focus_tags(entity):        overlay.status = CURRENT_FOCUS    if contains_conflict_signals(entity):        overlay.status = QUESTIONED    if superseded_by_exists(entity):        overlay.status = SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED    return overlay
```

```

# 11. Step 8 — Cross Reference Extraction

```
function extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):    refs = []    for token in chunk.text:        if token matches artifact_key:            refs.append(                CrossReference(                    source=chunk.id,                    target=artifact_id(token),                    type=DEPENDS_ON                )            )        if token matches section_heading:            refs.append(                CrossReference(                    source=chunk.id,                    target=section_id(token),                    type=REFERENCES                )            )        if token matches known_concept:            refs.append(                CrossReference(                    source=chunk.id,                    target=concept_id(token),                    type=MENTIONS                )            )    return refs
```

```
function extract_cross_references(chunk, registry):    refs = []    for token in chunk.text:        if token matches artifact_key:            refs.append(                CrossReference(                    source=chunk.id,                    target=artifact_id(token),                    type=DEPENDS_ON                )            )        if token matches section_heading:            refs.append(                CrossReference(                    source=chunk.id,                    target=section_id(token),                    type=REFERENCES                )            )        if token matches known_concept:            refs.append(                CrossReference(                    source=chunk.id,                    target=concept_id(token),                    type=MENTIONS                )            )    return refs
```

# 12. Step 9 — Emit Graph

```
function emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):    graph = NebulaGraph()    graph.add(artifact)    for section in sections:        graph.add(section)    for chunk in chunks:        graph.add(chunk)    for ref in refs:        graph.add(ref)    return graph
```

function emit_graph(artifact, sections, chunks, refs):    graph = NebulaGraph()    graph.add(artifact)    for section in sections:        graph.add(section)    for chunk in chunks:        graph.add(chunk)    for ref in refs:        graph.add(ref)    return graph
```

# 13. Step 10 — Upsert Store (Idempotent)

```
function upsert_store(graph, db):    for node in graph.nodes:        db.upsert(node.id, node)    for edge in graph.edges:        db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)
```

function upsert_store(graph, db):    for node in graph.nodes:        db.upsert(node.id, node)    for edge in graph.edges:        db.upsert_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.type)
```

# 14. Determinism Rules

Projection MUST be deterministic:

- same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunks
same markdown → same AST → same sections → same chunks

- no LLM-based randomness in core pipeline
no LLM-based randomness in core pipeline

- only heuristic classification allowed
only heuristic classification allowed

- no sampling variability
no sampling variability

If classifier improves:

- version bump required
version bump required

- new projection run produces new revision lineage
new projection run produces new revision lineage

## 15.1 Unknown artifact

→ fail in STRICT_MODE

## 15.2 ambiguous chunk boundaries

→ prefer splitting over merging

## 15.3 classification uncertainty

→ default to OVERVIEW + INFORMATIVE

## 15.4 missing references

→ ignore silently (do not fail pipeline)

parse markdown into structured AST

OverviewNebula does not retrieve documents.It retrieves a **ranked subgraph of semantic chunks**.Every query is evaluated through:- role profile (Builder / Architect / Inspector / Explorer / Conduit)- chunk kind (semantic intent)- level (L1–L4 abstraction)- review state (trust + attention overlay)- cross-reference density (graph connectivity)- task intent (implicit or explicit)The output is a **scored ranked set of chunks + their local graph neighborhood**.---# 2. Retrieval Pipelinequery→ intent_classification→ role_profile_resolution→ candidate_chunk_selection→ scoring→ graph_expansion→ reranking→ filtering→ return---# 4. Role ProfilesEach role defines **what “relevant” means**.---## 4.1 BuilderBuilder optimizes for implementation correctness.### Preferences:- L1 chunks strongly preferred- ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE- MIGRATION_STEP when executing transitions- REVIEWED and CURRENT_FOCUS### Demotions:- RATIONALE (unless directly tied to implementation)- OUTDATED- QUESTIONED### Boost factors:- normative chunks (REQUIRED > RECOMMENDED)- high retrievalBias chunks---## 4.2 ArchitectArchitect optimizes for system correctness and structure.### Preferences:- L2 chunks- PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DATA_MODEL- RATIONALE (strongly valued)- OPEN_QUESTION (for unresolved design space)### Demotions:- overly implementation-specific L1 noise- trivial EXAMPLE chunks---## 4.3 InspectorInspector optimizes for contradiction detection and system validation.### Preferences:- QUESTIONED- INVARIANT- OUTDATED- OPEN_QUESTION- cross-reference-heavy chunks### Behavior:- actively surfaces inconsistencies- boosts conflicting review states- prioritizes low-confidence or high-risk nodes---## 4.4 ExplorerExplorer optimizes for understanding and knowledge traversal.### Preferences:- OVERVIEW- RATIONALE- EXAMPLE- high connectivity chunks### Behavior:- expands neighborhoods aggressively- favors graph traversal depth over strict relevance- includes historical/superseded context when useful---## 4.5 Conduit (Execution Role)Conduit optimizes for executable transformation.### Preferences:- MIGRATION_STEP- ALGORITHM- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA- PROTOCOL_RULE- L1 chunks only### Behavior:- strips non-normative noise- prioritizes determinism- prefers minimal required graph for execution---# 5. Chunk Scoring FunctionEvery chunk receives a score:score =role_weightkind_weightlevel_weightreview_weightgraph_weightfreshness_weight---## 5.1 Role weightDefined per role profile preferences.Example:- Builder: +2 for L1- Architect: +2 for L2- Inspector: +3 for QUESTIONED- Explorer: +2 for OVERVIEW---## 5.2 Chunk kind weightFrom `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`:- PROTOCOL_RULE → +3 for Architect- ALGORITHM → +3 for Builder/Conduit- RATIONALE → +3 for Architect/Explorer- OPEN_QUESTION → +3 for Inspector/Architect- EXAMPLE → moderate boost for Explorer---## 5.3 Level weightL1: +3 for Builder/ConduitL2: +3 for ArchitectL3: +2 for ExplorerL4: +2 for all roles (meta awareness bonus)---## 5.4 Review weightCURRENT_FOCUS → +4REVIEWED → +2NEEDS_REVIEW → +1UNREVIEWED → 0OUTDATED → -2QUESTIONED → +2 for Inspector, -2 for BuilderSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED → -4 (default)---## 5.5 Graph weightChunks gain score from graph structure:- + connectivity (degree centrality)- + cross-reference richness- + being referenced by current focus nodes- + participation in migration chains---## 5.6 Freshness weightBased on:- last reviewed timestamp- recency of updates- proximity to current focus artifacts---# 6. Candidate SelectionBefore scoring, Nebula selects a candidate set:```pseudo id="c8xk1a"function select_candidates(query):if query.role_hint exists:seed = role_preferred_chunks(query.role)else:seed = semantic_search(query.text)expand seed using:- direct references- parent sections- sibling chunksreturn seed7. Graph Expansion PhaseAfter scoring top candidates:for chunk in top_results:expand:parent sectionreferenced chunksupstream dependenciesdownstream dependenciesThis produces alocal subgraph, not just a ranked list.8. Filtering RulesAfter scoring:removeSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDunless explicitly requestedremoveOUTDATEDfor Builder unless overriddenpreserveQUESTIONEDfor InspectorpreserveRATIONALEfor Architect/Explorerenforce role-level safety filters9. Explanation GenerationEvery retrieval result MUST include:explanation = {"why_selected": [],"role_alignment": "","chunk_kind_match": "","review_state_influence": "","graph_signals": []}``` id="v1k2zq"This is critical for debugging the system and for human trust calibration.---# 10. Retrieval Modes## 10.1 STRICT MODE- only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS- no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED- minimal graph expansionUsed for execution / Conduit---## 10.2 EXPLORATION MODE- broad inclusion- heavy graph traversal- includes OUTDATED + SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED if relevantUsed for learning / architecture discovery---## 10.3 DIAGNOSTIC MODE- Inspector role default mode- boosts QUESTIONED and conflicts- surfaces contradictions explicitly---## 10.4 EXECUTION MODE- Builder + Conduit hybrid- minimal graph- deterministic chunks only- excludes RATIONALE unless required---# 11. Conflict ResolutionIf two chunks compete:Priority resolution:1. CURRENT_FOCUS overrides all2. REVIEWED overrides NEARLY EVERYTHING except CURRENT_FOCUS3. QUESTIONED overrides OUTDATED for Inspector4. SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED loses by default5. graph centrality can override weak semantic differences---# 12. Key Design Principle> Nebula retrieval is not search. It is weighted cognitive reconstruction.The system is not trying to find documents.It is trying to reconstruct the **relevant slice of the system’s mental model for a role and intent**.---# 13. Corpus compilermarkdown → graph2. Governance systemreview state + attention flow3. Ontology classifierchunk kinds + levels + normative strength4. Core Retrieval ObjectA retrieval result is not a document.It is:RetrievalResult {chunkscoreexplanationneighborhood[]}Neighborhood includes:- parent section- sibling chunks- referenced chunks- optionally upstream/downstream traversal nodes---# 3. Retrieval Pipelinequery→ intent_classification→ role_profile_resolution→ candidate_chunk_selection→ scoring→ graph_expansion→ reranking→ filtering→ return---# 4. Role ProfilesEach role defines **what “relevant” means**.---## 4.1 BuilderBuilder optimizes for implementation correctness.### Preferences:- L1 chunks strongly preferred- ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE- MIGRATION_STEP when executing transitions- REVIEWED and CURRENT_FOCUS### Demotions:- RATIONALE (unless directly tied to implementation)- OUTDATED- QUESTIONED### Boost factors:- normative chunks (REQUIRED > RECOMMENDED)- high retrievalBias chunks---## 4.2 ArchitectArchitect optimizes for system correctness and structure.### Preferences:- L2 chunks- PROTOCOL_RULE, INVARIANT, DATA_MODEL- RATIONALE (strongly valued)- OPEN_QUESTION (for unresolved design space)### Demotions:- overly implementation-specific L1 noise- trivial EXAMPLE chunks---## 4.3 InspectorInspector optimizes for contradiction detection and system validation.### Preferences:- QUESTIONED- INVARIANT- OUTDATED- OPEN_QUESTION- cross-reference-heavy chunks### Behavior:- actively surfaces inconsistencies- boosts conflicting review states- prioritizes low-confidence or high-risk nodes---## 4.4 ExplorerExplorer optimizes for understanding and knowledge traversal.### Preferences:- OVERVIEW- RATIONALE- EXAMPLE- high connectivity chunks### Behavior:- expands neighborhoods aggressively- favors graph traversal depth over strict relevance- includes historical/superseded context when useful---## 4.5 Conduit (Execution Role)Conduit optimizes for executable transformation.### Preferences:- MIGRATION_STEP- ALGORITHM- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA- PROTOCOL_RULE- L1 chunks only### Behavior:- strips non-normative noise- prioritizes determinism- prefers minimal required graph for execution---# 5. Chunk Scoring FunctionEvery chunk receives a score:score =role_weightkind_weightlevel_weightreview_weightgraph_weightfreshness_weight---## 5.1 Role weightDefined per role profile preferences.Example:- Builder: +2 for L1- Architect: +2 for L2- Inspector: +3 for QUESTIONED- Explorer: +2 for OVERVIEW---## 5.2 Chunk kind weightFrom `nebula-chunk-kinds.jsonld`:- PROTOCOL_RULE → +3 for Architect- ALGORITHM → +3 for Builder/Conduit- RATIONALE → +3 for Architect/Explorer- OPEN_QUESTION → +3 for Inspector/Architect- EXAMPLE → moderate boost for Explorer---## 5.3 Level weightL1: +3 for Builder/ConduitL2: +3 for ArchitectL3: +2 for ExplorerL4: +2 for all roles (meta awareness bonus)---## 5.4 Review weightCURRENT_FOCUS → +4REVIEWED → +2NEEDS_REVIEW → +1UNREVIEWED → 0OUTDATED → -2QUESTIONED → +2 for Inspector, -2 for BuilderSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED → -4 (default)---## 5.5 Graph weightChunks gain score from graph structure:- + connectivity (degree centrality)- + cross-reference richness- + being referenced by current focus nodes- + participation in migration chains---## 5.6 Freshness weightBased on:- last reviewed timestamp- recency of updates- proximity to current focus artifacts---# 6. Candidate SelectionBefore scoring, Nebula selects a candidate set:```pseudo id="c8xk1a"function select_candidates(query):if query.role_hint exists:seed = role_preferred_chunks(query.role)else:seed = semantic_search(query.text)expand seed using:- direct references- parent sections- sibling chunksreturn seed7. Graph Expansion PhaseAfter scoring top candidates:for chunk in top_results:expand:parent sectionreferenced chunksupstream dependenciesdownstream dependenciesThis produces alocal subgraph, not just a ranked list.8. Filtering RulesAfter scoring:removeSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMEDunless explicitly requestedremoveOUTDATEDfor Builder unless overriddenpreserveQUESTIONEDfor InspectorpreserveRATIONALEfor Architect/Explorerenforce role-level safety filters9. Explanation GenerationEvery retrieval result MUST include:explanation = {"why_selected": [],"role_alignment": "","chunk_kind_match": "","review_state_influence": "","graph_signals": []}``` id="v1k2zq"This is critical for debugging the system and for human trust calibration.---# 10. Retrieval Modes## 10.1 STRICT MODE- only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS- no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED- minimal graph expansionUsed for execution / Conduit---## 10.2 EXPLORATION MODE- broad inclusion- heavy graph traversal- includes OUTDATED + SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED if relevantUsed for learning / architecture discovery---## 10.3 DIAGNOSTIC MODE- Inspector role default mode- boosts QUESTIONED and conflicts- surfaces contradictions explicitly---## 10.4 EXECUTION MODE- Builder + Conduit hybrid- minimal graph- deterministic chunks only- excludes RATIONALE unless required---# 11. Conflict ResolutionIf two chunks compete:Priority resolution:1. CURRENT_FOCUS overrides all2. REVIEWED overrides NEARLY EVERYTHING except CURRENT_FOCUS3. QUESTIONED overrides OUTDATED for Inspector4. SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED loses by default5. graph centrality can override weak semantic differences---# 12. Key Design Principle> Nebula retrieval is not search. It is weighted cognitive reconstruction.The system is not trying to find documents.It is trying to reconstruct the **relevant slice of the system’s mental model for a role and intent**.---# 13. SummaryThis model introduces:- role-aware retrieval- semantic scoring across multiple axes- graph expansion instead of flat ranking- review-state-aware trust filtering- execution-safe strict modes- explainable retrieval decisionsThis is the layer where Nebula becomes:> a multi-role semantic runtime over a structured knowledge graphWhat you now have (full stack checkpoint)At this point, the system is complete enough to function as:1. # 7. Graph Expansion Phase

After scoring top candidates:

```
for chunk in top_results:    expand:        parent section        referenced chunks        upstream dependencies        downstream dependencies
```
