OverviewNebula produces a **ranked semantic subgraph**.Conduit consumes a **deterministic execution DAG**.This document defines the transformation layer between them.Input:- NebulaChunks- NebulaSections- NebulaArtifacts- CrossReferences- Review overlays- Role-scored retrieval result setOutput:- ConduitExecutionGraph (DAG)- ExecutionNodes- TransitionEdges- ExecutionReceipts---# 2. Core Principle> Nebula explains what is relevant. Conduit decides what is executable.Not all retrieved content is executable.Only chunks that satisfy **execution constraints** may become DAG nodes.---# 3. Execution Eligibility RulesA Nebula chunk is eligible for execution if:```pseudo id="elig1"function isExecutable(chunk):return (chunk.kind in EXECUTABLE_KINDSAND chunk.reviewStatus NOT IN {OUTDATED, SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED}AND chunk.normativeStrength in {REQUIRED, RECOMMENDED})3.1 Executable chunk kindsALGORITHMPROTOCOL_RULEINVARIANTMIGRATION_STEPDATA_MODELACCEPTANCE_CRITERIAIMPLEMENTATION_NOTE``` id="execk1"---# 4. Node ConstructionEach executable chunk becomes a **Conduit Node**.```pseudo id="node1"function toExecutionNode(chunk):return ExecutionNode(id = chunk.id,type = chunk.kind,level = chunk.level,payload = extract_semantic_payload(chunk),preconditions = infer_preconditions(chunk),postconditions = infer_postconditions(chunk),review_state = chunk.reviewStatus)4.1 Payload extractionPayload depends on chunk kind:ALGORITHM → pseudocode / structured logicDATA_MODEL → schema definitionPROTOCOL_RULE → constraint logicMIGRATION_STEP → imperative actionACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA → validation predicates5. Edge Construction (DAG Formation)Edges are derived from Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction build_edges(nodes, references):edges = []for ref in references:if ref.type == DEPENDS_ON:edges.add(DependencyEdge(ref.source, ref.target))if ref.type == REFERENCES:edges.add(ReferenceEdge(ref.source, ref.target))if ref.type == MENTIONS:edges.add(SoftLinkEdge(ref.source, ref.target))return edges5.1 Edge typesDependencyEdge (hard constraint)execution order requiredReferenceEdge (soft ordering)preferred ordering but not requiredSoftLinkEdge (contextual)informational only, no execution ordering6. DAG Constructionpseudofunction build_execution_dag(nodes, edges):dag = DirectedAcyclicGraph()for node in nodes:dag.add_node(node)for edge in edges:dag.add_edge(edge)if dag.has_cycles():resolve_cycles(dag)return dag6.1 Cycle resolution strategyIf cycles exist:Priority resolution:break edges from LOWER level → HIGHER levelbreak edges from RATIONALE → ALGORITHMpreserve PROTOCOL_RULE dependencies over EXAMPLE linksif unresolved → mark as NEEDS_REVIEW in Nebula7. Execution Plan CompilationOnce DAG is constructed:pseudofunction compile_execution_plan(dag):topo_order = topological_sort(dag)plan = []for node in topo_order:step = ExecutionStep(node_id=node.id,action=resolve_executor(node),inputs=get_inputs(node),outputs=declare_outputs(node))plan.append(step)return plan8. Executor ResolutionEach node type maps to an execution handler.pseudofunction resolve_executor(node):switch node.type:case ALGORITHM:return AlgorithmExecutorcase DATA_MODEL:return SchemaExecutorcase PROTOCOL_RULE:return ConstraintExecutorcase MIGRATION_STEP:return MigrationExecutorcase ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:return ValidationExecutor9. Execution Context BindingEach execution step runs with:JSON{"role":"Conduit","mode":"EXECUTION","strict_mode":true,"allowed_chunk_kinds": ["ALGORITHM","MIGRATION_STEP","PROTOCOL_RULE"],"review_filter": ["REVIEWED","CURRENT_FOCUS"],"determinism":true}10. Execution Order SemanticsExecution follows:DATA_MODEL first (schema foundation)PROTOCOL_RULE second (constraints)ALGORITHM third (logic)MIGRATION_STEP fourth (state transitions)ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA last (validation)This is asemantic ordering constraint, not just topological sorting.11. Execution ReceiptsEvery execution step produces a receipt:JSON{"node_id":"...","status":"SUCCESS | FAILED | SKIPPED","timestamp":"...","inputs": [],"outputs": [],"validation_result": {},"trace": []}Receipts are stored back into Nebula as:execution provenancerollback anchor pointsaudit trail for WRP transitions12. Failure Handling12.1 Execution failureIf a node fails:mark ExecutionReceipt = FAILEDpropagate failure upward via dependency edgesflag Nebula chunk as NEEDS_REVIEW12.2 Invalid nodeIf chunk is not executable:keep in Nebula graphexclude from DAGoptionally mark:REVIEW_STATUS = QUESTIONED12.3 Cycle resolution failureIf DAG cannot be resolved:halt executionemit diagnostic graphsend Inspector mode review request13. Role Interaction ModelExecution binding respects Nebula role system:Builderconsumes ExecutionPlanproduces code / system changesArchitectvalidates DAG structureensures invariants preservedInspectorreviews failures and contradictionsConduitexecutes deterministicallyExplorernot part of execution path14. Key InvariantsThese MUST always hold:Execution DAG is acyclicOnly eligible chunks become nodesReview-filtered chunks cannot executeReceipts are immutable once writtenNebula is source of truth, Conduit is execution engineNo execution without resolved role context15. Conceptual ShiftThis is the critical transition:Nebula describes structureConduit enacts structureWRP defines legality of transformationTogether they form:Nebula = semantic graphWRP = formal rulesConduit = execution runtime16. SummaryThis binding layer enables:deterministic execution from semantic graphstraceable DAG-based system evolutionreview-state-aware execution safetyrole-driven execution semanticsbidirectional traceability (execution → Nebula → WRP)17. Final PrincipleNothing executes unless it exists as a validated semantic node in Nebula.And:Nothing exists in Conduit unless it can be traced back to a Nebula chunk.---# What you now have (full system closure point)At this moment, you’ve defined a complete closed loop:## 1. WRP (formal system rules)→ defines legality + structure## 2. Nebula (semantic graph)→ stores meaning + review + classification## 3. Retrieval model→ decides what is relevant per role## 4. Execution binding (Conduit)→ converts meaning into runnable DAGs---# You’ve effectively built:> A multi-layer semantic compiler + execution runtime for knowledge → action systems---# Where this naturally goes next (optional but obvious)If we continue, the next missing layer is:## 🔷 WRP → Validation & Formal Proof LayerThat would define:- invariant verification rules- contradiction detection across DAGs- schema-level consistency checks- “proof-of-correctness” style validation for execution plansOR## 🔷 Conduit Runtime Spec- scheduling- concurrency model- retry semantics- distributed execution (if you ever push it there)---If you want to continue, I’d suggest next:> “WRP validation + invariant checking engine”That’s the point where this stops being a pipeline and starts becoming a **self-verifying system**.Gravitee Topco LimitedSponsoredGravitee API Management PlatformYou know how valuable your data is. Build security into your APIs with Gravitee.

## 4.1 Payload extraction

Payload depends on chunk kind:

- ALGORITHM → pseudocode / structured logic
ALGORITHM → pseudocode / structured logic

- DATA_MODEL → schema definition
DATA_MODEL → schema definition

- PROTOCOL_RULE → constraint logic
PROTOCOL_RULE → constraint logic

- MIGRATION_STEP → imperative action
MIGRATION_STEP → imperative action

- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA → validation predicates
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA → validation predicates

---

# 5. Edge Construction (DAG Formation)

Edges are derived from Nebula cross-references.

```
function build_edges(nodes, references):    edges = []    for ref in references:        if ref.type == DEPENDS_ON:            edges.add(DependencyEdge(ref.source, ref.target))        if ref.type == REFERENCES:            edges.add(ReferenceEdge(ref.source, ref.target))        if ref.type == MENTIONS:            edges.add(SoftLinkEdge(ref.source, ref.target))    return edges
```

```
function build_edges(nodes, references):    edges = []    for ref in references:        if ref.type == DEPENDS_ON:            edges.add(DependencyEdge(ref.source, ref.target))        if ref.type == REFERENCES:            edges.add(ReferenceEdge(ref.source, ref.target))        if ref.type == MENTIONS:            edges.add(SoftLinkEdge(ref.source, ref.target))    return edges
```

---

## 5.1 Edge types

### DependencyEdge (hard constraint)

- execution order required
execution order required

### ReferenceEdge (soft ordering)

- preferred ordering but not required
preferred ordering but not required

### SoftLinkEdge (contextual)

- informational only, no execution ordering
informational only, no execution ordering

---

# 6. DAG Construction

```
function build_execution_dag(nodes, edges):    dag = DirectedAcyclicGraph()    for node in nodes:        dag.add_node(node)    for edge in edges:        dag.add_edge(edge)    if dag.has_cycles():        resolve_cycles(dag)    return dag
```

```
function build_execution_dag(nodes, edges):    dag = DirectedAcyclicGraph()    for node in nodes:        dag.add_node(node)    for edge in edges:        dag.add_edge(edge)    if dag.has_cycles():        resolve_cycles(dag)    return dag
```

---

## 6.1 Cycle resolution strategy

If cycles exist:

Priority resolution:

- break edges from LOWER level → HIGHER level
break edges from LOWER level → HIGHER level

- break edges from RATIONALE → ALGORITHM
break edges from RATIONALE → ALGORITHM

- preserve PROTOCOL_RULE dependencies over EXAMPLE links
preserve PROTOCOL_RULE dependencies over EXAMPLE links

- if unresolved → mark as NEEDS_REVIEW in Nebula
if unresolved → mark as NEEDS_REVIEW in Nebula

---

# 7. Execution Plan Compilation

Once DAG is constructed:

```
function compile_execution_plan(dag):    topo_order = topological_sort(dag)    plan = []    for node in topo_order:        step = ExecutionStep(            node_id=node.id,            action=resolve_executor(node),            inputs=get_inputs(node),            outputs=declare_outputs(node)        )        plan.append(step)    return plan
```

```
function compile_execution_plan(dag):    topo_order = topological_sort(dag)    plan = []    for node in topo_order:        step = ExecutionStep(            node_id=node.id,            action=resolve_executor(node),            inputs=get_inputs(node),            outputs=declare_outputs(node)        )        plan.append(step)    return plan
```

---

# 8. Executor Resolution

Each node type maps to an execution handler.

```
function resolve_executor(node):    switch node.type:        case ALGORITHM:            return AlgorithmExecutor        case DATA_MODEL:            return SchemaExecutor        case PROTOCOL_RULE:            return ConstraintExecutor        case MIGRATION_STEP:            return MigrationExecutor        case ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:            return ValidationExecutor
```

```
function resolve_executor(node):    switch node.type:        case ALGORITHM:            return AlgorithmExecutor        case DATA_MODEL:            return SchemaExecutor        case PROTOCOL_RULE:            return ConstraintExecutor        case MIGRATION_STEP:            return MigrationExecutor        case ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:            return ValidationExecutor
```

---

# 9. Execution Context Binding

Each execution step runs with:

```
{  "role": "Conduit",  "mode": "EXECUTION",  "strict_mode": true,  "allowed_chunk_kinds": ["ALGORITHM","MIGRATION_STEP","PROTOCOL_RULE"],  "review_filter": ["REVIEWED","CURRENT_FOCUS"],  "determinism": true}
```

```

---

# 10. Execution Order Semantics

Execution follows:

- DATA_MODEL first (schema foundation)
DATA_MODEL first (schema foundation)

- PROTOCOL_RULE second (constraints)
PROTOCOL_RULE second (constraints)

- ALGORITHM third (logic)
ALGORITHM third (logic)

- MIGRATION_STEP fourth (state transitions)
MIGRATION_STEP fourth (state transitions)

- ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA last (validation)
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA last (validation)

This is asemantic ordering constraint, not just topological sorting.

---

# 11. Execution Receipts

Every execution step produces a receipt:

```
{  "node_id": "...",  "status": "SUCCESS | FAILED | SKIPPED",  "timestamp": "...",  "inputs": [],  "outputs": [],  "validation_result": {},  "trace": []}
```

```
{  "node_id": "...",  "status": "SUCCESS | FAILED | SKIPPED",  "timestamp": "...",  "inputs": [],  "outputs": [],  "validation_result": {},  "trace": []}
```

Receipts are stored back into Nebula as:

- execution provenance
execution provenance

- rollback anchor points
rollback anchor points

- audit trail for WRP transitions
audit trail for WRP transitions

---

# 12. Failure Handling

## 12.1 Execution failure

If a node fails:

- mark ExecutionReceipt = FAILED
mark ExecutionReceipt = FAILED

- propagate failure upward via dependency edges
propagate failure upward via dependency edges

- flag Nebula chunk as NEEDS_REVIEW
flag Nebula chunk as NEEDS_REVIEW

---

## 12.2 Invalid node

If chunk is not executable:

- keep in Nebula graph
keep in Nebula graph

- exclude from DAG
exclude from DAG

- optionally mark:REVIEW_STATUS = QUESTIONED
optionally mark:

- REVIEW_STATUS = QUESTIONED
REVIEW_STATUS = QUESTIONED

---

## 12.3 Cycle resolution failure

If DAG cannot be resolved:

- halt execution
halt execution

- emit diagnostic graph
emit diagnostic graph

- send Inspector mode review request
send Inspector mode review request

---

# 13. Role Interaction Model

Execution binding respects Nebula role system:

## Builder

- consumes ExecutionPlan
consumes ExecutionPlan

- produces code / system changes
produces code / system changes

## Architect

- validates DAG structure
validates DAG structure

- ensures invariants preserved
ensures invariants preserved

## Inspector

- reviews failures and contradictions
reviews failures and contradictions

## Conduit

- executes deterministically
executes deterministically

## Explorer

- not part of execution path
not part of execution path

---

# 14. Key Invariants

These MUST always hold:

- Execution DAG is acyclic
Execution DAG is acyclic

- Only eligible chunks become nodes
Only eligible chunks become nodes

- Review-filtered chunks cannot execute
Review-filtered chunks cannot execute

- Receipts are immutable once written
Receipts are immutable once written

- Nebula is source of truth, Conduit is execution engine
Nebula is source of truth, Conduit is execution engine

- No execution without resolved role context
No execution without resolved role context

---

# 15. Conceptual Shift

This is the critical transition:

> Nebula describes structureConduit enacts structureWRP defines legality of transformation

Nebula describes structureConduit enacts structureWRP defines legality of transformation

Together they form:

- Nebula = semantic graph
Nebula = semantic graph

- WRP = formal rules
WRP = formal rules

- Conduit = execution runtime
Conduit = execution runtime

---

# 16. Summary

This binding layer enables:

- deterministic execution from semantic graphs
deterministic execution from semantic graphs

- traceable DAG-based system evolution
traceable DAG-based system evolution

- review-state-aware execution safety
review-state-aware execution safety

- role-driven execution semantics
role-driven execution semantics

- bidirectional traceability (execution → Nebula → WRP)
bidirectional traceability (execution → Nebula → WRP)

---

# 17. Final Principle

> Nothing executes unless it exists as a validated semantic node in Nebula.

Nothing executes unless it exists as a validated semantic node in Nebula.

And:

> Nothing exists in Conduit unless it can be traced back to a Nebula chunk.

Nothing exists in Conduit unless it can be traced back to a Nebula chunk.

OverviewThe WRP Validation Engine sits between:- Nebula → semantic graph- Conduit → execution DAGIt ensures that:> Every executable plan is consistent with WRP rules, Nebula semantics, and system invariants.It is a **pre-execution proof gate**, not a runtime monitor.---# 2. Validation Pipelineinput_dag→ structural_validation→ semantic_validation→ invariant_verification→ dependency_consistency_check→ execution_safety_check→ validation_report---# 3. Core Data Structures## Validation Report```json id="vr1"ValidationReport {dag_idstatus: PASS | FAIL | DEGRADEDstructural_issues[]semantic_issues[]invariant_violations[]warnings[]suggested_fixes[]}Invariant DefinitionJSONInvariant {iddescriptionscope: GLOBAL | ARTIFACT | CHUNK | EXECUTION_STEPseverity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUMcondition_expression}4. Structural ValidationEnsures DAG correctness independent of semantics.pseudofunction structural_validation(dag):assert dag.is_acyclic()assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)return PASSStructural rulesDAG MUST be acyclicall nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunksno dangling references allowedall edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs5. Semantic ValidationEnsures node meaning aligns with WRP + Nebula expectations.pseudofunction semantic_validation(dag):for node in dag.nodes:if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")if node.review_state == OUTDATED:mark_warning(node)if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")return reportSemantic constraints5.1 Protocol purity rulePROTOCOL_RULE nodes MUST NOT contain:side-effect logicmutation operationsexecution commandsThey define constraints only.5.2 Algorithm determinism ruleALGORITHM nodes MUST:be deterministicnot depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration5.3 Migration consistency ruleMIGRATION_STEP nodes MUST:reference a valid prior statedefine explicit transition target6. Invariant Verification EngineThis is the core of WRP correctness.6.1 Invariant evaluation looppseudofunction invariant_verification(dag, invariants):violations = []for invariant in invariants:for node in dag.nodes:if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):violations.append({"node": node.id,"invariant": invariant.id})return violations6.2 Example invariantsGlobal execution invariantsNo node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution pathAll PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chainNo cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chainsWRP-specific invariantsEvery ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULEEvery MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transitionEvery ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node7. Dependency Consistency CheckEnsures graph coherence across Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction dependency_consistency(dag):for edge in dag.edges:if edge.type == DEPENDS_ON:assert topological_order(edge.source) < topological_order(edge.target)if violates_level_constraints(edge):mark_error(edge)Level constraint rulesL1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logicL2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationaleL3 nodes MUST NOT define execution dependencies8. Execution Safety CheckThis step ensures the DAG is safe to run under Conduit.8.1 Safety rulespseudofunction execution_safety(dag):assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)return PASS8.2 Strict mode constraintsIn STRICT execution mode:only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowedQUESTIONED nodes forbiddenOUTDATED nodes forbiddenSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely9. Validation Severity ModelEach issue is classified:CRITICAL → blocks executionHIGH → requires interventionMEDIUM → warningLOW → informationalFailure policypseudoif CRITICAL exists:status = FAILhalt_execution()elif HIGH exists:status = DEGRADEDrequire_human_review()else:status = PASS10. Suggested Fix GeneratorFor each violation:pseudofunction suggest_fix(issue):switch issue.type:case OUTDATED_DEPENDENCY:suggest("Replace with superseding artifact")case INVALID_PROTOCOL_MUTATION:suggest("Move logic to ALGORITHM chunk")case MISSING_REFERENCE:suggest("Add cross-reference or dependency edge")case LEVEL_VIOLATION:suggest("Promote/demote chunk level or split chunk")return suggestion11. Validation Modes11.1 STRICT MODEUsed for Conduit executionno warnings allowed to escalateCRITICAL = immediate stop11.2 DEVELOPMENT MODEUsed during ingestionallows warningsgenerates fix suggestionsdoes not block graph creation11.3 INSPECTOR MODEUsed for audit / debugginghighlights contradictionssurfaces all invariant violationsmaximizes visibility over pass/fail12. Integration with NebulaValidation engine consumes:NebulaChunksReview overlaysCross-reference graphChunk kindsLevel assignmentsIt produces:ValidationReport nodes in Nebulaexecution gating signals to Conduitoptional review state updates13. Integration with ConduitConduit MUST NOT execute a DAG unless:pseudoValidationReport.status == PASSOR(status == DEGRADED AND human_override == true)14. Key System PropertyWRP Validation is the final gate before execution.It ensures:Nebula is structurally consistentWRP rules are obeyedConduit receives only safe, deterministic DAGsruntime failures are minimized by pre-execution reasoning15. System Closure LoopThis completes the full loop:WRP (rules)↓Nebula (semantic graph)↓Retrieval (role-scored relevance)↓Conduit (execution DAG)↓WRP Validation Engine (proof gate)↓Execution↓Receipts → back into Nebula``` id="loop1"---# 16. Final Principle> Nothing is executed unless it is structurally valid, semantically consistent, and invariantly sound under WRP.And more importantly:> Every execution strengthens the correctness of future validation.What you now have (this is the real milestone)You now have aclosed-loop cognitive execution system:1. WRPDefines legality2. NebulaStores meaning + review + structure3. Retrieval modelSelects relevant subgraphs per role4. Conduit execution bindingTurns subgraphs into DAGs5. Validation engine (this doc)Proves DAG correctness before executionSystem behavior now becomes:“understand”“select”“compile”“validate”“execute”“record”“re-ingest”What comes next (if we continue)At this point, the only missinghigh-value layersare:A. Execution Scheduler / Runtime (Conduit core)concurrency modelqueueingretry semanticspartial execution recoveryB. Receipt → Learning Loophow execution outcomes modify Nebula review statehow the system self-corrects over timeIf you want to continue, the most powerful next step is:“Conduit runtime scheduler + execution lifecycle manager”That’s where this system stops being a pipeline and becomes aliving distributed cognitive runtime.PrismaticSponsoredEmbedded iPaaS, No Low-Code CeilingBuild integrations in TypeScript with your IDE, CI/CD, and AI copilots.

Core Data Structures## Validation Report```json id="vr1"ValidationReport {dag_idstatus: PASS | FAIL | DEGRADEDstructural_issues[]semantic_issues[]invariant_violations[]warnings[]suggested_fixes[]}Invariant DefinitionJSONInvariant {iddescriptionscope: GLOBAL | ARTIFACT | CHUNK | EXECUTION_STEPseverity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUMcondition_expression}4. Structural ValidationEnsures DAG correctness independent of semantics.pseudofunction structural_validation(dag):assert dag.is_acyclic()assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)return PASSStructural rulesDAG MUST be acyclicall nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunksno dangling references allowedall edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs5. Semantic ValidationEnsures node meaning aligns with WRP + Nebula expectations.pseudofunction semantic_validation(dag):for node in dag.nodes:if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")if node.review_state == OUTDATED:mark_warning(node)if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")return reportSemantic constraints5.1 Protocol purity rulePROTOCOL_RULE nodes MUST NOT contain:side-effect logicmutation operationsexecution commandsThey define constraints only.5.2 Algorithm determinism ruleALGORITHM nodes MUST:be deterministicnot depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration5.3 Migration consistency ruleMIGRATION_STEP nodes MUST:reference a valid prior statedefine explicit transition target6. Invariant Verification EngineThis is the core of WRP correctness.6.1 Invariant evaluation looppseudofunction invariant_verification(dag, invariants):violations = []for invariant in invariants:for node in dag.nodes:if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):violations.append({"node": node.id,"invariant": invariant.id})return violations6.2 Example invariantsGlobal execution invariantsNo node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution pathAll PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chainNo cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chainsWRP-specific invariantsEvery ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULEEvery MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transitionEvery ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node7. Dependency Consistency CheckEnsures graph coherence across Nebula cross-references.pseudofunction dependency_consistency(dag):for edge in dag.edges:if edge.type == DEPENDS_ON:assert topological_order(edge.source) < topological_order(edge.target)if violates_level_constraints(edge):mark_error(edge)Level constraint rulesL1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logicL2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationaleL3 nodes MUST NOT define execution dependencies8. Execution Safety CheckThis step ensures the DAG is safe to run under Conduit.8.1 Safety rulespseudofunction execution_safety(dag):assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)return PASS8.2 Strict mode constraintsIn STRICT execution mode:only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowedQUESTIONED nodes forbiddenOUTDATED nodes forbiddenSUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely9. Validation Severity ModelEach issue is classified:CRITICAL → blocks executionHIGH → requires interventionMEDIUM → warningLOW → informationalFailure policypseudoif CRITICAL exists:status = FAILhalt_execution()elif HIGH exists:status = DEGRADEDrequire_human_review()else:status = PASS10. Suggested Fix GeneratorFor each violation:pseudofunction suggest_fix(issue):switch issue.type:case OUTDATED_DEPENDENCY:suggest("Replace with superseding artifact")case INVALID_PROTOCOL_MUTATION:suggest("Move logic to ALGORITHM chunk")case MISSING_REFERENCE:suggest("Add cross-reference or dependency edge")case LEVEL_VIOLATION:suggest("Promote/demote chunk level or split chunk")return suggestion11. Validation Modes11.1 STRICT MODEUsed for Conduit executionno warnings allowed to escalateCRITICAL = immediate stop11.2 DEVELOPMENT MODEUsed during ingestionallows warningsgenerates fix suggestionsdoes not block graph creation11.3 INSPECTOR MODEUsed for audit / debugginghighlights contradictionssurfaces all invariant violationsmaximizes visibility over pass/fail12. Integration with NebulaValidation engine consumes:NebulaChunksReview overlaysCross-reference graphChunk kindsLevel assignmentsIt produces:ValidationReport nodes in Nebulaexecution gating signals to Conduitoptional review state updates13. Integration with ConduitConduit MUST NOT execute a DAG unless:pseudoValidationReport.status == PASSOR(status == DEGRADED AND human_override == true)14. Key System PropertyWRP Validation is the final gate before execution.It ensures:Nebula is structurally consistentWRP rules are obeyedConduit receives only safe, deterministic DAGsruntime failures are minimized by pre-execution reasoning15. System Closure LoopThis completes the full loop:WRP (rules)↓Nebula (semantic graph)↓Retrieval (role-scored relevance)↓Conduit (execution DAG)↓WRP Validation Engine (proof gate)↓Execution↓Receipts → back into Nebula``` id="loop1"---# 16. Final Principle> Nothing is executed unless it is structurally valid, semantically consistent, and invariantly sound under WRP.And more importantly:> Every execution strengthens the correctness of future validation.What you now have (this is the real milestone)You now have aclosed-loop cognitive execution system:1. WRPDefines legality2. NebulaStores meaning + review + structure3. Retrieval modelSelects relevant subgraphs per role4. Conduit execution bindingTurns subgraphs into DAGs5. Validation engine (this doc)Proves DAG correctness before executionSystem behavior now becomes:“understand”“select”“compile”“validate”“execute”“record”“re-ingest”What comes next (if we continue)At this point, the only missinghigh-value layersare:A. Execution Scheduler / Runtime (Conduit core)concurrency modelqueueingretry semanticspartial execution recoveryB. Receipt → Learning Loophow execution outcomes modify Nebula review statehow the system self-corrects over timeIf you want to continue, the most powerful next step is:“Conduit runtime scheduler + execution lifecycle manager”That’s where this system stops being a pipeline and becomes aliving distributed cognitive runtime.

Good. This is the layer you’ve been implicitly building toward the whole time:the system that checks itself before it runs.

Up until now:

- Nebula decideswhat exists and what it means
Nebula decideswhat exists and what it means

- Conduit decideshow to execute it
Conduit decideshow to execute it

- WRP defineswhat is legal
WRP defineswhat is legal

What’s missing is the thing that answers:

> “Can we prove this execution plan is internally consistent before we run it?”

“Can we prove this execution plan is internally consistent before we run it?”

That’s what this layer does.

# 4. Structural Validation

Ensures DAG correctness independent of semantics.

```
function structural_validation(dag):    assert dag.is_acyclic()    assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)    assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)    assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)    return PASS
```

```
function structural_validation(dag):    assert dag.is_acyclic()    assert all_nodes_have_valid_ids(dag)    assert all_edges_reference_valid_nodes(dag)    assert no_orphan_nodes(dag)    return PASS
```

---

## Structural rules

- DAG MUST be acyclic
DAG MUST be acyclic

- all nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunks
all nodes MUST originate from Nebula chunks

- no dangling references allowed
no dangling references allowed

- all edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs
all edges MUST resolve to valid node IDs

# 5. Semantic Validation

Ensures node meaning aligns with WRP + Nebula expectations.

```
function semantic_validation(dag):    for node in dag.nodes:        if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:            mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")        if node.review_state == OUTDATED:            mark_warning(node)        if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():            mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")    return report
```

```
function semantic_validation(dag):    for node in dag.nodes:        if node.type not in EXECUTABLE_KINDS:            mark_error(node, "Non-executable chunk in DAG")        if node.review_state == OUTDATED:            mark_warning(node)        if node.kind == PROTOCOL_RULE and node.has_mutation_behavior():            mark_error(node, "Protocol rule cannot define mutation logic")    return report
```

---

## Semantic constraints

### 5.1 Protocol purity rule

PROTOCOL_RULE nodes MUST NOT contain:

- side-effect logic
side-effect logic

- mutation operations
mutation operations

- execution commands
execution commands

They define constraints only.

---

### 5.2 Algorithm determinism rule

ALGORITHM nodes MUST:

- be deterministic
be deterministic

- not depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration
not depend on external mutable state without explicit input declaration

---

### 5.3 Migration consistency rule

MIGRATION_STEP nodes MUST:

- reference a valid prior state
reference a valid prior state

- define explicit transition target
define explicit transition target

# 6. Invariant Verification Engine

This is the core of WRP correctness.

---

## 6.1 Invariant evaluation loop

```
function invariant_verification(dag, invariants):    violations = []    for invariant in invariants:        for node in dag.nodes:            if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):                violations.append({                    "node": node.id,                    "invariant": invariant.id                })    return violations
```

```
function invariant_verification(dag, invariants):    violations = []    for invariant in invariants:        for node in dag.nodes:            if not evaluate(invariant.condition_expression, node):                violations.append({                    "node": node.id,                    "invariant": invariant.id                })    return violations
```

---

## 6.2 Example invariants

### Global execution invariants

- No node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution path
No node may depend on an OUTDATED node in execution path

- All PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chain
All PROTOCOL_RULE nodes must precede ALGORITHM nodes in dependency chain

- No cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chains
No cyclic dependency across MIGRATION_STEP chains

---

### WRP-specific invariants

- Every ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULE
Every ALGORITHM must be traceable to at least one PROTOCOL_RULE

- Every MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transition
Every MIGRATION_STEP must reference a DATA_MODEL change or state transition

- Every ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node
Every ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA must map to at least one executable node

# 7. Dependency Consistency Check

Ensures graph coherence across Nebula cross-references.

```
function dependency_consistency(dag):    for edge in dag.edges:        if edge.type == DEPENDS_ON:            assert topological_order(edge.source) < topological_order(edge.target)        if violates_level_constraints(edge):            mark_error(edge)
```

```

## Level constraint rules

- L1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logic
L1 nodes MUST NOT depend on L3 nodes for execution logic

- L2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationale
L2 nodes MAY depend on L3 for rationale

- L3 nodes MUST NOT define execution dependencies

## 8.1 Safety rules

```
function execution_safety(dag):    assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)    assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)    assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)    assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)    return PASS
```

```
function execution_safety(dag):    assert no_unresolved_nodes(dag)    assert all_nodes_have_executor(dag)    assert no_questioned_nodes_in_execution_path(dag)    assert strict_mode_compliance(dag)    return PASS
```

---

## 8.2 Strict mode constraints

In STRICT execution mode:

- only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowed
only REVIEWED or CURRENT_FOCUS nodes allowed

- QUESTIONED nodes forbidden
QUESTIONED nodes forbidden

- OUTDATED nodes forbidden
OUTDATED nodes forbidden

- SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely
SUPERSEDED_CONFIRMED nodes excluded entirely

# 9. Validation Severity Model

Each issue is classified:

- CRITICAL → blocks execution
CRITICAL → blocks execution

- HIGH → requires intervention
HIGH → requires intervention

- MEDIUM → warning
MEDIUM → warning

- LOW → informational
LOW → informational

## Failure policy

```
if CRITICAL exists:    status = FAIL    halt_execution()elif HIGH exists:    status = DEGRADED    require_human_review()else:    status = PASS
```

# 10. Suggested Fix Generator

For each violation:

```
function suggest_fix(issue):    switch issue.type:        case OUTDATED_DEPENDENCY:            suggest("Replace with superseding artifact")        case INVALID_PROTOCOL_MUTATION:            suggest("Move logic to ALGORITHM chunk")        case MISSING_REFERENCE:            suggest("Add cross-reference or dependency edge")        case LEVEL_VIOLATION:            suggest("Promote/demote chunk level or split chunk")    return suggestion
```

```

```

- no warnings allowed to escalate
no warnings allowed to escalate

CRITICAL = immediate stop

Used during ingestion

allows warnings

generates fix suggestions

does not block graph creation

Used for audit / debugging

- highlights contradictions

- surfaces all invariant violations

- maximizes visibility over pass/fail

Scheduler ModelConduit uses a **dependency-aware priority scheduler**.---## 4.1 Scheduling loop```pseudo id="sched1"while true:ready_nodes = get_ready_nodes(dag)prioritized = rank(ready_nodes,priority_function)for node in prioritized:if can_run(node):dispatch(node)4.2 Priority functionpseudopriority(node) =role_priority_weight(node)+ review_priority_weight(node)+ chunk_kind_weight(node)+ dependency_depth_weight(node)- failure_penalty(node)4.3 Dependency depth weightNodes deeper in dependency chains may be prioritized to unlock downstream execution faster.depth_score = longest_path_from_root(node)5. Concurrency ModelConduit supports controlled parallel execution.5.1 Execution constraintsA node MAY execute in parallel if:pseudocan_parallelize(node) =node.has_no_shared_mutation_targetsAND node.dependencies_satisfiedAND not_conflicting_with_running_nodes(node)5.2 Conflict rulesTwo nodes conflict if:they modify same conceptual statethey depend on each other's outputsthey share non-isolated resource contexts5.3 Concurrency policydefault: conservative parallelismmigration mode: stricter (serial execution preferred)exploration mode: relaxed (higher parallelism allowed)6. Execution Dispatcherpseudofunction dispatch(node):mark(node, RUNNING)executor = resolve_executor(node.type)context = build_execution_context(node)try:result = executor.execute(node.payload, context)mark(node, COMPLETED)emit_receipt(node, result)except error:handle_failure(node, error)7. Execution Context BuilderEach node executes with a structured context:JSON{"node_id":"...","dag_id":"...","role":"Conduit","mode":"EXECUTION","strict_mode":true,"nebula_trace": [],"allowed_chunk_kinds": [],"validation_signature":"WRP_VALIDATED","determinism":true}8. Failure Handling System8.1 Failure classificationpseudofunction classify_failure(error):if transient(error):return RETRYABLEif dependency_missing(error):return BLOCKINGif semantic_violation(error):return INVALID_DAGreturn FATAL8.2 Retry policypseudoif RETRYABLE:if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:schedule_retry(node)else:mark(node, FAILED)8.3 Blocking failure propagationIf a node fails due to dependency:downstream nodes → SKIPPED or PENDINGupstream nodes unaffectedDAG remains valid but partially executable8.4 Compensation modelFor MIGRATION_STEP nodes:failures MAY trigger compensating stepsrollback DAG may be generated9. DAG Execution GuaranteesConduit guarantees:deterministic execution order for identical inputsidempotent retries (when possible)no execution without READY stateno execution of invalidated nodesstrict adherence to WRP validation outputs10. Execution ReceiptsEvery execution produces a receipt:JSONExecutionReceipt {node_iddag_idstatusstart_timeend_timeinputsoutputslogsvalidation_ref}Receipts are:immutablestored in Nebulaused for future graph refinementused for failure analysis and review updates11. Scheduling Policies11.1 STRICT POLICYUsed for production execution:no speculative executionno retry beyond limitno OUTDATED or QUESTIONED nodesminimal concurrency11.2 OPTIMIZED POLICYUsed for performance execution:moderate concurrencypredictive schedulingprioritizes unlocking downstream nodes11.3 EXPLORATION POLICYUsed for discovery:high concurrencyrelaxed ordering constraintsallows partial execution of graph branches12. Deadlock PreventionDeadlocks are prevented via:topological schedulingcycle detection (from WRP validation layer)fallback serial executionforced dependency resolution orderingIf deadlock is detected:1. pause execution2. emit diagnostic subgraph3. request inspector review13. System Integration13.1 Nebula integrationConduit reads:validated DAGschunk metadatareview overlayscross-reference structureConduit writes:ExecutionReceiptsfailure annotationsinferred review updates13.2 WRP integrationConduit only executes DAGs that:pass WRP validation enginesatisfy invariant checkscomply with strict mode rules13.3 Validation gate couplingpseudoif not WRPValidationReport.PASS:abort_execution()14. Feedback Loop (Critical)Execution results feed back into Nebula:failed nodes → QUESTIONEDrepeatedly failing nodes → OUTDATED candidatefrequently executed nodes → CURRENT_FOCUS candidatestable nodes → REVIEWEDThis closes theadaptive system loop.15. Key System PropertyConduit is not just an executor — it is a stateful runtime that evolves Nebula’s trust model over time.16. Final Architecture ViewWRP↓Nebula (semantic graph + review state)↓Retrieval (role-scored subgraph selection)↓WRP Validation Engine (pre-execution proof gate)↓Conduit Scheduler (this layer)↓Execution Nodes↓Receipts↓Nebula update cycle↓(continuous loop)``` id="loop2"---# 17. Final Principle> Execution is not a stateless operation.It is a **governed traversal of a validated semantic graph over time**, where every run modifies the system’s confidence in its own knowledge.What you now have (this is the full runtime)You now have a complete layered system:1. WRPdefines legality2. Nebulastores meaning + structure + trust3. Retrieval modelrole-based semantic cognition4. Execution bindinggraph → DAG conversion5. Validation enginepre-execution proof system6. Conduit runtime (this doc)scheduling + concurrency + lifecycle + failure recoveryYou have effectively built:A self-validating, role-aware, graph-driven execution operating system for structured knowledge systems.What remains (final frontier layer)At this point there are only two meaningful extensions left:A. Self-correction learning loop (very important)How Nebula updates itself from execution receipts over timeB. Distributed execution model (optional scaling layer)How Conduit runs across multiple workers/nodes/servicesIf you want to continue, the next most powerful step is:“Nebula Self-Healing & Feedback Learning System (Receipt → Graph Mutation Engine)”That is where the system becomesadaptive instead of just deterministic.SalesforceSponsoredOrchestrate AI Agent WorkflowsMake any API agent-ready with MuleSoft Agent Fabric.

# Conduit Runtime Scheduler & Execution Lifecycle Manager**Status:** Draft  **Owner:** Conduit core runtime  **Purpose:** Define scheduling, execution lifecycle, concurrency model, and failure recovery semantics for WRP-derived execution DAGs.---# 1. OverviewConduit is a deterministic execution runtime for validated Nebula-derived DAGs.It is responsible for:- scheduling execution steps- managing concurrency- tracking execution state- handling retries and failures- emitting execution receipts- ensuring deterministic replayability---# 2. Core Principle> Conduit does not “run code.” It executes validated semantic graphs under strict lifecycle control.Every execution is:- deterministic where possible- replayable- traceable to Nebula chunks- governed by WRP validation guarantees---# 3. Execution Lifecycle StatesEach node transitions through a lifecycle:
```

PENDING→ READY→ RUNNING→ COMPLETED→ FAILED→ RETRYING→ SKIPPED→ COMPENSATED

```
---## 3.1 State definitions### PENDINGNode is waiting for dependencies or scheduling.### READYAll dependencies satisfied; eligible for execution.### RUNNINGNode is actively executing.### COMPLETEDExecution succeeded and produced valid output.### FAILEDExecution failed irrecoverably for current attempt.### RETRYINGNode is scheduled for re-execution.### SKIPPEDNode is intentionally bypassed (policy or conditional logic).### COMPENSATEDNode failure has been resolved via compensating action (migration or rollback logic).---# 4. Scheduler ModelConduit uses a **dependency-aware priority scheduler**.---## 4.1 Scheduling loop```pseudo id="sched1"while true:    ready_nodes = get_ready_nodes(dag)    prioritized = rank(ready_nodes,        priority_function    )    for node in prioritized:        if can_run(node):            dispatch(node)
```

```
---## 3.1 State definitions### PENDINGNode is waiting for dependencies or scheduling.### READYAll dependencies satisfied; eligible for execution.### RUNNINGNode is actively executing.### COMPLETEDExecution succeeded and produced valid output.### FAILEDExecution failed irrecoverably for current attempt.### RETRYINGNode is scheduled for re-execution.### SKIPPEDNode is intentionally bypassed (policy or conditional logic).### COMPENSATEDNode failure has been resolved via compensating action (migration or rollback logic).---# 4. Scheduler ModelConduit uses a **dependency-aware priority scheduler**.---## 4.1 Scheduling loop```pseudo id="sched1"while true:    ready_nodes = get_ready_nodes(dag)    prioritized = rank(ready_nodes,        priority_function    )    for node in prioritized:        if can_run(node):            dispatch(node)
```

## 4.2 Priority function

```
priority(node) =    role_priority_weight(node)  + review_priority_weight(node)  + chunk_kind_weight(node)  + dependency_depth_weight(node)  - failure_penalty(node)
```

```
priority(node) =    role_priority_weight(node)  + review_priority_weight(node)  + chunk_kind_weight(node)  + dependency_depth_weight(node)  - failure_penalty(node)
```

---

## 4.3 Dependency depth weight

Nodes deeper in dependency chains may be prioritized to unlock downstream execution faster.

```
depth_score = longest_path_from_root(node)
```

```
depth_score = longest_path_from_root(node)
```

# 5. Concurrency Model

Conduit supports controlled parallel execution.

---

## 5.1 Execution constraints

A node MAY execute in parallel if:

```
can_parallelize(node) =    node.has_no_shared_mutation_targets    AND node.dependencies_satisfied    AND not_conflicting_with_running_nodes(node)
```

```
can_parallelize(node) =    node.has_no_shared_mutation_targets    AND node.dependencies_satisfied    AND not_conflicting_with_running_nodes(node)
```

---

## 5.2 Conflict rules

Two nodes conflict if:

- they modify same conceptual state
they modify same conceptual state

- they depend on each other's outputs
they depend on each other's outputs

- they share non-isolated resource contexts
they share non-isolated resource contexts

---

## 5.3 Concurrency policy

- default: conservative parallelism
default: conservative parallelism

- migration mode: stricter (serial execution preferred)
migration mode: stricter (serial execution preferred)

- exploration mode: relaxed (higher parallelism allowed)
exploration mode: relaxed (higher parallelism allowed)

---

# 6. Execution Dispatcher

```
function dispatch(node):    mark(node, RUNNING)    executor = resolve_executor(node.type)    context = build_execution_context(node)    try:        result = executor.execute(node.payload, context)        mark(node, COMPLETED)        emit_receipt(node, result)    except error:        handle_failure(node, error)
```

# 8. Failure Handling System

---

## 8.1 Failure classification

```
function classify_failure(error):    if transient(error):        return RETRYABLE    if dependency_missing(error):        return BLOCKING    if semantic_violation(error):        return INVALID_DAG    return FATAL
```

```
function classify_failure(error):    if transient(error):        return RETRYABLE    if dependency_missing(error):        return BLOCKING    if semantic_violation(error):        return INVALID_DAG    return FATAL
```

---

## 8.2 Retry policy

```
if RETRYABLE:    if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:        schedule_retry(node)    else:        mark(node, FAILED)
```

```
if RETRYABLE:    if retry_count < MAX_RETRIES:        schedule_retry(node)    else:        mark(node, FAILED)
```

---

## 8.3 Blocking failure propagation

If a node fails due to dependency:

- downstream nodes → SKIPPED or PENDING
downstream nodes → SKIPPED or PENDING

- upstream nodes unaffected
upstream nodes unaffected

- DAG remains valid but partially executable
DAG remains valid but partially executable

---

## 8.4 Compensation model

For MIGRATION_STEP nodes:

- failures MAY trigger compensating steps
failures MAY trigger compensating steps

- rollback DAG may be generated
rollback DAG may be generated

deterministic execution order for identical inputs

idempotent retries (when possible)

no execution without READY state

- no execution of invalidated nodes
no execution of invalidated nodes

Used for production execution:

- no speculative execution
no speculative execution

- no retry beyond limit
no retry beyond limit

- no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED nodes
no OUTDATED or QUESTIONED nodes

- minimal concurrency
minimal concurrency

moderate concurrency

forced dependency resolution ordering

1. pause execution2. emit diagnostic subgraph3. request inspector review

Graph Update PlanningNebula does NOT mutate immediately.It generates amutation plan.7.1 Mutation plan structureJSONGraphMutationPlan {target_node_idmutation_typereasonconfidenceproposed_change}7.2 Mutation typesRECLASSIFY_CHUNK_KINDUPDATE_REVIEW_STATEMODIFY_EDGEADD_EDGEREMOVE_EDGEPROMOTE_LEVELDEMOTE_LEVELMARK_SUPERSEDEDSPLIT_CHUNKMERGE_CHUNK8. Review State UpdatesExecution directly influences trust model:8.1 SUCCESS influenceIf node repeatedly succeeds:OUTDATED → REVIEWEDREVIEWED → CURRENT_FOCUS candidate (if frequently used)NEEDS_REVIEW → REVIEWED8.2 FAIL_SEMANTIC influenceREVIEWED → QUESTIONEDCURRENT_FOCUS → NEEDS_REVIEWchunk_kind marked suspect8.3 FAIL_INVARIANT influencenode → QUESTIONED (immediate)parent section → NEEDS_REVIEWrelated dependencies → flagged8.4 REPEATED FAILURE RULEIf node fails ≥ N times:pseudomark(node, OUTDATED)propagate_to_dependents(node)9. Cross-Reference AdjustmentExecution reveals incorrect or missing edges.9.1 Missing dependency discoveryIf runtime shows implicit dependency:pseudoif runtime_dependency_detected and no_edge_exists:add_edge(source, target, type=DEPENDS_ON)9.2 Broken dependency pruningIf dependency never used:downgrade to MENTIONSor remove edge entirely9.3 Over-constrained graph correctionIf SKIPPED nodes are frequent:dependency edges may be too strictdowngrade to soft references10. Chunk Reclassification EngineExecution results refine chunk taxonomy.10.1 Heuristic correction rulespseudoif ALGORITHM fails frequently:reconsider_chunk_kind(node)if PROTOCOL_RULE causes mutation logic:split_into(PROTOCOL_RULE, ALGORITHM)if RATIONALE is executed:likely misclassified → promote to PROTOCOL_RULE or DATA_MODEL11. Validation Feedback LoopValidation engine and runtime co-evolve.11.1 Rule reinforcementIf invariant is repeatedly violated:strengthen WRP invariantupdate validation engineincrease strictness11.2 Rule relaxationIf invariant blocks correct execution repeatedly:downgrade severityor refine condition expression12. Self-Healing ActionsNebula can automatically propose:12.1 Structural repairfix DAG cyclesre-order dependenciesisolate unstable subgraphs12.2 Semantic repairfix chunk misclassificationsplit overloaded chunksmerge redundant definitions12.3 Trust repairadjust review statesrecalibrate retrieval scoring weightsre-evaluate CURRENT_FOCUS artifacts13. Learning SignalsNebula tracks:failure frequency per chunk kindfailure frequency per artifactinvariant violation hotspotshigh-risk dependency edgesunstable execution pathsThese becomemeta-knowledge signals.14. Stability ModelEach node gets a stability score:pseudostability =success_rate- failure_rate- invariant_violation_rate+ reuse_frequency14.1 Stability interpretationhigh stability → REVIEWED / trustedmedium stability → NEEDS_REVIEWlow stability → QUESTIONED or OUTDATED candidate15. Closed Feedback LoopNebula graph↓Retrieval (role-based selection)↓Conduit execution↓Receipts↓Validation engine↓Self-healing system↓Graph mutation↓Improved Nebula↓(repeat)``` id="loop3"---# 16. Key System Property> The system is not only executable — it is continuously self-correcting based on execution reality.---# 17. Final Principle> Truth in Nebula is not declared. It is inferred from execution behavior over time.The graph becomes more accurate not because it is edited, but because it is **tested against itself repeatedly**.What you now have (this is the full cognitive loop)You now have a completeself-evolving system architecture:1. WRPdefines correctness constraints2. Nebulastores semantic structure + trust model3. Retrieval enginerole-based cognition4. Conduit runtimeexecution engine + scheduler5. Validation enginepre-execution proof gate6. Self-healing system (this doc)post-execution learning + mutationYou’ve now built:A closed-loop semantic operating system that compiles, executes, validates, and improves itself over time.At this point, there are only two “final form” extensions left:A. Global governance model (who/what can mutate truth)→ prevents runaway self-modificationB. Multi-agent orchestration layer→ Inspector/Builder/Architect as concurrent reasoning actors inside the runtimeIf you want to continue, the next most important artifact is:“Nebula Governance & Mutation Authority Model”That’s where you definewhat is allowed to change the system’s own truth layer.Stonebranch Inc.SponsoredWorkload Automation Designed to ScaleTurn static job scheduling into AI-Powered workload orchestration

# 5. Outcome Classification

Each receipt is classified into a semantic outcome category:

---

## 5.1 SUCCESS

Execution succeeded without deviation.

Implication:

- graph likely correct
graph likely correct

- chunk classification likely valid
chunk classification likely valid

- dependencies likely sound
dependencies likely sound

---

## 5.2 FAIL_TRANSIENT

Temporary failure:

- network
network

- resource
resource

- external dependency
external dependency

Implication:

- no graph mutation
no graph mutation

- possible retry scheduling adjustment
possible retry scheduling adjustment

---

## 5.3 FAIL_SEMANTIC

Execution failed due to logic or structural mismatch.

Implication:

- chunk likely misclassified
chunk likely misclassified

- WRP assumption violated
WRP assumption violated

- dependency graph potentially incorrect
dependency graph potentially incorrect

---

## 5.4 FAIL_INVARIANT

A WRP invariant was violated.

Implication:

- critical structural issue
critical structural issue

- requires Inspector review
requires Inspector review

- may invalidate subgraph
may invalidate subgraph

---

## 5.5 SKIPPED

Execution intentionally skipped.

Implication:

- graph may be over-specified
graph may be over-specified

- dependency edges may be too strict
dependency edges may be too strict

---

# 6. Semantic Diff Analysis

When execution diverges from expected behavior:

```
function semantic_diff(receipt, expected_behavior):    diff = compare(        expected_inputs,        actual_inputs,        expected_outputs,        actual_outputs    )    return diff
```

```
function semantic_diff(receipt, expected_behavior):    diff = compare(        expected_inputs,        actual_inputs,        expected_outputs,        actual_outputs    )    return diff
```

---

## 6.1 Types of semantic drift

### A. Input drift

Node received unexpected inputs

→ suggests incorrect dependency edges

---

### B. Output drift

Node produced unexpected outputs

→ suggests wrong chunk kind classification

---

### C. Control-flow drift

Execution order violated expectations

→ suggests DAG ordering issue

---

### D. Invariant drift

Invariant violated during execution

→ suggests WRP model mismatch

---

# 7. Graph Update Planning

Nebula does NOT mutate immediately.

It generates amutation plan.

---

## 7.1 Mutation plan structure

```
GraphMutationPlan {  target_node_id  mutation_type  reason  confidence  proposed_change}
```

```
GraphMutationPlan {  target_node_id  mutation_type  reason  confidence  proposed_change}
```

- RECLASSIFY_CHUNK_KIND
RECLASSIFY_CHUNK_KIND

- UPDATE_REVIEW_STATE
UPDATE_REVIEW_STATE

- MODIFY_EDGE
MODIFY_EDGE

- ADD_EDGE
ADD_EDGE

- REMOVE_EDGE

PROMOTE_LEVEL

DEMOTE_LEVEL

MARK_SUPERSEDED

SPLIT_CHUNK

MERGE_CHUNK

# 8. Review State Updates

Execution directly influences trust model:

---

## 8.1 SUCCESS influence

If node repeatedly succeeds:

- OUTDATED → REVIEWED
OUTDATED → REVIEWED

- REVIEWED → CURRENT_FOCUS candidate (if frequently used)
REVIEWED → CURRENT_FOCUS candidate (if frequently used)

- NEEDS_REVIEW → REVIEWED
NEEDS_REVIEW → REVIEWED

---

## 8.2 FAIL_SEMANTIC influence

- REVIEWED → QUESTIONED
REVIEWED → QUESTIONED

- CURRENT_FOCUS → NEEDS_REVIEW
CURRENT_FOCUS → NEEDS_REVIEW

- chunk_kind marked suspect
chunk_kind marked suspect

---

## 8.3 FAIL_INVARIANT influence

- node → QUESTIONED (immediate)
node → QUESTIONED (immediate)

- parent section → NEEDS_REVIEW
parent section → NEEDS_REVIEW

- related dependencies → flagged
related dependencies → flagged

---

## 8.4 REPEATED FAILURE RULE

If node fails ≥ N times:

```
mark(node, OUTDATED)propagate_to_dependents(node)
```

```
mark(node, OUTDATED)propagate_to_dependents(node)
```

# 9. Cross-Reference Adjustment

Execution reveals incorrect or missing edges.

---

## 9.1 Missing dependency discovery

If runtime shows implicit dependency:

```
if runtime_dependency_detected and no_edge_exists:    add_edge(source, target, type=DEPENDS_ON)
```

```
if runtime_dependency_detected and no_edge_exists:    add_edge(source, target, type=DEPENDS_ON)
```

---

## 9.2 Broken dependency pruning

If dependency never used:

- downgrade to MENTIONS
downgrade to MENTIONS

- or remove edge entirely
or remove edge entirely

---

## 9.3 Over-constrained graph correction

If SKIPPED nodes are frequent:

- dependency edges may be too strict
dependency edges may be too strict

- downgrade to soft references
downgrade to soft references

Execution results refine chunk taxonomy.

if ALGORITHM fails frequently:    reconsider_chunk_kind(node)if PROTOCOL_RULE causes mutation logic:    split_into(PROTOCOL_RULE, ALGORITHM)if RATIONALE is executed:    likely misclassified → promote to PROTOCOL_RULE or DATA_MODEL
```

Each node gets a stability score:

```
stability =    success_rate  - failure_rate  - invariant_violation_rate  + reuse_frequency

Authority LayersNebula defines four governance layers:L0: Execution Layer (Conduit runtime)L1: Learning Layer (Self-healing system)L2: Validation Layer (WRP engine)L3: Governance Layer (authority controller)---## 3.1 L0 — Execution Layer (Conduit)### Permissions:- emit ExecutionReceipts- propose GraphMutationPlans### Restrictions:- cannot directly mutate Nebula graph- cannot modify WRP rules- cannot alter validation logic### Role:> Observes reality, does not define it---## 3.2 L1 — Learning Layer (Self-Healing)### Permissions:- propose chunk reclassification- propose edge modifications- propose review state updates- propose stability recalibration### Restrictions:- cannot finalize mutations- cannot override invariants- cannot modify protocol rules### Role:> Suggests evolution based on evidence---## 3.3 L2 — Validation Layer (WRP Engine)### Permissions:- accept/reject mutation proposals- mark violations- adjust invariant strictness (bounded)- trigger review escalation### Restrictions:- cannot directly mutate execution graph- cannot create new semantic chunks### Role:> Enforces correctness constraints---## 3.4 L3 — Governance Layer (Authority Controller)### Permissions:- approve or deny all mutations- resolve conflicting proposals- enforce schema-level changes- modify chunk kind definitions (controlled)- approve WRP invariant changes### Role:> Final arbiter of truth changes---# 4. Mutation TypesAll graph mutations fall into controlled categories:---## 4.1 Structural mutations- ADD_EDGE- REMOVE_EDGE- MODIFY_EDGE- SPLIT_NODE- MERGE_NODE---## 4.2 Semantic mutations- RECLASSIFY_CHUNK_KIND- UPDATE_LEVEL- MARK_SUPERSEDED- UPDATE_REVIEW_STATE---## 4.3 Governance mutations- ADD_INVARIANT- MODIFY_INVARIANT- UPDATE_EXECUTION_POLICY- CHANGE_VALIDATION_STRICTNESS---# 5. Mutation Permission Matrix| Mutation Type         | L0 | L1 | L2 | L3 ||----------------------|----|----|----|----|| Emit Proposal        | ✔  | ✔  | ✖  | ✖  || Structural Change    | ✖  | ✔  | ✖  | ✔* || Semantic Change      | ✖  | ✔  | ✔  | ✔* || Validation Change    | ✖  | ✖  | ✔  | ✔  || Invariant Change     | ✖  | ✖  | ✔  | ✔  |\* only via approved mutation pipeline---# 6. Mutation PipelineNo mutation is applied directly.All mutations follow this process:proposal→ validation check→ conflict analysis→ governance evaluation→ approval decision→ application→ audit logging---# 7. Mutation Proposal Format```json id="mp2"MutationProposal {idsource_layertarget_nodemutation_typerationaleconfidenceevidence[]affected_nodes[]}8. Conflict Resolution SystemWhen multiple mutation proposals conflict:8.1 Priority orderingWRP invariant-preserving mutationsExecution-failure-driven correctionsHigh-frequency failure correctionsStructural consistency repairsOptimization-only mutations8.2 Tie-breaking rulesIf equal priority:prefer minimal graph changeprefer localized mutationprefer reversible mutationprefer validation-backed mutation9. Safety Constraints9.1 No uncontrolled mutationpseudoif mutation.source not in APPROVED_LAYERS:reject(mutation)9.2 Invariant lock ruleIf mutation violates CRITICAL invariant:reject immediatelyescalate to L3 governance review9.3 Stability threshold ruleIf node stability < threshold:allow mutation proposalsbut require dual approval (L1 + L3)10. Mutation Audit TrailEvery accepted mutation produces an immutable record:JSONMutationRecord {mutation_idapplied_bytimestampbefore_stateafter_statejustificationvalidation_result}Stored in Nebula ashistorical truth layer.11. Governance Decision EngineL3 uses a deterministic scoring system:pseudoscore(mutation) =evidence_strength+ validation_support+ execution_failure_correlation- risk_score- graph_impact_radiusApproval thresholds:≥ 0.75 → approved0.5–0.75 → review required< 0.5 → rejected12. Execution vs Truth SeparationCritical system rule:Execution success does not automatically imply truth correctness.And:Truth correction does not automatically imply execution change.They are decoupled intentionally.13. Recovery ModeIf system instability is detected:L1 freezes mutation generationL2 tightens validation rulesL3 enters manual review modeConduit continues only on VERIFIED subgraph14. System Stability ModelNebula tracks:mutation frequencyrollback frequencyinvariant violation densitygraph churn rateHigh churn triggers:stricter governancereduced L1 autonomyincreased validation strictness15. Key System PropertyNebula is self-modifying, but not self-authorizing.Modification and authorization are permanently separated.16. Full System Architecture (Final Form)WRP (rules of correctness)↓Nebula (semantic + trust graph)↓Retrieval (role-based cognition)↓Conduit (execution runtime)↓WRP Validation Engine (proof gate)↓Self-Healing Layer (mutation proposals)↓Governance Layer (mutation authority)↓Approved Graph Mutation↓Updated Nebula↓(loop)``` id="loop4"---# 17. Final Principle> A system that can change itself must also define who is allowed to change it.Without governance, self-modification becomes noise.With governance, it becomes **controlled evolution of a semantic system of truth**.What you now have (this is essentially system completion)You’ve now defined a full operating architecture:1. WRPformal correctness system2. Nebulasemantic graph + trust + review3. Retrieval systemrole-aware cognitive selection4. Conduit runtimeexecution scheduler + DAG runtime5. Validation enginepre-execution proof gate6. Self-healing systempost-execution learning7. Governance model (this doc)authority + mutation controlWhat this actually is (stepping back)You’ve constructed:A self-evolving, role-aware, validated semantic execution system with bounded authority mutation.Or more simply:A controlled cognitive operating system for structured knowledge and execution.If we continue (optional final expansions)There are only two remaining “advanced system layers”:A. Multi-agent reasoning fabric(Builder / Architect / Inspector running concurrently over the same graph)B. Temporal versioning & branching system(“Nebula forks”, time-travel, scenario simulation, rollback branches)If you want to continue, the next natural artifact is:“Nebula Temporal Graph Versioning & Branching Model”That’s where this system gainshistory, parallel futures, and simulation capability.AttioSponsoredBeyond AffinityRelationship intelligence plus everything else. Try Attio Free.

# 8. Conflict Resolution System

When multiple mutation proposals conflict:

---

## 8.1 Priority ordering

- WRP invariant-preserving mutations
WRP invariant-preserving mutations

- Execution-failure-driven corrections
Execution-failure-driven corrections

- High-frequency failure corrections
High-frequency failure corrections

- Structural consistency repairs
Structural consistency repairs

- Optimization-only mutations
Optimization-only mutations

---

## 8.2 Tie-breaking rules

If equal priority:

- prefer minimal graph change
prefer minimal graph change

- prefer localized mutation
prefer localized mutation

- prefer reversible mutation
prefer reversible mutation

- prefer validation-backed mutation
prefer validation-backed mutation

# 9. Safety Constraints

---

## 9.1 No uncontrolled mutation

```
if mutation.source not in APPROVED_LAYERS:    reject(mutation)
```

```
if mutation.source not in APPROVED_LAYERS:    reject(mutation)
```

---

## 9.2 Invariant lock rule

If mutation violates CRITICAL invariant:

- reject immediately
reject immediately

- escalate to L3 governance review
escalate to L3 governance review

---

## 9.3 Stability threshold rule

If node stability < threshold:

- allow mutation proposals
allow mutation proposals

- but require dual approval (L1 + L3)
but require dual approval (L1 + L3)

---

# 10. Mutation Audit Trail

Every accepted mutation produces an immutable record:

```
MutationRecord {  mutation_id  applied_by  timestamp  before_state  after_state  justification  validation_result}
```

```
MutationRecord {  mutation_id  applied_by  timestamp  before_state  after_state  justification  validation_result}
```

Stored in Nebula ashistorical truth layer.

# 11. Governance Decision Engine

L3 uses a deterministic scoring system:

```
score(mutation) =    evidence_strength  + validation_support  + execution_failure_correlation  - risk_score  - graph_impact_radius
```

```
score(mutation) =    evidence_strength  + validation_support  + execution_failure_correlation  - risk_score  - graph_impact_radius
```

Approval thresholds:

- ≥ 0.75 → approved
≥ 0.75 → approved

- 0.5–0.75 → review required
0.5–0.75 → review required

- < 0.5 → rejected
< 0.5 → rejected

# 12. Execution vs Truth Separation

Critical system rule:

> Execution success does not automatically imply truth correctness.

Execution success does not automatically imply truth correctness.

And:

> Truth correction does not automatically imply execution change.

Truth correction does not automatically imply execution change.

They are decoupled intentionally.

---

# 13. Recovery Mode

If system instability is detected:

- L1 freezes mutation generation
L1 freezes mutation generation

- L2 tightens validation rules
L2 tightens validation rules

- L3 enters manual review mode
L3 enters manual review mode

- Conduit continues only on VERIFIED subgraph
Conduit continues only on VERIFIED subgraph

Nebula tracks:

- mutation frequency
mutation frequency

- rollback frequency
rollback frequency

- invariant violation density
invariant violation density

- graph churn rate
graph churn rate

High churn triggers:

- stricter governance
stricter governance

reduced L1 autonomy

increased validation strictness

# 15. Key System Property

> Nebula is self-modifying, but not self-authorizing.

Nebula is self-modifying, but not self-authorizing.

Modification and authorization are permanently separated.

# 8. Rollback System

Nebula supports deterministic rollback.

---

## 8.1 Rollback rules

Rollback produces a new version:

```
function rollback(target_version):    base = load(target_version)    new_version = clone(base)    mark_as_rollback(new_version)    return new_version
```

Shared Execution ModelAll agents operate over:GraphState(version_id, branch_id)Important constraint:> All agents see the same frozen snapshot of Nebula per execution cycle.No live mutation during reasoning phase.---# 5. Cognitive CycleEach execution tick follows:Snapshot GraphStateDispatch role-based agentsRun parallel retrieval per agentGenerate agent-specific subgraphsEmit proposals (not mutations)Aggregate resultsResolve conflictsSend to governance or execution layer---# 6. Agent Execution Model---## 6.1 Builder AgentPurpose:> Construct executable interpretations of the graph### Output:- Execution plans- Candidate DAG expansions- Implementation-oriented subgraphs### Retrieval bias:- L1 heavy- ALGORITHM, DATA_MODEL, MIGRATION_STEP---## 6.2 Architect AgentPurpose:> Evaluate structural correctness and system design coherence### Output:- Structural critiques- Invariant suggestions- Dependency rebalancing proposals### Retrieval bias:- L2 heavy- INVARIANT, PROTOCOL_RULE, RATIONALE---## 6.3 Inspector AgentPurpose:> Detect contradictions, violations, and unstable assumptions### Output:- Conflict reports- Invariant violations- Risk maps### Retrieval bias:- QUESTIONED, OUTDATED, INVARIANT---## 6.4 Explorer AgentPurpose:> Maximize semantic discovery and coverage### Output:- Expanded subgraphs- Alternative interpretations- Hidden dependency suggestions### Retrieval bias:- OVERVIEW, EXAMPLE, RATIONALE---## 6.5 Conduit AgentPurpose:> Convert validated outputs into executable DAGs### Output:- Execution DAG proposals- Scheduling plans- Deterministic execution graphs### Retrieval bias:- STRICT EXECUTION SUBSET ONLY---# 7. Parallel Retrieval LayerEach agent performs independent retrieval:```pseudo id="pr1"for agent in agents:subgraph[agent] =retrieve(GraphState,role_profile = agent.role,time_context = snapshot.version_id)No shared mutable state during retrieval phase.8. Proposal Emission ModelAgents do NOT mutate the graph.They emit:AgentProposal {agent_idproposal_typetarget_nodes[]confidencerationaleevidence[]}``` id="prop1"---# 9. Conflict ModelMultiple agents may propose contradictory actions.---## 9.1 Conflict types- STRUCTURAL_CONFLICT (edge/node disagreement)- SEMANTIC_CONFLICT (chunk classification disagreement)- EXECUTION_CONFLICT (DAG ordering disagreement)- INVARIANT_CONFLICT (rule disagreement)---## 9.2 Conflict resolution pipelinecluster proposals by targetgroup conflicting proposalsscore by agent authority weightevaluate via governance rulesemit resolved mutation plan---# 10. Agent Authority WeightsNot all agents are equal in all contexts.| Agent      | Structural | Semantic | Execution | Invariant ||------------|------------|----------|-----------|-----------|| Builder    | Medium     | High     | High      | Low       || Architect  | High       | High     | Medium    | High      || Inspector  | Medium     | High     | Low       | Very High || Explorer   | Low        | Medium   | Low       | Low       || Conduit    | High       | Medium   | Very High | Medium    |Authority is **context-sensitive**, not absolute.---# 11. Aggregation EngineAfter all agents produce proposals:```pseudo id="agg1"function aggregate(proposals):grouped = group_by_target(proposals)for group in grouped:resolved = resolve_conflicts(group)ranked = rank_by(confidence,agent_authority,evidence_strength)output.append(top(ranked))12. Execution GateOnly aggregated outputs may proceed to:WRP Validation EngineConduit SchedulerNebula Mutation SystemRaw agent outputs arenever executed directly.13. Temporal Consistency RuleAll agents operate on:identical GraphState snapshot per cycleThis guarantees:no temporal driftno inconsistent reasoningreproducible multi-agent outputs14. Cognitive Divergence PrincipleAgents are expected to disagree.This is not a bug.It is a signal:divergence → missing structureconvergence → stable knowledgeoscillation → unstable ontology15. Stability ScoringEach proposal receives:stability_score =agent_confidence+ cross_agent_agreement+ validation_support- contradiction_density``` id="stab3"High stability → safe to promoteLow stability → Inspector review required---# 16. System LoopGraphState snapshot↓Parallel agent execution↓Proposal emission↓Conflict resolution↓WRP validation↓Governance approval↓Conduit execution↓Receipts↓Nebula update↓(next cycle)---# 17. Key System Property> Nebula does not rely on a single reasoning process. It relies on structured disagreement between specialized cognitive projections over a shared semantic state.---# 18. Final Principle> Intelligence emerges not from one model seeing everything correctly, but from multiple constrained perspectives negotiating a shared structured reality.What you now have (this is the real “final architecture”)You now have a complete multi-layer system:1. WRPformal correctness constraints2. Nebula (temporal + evolving)semantic graph + trust + version history3. Retrieval systemrole + time aware projection4. Multi-agent fabric (this doc)parallel reasoning system5. Conduit runtimedeterministic execution engine6. Validation enginepre-execution proof system7. Self-healing systempost-execution learning8. Governance modelmutation authority control9. Temporal versioningbranching semantic timelinesWhat you’ve actually built (honest framing)This is no longer:a pipelinea frameworkor a graph systemIt is:Amulti-agent, versioned, self-validating semantic execution operating system with governed mutation and temporal cognitionWhere this naturally goes next (final possible layers)At this point, only two expansions remain meaningful:A. Cross-branch simulation engine(run multiple futures and compare outcomes)B. Global consistency compiler(ensures long-range invariants across the entire Nebula timeline graph)If you want to continue, the next artifact is:“Nebula Cross-Branch Simulation & Counterfactual Execution System”That’s where the system starts asking:“whatwouldhappen if we evolved differently?”SourcesSuperblocksSponsoredVibe code the app. Not the audit log.AI writes code. divergence → missing structure
